  32: 
  33: ## Quick Start Wizard
  34: 
  35: Run the interactive setup/menu wizard:
  36: 
  37: ```bash
  38: ./start.sh
  39: ```
  40: 
  41: Optional Rust-native operator menu (baseline UX path):
  42: 
  43: ```bash
  44: rustynet operator menu
  45: ```
  46: 
  47: If you are starting from local UTM VMs and want the fastest first-pass inventory,
  48: use the compact discovery summary first:
  49: 
  50: ```bash
  51: cargo run --quiet -p rustynet-cli -- ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm-summary --inventory documents/operations/active/vm_lab_inventory.json
  52: ```
  53: 
  54: Use the full JSON discovery report when you need the raw bundle, IP, SSH, and
  55: readiness details:
  56: 
  57: ```bash
  58: cargo run --quiet -p rustynet-cli -- ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm --inventory documents/operations/active/vm_lab_inventory.json
  59: ```
  60: 
  61: Add `--update-inventory-live-ips` when you want a fully ready discovery pass to
  62: refresh `documents/operations/active/vm_lab_inventory.json` without first
  63: forcing a restart. Add `--report-dir <path>` when you want the JSON report and
  64: summary written as artifacts.
  65: 
  66: ## Live Lab Workflow
  67: 
  68: Use this four-step path when you want to exercise the local UTM lab end to end:
  69: 
  70: 1. Discover
  71:    - `ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm-summary`
  72:    - Finds the local UTM bundles, live IPs, SSH readiness, and the fastest
  73:      “can I use this lab?” summary.
  74:    - Use `ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm` when you need the full JSON evidence.
  75:    - If discovery shows live IPs but `readiness.execution_ready=false`,
  76:      restart the local UTM fleet and wait for SSH auth readiness before you
  77:      proceed:
  78:      `ops vm-lab-restart --all --wait-ready --ssh-identity-file ~/.ssh/rustynet_lab_ed25519 --known-hosts-file ~/.ssh/known_hosts`
  79:    - A successful `ops vm-lab-restart --wait-ready` run also refreshes the
  80:      local UTM inventory IP tracking in
  81:      `documents/operations/active/vm_lab_inventory.json` so `ssh_target` and
  82:      `last_known_ip` match the authoritative live IPs that actually came back.
  83:    - Add `--json` when you want a machine-readable restart result, and
  84:      `--report-dir <path>` when you want restart artifacts written to disk.
  85: 2. Setup
  86:    - `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab`
  87:    - Generates or validates the live-lab profile, runs preflight plus the
  88:      setup-only stages, writes the report directory, and supports
  89:      `--resume-from` or `--rerun-stage` for deterministic reruns.
  90:    - The setup wrapper now writes provenance-bound `state/setup_manifest.json`
  91:      and `state/report_state.json` before execution. A reused setup report
  92:      directory is accepted only when the current commit, dirty/clean tree
  93:      state, profile, inventory identity, wrapper version/source, and setup
  94:      flags match the recorded setup provenance.
  95: 3. Link and Test
  96:    - `ops vm-lab-run-live-lab`
  97:    - Runs the full live-lab suite and validates the report contract instead of
  98:      trusting the shell exit code alone.
  99:    - If the report directory already contains only completed setup stages from
 100:      `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab`, it continues with the test stages without
 101:      rerunning setup, but only when the existing report directory passes the
 102:      full provenance check. Any commit, dirty-tree, profile, inventory, or
 103:      wrapper mismatch fails closed instead of attempting best-effort reuse.
 104: 4. Diagnose
 105:    - `ops vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure`
 106:    - Collects the first failed stage and packages stage-aware failure context
 107:      for triage.
 108: 
 109: This is the recommended operator path for live-lab work:
 110: discover, set up, link and test, then diagnose if something fails.
 111: 
 112: This four-step live-lab wrapper path is currently Linux-runtime only. Profiles
 113: with missing target platform metadata, or with any target that is not
 114: `platform=linux`, `remote_shell=posix`, `guest_exec_mode=linux_bash`, and
 115: `service_manager=systemd`, fail closed before any `live_linux_*` shell stage
 116: runs.
 117: 
 118: Live-lab automation security expectations:
 119: 
 120: - SSH host trust must be pinned with `--ssh-known-hosts-file` or a pre-populated `~/.ssh/known_hosts`
 121: - SSH TOFU (`accept-new`) is not part of the active wrapper path
 122: - automation targets are expected to satisfy `sudo -n`
 123: - unattended runtime secret custody remains credential-only; plaintext passphrase files are not an acceptable substitute
 124: - canonical cross-network pass reports now require per-suite SSH trust summaries plus daemon path evidence showing `transport_socket_identity_state=authoritative_backend_shared_transport`
 125: - canonical cross-network soak evidence now fails closed unless the direct path stays direct for the full soak with zero fallback/drift samples
 126: 
 127: If you want the CLI to make the discovery-versus-restart decision for you and
 128: then run the standard workflow in one shot, use:
 129: 
 130: - `ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab`
 131: - It discovers the selected local UTM VMs, restarts only the aliases that are
 132:   not `readiness.execution_ready`, reruns discovery, then proceeds through
 133:   setup, full live-lab execution, and diagnose-on-failure using the same report
 134:   directory.
 135: - It now writes stage pass/fail progress lines to the terminal during the run
 136:   and prints the final `orchestrate_result.json` path when the command
 137:   completes.
 138: - The orchestration wrapper requires a fresh report directory and refuses to
 139:   write into a populated one.
 140: - Add `--stop-after-ready` when you want it to stop after proving VM
 141:   reachability and inventory freshness, without starting setup.
 142: 
 143: If report-directory reuse is rejected, do one of these:
 144: 
 145: - use a new empty `--report-dir`, or
 146: - rerun the original setup/report flow from the exact same commit and inputs on
 147:   the original directory
 148: 
 149: Supporting wrappers remain available when you need tighter control over one part
 150: of the flow:
 151: - `ops vm-lab-write-live-lab-profile`
 152: - `ops vm-lab-validate-live-lab-profile`
 153: - `ops vm-lab-bootstrap-phase --phase all`
 154: 
 155: Current VM-lab Windows truth on this branch:
 156: 
 157: - Windows UTM guests are `runtime-host-capable only` in the current
 158:   `ops vm-lab-*` surface.
 159: - Windows-safe helper surfaces currently include `vm-lab-discover-local-utm`,
 160:   `vm-lab-start`, `vm-lab-restart`, `vm-lab-sync-repo`, the PowerShell-first
 161:   access bootstrap under
 162:   `scripts/vm_lab/windows/Enable-WindowsVmLabAccess.ps1`, diagnostics via
 163:   `scripts/bootstrap/windows/Collect-RustyNetWindowsDiagnostics.ps1`, the
 164:   direct SCM host-surface smoke helper
 165:   `scripts/bootstrap/windows/Smoke-RustyNetWindowsServiceHost.ps1`, and Windows
 166:   `vm-lab-bootstrap-phase` entrypoints for `sync-source`, `build-release`,
 167:   `smoke-service-host`, `install-release`, `restart-runtime`, `verify-runtime`,
 168:   and `all`.
 169: - Mixed Linux/Windows inventories dispatch bootstrap helpers by target platform;
 170:   Windows targets are not sent into the Linux `live_linux_*` stage scripts.
 171: - The live-lab wrapper family `vm-lab-validate-live-lab-profile`,
 172:   `vm-lab-setup-live-lab`, `vm-lab-run-live-lab`,
 173:   `vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab`, `vm-lab-iterate-live-lab`,
 174:   `vm-lab-run-suite`, and `vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure` remains
 175:   Linux-runtime only and fails closed on missing or incompatible target
 176:   metadata.
 177: - On the current branch, `rustynetd` exposes a reviewed Windows
 178:   `--windows-service --env-file` host path and now carries both the explicit
 179:   fail-closed backend label `windows-unsupported` and the opt-in reviewed
 180:   backend label `windows-wireguard-nt` behind the stable backend abstraction.
 181:   The reviewed Windows runtime boundary now pins service/runtime state under
 182:   `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\{config,logs,trust,membership,keys,secrets}`,
 183:   requires a protected `secrets\key-custody` root, stores reviewed runtime
 184:   passphrase material as DPAPI-protected `.dpapi` blobs, and only permits
 185:   reviewed local named-pipe IPC under `\\.\pipe\RustyNet\...` for probe and
 186:   ACL-inspection self-check requests. The install/verify/diagnostics helpers
 187:   now make Windows 11, elevation, service SID, and runtime-boundary state
 188:   explicit without claiming backend capability. `build-release` is still
 189:   conditional on verified Windows/MSVC tooling being present. On the current
 190:   branch, when local Windows UTM execution lands in the service-style/system
 191:   profile context and per-user tooling is missing there, the Windows bootstrap
 192:   helper now hands off `build-release` to a one-shot interactive scheduled
 193:   task under the logged-in Windows user and waits for the same guest-authored
 194:   build report. That path fails closed if there is no logged-in interactive
 195:   administrator session or if the user-scoped App Installer/WinGet bootstrap
 196:   still cannot be proven. The Windows install/restart/verify entrypoints must
 197:   not be treated as dataplane-capable or release-gated proof. The latest
 198:   measured local Windows UTM attempt on 2026-04-19 showed App Installer
 199:   present on the guest but no interactive Windows user session available, so
 200:   `build-release` now fails honestly on that prerequisite instead of reporting
 201:   a generic missing-`winget.exe` state from Local System. There is still no
 202:   fresh Windows install/runtime/node evidence for current `HEAD`.
 203: - Windows is not `release-gated and evidenced` on the current branch. The
 204:   required fresh-install/release-gate OS set remains Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora,
 205:   Mint, and macOS until measured Windows evidence exists.

 207: ## Release Readiness
 208: 
 209: Use this final sign-off command when you want the repo-level release-readiness
 210: guardrail:
 211: 
 212: ```bash
 213: ./scripts/ci/release_readiness_gates.sh
 214: ```
 215: 
 216: That wrapper keeps the Phase 5 release-doc/provenance path and the Phase 10
 217: fresh-install/cross-network evidence path on one fail-closed command. Reduced
 218: helper evidence is useful for narrowing defects, but it is not treated as a
 219: substitute for full release-gate evidence.
 220: 
 221: Authoritative release-gate reporting is generated during gate execution:
 222: 
 223: - `artifacts/release/phase5_gate_report.json`
 224: - `artifacts/release/phase5_readiness_bundle.json`
 225: 
 226: Those files must come from the current gate run. They record
 227: `executed_passed`, `executed_failed`, and `not_executed` states; pre-existing
 228: files are not accepted as proof.
 229: 
 230: Current sign-off references:
 231: 
 232: - [documents/operations/ReleaseReadinessGuardrails.md](./documents/operations/ReleaseReadinessGuardrails.md)
 233: - [documents/operations/active/Phase5ReleaseReadinessSummary_2026-04-12.md](./documents/operations/active/Phase5ReleaseReadinessSummary_2026-04-12.md)
 234: 
 235: The wizard handles:
 236: - role selection (`admin`, `client`, or `blind_exit`) during setup, with role-specific console permissions
 237: - guided in-menu role switching (`client` <-> `admin`) with local signed assignment refresh support on Linux
 238: - host OS detection on startup with strict host-profile enforcement (`linux` dataplane vs `macos` compatibility)
 239: - first-run bootstrap (dependencies, keys, trust material, systemd wiring)
 240: - optional signer-backed trust-evidence auto-refresh timer on Linux to keep trust freshness valid during unattended runtime
 241: - daemon/service lifecycle
 242: - centrally signed auto-tunnel defaults with fail-closed enforcement
 243: - manual peer break-glass mutation paths removed; signed assignment workflows are the only supported peer/routing mutation path
 244: - encrypted key custody at rest + runtime key management
 245: - Rust-backed WireGuard custody bootstrap (`rustynet ops bootstrap-wireguard-custody`) is mandatory in setup paths; unsupported/failed ops invocation is fail-closed (no shell fallback)
 246: - sensitive bootstrap/migration artifacts (legacy key files and temporary passphrase files) are scrubbed before removal
 247: - startup config integrity is strict for security-critical fields: invalid persisted role/chain/backend/interface/port values are fail-closed errors (no silent coercion)
 248: - macOS canonical storage paths are enforced (`.../trust`, `.../assignment`, `.../keys`, `.../membership`); non-canonical legacy path values are fail-closed
 249: - dependency bootstrap is single-route hardening: `start.sh` installs `rustup` from the approved host package manager and then installs the pinned workspace toolchain from `rust-toolchain.toml`; ambient distro `cargo`/`rustc` fallback and remote installer scripts are disabled
 250: - Linux runtime passphrase handling is credential-only: `rustynetd` requires a systemd
 251:   encrypted credential (`/etc/rustynet/credentials/wg_key_passphrase.cred`) and
 252:   rejects direct plaintext passphrase-file fallback at daemon runtime
 253: - Linux signing-key passphrase handling is also credential-only for unattended jobs:
 254:   `/etc/rustynet/credentials/signing_key_passphrase.cred` is loaded into refresh
 255:   services via `LoadCredentialEncrypted` (no persistent plaintext passphrase files)
 256: - signing credential decrypt flows pin embedded credential name for cross-distro
 257:   systemd compatibility: `systemd-creds decrypt --name=signing_key_passphrase ...`
 258: - signing passphrase materialization is Rust-backed and fail-closed: the CLI decrypts
 259:   into a fresh secure temp path and atomically publishes the requested output, rather
 260:   than writing credential material through ad hoc direct-to-existing-file flows
 261: - local key rotation/revocation through signed control-plane workflows
 262: - membership bootstrap with encrypted persisted owner signing key (default Linux path: `/etc/rustynet/membership.owner.key`)
 263: - exit-node and LAN-access toggles, including one-hop and two-hop chain selection in `start.sh` (re-selecting the active chain disconnects/clears selection)
 264: - main menu quick actions keep VPN connect-state explicit: option `1` toggles between `CONNECT TO VPN` and `DISCONNECT FROM NETWORK`; option `2` is `SELECT EXIT NODE` for `admin`/`client`
 265: - `SELECT EXIT NODE` performs a per-candidate readiness probe (`membership + tunnel`) and prints `membership`, `tunnel`, and `readiness`; current selection is marked with `*`
 266: - connectivity architecture is staged toward direct-UDP-first with signed traversal endpoint hints and ciphertext-only relay for hard NAT paths; current runtime validates signed traversal bundles and signed coordination records, requires traversal-authoritative peer coverage for all managed peers in enforced auto-tunnel mode, collects bounded backend handshake evidence via `wg show ... latest-handshakes`, and only promotes `direct_active` or `relay_active` from fresh live proof rather than programmed state; relay-backed sessions are periodically reprobed on reconcile, and direct-active peers now use live backend handshake evidence to avoid stale cached path decisions before failing back from relay when direct becomes healthy again; traversal probe fanout, freshness, and reprobe cadence are explicit daemon policy (`--traversal-probe-max-candidates`, `--traversal-probe-max-pairs`, `--traversal-probe-rounds`, `--traversal-probe-round-spacing-ms`, `--traversal-probe-relay-switch-after-failures`, `--traversal-probe-handshake-freshness-secs`, `--traversal-probe-reprobe-interval-secs`) instead of implicit runtime defaults; the daemon now consumes an explicit backend-owned authoritative shared-transport contract for STUN round trips, relay hello/refresh, keepalive, and transport-identity diagnostics when a backend provides it, but current production WireGuard backends still explicitly block those workflows on separate daemon-owned sockets because they remain command-only adapters over OS-managed peer sockets and do not yet expose authoritative packet I/O or a backend-owned datagram multiplexer; the explicit non-default mode names `linux-wireguard-userspace-shared` and `macos-wireguard-userspace-shared` are now wired through daemon/start parsing and host-profile enforcement, but both still fail closed with that precise blocker, so plug-and-play cross-network completion remains blocked on a production backend mode that can satisfy the shared-transport contract plus fresh commit-bound live direct/relay/failback evidence
 267: - `rustynet netcheck` now reports structured traversal diagnostics (`path_mode`, `path_reason`, traversal artifact freshness, candidate counts by type, and validation error state) and uses runtime-authored path states (`direct_active`, `relay_active`, `fail_closed`) instead of a static transport string
 268: - traversal artifact custody and probe policy are configurable end-to-end (`--traversal-bundle`, `--traversal-verifier-key`, `--traversal-watermark`, `--traversal-max-age-secs`, `--traversal-probe-*`), and Linux systemd install wiring now propagates `RUSTYNET_TRAVERSAL_*` into `rustynetd.service`
 269: - Magic DNS is now a signed control-plane path only: `rustynetd` loads a signed DNS-zone bundle from pinned custody paths, cross-checks every managed record against signed assignment state, answers the managed zone from a loopback-only authoritative resolver (`--dns-zone-*`, `--dns-resolver-bind-addr`), returns `SERVFAIL` for managed-name queries when signed DNS state is missing/invalid/stale, and refuses non-managed names rather than falling back to ad hoc local overrides or `/etc/hosts`; the supported Linux host-integration path is a dedicated `systemd-resolved` unit (`rustynetd-managed-dns.service`) that routes the private zone through the Rustynet interface only, with no `/etc/hosts` or raw resolver fallback
 270: - route advertisement and status checks
 271: 
 272: Host-profile behavior:
 273: - Linux host: full runtime/dataplane provisioning.
 274: - macOS host: full client/runtime dataplane provisioning using userspace WireGuard (`wireguard-go`) with privileged-helper mediated system operations.
 275: - macOS service lifecycle hardening: daemon and privileged helper are managed through `launchd` (`launchctl bootstrap`/`kickstart`) rather than ad-hoc background processes.
 276: - macOS dependency hardening: privileged networking tools (`wg`, `wireguard-go`) must be installed with admin privileges in root-owned paths; non-admin local fallback is intentionally blocked.
 277: - macOS key custody hardening: WireGuard passphrase custody is Keychain-backed (`rustynet.wg_passphrase` service); persistent plaintext passphrase files are rejected by startup preflight.
 278: - macOS passphrase-file runtime fallback is removed; daemon runtime requires keychain-backed passphrase custody (`RUSTYNET_WG_KEY_PASSPHRASE_KEYCHAIN_ACCOUNT` + keychain item).
 279: - macOS path policy: Linux runtime roots (`/etc/rustynet`, `/var/lib/rustynet`, `/run/rustynet`, `/var/log/rustynet`) are not used; user-space paths are enforced instead.
 280: - macOS dependency hardening: Homebrew must already be installed via approved operator workflow; automated remote-script install fallback is blocked.
 281: - macOS PF safety: stale Rustynet PF anchors (`com.apple/rustynet_g*`) are pruned on dataplane generation apply to prevent residual fail-closed anchors after crashes/restarts.

 292: After first setup, run `./start.sh` again anytime to open the terminal control menu.
 293: 
 294: Role model:
 295: - `admin`: full operational console (policy/trust/key/exit-node administration) with signed control-plane enforcement.
 296: - `client`: limited console for joining/using the network (status, connect/disconnect from exit nodes, LAN toggle), with admin-only actions blocked at daemon runtime.
 297: - `blind_exit`: least-knowledge exit-serving role intended as a final hop. It is immutable after setup (factory reset + fresh key provisioning required to change role), blocks local control-plane mutation commands, auto-enforces exit-serving posture, and sanitizes client-only assignment fields (selected exit/LAN flags) instead of fail-closing on role conversion.
 298: 
 299: Two-hop chain notes:
 300: - Client chain selection supports `1-hop` (`client -> exit`) and `2-hop` (`client -> entry relay -> final exit`) in `start.sh` under `SELECT EXIT NODE`.
 301: - For secure two-hop operation, the entry relay must be configured to use its upstream exit and advertise `0.0.0.0/0` (exit-serving) so it can relay downstream client traffic while tunneling upstream.
 302: - In relay-with-upstream mode, Linux dataplane enforcement now explicitly allows `rustynet0 -> rustynet0` forwarding and applies scoped tunnel-to-tunnel NAT (`iif rustynet0`, `oif rustynet0`) on the entry relay so return traffic from the final hop stays fail-closed and routable.
 303: - `blind_exit` remains final-hop oriented: it can serve exit but cannot be configured to select an upstream exit.
 304: 
 305: Linux trust-refresh behavior:
 306: - When admin setup has signer-key access (`AUTO_REFRESH_TRUST=1`), install flow enables `rustynetd-trust-refresh.timer` and performs periodic signed trust evidence refreshes.
 307: - Linux trust refresh service path is Rust-only: `rustynetd-trust-refresh.service` executes `rustynet ops refresh-trust` directly (no shell wrapper in the active path), then enforces daemon-side signed state revalidation via `rustynet state refresh`.
 308: - systemd refresh units pin `/usr/local/bin/rustynet` and run `ops verify-runtime-binary-custody` as `ExecStartPre`, enforcing root-owned/non-group-writable binary custody before refresh execution.
 309: - `start.sh` manual trust refresh path is Rust-backed via `rustynet ops refresh-signed-trust` (typed passphrase materialization + scrubbed temp cleanup) with fail-closed behavior (no shell fallback).
 310: - Guided role switching no longer force-disables `AUTO_REFRESH_TRUST` for `client` mode when a local signer key is available; this prevents avoidable trust-staleness fail-closed transitions during long-running client operation.
 311: - If a node is switched to `client` mode without signer-key access, `AUTO_REFRESH_TRUST` is disabled with an explicit warning.
 312: - Trust refresh jobs write trust evidence as `root:<daemon-group>` with `0640` mode so `rustynetd` can validate trust state without exposing signer key material.
 313: - Trust signer keys are encrypted-at-rest and are signed/refreshed with explicit passphrase-file input (credential-injected under systemd).
 314: 
 315: Linux assignment-refresh behavior:
 316: - Auto-tunnel enforcement remains fail-closed: stale/invalid signed assignment bundles are rejected.
 317: - Trust and auto-tunnel watermark parsers are strict: only digest-bound `version=2` watermark files are accepted (legacy `version=1` is rejected fail-closed).
 318: - Linux assignment refresh service path is Rust-only: `rustynetd-assignment-refresh.service` executes `rustynet ops refresh-assignment` directly (no shell wrapper in the active path), then enforces daemon-side signed state revalidation via `rustynet state refresh`.
 319: - Linux service installer path is Rust-backed: `scripts/systemd/install_rustynetd_service.sh` is a thin wrapper to `rustynet ops install-systemd` (with `RUSTYNET_INSTALL_SOURCE_ROOT` pinned by the wrapper).
 320: - Linux `start.sh` exit-node selection/disable flows now require local signed assignment refresh support; if assignment refresh is unavailable, interactive exit-node mutation fails closed instead of falling back to raw direct CLI mutation.
 321: - Legacy Linux WireGuard key paths are no longer implicitly migrated in custody bootstrap/install flows; canonical paths must be present, or operators must perform explicit key re-enrollment/rotation.
 322: - Linux signing artifact custody expects `/etc/rustynet` parent directory mode
 323:   `0750` (`root:<daemon-group>`) with encrypted key files remaining `0600`.
 324: - For unattended runtime, enable signer-backed assignment refresh with:
 325:   - `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_AUTO_REFRESH=true` in `/etc/default/rustynetd`
 326:   - `/etc/rustynet/assignment-refresh.env` containing:
 327:     - `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_TARGET_NODE_ID`
 328:     - `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_NODES`
 329:     - `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_ALLOW`
 330:     - optional `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_EXIT_NODE_ID`
 331:     - `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_SIGNING_SECRET` (default `/etc/rustynet/assignment.signing.secret`, `0600 root:root`)
 332:     - `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_SIGNING_SECRET_PASSPHRASE_FILE` (default credential path injected by `rustynetd-assignment-refresh.service`)
 333:     - `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_TTL_SECS` and `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_MIN_REMAINING_SECS`
 334:   - assignment refresh env files are written in quoted `EnvironmentFile` format; structured values such as `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_NODES` and `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_ALLOW` must not be emitted as raw unquoted shell text
 335: - Installer enables `rustynetd-assignment-refresh.timer` when assignment auto-refresh is enabled.
 336: - Refresh jobs rewrite assignment artifacts with strict custody:
 337:   - bundle: `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.assignment` (`0640 root:<daemon-group>`)
 338:   - verifier key: `/etc/rustynet/assignment.pub` (`0644 root:root`)
 339: 
 340: Signed auto-tunnel assignment issuance:
 341: - Issue centrally signed per-node assignment bundles with explicit allow rules:
 342: ```bash
 343: rustynet assignment issue \
 344:   --target-node-id client-40 \
 345:   --nodes "client-40|192.168.18.40:51820|<client_pubkey_hex>;exit-37|192.168.18.37:51820|<exit_pubkey_hex>" \
 346:   --allow "client-40|exit-37" \
 347:   --signing-secret /etc/rustynet/assignment.signing.secret \
 348:   --signing-secret-passphrase-file /run/credentials/rustynetd-assignment-refresh.service/signing_key_passphrase \
 349:   --output /tmp/client-40.assignment \
 350:   --verifier-key-output /tmp/assignment.pub \
 351:   --exit-node-id exit-37 \
 352:   --ttl-secs 300
 353: ```
 354: - Initialize an encrypted assignment signing secret:
 355: ```bash
 356: rustynet assignment init-signing-secret \
 357:   --output /etc/rustynet/assignment.signing.secret \
 358:   --signing-secret-passphrase-file /run/credentials/rustynetd-assignment-refresh.service/signing_key_passphrase \
 359:   --force
 360: ```
 361: - `--nodes` format: `node_id|endpoint|public_key_hex[|owner|hostname|os|tags_csv]` entries separated by `;`.
 362: - `--allow` format: `source_node_id|destination_node_id` entries separated by `;` (default-deny unless explicitly allowed).
 363: - Endpoint stability: set a fixed WireGuard listen port on each node (`RUSTYNET_WG_LISTEN_PORT`, default `51820`) so signed assignment endpoints remain valid across daemon restarts.
 364: - Optional internet reachability assist for Linux exit-serving nodes: setup now exposes opt-in NAT-PMP auto port-forward (`AUTO_PORT_FORWARD_EXIT=1`, default `0`; lease via `AUTO_PORT_FORWARD_LEASE_SECS`, default `1200`). This path is intentionally best-effort and fail-safe: unsupported routers/backends keep normal tunnel operation but leave external mapping unavailable.
 365: - NAT-PMP/PCP/UPnP-style mapping is an optimization only and is not the primary connectivity architecture.
 366: - Exit-serving mode under enforced auto-tunnel: advertise `0.0.0.0/0` on the serving node (`rustynet route advertise 0.0.0.0/0`). This is the only route mutation allowed while auto-tunnel enforcement is enabled.
 367: - When `0.0.0.0/0` is advertised and the node is not itself using an exit node, `rustynetd` applies forwarding+NAT for secure exit serving during reconcile.
 368: - Linux fail-closed management and peer-endpoint bypass routes resolve interface per destination (`ip route get`) before installing table `51820` host/CIDR routes. This prevents dual-NIC lockouts when management and internet egress interfaces differ.
 369: - Linux service egress hardening now derives `RUSTYNET_EGRESS_INTERFACE` from the selected exit endpoint route when a client exit is selected (assignment-backed); explicit env overrides that do not match the route-derived interface are rejected fail-closed.
 370: - `rustynetd` no longer ships with a stale `eth0` assumption: daemon default `egress_interface` is `auto`, and service startup resolves the actual default-route interface before dataplane preflight.
 371: - Keep assignment TTL aligned to `RUSTYNET_AUTO_TUNNEL_MAX_AGE_SECS` (default max-age is 300s). If TTL exceeds max-age, max-age still enforces fail-closed expiration.
 372: 
 373: Signed Magic DNS zone issuance and verification:
 374: - Issue a signed managed-zone bundle from the same control-plane signing root used for other signed artifacts:
 375: ```bash
 376: rustynet dns zone issue \
 377:   --signing-secret /etc/rustynet/membership.owner.key \
 378:   --signing-secret-passphrase-file /run/credentials/rustynetd-trust-refresh.service/membership_owner_signing_key_passphrase \
 379:   --subject-node-id client-40 \
 380:   --nodes "client-40|192.168.18.40:51820|<client_pubkey_hex>;exit-37|192.168.18.37:51820|<exit_pubkey_hex>" \
 381:   --allow "client-40|exit-37" \
 382:   --records-manifest /tmp/dns-zone-records.manifest \
 383:   --output /tmp/client-40.dns-zone \
 384:   --verifier-key-output /tmp/dns-zone.pub \
 385:   --zone-name rustynet \
 386:   --ttl-secs 300
 387: ```
 388: - Verify a signed managed-zone bundle before deployment:
 389: ```bash
 390: rustynet dns zone verify \
 391:   --bundle /tmp/client-40.dns-zone \
 392:   --verifier-key /tmp/dns-zone.pub \
 393:   --expected-zone-name rustynet \
 394:   --expected-subject-node-id client-40
 395: ```
 396: - `--records-manifest` must be canonical UTF-8 `key=value` text:
 397:   - required top-level fields: `version=1`, `record_count=<n>`
 398:   - required per-record fields: `record.<i>.label`, `record.<i>.target_node_id`, `record.<i>.ttl_secs`, `record.<i>.alias_count`
 399:   - aliases are indexed as `record.<i>.alias.<j>=<label>`
 400:   - unknown fields, sparse indices, duplicate fields, and whitespace-padded fields are rejected fail-closed
 401: - `rustynetd` authoritative DNS defaults:
 402:   - zone bundle: `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.dns-zone`
 403:   - verifier key: `/etc/rustynet/dns-zone.pub`
 404:   - watermark: `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.dns-zone.watermark`
 405:   - max age: `300s`
 406:   - managed zone: `rustynet`
 407:   - loopback bind: `127.0.0.1:53535`
 408: - The authoritative resolver is loopback-only; non-loopback bind addresses are rejected fail-closed.
 409: - Linux systemd install now also wires a dedicated managed-DNS routing unit:
 410:   - unit: `rustynetd-managed-dns.service`
 411:   - resolver integration: `systemd-resolved` via `resolvectl`
 412:   - routing scope: the Rustynet interface only (`RUSTYNET_WG_INTERFACE`)
 413:   - Linux managed-DNS routing currently requires an IPv4 loopback resolver bind such as `127.0.0.1:53535`
 414: 
 415: ## Automated Debian Pair Clean Install + Tunnel Validation
 416: 
 417: To repeat a full two-node Debian 13 clean install and secure tunnel validation from one operator machine:
 418: 
 419: ```bash
 420: umask 077 && printf 'tempo\n' > /tmp/rustynet_sudo.pass
 421: ./scripts/e2e/debian_two_node_clean_install_and_tunnel_test.sh \
 422:   --exit-host 192.168.18.37 \
 423:   --client-host 192.168.18.40 \
 424:   --ssh-user debian \
 425:   --ssh-known-hosts-file ~/.ssh/known_hosts \
 426:   --sudo-password-file /tmp/rustynet_sudo.pass \
 427:   --ssh-allow-cidrs 192.168.18.2/32 \
 428:   --skip-apt
 429: ```
 430: 
 431: What this script does:
 432: - pushes the selected local git ref (`HEAD` by default) to both hosts as a clean source archive
 433: - performs clean Rustynet runtime reset on each host (service stop + Rustynet-owned dataplane cleanup)
 434: - builds and installs `rustynetd` + `rustynet`
 435: - initializes encrypted key custody using `systemd-creds` credential blob (no persistent plaintext passphrase files)
 436: - decrypts signing credential blobs with explicit embedded-name pinning
 437:   (`systemd-creds decrypt --name=signing_key_passphrase`) for distro portability
 438: - initializes trust + membership state, issues signed assignment bundles, and enables auto-tunnel enforcement
 439: - configures exit-node routing and validates tunnel/dataplane/security invariants
 440: - writes a validation report to `artifacts/phase10/debian_two_node_remote_validation.md`
 441: 
 442: Important:
 443: - `--ssh-allow-cidrs` is required and should be your management CIDR(s), not `0.0.0.0/0`.
 444: - SSH host trust is pinned: provide `--ssh-known-hosts-file` or pre-populate `~/.ssh/known_hosts` with the target host keys. TOFU (`accept-new`) is intentionally disabled.
 445: - SSH control-master sessions are used; password-based SSH is supported interactively.
 446: - When SSH user is non-root, provide `--sudo-password-file` (mode `0600`); this keeps sudo secrets out of command arguments.
 447: 
 448: ## Active-Network Adversarial Security Tests
 449: 
 450: Run hardened, active-network adversarial tests against real hosts:
 451: 
 452: ```bash
 453: ./scripts/e2e/real_wireguard_signed_state_tamper_e2e.sh \
 454:   --exit-host 192.168.18.49 \
 455:   --client-host 192.168.18.50 \
 456:   --ssh-user root \
 457:   --ssh-known-hosts-file ~/.ssh/known_hosts \
 458:   --ssh-allow-cidrs 192.168.18.2/32 \
 459:   --skip-apt
 460: 
 461: ./scripts/e2e/real_wireguard_rogue_path_hijack_e2e.sh \
 462:   --exit-host 192.168.18.49 \
 463:   --client-host 192.168.18.50 \
 464:   --ssh-user root \
 465:   --ssh-known-hosts-file ~/.ssh/known_hosts \
 466:   --ssh-allow-cidrs 192.168.18.2/32 \
 467:   --rogue-endpoint-ip 203.0.113.250 \
 468:   --skip-apt
 469: ```
 470: 
 471: Security intent:
 472: - signed-state tamper test mutates the active assignment bundle and requires daemon fail-closed behavior (`state=FailClosed`, `restricted_safe_mode=true`) until valid signed state is restored.
 473: - rogue-path hijack test forges assignment endpoints to a rogue IP (with invalid signature) and requires explicit rejection, no rogue endpoint adoption in `wg show`, and secure recovery after restoration.
 474: 
 475: Optional combined gate wrapper:
 476: 
 477: ```bash
 478: RUSTYNET_ACTIVE_NET_EXIT_HOST=192.168.18.49 \
 479: RUSTYNET_ACTIVE_NET_CLIENT_HOST=192.168.18.50 \
 480: RUSTYNET_ACTIVE_NET_SSH_USER=root \
 481: RUSTYNET_ACTIVE_NET_SSH_KNOWN_HOSTS_FILE=~/.ssh/known_hosts \
 482: RUSTYNET_ACTIVE_NET_SSH_ALLOW_CIDRS=192.168.18.2/32 \
 483: RUSTYNET_ACTIVE_NET_ROGUE_ENDPOINT_IP=203.0.113.250 \
 484: RUSTYNET_ACTIVE_NET_SKIP_APT=1 \
 485: ./scripts/ci/active_network_security_gates.sh
 486: ```
 487: 
 488: To include these tests in security regression gates:
 489: - set `RUSTYNET_SECURITY_RUN_ACTIVE_NETWORK_GATES=1`.
 490: - set `RUSTYNET_SECURITY_REQUIRE_ACTIVE_NETWORK_GATES=1` to fail closed when active-network gates are not run.
 491: 
 492: Additional live Linux regression scenarios on the active VM lab:
 493: 
 494: ```bash
 495: umask 077 && printf 'tempo\n' > /tmp/rustynet_lab.pass
 496: 
 497: ./scripts/e2e/live_linux_two_hop_test.sh \
 498:   --ssh-known-hosts-file ~/.ssh/known_hosts \
 499:   --ssh-password-file /tmp/rustynet_lab.pass \
 500:   --sudo-password-file /tmp/rustynet_lab.pass
 501: 
 502: ./scripts/e2e/live_linux_exit_handoff_test.sh \
 503:   --ssh-known-hosts-file ~/.ssh/known_hosts \
 504:   --ssh-password-file /tmp/rustynet_lab.pass \
 505:   --sudo-password-file /tmp/rustynet_lab.pass
 506: 
 507: ./scripts/e2e/live_linux_lan_toggle_test.sh \
 508:   --ssh-known-hosts-file ~/.ssh/known_hosts \
 509:   --ssh-password-file /tmp/rustynet_lab.pass \
 510:   --sudo-password-file /tmp/rustynet_lab.pass
 511: ```
 512: 
 513: These scripts are measured live-network regressions for:
 514: - two-hop client -> entry relay -> final exit routing
 515: - exit handoff under load without route leak or restricted-safe regressions
 516: - LAN-access toggle enforcement, including blind-exit deny behavior
 517: 
 518: Security properties asserted by the live harness:
 519: - assignment issuance uses the Rust signing/passphrase path (`rustynet ops materialize-signing-passphrase`)
 520: - remote sudo password material is securely scrubbed on cleanup (`rustynet ops secure-remove`)
 521: - plaintext passphrase-file residue checks are enforced on the tested hosts
 522: - reports are bound to the current git commit and written under `artifacts/phase10/`

 524: ## Release Readiness Evidence (Fail-Closed)
 525: 
 526: Rustynet no longer accepts static/pass-through readiness JSON artifacts.
 527: 
 528: Before Phase 6/9/10 gates can pass, generate measured evidence artifacts from real inputs:
 529: 
 530: ```bash
 531: # Phase 6 probe collection + parity evidence
 532: ./scripts/release/collect_platform_parity_bundle.sh
 533: 
 534: # Phase 6 platform parity evidence
 535: RUSTYNET_PHASE6_PARITY_ENVIRONMENT=lab \
 536: ./scripts/release/generate_platform_parity_report.sh
 537: cargo run --quiet -p rustynet-cli -- ops verify-phase6-parity-evidence
 538: 
 539: # Phase 9 raw evidence collection from logs/probes
 540: ./scripts/operations/collect_phase9_raw_evidence.sh
 541: 
 542: # Phase 9 operational evidence
 543: RUSTYNET_PHASE9_EVIDENCE_ENVIRONMENT=prod-lab \
 544: ./scripts/operations/generate_phase9_artifacts.sh
 545: cargo run --quiet -p rustynet-cli -- ops verify-phase9-evidence
 546: 
 547: # Phase 10 operational evidence
 548: RUSTYNET_PHASE10_EVIDENCE_ENVIRONMENT=prod-lab \
 549: ./scripts/operations/generate_phase10_artifacts.sh
 550: ```
 551: 
 552: Phase10 provenance defaults:
 553: - if `RUSTYNET_PHASE10_PROVENANCE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH` / `RUSTYNET_PHASE10_PROVENANCE_VERIFIER_KEY_PATH` are unset, Rustynet uses `artifacts/phase10/provenance/signing_seed.hex` and `artifacts/phase10/provenance/verifier_key.hex`.
 554: - when both default key files are absent, Rustynet generates a matching Ed25519 keypair through the Rust command path and writes owner-only files (`0600`) under an owner-only directory (`0700`).
 555: - if `RUSTYNET_PHASE10_PROVENANCE_HOST_ID` is unset, Rustynet uses `ci-localhost`.
 556: - for production, set all three provenance env vars explicitly to stable host-specific values under controlled key paths.
 557: 
 558: Phase 6 release scripts are thin wrappers to Rust-only ops commands:
 559: - `rustynet ops collect-platform-probe`
 560: - `rustynet ops generate-platform-parity-report`
 561: - `rustynet ops collect-platform-parity-bundle`
 562: - `rustynet ops verify-phase6-parity-evidence`
 563: 
 564: Phase 9/10 operations scripts are also thin wrappers to Rust-only ops commands:
 565: - `rustynet ops collect-phase9-raw-evidence`
 566: - `rustynet ops generate-phase9-artifacts`
 567: - `rustynet ops verify-phase9-evidence`
 568: - `rustynet ops generate-phase10-artifacts`
 569: - `rustynet ops verify-phase10-provenance`
 570: - `rustynet ops sign-release-artifact`
 571: - `rustynet ops verify-release-artifact`
 572: 
 573: Signed evidence attestations:
 574: - Phase 6 parity report attestation: `artifacts/release/platform_parity_report.attestation.json`
 575: - Phase 9 operational evidence attestation: `artifacts/operations/phase9_evidence.attestation.json`
 576: - both attestations are fail-closed verified, signed with release provenance keys, and bound to the current git commit.
 577: 
 578: Raw measured inputs must exist first:
 579: - `artifacts/release/raw/platform_parity_linux.json`
 580: - `artifacts/release/raw/platform_parity_macos.json`
 581: - `artifacts/release/raw/platform_parity_windows.json`
 582: - if a fresh measured platform probe was collected on another host first, stage it into the Phase 6 bundle with `RUSTYNET_PHASE6_{LINUX|MACOS|WINDOWS}_PROBE_SOURCE=/absolute/path/to/platform_parity_<platform>.json` before running the parity bundle/gates
 583: - `artifacts/operations/source/*.ndjson|*.json` phase9 source logs/config:
 584:   - `compatibility_policy.json`
 585:   - `crypto_deprecation_schedule.json`
 586:   - `slo_windows.ndjson`
 587:   - `performance_samples.ndjson`
 588:   - `incident_drills.ndjson`
 589:   - `dr_drills.ndjson`
 590:   - `backend_security_review.json`
 591: - `artifacts/phase10/source/*.json|*.log` phase10 source evidence:
 592:   - `netns_e2e_report.json`
 593:   - `leak_test_report.json`
 594:   - `perf_budget_report.json`
 595:   - `direct_relay_failover_report.json`
 596:   - `traversal_path_selection_report.json`
 597:   - `traversal_probe_security_report.json`
 598:   - `managed_dns_report.json`
 599:   - `state_transition_audit.log`
 600: - `artifacts/phase10/fresh_install_os_matrix_report.json` cross-platform fresh-install release evidence:
 601:   - must include Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/Mint/macOS clean-install checks
 602:   - must include one-hop + two-hop enforcement checks per OS
 603:   - must include role-switch validation checks per OS
 604:   - must bind evidence to current `HEAD` commit SHA
 605:   - for Linux-only validation runs, set `RUSTYNET_FRESH_INSTALL_OS_MATRIX_PROFILE=linux` (requires Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/Mint scenarios; default remains `cross_platform`)
 606: 
 607: Then run gates:
 608: 
 609: ```bash

 611: ./scripts/ci/phase9_gates.sh
 612: ./scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh

 614: ./scripts/ci/supply_chain_integrity_gates.sh
 615: ./scripts/ci/active_network_security_gates.sh

 618: ./scripts/ci/fresh_install_os_matrix_release_gate.sh
 619: ./scripts/ci/secrets_hygiene_gates.sh
 620: ./scripts/ci/membership_gates.sh
 621: ```
 622: 
 623: High-assurance no-leak dataplane gate (root Linux netns + underlay packet capture):
 624: 
 625: ```bash
 626: sudo -E ./scripts/ci/no_leak_dataplane_gate.sh
 627: ```
 628: 
 629: Security gate toolchain note:
 630: - phase gate scripts require the pinned Rust security toolchain (`RUSTYNET_SECURITY_TOOLCHAIN`, default `1.88.0-<host-triple>`) to be installed; ambient cargo toolchain fallback is disabled.
 631: - interactive/operator bootstrap now follows the same provenance rule: install `rustup` from the host package manager, then install/use the pinned workspace toolchain declared in [`rust-toolchain.toml`](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/rust-toolchain.toml).

 633: ## Phase 1 Measured Baseline Inputs
 634: 
 635: Phase 1 baseline gates require measured source evidence from
 636: `RUSTYNET_PHASE1_PERF_SAMPLES_PATH` (no source-fallback chain).
 637: 
 638: Canonical flow:
 639: 
 640: ```bash
 641: ./scripts/perf/collect_phase1_measured_env.sh
 642: ./scripts/perf/run_phase1_baseline.sh
 643: ```
 644: 
 645: Both scripts resolve `RUSTYNET_PHASE1_PERF_SAMPLES_PATH` to:
 646: - default `artifacts/perf/phase1/source/performance_samples.ndjson`, or
 647: - an explicit operator override.
 648: 
 649: If the source file is missing, both scripts fail closed.
 650: 
 651: The collector writes structured measured input JSON
 652: (`artifacts/perf/phase1/measured_input.json` by default) and no longer emits shell
 653: `export` scripts.
 654: 
 655: `run_phase1_baseline.sh` exports the validated source path into the Rust command path
 656: and runs baseline generation directly (no shell `source`, no legacy fallback chain).
 657: 
 658: Optional output override:
 659: - `RUSTYNET_PHASE1_MEASURED_INPUT_OUT` for collector output path.
 660: - collector source files and output directories fail closed when group/world writable.
 661: 
 662: The repo also seeds `artifacts/perf/phase1/source/performance_samples.ndjson`
 663: for first-run CI/bootstrap; refresh this with current measured samples before release evidence sign-off.

   1: name: Cross Platform CI
   2: 
   3: on:
   4:   push:
   5:     branches: ["main"]
   6:   pull_request:
   7: 
   8: permissions:
   9:   contents: read

  15:     steps:
  16:       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  17:       - name: Bootstrap CI tools
  18:         run: |
  19:           RUSTYNET_CI_BOOTSTRAP_SYSTEM=0 ./scripts/ci/bootstrap_ci_tools.sh
  20:       - name: Workspace validation
  21:         run: |
  22:           cargo fmt --all -- --check
  23:           cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
  24:           cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features
  25:           cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features
  26:       - name: macOS dataplane smoke gates
  27:         run: |
  28:           ./scripts/ci/macos_dataplane_smoke.sh
  29:       - name: Security gates
  30:         run: |
  31:           cargo audit --deny warnings
  32:           cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories
  33: 
  34:   debian13:
  35:     name: Debian 13 build+security
  36:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  37:     container:
  38:       image: debian:trixie
  39:     steps:
  40:       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  41:       - name: Bootstrap CI tools
  42:         run: |
  43:           ./scripts/ci/bootstrap_ci_tools.sh
  44:       - name: Workspace validation
  45:         run: |
  46:           cargo fmt --all -- --check
  47:           cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
  48:           cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features
  49:           cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features
  50:       - name: Security gates
  51:         run: |
  52:           cargo audit --deny warnings
  53:           cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories
  54: 
  55:   linux_e2e:
  56:     name: Linux real WireGuard E2E
  57:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  58:     steps:
  59:       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  60:       - name: Bootstrap CI tools
  61:         run: |
  62:           ./scripts/ci/bootstrap_ci_tools.sh
  63:       - name: Run real dataplane E2E harness

  65:           sudo -E ./scripts/e2e/real_wireguard_exitnode_e2e.sh
  66: 
  67:   windows:
  68:     name: Windows build+security (rustynetd + windows-native)
  69:     runs-on: windows-2022
  70:     # Scope: this job exercises the Windows-portable crates that
  71:     # carry the W1.x / W2.x / W4.x Windows verifier surface (the
  72:     # SCM API bindings + DPAPI / SDDL / named-pipe / WinVerifyTrust
  73:     # FFI in rustynet-windows-native, the `windows-…-check`
  74:     # subcommands in rustynetd). The orchestrator crate
  75:     # (rustynet-cli) deliberately ships unix-only modules
  76:     # (ops_install_systemd, ops_phase9) at top level and therefore
  77:     # cannot build on Windows; cross-target check from the macOS +
  78:     # Debian jobs above already covers rustynet-cli's wire-format
  79:     # compatibility with the Windows daemon.
  80:     defaults:
  81:       run:
  82:         # Use Git Bash (pre-installed on windows-2022 runners) so
  83:         # the cargo invocations match the macOS / Debian jobs above.
  84:         shell: bash
  85:     steps:
  86:       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  87:       - name: Pin toolchain + install cargo-audit / cargo-deny
  88:         run: |
  89:           # The bash bootstrap wrapper invokes `cargo run -p
  90:           # rustynet-cli --bin bootstrap_ci_tools`; rustynet-cli
  91:           # does not build on Windows so we cannot use the wrapper
  92:           # here. Pin the same versions inline, mirroring the
  93:           # bootstrap binary's contract (PINNED_TOOLCHAIN=1.85.0,
  94:           # security toolchain=1.88.0, cargo-audit=0.22.1,
  95:           # cargo-deny=0.19.1).
  96:           rustup toolchain install 1.85.0 --profile minimal --component rustfmt --component clippy
  97:           rustup default 1.85.0
  98:           rustup toolchain install 1.88.0 --profile minimal
  99:           cargo install cargo-audit --locked --version 0.22.1 --force
 100:           cargo install cargo-deny --locked --version 0.19.1 --force
 101:       - name: Build + test Windows-portable crates
 102:         run: |
 103:           # Crate selection is intentional. rustynetd carries every
 104:           # Windows-side validator (windows_paths,
 105:           # windows_authenticode, windows_dns_failclosed,
 106:           # windows_key_custody, windows_mesh_status,
 107:           # windows_runtime_boundary, windows_service,
 108:           # windows_service_hardening, windows_ipc, etc.).
 109:           # rustynet-windows-native carries the FFI wrappers (DPAPI,
 110:           # SDDL, named-pipe, WinVerifyTrust). The remaining crates
 111:           # are the protocol-agnostic primitives the Windows daemon
 112:           # links against; building them here exercises both
 113:           # platform-conditional cfg paths AND any unix-only
 114:           # regression that would slip past the Linux-side jobs.
 115:           PKGS=(
 116:             -p rustynetd
 117:             -p rustynet-windows-native
 118:             -p rustynet-crypto
 119:             -p rustynet-policy
 120:             -p rustynet-dns-zone
 121:             -p rustynet-control
 122:             -p rustynet-backend-api
 123:             -p rustynet-backend-stub
 124:             -p rustynet-relay
 125:             -p rustynet-local-security
 126:           )
 127:           cargo fmt "${PKGS[@]}" -- --check
 128:           cargo clippy "${PKGS[@]}" --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
 129:           cargo check "${PKGS[@]}" --all-targets --all-features
 130:           cargo test "${PKGS[@]}" --all-targets --all-features
 131:       - name: Security gates
 132:         run: |
 133:           # cargo-audit + cargo-deny operate on Cargo.lock + the
 134:           # workspace manifest, so they validate the whole
 135:           # dependency surface (including rustynet-cli's deps) even
 136:           # though we only built the Windows-portable subset above.
 137:           cargo audit --deny warnings
 138:           cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories

===== /.github/workflows/release-windows.yml =====

   1: name: Windows Release Signing
   2: 
   3: # Triggers on tag pushes matching `v*.*.*` (e.g. v0.1.0). The job
   4: # builds rustynetd.exe, Authenticode-signs it via the reviewed
   5: # Sign-RustyNetWindowsBinary.ps1 helper, and uploads the signed
   6: # artifact to the release. If the signing secrets are not configured
   7: # in the repository's GitHub Secrets, the job fails LOUD — never
   8: # silently falls back to shipping an unsigned release.
   9: #
  10: # Required GitHub Secrets (configured by the operator per
  11: # documents/operations/ReleaseSigningRunbook.md):
  12: #   RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_BASE64   — base64 of the PFX file
  13: #   RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD — PFX password
  14: #
  15: # Optional (overrides):
  16: #   RUSTYNET_SIGNING_TIMESTAMP_URL — RFC 3161 timestamp authority
  17: #                                    (defaults to DigiCert)
  18: #
  19: # This workflow consumes the W2.1b chain-validation contract from
  20: # crates/rustynetd/src/windows_authenticode.rs as its post-sign gate
  21: # (signtool verify /pa). Any signed binary that fails WinVerifyTrust
  22: # fails the workflow before the artifact is uploaded.
  23: 
  24: on:
  25:   push:
  26:     tags:
  27:       - 'v*.*.*'
  28:   # Allow manual dispatch with no signing — used for dry-run testing
  29:   # of the build path on PRs / branches without a tagged release.
  30:   workflow_dispatch:
  31:     inputs:
  32:       dry_run:
  33:         description: 'Build only — skip signing + artifact upload'
  34:         type: boolean
  35:         required: false
  36:         default: true
  37: 
  38: permissions:
  39:   contents: write  # release upload
  40: 
  41: jobs:
  42:   windows-release:
  43:     name: Windows release build + sign
  44:     runs-on: windows-2022
  45:     defaults:
  46:       run:
  47:         shell: bash
  48:     steps:
  49:       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
  50: 
  51:       - name: Pin toolchain
  52:         run: |
  53:           # Same pinning the cross-platform-ci.yml windows job uses,
  54:           # mirroring bootstrap_ci_tools' contract.
  55:           rustup toolchain install 1.85.0 --profile minimal
  56:           rustup default 1.85.0
  57: 
  58:       - name: Build rustynetd.exe
  59:         run: |
  60:           cargo build --release -p rustynetd --locked
  61:           # Confirm the binary landed where the helper expects.
  62:           ls -la target/release/rustynetd.exe
  63: 
  64:       - name: Decide whether to sign
  65:         id: signing-decision
  66:         run: |
  67:           # Tag pushes ALWAYS sign (release is shipping). Manual
  68:           # dispatch can dry-run (build-only) for path validation.
  69:           if [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "push" ]]; then
  70:             echo "should_sign=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  71:           elif [[ "${{ github.event_name }}" == "workflow_dispatch" && "${{ inputs.dry_run }}" == "false" ]]; then
  72:             echo "should_sign=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  73:           else
  74:             echo "should_sign=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
  75:           fi
  76: 
  77:       - name: Verify signing secrets are configured
  78:         if: steps.signing-decision.outputs.should_sign == 'true'
  79:         env:
  80:           PFX_BASE64: ${{ secrets.RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_BASE64 }}
  81:           PFX_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD }}
  82:         run: |
  83:           # Fail LOUD if either signing secret is missing. The
  84:           # repository-level rule is: tag pushes ship signed
  85:           # binaries; if the operator hasn't configured signing,
  86:           # the release cannot proceed. No silent unsigned fallback.
  87:           if [[ -z "$PFX_BASE64" ]]; then
  88:             echo "::error::RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_BASE64 secret is not configured"
  89:             echo "::error::See documents/operations/ReleaseSigningRunbook.md for setup"
  90:             exit 1
  91:           fi
  92:           if [[ -z "$PFX_PASSWORD" ]]; then
  93:             echo "::error::RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD secret is not configured"
  94:             echo "::error::See documents/operations/ReleaseSigningRunbook.md for setup"
  95:             exit 1
  96:           fi
  97: 
  98:       - name: Materialise signing PFX
  99:         if: steps.signing-decision.outputs.should_sign == 'true'
 100:         env:
 101:           PFX_BASE64: ${{ secrets.RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_BASE64 }}
 102:         shell: pwsh
 103:         run: |
 104:           # Decode the base64 PFX to a temp path the runner can reach
 105:           # but no other process should. Permissions on the runner's
 106:           # _work tree are scoped to the job's session.
 107:           $pfxBytes = [System.Convert]::FromBase64String($env:PFX_BASE64)
 108:           $pfxPath = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'release-signing.pfx'
 109:           [System.IO.File]::WriteAllBytes($pfxPath, $pfxBytes)
 110:           # Lock down to the runner user only.
 111:           icacls $pfxPath /inheritance:r | Out-Null
 112:           icacls $pfxPath /grant:r "$env:USERNAME`:F" | Out-Null
 113:           # Clear the env var so the base64 doesn't linger in
 114:           # subsequent step env contexts.
 115:           "PFX_BASE64=" | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV
 116:           "RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PATH=$pfxPath" | Out-File -Append -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV
 117: 
 118:       - name: Sign rustynetd.exe
 119:         if: steps.signing-decision.outputs.should_sign == 'true'
 120:         env:
 121:           # PFX password is loaded by the helper script via the
 122:           # named env var; never appears on the helper's command line.
 123:           RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD }}
 124:         shell: pwsh
 125:         run: |
 126:           $timestampUrl = $env:RUSTYNET_SIGNING_TIMESTAMP_URL
 127:           if ([string]::IsNullOrEmpty($timestampUrl)) {
 128:               $timestampUrl = 'http://timestamp.digicert.com'
 129:           }
 130:           $binaryPath = (Resolve-Path target/release/rustynetd.exe).Path
 131:           & .\scripts\release\Sign-RustyNetWindowsBinary.ps1 `
 132:               -BinaryPath $binaryPath `
 133:               -CertificatePath $env:RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PATH `
 134:               -CertificatePasswordEnvVar 'RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD' `
 135:               -TimestampUrl $timestampUrl
 136: 
 137:       - name: Run W2.1b chain validation against the signed binary
 138:         if: steps.signing-decision.outputs.should_sign == 'true'
 139:         run: |
 140:           # Eat our own dogfood: the W2.1b daemon-side gate is the
 141:           # final say on whether a release-signed binary is
 142:           # trustworthy. Any release that signtool says it signed
 143:           # but our own WinVerifyTrust wrapper rejects fails the
 144:           # workflow before the artifact ships.
 145:           ./target/release/rustynetd.exe windows-authenticode-check \
 146:               --binary-path "$(pwd)/target/release/rustynetd.exe"
 147: 
 148:       - name: Compute SHA-256 of signed binary
 149:         if: steps.signing-decision.outputs.should_sign == 'true'
 150:         shell: pwsh
 151:         run: |
 152:           $hash = Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 target/release/rustynetd.exe
 153:           "$($hash.Hash)  rustynetd.exe" | Out-File -Encoding ascii -FilePath target/release/rustynetd.exe.sha256
 154:           Write-Host "[release-signing] sha256: $($hash.Hash)"
 155: 
 156:       - name: Upload to release
 157:         if: steps.signing-decision.outputs.should_sign == 'true' && github.event_name == 'push'
 158:         uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
 159:         with:
 160:           files: |
 161:             target/release/rustynetd.exe
 162:             target/release/rustynetd.exe.sha256
 163: 
 164:       - name: Cleanup signing material
 165:         if: always() && steps.signing-decision.outputs.should_sign == 'true'
 166:         shell: pwsh
 167:         run: |
 168:           # Belt-and-braces: scrub the materialised PFX. The runner
 169:           # also tears down the _work tree at end-of-job, but
 170:           # leaving the PFX on disk after sign + verify is a
 171:           # needless exposure window.
 172:           if ($env:RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PATH -and (Test-Path -LiteralPath $env:RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PATH)) {
 173:               Remove-Item -LiteralPath $env:RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PATH -Force
 174:           }
 175: 
 176:   release-sbom:
 177:     name: SBOM generation + release upload
 178:     runs-on: ubuntu-latest
 179:     # Runs in parallel with windows-release; only attaches to a real
 180:     # release on tag push. Workflow_dispatch dry-runs still produce
 181:     # the SBOM (so operators can validate the path) but do not
 182:     # upload it anywhere.
 183:     needs: []
 184:     steps:
 185:       - uses: actions/checkout@v4
 186:       - name: Pin toolchain
 187:         run: |
 188:           rustup toolchain install 1.85.0 --profile minimal
 189:           rustup default 1.85.0
 190:       - name: Generate release SBOM
 191:         run: |
 192:           # Reuses the reviewed `ops generate-release-sbom`
 193:           # subcommand under crates/rustynet-cli/src/ops_ci_release_perf.rs.
 194:           # Produces:
 195:           #   artifacts/release/sbom.cargo-metadata.json
 196:           #   artifacts/release/sbom.sha256
 197:           # The .json is `cargo metadata --format-version 1` output —
 198:           # a complete dependency tree with versions, sources,
 199:           # features, and repository links. The .sha256 is the
 200:           # content digest for tamper-evidence.
 201:           cargo run --release --quiet -p rustynet-cli -- ops generate-release-sbom
 202:           ls -la artifacts/release/sbom.cargo-metadata.json artifacts/release/sbom.sha256
 203:       - name: Upload SBOM to release
 204:         if: github.event_name == 'push'
 205:         uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
 206:         with:
 207:           files: |
 208:             artifacts/release/sbom.cargo-metadata.json
 209:             artifacts/release/sbom.sha256

===== /AGENTS.md =====

   1: # Rustynet Agent Operating Contract
   2: 
   3: Use this file as mandatory execution guidance for AI implementation agents working in this repository.
   4: 
   5: `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` are intentionally mirrored. Keep them aligned.
   6: 
   7: ## 1) Mission
   8: - Build Rustynet to production-grade quality.
   9: - Keep security as the first priority.
  10: - Keep architecture Rust-first and transport-backend modular.
  11: - Prefer code, tests, gates, and evidence over design-only churn.
  12: 
  13: ## 2) Read Order and Source of Truth
  14: When documents disagree, apply this precedence:
  15: 1. `documents/Requirements.md`
  16: 2. `documents/SecurityMinimumBar.md`
  17: 3. The active scope document for the task
  18: 4. Supporting design docs
  19: 5. `README.md` and operational runbooks
  20: 
  21: Read in this order before touching code:
  22: 1. `AGENTS.md`
  23: 2. `CLAUDE.md`
  24: 3. `README.md`
  25: 4. `documents/README.md`
  26: 5. `documents/Requirements.md`
  27: 6. `documents/SecurityMinimumBar.md`
  28: 7. The active scope document
  29: 8. Relevant runbooks under `documents/operations/`
  30: 
  31: Current primary execution ledgers:
  32: - `documents/operations/active/MasterWorkPlan_2026-03-22.md` for repo-wide remaining work
  33: - `documents/operations/active/PlugAndPlayTraversalRelayDeltaPlan_2026-03-29.md` for traversal, relay, and live-lab readiness
  34: 
  35: Current lab-reference assets:
  36: - `documents/operations/active/UTMVirtualMachineInventory_2026-03-31.md`
  37: - `documents/operations/active/vm_lab_inventory.json`
  38: 
  39: Rules:
  40: - If ambiguity exists, choose the strictest secure practical default and document that choice.
  41: - Never weaken a higher-precedence requirement.
  42: - Standalone prompt documents are not part of the repository source of truth. Use the active ledgers, runbooks, and index files instead.
  43: 
  44: ## 3) Non-Negotiable Engineering Constraints
  45: - Rust-first codebase. Non-Rust only for unavoidable OS integration boundaries.
  46: - No custom cryptography and no custom VPN protocol invention in production paths.
  47: - WireGuard must remain an adapter behind stable backend abstractions and be easy to replace.
  48: - No WireGuard-specific leakage into protocol-agnostic control, policy, or domain crates.
  49: - Default-deny policy is mandatory across ACL, routes, and trust-sensitive flows.
  50: - Fail closed when trust/security state is missing, invalid, stale, or unavailable.
  51: - Do not defer in-scope requirements behind TODO/FIXME/placeholders in completed deliverables.
  52: - Enforce one hardened execution path per security-sensitive workflow. No runtime fallback, downgrade, or legacy branch in production paths.
  53: 
  54: ## 4) Security Baseline Requirements
  55: - Enforce signed control/trust state validation before mutation.
  56: - Enforce anti-replay and rollback protection where state freshness matters.
  57: - Enforce strict key custody behavior:
  58:   - use OS-secure key storage when available
  59:   - otherwise use encrypted-at-rest fallback with strict permissions and startup permission checks
  60: - Never log secrets or private key material.
  61: - Preserve privileged-boundary hardening: argv-only exec for helpers, strict input validation, no shell construction with untrusted values.
  62: - Preserve tunnel and DNS fail-closed behavior in protected modes.
  63: - During shell-to-Rust migration, remove superseded shell implementations from active paths. Wrappers may only dispatch to the Rust command and must fail closed on error.
  64: 
  65: Each implemented security control must include:
  66: 1. an enforcement point in code
  67: 2. a verification method such as a unit test, integration test, negative test, or gate check
  68: 
  69: ## 5) Required Working Style
  70: - Before coding, read the relevant docs in precedence order.
  71: - Build a concrete checklist from the scope requirements.
  72: - Implement in small, verifiable increments.
  73: - Run the closest relevant tests and gates during implementation, not only at the end.
  74: - Keep the owning ledger or work document current. Do not maintain a hidden private checklist that diverges from repository state.
  75: - Keep documentation synchronized with implementation changes.
  76: - Remove dead links, stale index entries, and prompt-only guidance when you find them.
  77: 
  78: ## 6) Documentation Rules
  79: - `documents/README.md` is the top-level map of the docs tree.
  80: - `documents/operations/README.md` is the operations/runbook map.
  81: - `documents/operations/active/README.md` is the active-work map.
  82: - If you add, remove, rename, archive, or materially repurpose docs, update the relevant index file in the same change.
  83: - If a document becomes historical rather than active, move or classify it honestly.
  84: - Do not reintroduce standalone prompt documents; keep execution guidance in the active ledgers themselves.
  85: 
  86: ## 7) Validation and CI Gates
  87: Run these as mandatory quality gates for substantial work:
  88: - `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
  89: - `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
  90: - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`
  91: - `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`
  92: - `cargo audit --deny warnings`
  93: - `cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories`
  94: 
  95: Run scope-specific scripts when present:
  96: - `./scripts/ci/phase9_gates.sh`
  97: - `./scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh`
  98: - `./scripts/ci/membership_gates.sh`
  99: - any active-phase gate script required by the scope document
 100: 
 101: If any gate fails:
 102: 1. stop phase progression
 103: 2. fix the root cause, not the symptom
 104: 3. re-run the impacted gates
 105: 4. record failure, fix, and proof in the relevant progress document when scope requires it
 106: 
 107: ## 8) Architecture Boundary Rules
 108: - Keep domain models and policy evaluation transport-agnostic.
 109: - Keep backend-specific behavior in backend adapter crates.
 110: - Expose capabilities via backend interfaces rather than leaking backend types.
 111: - Maintain deterministic, testable state transitions for trust-sensitive systems.
 112: 
 113: ## 9) Definition of Done
 114: Work is complete only when all are true:
 115: - in-scope requirements are implemented end-to-end
 116: - security minimum bar controls are satisfied for that scope
 117: - all mandatory gates pass, or the remaining blocker is explicitly documented and outside the claimed completion
 118: - required artifacts exist and validate
 119: - no unresolved in-scope blockers remain
 120: - no TODO/FIXME/placeholders remain in completed deliverables
