===== /documents/operations/MembershipGovernanceRunbook.md =====

   1: Membership Governance Runbook
   2: 
   3: Purpose
   4: 
   5: This runbook describes operator CLI flows and daemon gating for membership governance (quorum-signed membership updates).
   6: 
   7: CLI flows
   8: 
   9: - Propose an update (creates a raw update record):
  10:   rustynet membership propose <operation> --output <update.record>
  11: 
  12: - Sign an update (approver signs a record):
  13:   rustynet membership sign-update --record <update.record> --approver-id <id> --signing-key <key> --output <signed.update>
  14: 
  15: - Verify an update (locally verify signatures and integrity):
  16:   rustynet membership verify-update --signed-update <signed.update> --snapshot <membership.snapshot> --log <membership.log>
  17: 
  18: - Apply an update (apply to snapshot and append to log):
  19:   rustynet membership apply-update --signed-update <signed.update> --snapshot <membership.snapshot> --log <membership.log>
  20: 
  21: - Status (view current snapshot, root, and pending log entries):
  22:   rustynet membership status --snapshot <membership.snapshot> --log <membership.log>
  23: 
  24: Daemon gating and policy
  25: 
  26: - The daemon must load a verified membership snapshot before provisioning peers. If snapshot verification fails, provisioning is blocked (fail-closed).
  27: - Revoked nodes are denied by policy: the membership state is consulted when evaluating access; any node with status `revoked` is denied peer provisioning and marked in audit logs.
  28: - Membership files (snapshot, log) are integrity protected (digest + chained entries). The daemon verifies integrity and rejects tampered files.
  29: 
  30: Golden vectors and schema
  31: 
  32: - Canonical encoding and state-root golden vectors live in `crates/rustynet-control/tests/` as `membership_schema_golden_test.rs`. These must be updated only when schema version is bumped.
  33: 
  34: Operational notes
  35: 
  36: - All membership-related cargo commands and gates are intended to run on the Debian CI host (per repo policy). Use `scripts/ci/membership_gates.sh` to run the canonical gate sequence.
  37: - Keep private signing keys secure; never commit them.

===== /documents/operations/MembershipIncidentResponseRunbook.md =====

   1: # Membership Governance Incident Response Runbook
   2: 
   3: ## Purpose
   4: Define production incident response for Rustynet membership governance, covering approver compromise, node compromise, emergency revocation, quorum reconstitution, and backup/restore drills.
   5: 
   6: This runbook is authoritative for membership-related trust incidents and must be executed with fail-closed defaults.
   7: 
   8: ## Non-Negotiables
   9: - Rust-first codebase. Non-Rust only for unavoidable OS integration.
  10: - WireGuard remains adapter-only; membership logic is protocol-agnostic.
  11: - SecurityMinimumBar controls are release-blocking.
  12: - No custom cryptography/protocol design in production paths.
  13: - Fail closed when trust/security state is missing, invalid, stale, or unavailable.
  14: - Default-deny policy is mandatory.
  15: 
  16: ## Preconditions
  17: - Membership files are present and permission-hardened:
  18:   - `membership.snapshot` mode `0600`
  19:   - `membership.log` mode `0600`
  20:   - membership watermark mode `0600`
  21: - At least one owner approver and one guardian approver are active.
  22: - On-call operators have approved offline backups of:
  23:   - `membership.snapshot`
  24:   - `membership.log`
  25:   - approver public-key set and threshold policy
  26: 
  27: ## Detection and Triage
  28: Trigger this runbook immediately when any of the following is observed:
  29: - Unexpected membership update appears in log/audit.
  30: - Daemon enters restricted-safe mode due to membership trust failure.
  31: - Unauthorized node appears active in membership state.
  32: - Approver private key exposure is suspected.
  33: - Repeated watermark replay/rollback errors occur.
  34: 
  35: Initial triage checklist:
  36: 1. Freeze all membership applies (`membership apply-update` halted).
  37: 2. Collect forensic artifacts:
  38:    - `membership.snapshot`
  39:    - `membership.log`
  40:    - `membership_audit_integrity.log`
  41: 3. Validate integrity:
  42:    - `rustynet-cli membership verify-log --snapshot <snapshot> --log <log> --audit-output <audit>`
  43: 4. Confirm currently active root/epoch from each affected daemon.
  44: 5. Classify incident as `approver_compromise`, `node_compromise`, `replay_or_rollback`, or `unknown`.
  45: 
  46: ## Playbook A: Approver Key Compromise
  47: Objective: remove compromised approver authority without breaking quorum.
  48: 
  49: Steps:
  50: 1. Generate `rotate_approver` proposal for compromised approver with `status=revoked`.
  51: 2. Require owner + threshold signatures from still-trusted approvers.
  52: 3. Verify update on offline validation host:
  53:    - `rustynet-cli membership verify-update --signed-update <file> --snapshot <snapshot> --log <log> --dry-run`
  54: 4. Apply update:
  55:    - `rustynet-cli membership apply-update --signed-update <file> --snapshot <snapshot> --log <log>`
  56: 5. Rotate any quorum threshold only after compromised approver is revoked.
  57: 6. Publish updated approver public-key inventory to operators.
  58: 
  59: Fail-closed rule:
  60: - If minimum threshold cannot be reached, do not apply any membership change; keep cluster in restricted-safe for trust-required operations.
  61: 
  62: ## Playbook B: Node Key Compromise
  63: Objective: revoke compromised node immediately and prevent dataplane re-entry.
  64: 
  65: Steps:
  66: 1. Create `propose-revoke` for compromised `node_id`.
  67: 2. Obtain quorum signatures.
  68: 3. Verify and apply update.
  69: 4. Confirm daemon behavior:
  70:    - revoked node selection is denied,
  71:    - revoked node routes/peers are removed on reconcile/fail-closed transition.
  72: 5. If device is recoverable, perform controlled key rotation:
  73:    - `propose-rotate-key` + quorum signatures + apply.
  74: 
  75: Fail-closed rule:
  76: - Unknown/revoked node cannot be allowed by ACL, even if legacy policy would allow it.
  77: 
  78: ## Playbook C: Emergency Revocation
  79: Objective: remove active malicious membership influence in shortest safe path.
  80: 
  81: Steps:
  82: 1. Enter emergency mode:
  83:    - block non-essential operator changes,
  84:    - disable automated rollout for membership intents.
  85: 2. Generate and sign revoke/remove update for target node(s) or approver(s).
  86: 3. Apply update to authoritative membership log/snapshot.
  87: 4. Force daemon reconcile cycle (or restart daemons) to enforce immediate deny.
  88: 5. Confirm:
  89:    - `rustynet-cli status` shows no revoked node selected as exit,
  90:    - route mutation attempts through revoked node are denied.
  91: 
  92: ## Playbook D: Quorum Reconstitution
  93: Objective: recover governance after multiple key losses/compromises.
  94: 
  95: Steps:
  96: 1. Restore last known good snapshot/log from signed backup.
  97: 2. Validate log chain and replay.
  98: 3. Propose approver-set rebuild (new owner/guardian keys).
  99: 4. Require strictest currently valid quorum to authorize rebuild.
 100: 5. Apply and distribute new approver public keys.
 101: 6. Rotate all non-compromised but potentially exposed approver keys.
 102: 
 103: Hard stop:
 104: - If authoritative backup integrity cannot be proven, no membership apply is permitted.
 105: 
 106: ## Backup/Restore Integrity Drill
 107: Run weekly or before release:
 108: 1. Execute:
 109:    - `./scripts/operations/membership_incident_drill.sh`
 110: 2. Validate generated artifacts in drill output:
 111:    - `membership_conformance_report.json`
 112:    - `membership_negative_tests_report.json`
 113:    - `membership_recovery_report.json`
 114:    - `membership_audit_integrity.log`
 115:    - `drill_summary.log`
 116: 3. Record drill ID, operator, and pass/fail in incident tracker.
 117: 
 118: ## Patch-SLA Tracking Hooks
 119: Membership-critical vulnerabilities are tracked with these hooks:
 120: 1. Severity label must include `membership-critical`.
 121: 2. SLA timers:
 122:    - Critical: mitigation/patch in 48 hours.
 123:    - High: patch in 7 days.
 124:    - Medium: patch in 30 days.
 125: 3. CI blocker:
 126:    - unresolved `membership-critical` issue blocks release tag creation.
 127: 4. Each incident must link:
 128:    - root cause,
 129:    - remediation PR,
 130:    - verification evidence (tests + artifacts).
 131: 
 132: ## Evidence Requirements per Incident
 133: - Exact command transcript used for verify/apply actions.
 134: - Artifact bundle containing:
 135:   - pre-incident snapshot/log hash
 136:   - post-incident snapshot/log hash
 137:   - audit log diff
 138:   - daemon restricted-safe events (if triggered)
 139: - Final statement that default-deny and fail-closed behavior remained intact.
 140: 
 141: ## Closure Criteria
 142: Incident is closed only when:
 143: 1. Compromised principals are revoked or rotated.
 144: 2. Membership integrity chain verifies on all targeted nodes.
 145: 3. Daemon and policy behavior confirms revoked/unknown deny path.
 146: 4. Evidence bundle is archived and reviewed by security + engineering owners.

===== /documents/operations/Phase10ExitNodeDataplaneRunbook.md =====

   1: # Phase 10 Exit-Node Dataplane Runbook
   2: 
   3: Status correction (verified 2026-03-05):
   4: - Legacy `/etc/rustynet/wireguard.*` path assumptions are stale for current Linux runtime.
   5: - Current Linux hardened runtime uses encrypted key material under `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/` and encrypted systemd credential blob `/etc/rustynet/credentials/wg_key_passphrase.cred`.
   6: - Security risk truth: relying on legacy plaintext passphrase-file assumptions weakens key-custody posture and can cause unsafe operator workflows.
   7: 
   8: ## 1) Purpose
   9: This runbook defines deployment, validation, rollback, and incident procedures for Rustynet Phase 10 Linux dataplane enablement (exit-node full tunnel + LAN-toggle controls + direct/relay traversal path control + DNS/tunnel fail-close behavior).
  10: 
  11: ## 2) Preconditions
  12: - Linux host with required privileges for route/firewall/NAT operations.
  13: - `rustynetd` and `rustynet` binaries built from current workspace.
  14: - `scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh` completed and artifacts present in `artifacts/phase10/`.
  15: - Trust state and signed control data validation path healthy.
  16: - WireGuard encrypted key present at `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.key.enc` with mode `0600`.
  17: - `/etc/rustynet` directory present with mode `0750` (`root:<daemon-group>`).
  18: - `/etc/rustynet/credentials` directory present with mode `0700` (`root:root`).
  19: - Encrypted passphrase credential blob present at `/etc/rustynet/credentials/wg_key_passphrase.cred` with mode `0600`.
  20: - Encrypted signing-passphrase credential blob present at `/etc/rustynet/credentials/signing_key_passphrase.cred` with mode `0600`.
  21: - Persistent plaintext passphrase file is absent at `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.passphrase`.
  22: - Runtime decrypted key at `/run/rustynet/wireguard.key` with mode `0600` (managed by `rustynetd`).
  23: - Trust evidence file present at `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.trust`.
  24: - Trust verifier key present at `/etc/rustynet/trust-evidence.pub`.
  25: - If unattended trust auto-refresh is enabled: encrypted signer key present at `/etc/rustynet/trust-evidence.key` (`0600`) and passphrase injected via systemd credential (`%d/signing_key_passphrase`).
  26: - Phase10 provenance signing seed file present at absolute path configured by `RUSTYNET_PHASE10_PROVENANCE_SIGNING_KEY_PATH` (owner-only mode `<=0600`, 32-byte hex seed).
  27: - Matching phase10 provenance verifier key file present at absolute path configured by `RUSTYNET_PHASE10_PROVENANCE_VERIFIER_KEY_PATH` (owner-only mode `<=0600`, 32-byte hex key).
  28: - `RUSTYNET_PHASE10_PROVENANCE_HOST_ID` configured and stable for the host/environment.
  29: - Host clock synchronization healthy (for freshness-bound signed traversal endpoint-hint checks).
  30: 
  31: ## 3) Deployment Procedure
  32: 1. Run `./scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh` and verify PASS.
  33: 2. Recommended: run `./start.sh` and complete first-run wizard bootstrap.
  34: 3. Install and start hardened systemd service:
  35: - `sudo ./scripts/systemd/install_rustynetd_service.sh`
  36: 4. Confirm detected daemon environment:
  37: - `cat /etc/default/rustynetd`
  38: 5. If `RUSTYNET_TRUST_AUTO_REFRESH=true`, verify timer:
  39: - `sudo systemctl --no-pager --full status rustynetd-trust-refresh.timer`
  40: - `sudo systemctl start rustynetd-trust-refresh.service`
  41: 6. Validate baseline daemon status:
  42: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- status`
  43: 7. Validate traversal/path diagnostics baseline:
  44: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- netcheck`
  45: 8. Select exit node:
  46: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- exit-node select <node-id>`
  47: 9. Toggle LAN access only when required:
  48: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- lan-access on`
  49: 10. Validate DNS policy state:
  50: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- dns inspect`
  51: 
  52: ## 4) Rollback Procedure
  53: 1. Disable exit mode:
  54: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- exit-node off`
  55: 2. Disable LAN access:
  56: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- lan-access off`
  57: 3. Restart daemon in restricted-safe mode if trust or state integrity is suspect.
  58: 4. Revert to last-known-safe build and rerun `./scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh`.
  59: 5. Preserve `artifacts/phase10/state_transition_audit.log` for post-incident analysis.
  60: 6. If auto-refresh signer key is compromised or missing, disable refresh timer until key custody is restored:
  61: - `sudo systemctl disable --now rustynetd-trust-refresh.timer`
  62: 
  63: ## 5) Incident Response Checklist
  64: - Confirm whether daemon entered `FailClosed` state via `status` output.
  65: - Check for trust-state failures (signed-data freshness, signature validation, clock skew).
  66: - Check latest `state_transition_audit.log` for transition reason.
  67: - If stale trust evidence is reported during unattended runtime, verify `rustynetd-trust-refresh.timer` and `rustynetd-trust-refresh.service` journal output before any bypass actions.
  68: - If DNS leak protection fault is detected, keep fail-closed posture and do not bypass protection.
  69: - If route/firewall apply failed, enforce rollback and block egress until trusted state recovers.
  70: - For cross-network-specific containment and recovery workflow, execute:
  71:   - `documents/operations/CrossNetworkRemoteExitIncidentPlaybook.md`
  72: 
  73: ## 6) Verification Commands
  74: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- status`
  75: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- netcheck`
  76: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- dns inspect`
  77: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- route advertise 192.168.1.0/24`
  78: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- key rotate`
  79: - `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- key revoke`
  80: - `sudo systemctl list-timers --all | grep rustynetd-trust-refresh`
  81: - `sudo journalctl -u rustynetd-trust-refresh.service -n 50 --no-pager`
  82: - `sudo systemd-creds decrypt --name=signing_key_passphrase /etc/rustynet/credentials/signing_key_passphrase.cred /tmp/signing_key_passphrase.test && sudo rm -f /tmp/signing_key_passphrase.test`
  83: - `RUSTYNET_PHASE10_PROVENANCE_VERIFIER_KEY_PATH=<absolute-path> RUSTYNET_PHASE10_PROVENANCE_HOST_ID=<host-id> cargo run --quiet -p rustynet-cli -- ops verify-phase10-provenance`
  84: - `./scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh` (validates pre-generated measured artifacts in `artifacts/phase10`)
  85: 
  86: ## 7) Required Evidence for Sign-Off
  87: - `artifacts/phase10/netns_e2e_report.json`
  88: - `artifacts/phase10/leak_test_report.json`
  89: - `artifacts/phase10/perf_budget_report.json`
  90: - `artifacts/phase10/direct_relay_failover_report.json`
  91: - `artifacts/phase10/traversal_path_selection_report.json` (when traversal gate coverage is enabled)
  92: - `artifacts/phase10/state_transition_audit.log`
  93: - `artifacts/phase10/phase10_provenance.attestation.json`
  94: - Limitation note: current failover artifact demonstrates path-mode transition/audit evidence; full relay transport failover integration remains open code work.
  95: 
  96: ## 8) Security Invariants
  97: - Default-deny policy remains active.
  98: - Tunnel/DNS fail-close behavior is never bypassed.
  99: - Mutating daemon IPC commands require peer credential authorization.
 100: - WireGuard implementation remains behind `TunnelBackend` and replaceable.
 101: - No custom crypto/protocol behavior is introduced.
 102: - Direct/relay path transitions require signed, fresh traversal endpoint data; invalid traversal state must fail closed.
 103: - Dataplane firewall/NAT ownership is generation-tagged and must only clean up Rustynet-owned tables.
 104: 
 105: ## 9) External Cross-Network Lab Prerequisites
 106: Before running measured cross-network suites, satisfy:
 107: - `documents/operations/CrossNetworkLiveLabPrerequisitesChecklist.md`

===== /documents/operations/PlatformSupportMatrix.md =====

   1: # Rustynet Platform Support Matrix (Current Implementation)
   2: 
   3: Date verified: 2026-04-17
   4: Purpose: provide a single current-state view of platform capability, security posture, and evidence depth.
   5: 
   6: ## Scope
   7: - This matrix reflects **current implementation behavior**, not phase-plan scope text.
   8: - For historical phase boundaries, see `documents/phase10.md`.
   9: - Traversal architecture requirements are defined in `documents/Requirements.md` (section `3.2` + section `6`) and `documents/phase10.md`.
  10: - Windows notes in this document are scoped explicitly as VM-lab/runtime-host
  11:   truth unless a row or note says otherwise. They are not a release-gate
  12:   claim.
  13: 
  14: ## Windows VM-Lab Guest Truth
  15: 
  16: - `runtime-host-capable only`: `ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm`,
  17:   `ops vm-lab-start`, `ops vm-lab-restart`, `ops vm-lab-sync-repo`, the
  18:   PowerShell-first access bootstrap helper under
  19:   `scripts/vm_lab/windows/Enable-WindowsVmLabAccess.ps1`, and the canonical
  20:   helper root under `scripts/bootstrap/windows/` all dispatch through
  21:   Windows-specific PowerShell/ZIP/helper paths for `platform=windows`
  22:   inventory targets. The direct smoke helper
  23:   `scripts/bootstrap/windows/Smoke-RustyNetWindowsServiceHost.ps1` validates
  24:   the reviewed `rustynetd --windows-service --env-file` SCM host path and
  25:   intentionally reports `blocked` while the backend label remains
  26:   `windows-unsupported`.
  27: - `Windows bootstrap-phase entrypoints exist`: `sync-source`, `build-release`,
  28:   `smoke-service-host`, `install-release`, `restart-runtime`, `verify-runtime`,
  29:   and `all` route into Windows-specific helper/provider paths.
  30:   `smoke-service-host` validates the reviewed SCM host path and succeeds
  31:   in-scope when the helper reports `host_surface_validated=true` together with
  32:   the explicit `windows-unsupported` backend blocker. `build-release` still
  33:   depends on verified MSVC/toolchain availability or explicit bootstrap
  34:   configuration.
  35: - `runtime-boundary-capable only`: reviewed Windows runtime paths are pinned
  36:   under `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\{config,logs,trust,membership,keys,secrets}`,
  37:   the installer now provisions `secrets\key-custody` with protected ACLs plus
  38:   an unrestricted service SID, and reviewed runtime passphrase custody uses
  39:   DPAPI `.dpapi` blobs instead of plaintext long-lived files. The local
  40:   privileged IPC surface is limited to reviewed `\\.\pipe\RustyNet\...`
  41:   named-pipe probe/ACL-inspection requests, and
  42:   `rustynetd windows-runtime-boundary-check` is the authoritative self-check
  43:   that the Windows verify/diagnostics helpers call.
  44: - `live-lab wrapper boundary is fail-closed`: `ops vm-lab-validate-live-lab-profile`,
  45:   `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab`, `ops vm-lab-run-live-lab`,
  46:   `ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab`, `ops vm-lab-iterate-live-lab`,
  47:   `ops vm-lab-run-suite`, and `ops vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure` are
  48:   still Linux-runtime surfaces. They reject profiles with missing target
  49:   metadata or any configured target that is not
  50:   `platform=linux`/`remote_shell=posix`/`guest_exec_mode=linux_bash`/`service_manager=systemd`
  51:   before any `live_linux_*` stage runs.
  52: - `not dataplane-capable`: `rustynetd` now exposes a reviewed Windows
  53:   service/config host surface and carries the opt-in reviewed backend label
  54:   `windows-wireguard-nt`, but current measured VM-lab proof still stops before
  55:   install/runtime/node evidence and reviewed unsupported operations remain
  56:   explicit fail-closed blockers. Windows therefore still must not be described
  57:   as a supported dataplane target.
  58: - `not fresh-install evidenced`: the latest measured local Windows UTM attempt
  59:   for current `HEAD` on 2026-04-17 first recovered the guest to the shared
  60:   subnet as `192.168.64.14`, then resynced/build current `HEAD` and passed
  61:   `smoke-service-host`, but discovery still reported `execution_ready=false`
  62:   because the Windows local-UTM callback/readiness probe timed out. On the
  63:   same guest state, `install-release` failed closed on that callback timeout,
  64:   guest-side SSH state remained absent (`sshd_service_count=0`,
  65:   `sshd_registry_present=False`, `ssh_listener_count=0`), and diagnostics on
  66:   the blocked path still hit `UTM Windows capture output was missing rc
  67:   marker`. There is still no clean Windows install/runtime/service evidence to
  68:   promote into the release gate. See
  69:   `artifacts/windows_phase4/20260417T174942Z/phase4_evidence_summary.md`.
  70: - `not release-gated and evidenced`: Windows is intentionally excluded from the
  71:   current fresh-install OS matrix and Phase10 release gate because measured
  72:   Windows install/runtime/role-switch evidence does not yet exist.
  73: 
  74: ## Capability Matrix
  75: 
  76: | Capability | Linux | macOS | Security posture | Evidence |
  77: | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  78: | Runtime backend mode | `linux-wireguard` | `macos-wireguard` | Implemented | `crates/rustynetd/src/main.rs:450-451` |
  79: | Production in-memory backend | Disabled | Disabled | More secure than older findings | `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs:526-530` |
  80: | Service lifecycle hardening | `systemd` units | `launchd` daemon/helper bootstrap | Implemented | `scripts/systemd/rustynetd.service:47`, `start.sh:2214-2217` |
  81: | Privileged tool integrity | Root-owned path checks | Root-owned path checks + non-admin fallback blocked | Implemented | `start.sh:1076-1080`, `start.sh:1956-1957` |

  83: | Persistent plaintext passphrase file | Rejected in hardened runtime path | Rejected by macOS checks | More secure than older docs/assumptions | `start.sh:1378`, `start.sh:1907` |
  84: | DNS fail-closed controls | Implemented | Implemented (PF-backed with assertions) | Implemented | `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs:1422-1434`, `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs:1468-1495` |
  85: | Direct/relay failover path in Phase10 runtime | State tracking present | State tracking present | Needs more work for full relay dataplane transport switching | `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs:1954-1970`, `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs:2692-2730` |
  86: | Traversal architecture posture (direct hole punch + relay fallback/failback) | First-class requirement; implementation in progress | First-class requirement; implementation in progress | Secure target posture is defined; runtime parity remains open work | `documents/Requirements.md:59`, `documents/phase10.md:11`, `documents/operations/active/UdpHolePunchingAndRelayTraversalPlan_2026-03-07.md:1` |
  87: | IPv6 protected-mode parity | Supported | Explicitly not supported (`supports_ipv6=false`) until parity is complete | Secure short-term default | `crates/rustynet-backend-wireguard/src/lib.rs:775-781` |
  88: | CI dataplane evidence | Real Linux WireGuard E2E | macOS dataplane smoke + targeted security tests | Needs more work on macOS depth | `.github/workflows/cross-platform-ci.yml:55-65`, `.github/workflows/cross-platform-ci.yml:26-28`, `scripts/ci/macos_dataplane_smoke.sh:44-46` |
  89: | Manual peer break-glass mutation path | Removed (fail-closed) | Removed (fail-closed) | More secure than older docs/assumptions | `start.sh:3303-3356`, `start.sh:4213-4270` |
  90: | Exit-node selection readiness probe UX | Membership+tunnel probe in `SELECT EXIT NODE`; current selection marker + connect/disconnect quick action | Same menu behavior on macOS host profile (compat runtime) | Implemented | `start.sh:3711-3774`, `start.sh:4257-4327` |
  91: | Additional non-simulated backend implementation | Not present in-tree beyond WireGuard | Not present in-tree beyond WireGuard | Needs more work (policy/code discrepancy) | `crates/rustynet-backend-wireguard/src/lib.rs:54`, `crates/rustynet-backend-stub/src/lib.rs:38` |
  92: 
  93: ## Security Notes
  94: - More secure than older docs/findings:
  95:   - production in-memory backend path is blocked,
  96:   - macOS non-admin privileged-tool fallback is blocked,
  97:   - macOS key custody defaults to Keychain and plaintext passphrase files are rejected by default checks.
  98: - Still needs more work:
  99:   - macOS CI is currently smoke-level for dataplane security compared with Linux real E2E depth,
 100:   - policy expects a second non-simulated backend path, but current in-tree implementation set is WireGuard + stub,
 101:   - direct/relay failover in Phase10 runtime is currently state-mode signaling, not full relay transport path integration.
 102:   - traversal architecture is now a core documented requirement, but full hole-punch + relay dataplane integration is not yet complete in runtime code.
 103: 
 104: ## Operational Guidance
 105: - Treat this document as the current support truth source for platform/security behavior.
 106: - If this matrix conflicts with older phase/security reports, prefer this matrix plus direct code verification.

===== /documents/operations/PolicyRolloutRunbook.md =====

   1: # Rustynet Policy Rollout Runbook
   2: 
   3: ## Preconditions
   4: - Policy must pass `ContextualPolicySet` validation.
   5: - Any revision containing allow-all behavior is rejected.
   6: - Change owner and rollback owner are assigned before rollout.
   7: 
   8: ## Rollout Steps
   9: 1. Stage revision in `PolicyRolloutController`.
  10: 2. Run policy validation tests in CI.
  11: 3. Promote staged revision to canary.
  12: 4. Observe canary metrics and audit events.
  13: 5. Promote canary to active revision.
  14: 
  15: ## Rollback
  16: 1. Select previous known-good revision ID.
  17: 2. Execute rollback using `PolicyRolloutController::rollback_to`.
  18: 3. Verify policy evaluation and access controls with regression tests.
  19: 4. Record rollback reason and outcome in audit trail.
  20: 
  21: ## Safety Requirements
  22: - Default-deny behavior must be preserved across revisions.
  23: - Protocol filters must not widen in shared subnet-router/shared-exit contexts.
  24: - Rollout and rollback actions must be audited with actor identity and timestamp.

===== /documents/operations/PostQuantumTransitionPlan.md =====

   1: # Post-Quantum Transition and Hybrid Evaluation Plan
   2: 
   3: ## Constraints
   4: - No custom cryptography or custom VPN protocol is introduced in production paths.
   5: - WireGuard remains default backend while migration planning is validated through modular backend boundaries.
   6: 
   7: ## Goal
   8: Prepare a controlled path for future PQ/hybrid adoption without destabilizing current proven cryptography.
   9: 
  10: ## Hybrid Evaluation Stages
  11: 1. Lab-only hybrid candidate validation:
  12:    - Evaluate candidate stacks from established libraries/protocols only.
  13:    - Confirm compatibility with `TunnelBackend` abstraction and control-plane policy boundaries.
  14: 2. Interop test stage:
  15:    - Validate negotiated fallback behavior with existing WireGuard default path.
  16:    - Confirm fail-closed behavior when hybrid trust state is incomplete.
  17: 3. Canary stage:
  18:    - Enable only under explicit feature flag and risk acceptance.
  19:    - Collect latency, reconnect, and failure-mode metrics.
  20: 4. Decision gate:
  21:    - Security review complete.
  22:    - Performance regression within policy.
  23:    - Operational runbooks updated.
  24: 
  25: ## Decision Criteria
  26: - No regression against Security Minimum Bar controls.
  27: - No leakage of backend-specific types into control/policy domains.
  28: - No unresolved high-risk findings from security review.
  29: 
  30: ## Rollback Criteria
  31: - Any trust-state validation error.
  32: - Performance budget violation.
  33: - Control-plane or data-plane availability degradation beyond SLOs.
  34: 
  35: ## Ownership
  36: - Engineering owner: backend modularity and rollout sequencing.
  37: - Security owner: cryptographic review and risk acceptance governance.
  38: - Operations owner: runbook/on-call readiness for staged rollout.

===== /documents/operations/PrivacyRetentionPolicy.md =====

   1: # Privacy and Data Retention Policy
   2: 
   3: ## Data Classes
   4: - `auth_events`: authentication and abuse-control telemetry.
   5: - `audit_events`: security-relevant administrative actions.
   6: - `diagnostic_metrics`: operational health/performance metrics.
   7: - `credential_material_references`: non-secret references to vaulted secrets.
   8: 
   9: ## Retention Windows
  10: - `auth_events`: 90 days.
  11: - `audit_events`: 365 days.
  12: - `diagnostic_metrics`: 30 days raw, 180 days aggregated.
  13: - `credential_material_references`: lifetime of associated credential plus 30 days.
  14: 
  15: ## Minimization Rules
  16: - No plaintext secrets in telemetry or logs.
  17: - Hash or redact identity-sensitive fields when full fidelity is not required for operations.
  18: - Collect only fields needed for security triage and reliability diagnostics.
  19: 
  20: ## Deletion and Review
  21: - Retention expiration is enforced during scheduled maintenance jobs.
  22: - Quarterly privacy review validates class mappings and retention compliance.

===== /documents/operations/ProductionRunbook.md =====

   1: # Production Runbook
   2: 
   3: ## Scope
   4: Operational runbook for Rustynet control plane, relay plane, and client-release promotion pipeline.
   5: 
   6: ## Normal Operations
   7: 1. Verify service health and alert dashboards at shift start.
   8: 2. Confirm error-budget trend and active incident state.
   9: 3. Validate artifact integrity for current release channel.
  10: 4. Confirm backup jobs and restore checks completed in last 24 hours.
  11: 
  12: ## Deployment Procedure
  13: 1. Run `scripts/ci/phase9_gates.sh`.
  14: 2. Promote release in staged order: `unstable -> canary -> stable`.
  15: 3. Monitor canary for SLO regression before stable promotion.
  16: 4. If any gate regresses, stop promotion and roll back.
  17: 
  18: ## Incident Handling
  19: 1. Page primary on-call; page secondary if no ack within 5 minutes.
  20: 2. Classify severity and enforce response SLA.
  21: 3. Contain blast radius (auth/token revoke, route policy lockdown, relay traffic steering).
  22: 4. Record timeline and complete postmortem.
  23: 
  24: ## Emergency Rollback
  25: - Trigger conditions:
  26:   - trust-state verification failure,
  27:   - security gate failure,
  28:   - SLO/performance gate breach,
  29:   - DR readiness regression.
  30: - Actions:
  31:   1. Halt rollout.
  32:   2. Revert to last signed stable artifact.
  33:   3. Re-validate signing/SBOM/provenance.
  34:   4. Run incident bridge until service is stable.
  35: 
  36: ## On-Call Readiness Requirements
  37: - 24/7 rotation with primary and secondary responder.
  38: - Escalation chain documented and tested in drills.
  39: - Access credentials use least privilege and MFA.
  40: - On-call readiness must be asserted in drill evidence before GA.

===== /documents/operations/ProductionSLOAndIncidentReadiness.md =====

   1: # Production SLO and Incident Readiness
   2: 
   3: ## Service Level Objectives
   4: Release gate thresholds:
   5: - Availability SLO: `>= 99.9%`
   6: - Error budget consumed: `<= 100%` of monthly budget
   7: - Performance budgets:
   8:   - idle CPU `<= 2%` of one core
   9:   - idle memory `<= 120MB RSS`
  10:   - reconnect `<= 5s`
  11:   - route apply p95 `<= 2s`
  12:   - throughput overhead `<= 15%`
  13:   - soak duration `>= 24h`
  14: 
  15: Operational evidence artifacts:
  16: - `artifacts/operations/slo_error_budget_report.json`
  17: - `artifacts/operations/performance_budget_report.json`
  18: 
  19: Artifact generation:
  20: - `scripts/operations/generate_phase9_artifacts.sh` from measured raw inputs under `artifacts/operations/raw/`
  21: - `scripts/operations/collect_phase9_raw_evidence.sh` to build raw inputs from operational source logs/config under `artifacts/operations/source/`
  22: - Artifacts must include measured-evidence metadata (`evidence_mode`, `captured_at_unix`, `environment`, `source_artifacts`).
  23: 
  24: ## Alerting and Gate Behavior
  25: - Alerting policy is default-deny for release progression: if any SLO/performance gate fails, promotion blocks.
  26: - Promotion tracks remain staged (`unstable -> canary -> stable`).
  27: - Security-sensitive changes require canary stability and gate pass before stable.
  28: 
  29: ## Incident Drill Standard
  30: Required per drill:
  31: 1. Scenario scope and trigger conditions.
  32: 2. Detection, containment, and recovery timings.
  33: 3. Postmortem with actionable controls and closed actions.
  34: 4. Confirmation that on-call handoff and escalation paths worked.
  35: 
  36: Drill evidence artifact:
  37: - `artifacts/operations/incident_drill_report.json`
  38: 
  39: ## On-Call Readiness
  40: - 24/7 primary and secondary responder schedule for production incidents.
  41: - Escalation path: on-call -> security owner -> engineering owner -> operations owner.
  42: - Mandatory incident communications channels documented before GA.
  43: - Every drill must confirm on-call readiness flag.
  44: 
  45: ## Enforcement Points
  46: - `crates/rustynet-control/src/ga.rs`
  47:   - `ErrorBudgetGate::passes`
  48:   - `PerformanceBudgetSnapshot::passes`
  49:   - `GaReleaseReadiness::evaluate`
  50: - `scripts/ci/check_phase9_readiness.sh`
  51:   - blocks release when SLO/performance/incident evidence is out of policy.
  52: 
  53: ## Verification
  54: - `scripts/ci/check_phase9_readiness.sh`
  55: - `scripts/ci/phase9_gates.sh`

===== /documents/operations/ReleaseReadinessGuardrails.md =====

   1: # Release Readiness Guardrails
   2: 
   3: ## Purpose
   4: 
   5: Define the one durable sign-off path for Rustynet release readiness.
   6: 
   7: This guardrail is intentionally stricter than the reduced helper workflow. It is
   8: the operator and CI entrypoint that keeps the critical Rust, advisory, license,
   9: and live-lab evidence gates together instead of relying on ad hoc judgment.
  10: 
  11: ## Primary Command
  12: 
  13: Run:
  14: 
  15: ```bash
  16: ./scripts/ci/release_readiness_gates.sh
  17: ```
  18: 
  19: That wrapper executes:
  20: 
  21: 1. `./scripts/ci/phase5_gates.sh`
  22: 2. `./scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh`
  23: 
  24: The result is fail-closed:
  25: 
  26: - Rust formatting, clippy, check, and test gates must pass.
  27: - Phase 5 release-doc/provenance/SBOM gates must pass.
  28: - Advisory and license policy gates must pass.
  29: - Fresh-install release-gate evidence must validate.
  30: - Canonical Phase 10 cross-network evidence must validate.
  31: - The final readiness docs and bundle manifest must exist.
  32: 
  33: If any one of those inputs is missing, stale, malformed, or not bound to the
  34: current commit/evidence state, the release-readiness gate must fail.
  35: 
  36: ## Authoritative Reporting
  37: 
  38: The gate reports are generated by the gate commands themselves on every run:
  39: 
  40: - `artifacts/release/phase5_gate_report.json`
  41: - `artifacts/release/phase5_readiness_bundle.json`
  42: 
  43: Those reports must distinguish:
  44: 
  45: - `executed_passed`
  46: - `executed_failed`
  47: - `not_executed`
  48: 
  49: Pre-existing files are not proof. A stale bundle file or report file must not be
  50: treated as release evidence unless the current gate execution regenerated it and
  51: its required steps are recorded as `executed_passed`.
  52: 
  53: `cargo audit --deny warnings` and `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses
  54: sources` are Phase 5 hard gates. If either command is absent or fails, the
  55: Phase 5 gate and the top-level release-readiness gate must fail with a non-zero
  56: exit status.
  57: 
  58: ## Evidence Boundaries
  59: 
  60: Reduced helper evidence is useful for narrowing runtime defects, but it is not a
  61: substitute for full release-gate evidence.
  62: 
  63: The release-ready claim requires:
  64: 
  65: - current Phase 5 docs and final bundle
  66: - current fresh-install OS matrix evidence for the exact commit under test
  67: - current canonical cross-network evidence for the exact commit under test
  68: 
  69: Reduced helper or same-underlay local-lab reruns must not be presented as if
  70: they satisfy the full release-gate path.
  71: 
  72: ## Operator Security Preconditions
  73: 
  74: The release-readiness and live-lab automation path assumes all of the following:
  75: 
  76: - SSH host trust is pinned
  77:   - use a pinned `known_hosts` file
  78:   - no TOFU / `accept-new` in automation
  79: - SSH authentication uses operator key material with owner-only permissions
  80: - passwordless sudo is available on automation targets
  81:   - `sudo -n` must succeed
  82:   - password-file based sudo is not part of the active live-lab wrapper path
  83: - secret custody for unattended runtime remains credential-only
  84:   - encrypted systemd credentials
  85:   - no plaintext runtime passphrase files at rest
  86: 
  87: If any of those expectations are not true, stop before claiming release
  88: evidence.
  89: 
  90: ## Related Docs
  91: 
  92: - [FreshInstallOSMatrixReleaseGate.md](./FreshInstallOSMatrixReleaseGate.md)
  93: - [LiveLinuxLabOrchestrator.md](./LiveLinuxLabOrchestrator.md)
  94: - [CrossNetworkLiveLabPrerequisitesChecklist.md](./CrossNetworkLiveLabPrerequisitesChecklist.md)
  95: - [Phase5ReleaseReadinessChecklist_2026-04-12.md](./active/Phase5ReleaseReadinessChecklist_2026-04-12.md)
  96: - [Phase5ReleaseReadinessSummary_2026-04-12.md](./active/Phase5ReleaseReadinessSummary_2026-04-12.md)

===== /documents/operations/ReleaseSigningRunbook.md =====

   1: # Release Signing Runbook (Windows Authenticode)
   2: 
   3: Last updated: 2026-04-28
   4: 
   5: ## 1) Mission
   6: 
   7: Every Rustynet Windows release artefact (`rustynetd.exe`) ships
   8: Authenticode-signed. The signature is the trust anchor the W2.1b
   9: chain validator (`crates/rustynetd/src/windows_authenticode.rs` +
  10: `rustynet_windows_native::verify_authenticode_chain`) gates daemon
  11: startup against; an unsigned or self-signed artefact gets
  12: `TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE` / `CERT_E_UNTRUSTEDROOT` and the daemon
  13: refuses to start.
  14: 
  15: This runbook captures the operator-facing setup. The reviewed
  16: workflow + helper landed in:
  17: - [.github/workflows/release-windows.yml](../../.github/workflows/release-windows.yml)
  18: - [scripts/release/Sign-RustyNetWindowsBinary.ps1](../../scripts/release/Sign-RustyNetWindowsBinary.ps1)
  19: 
  20: ## 2) Prerequisites
  21: 
  22: Before tagging a release the operator MUST have configured one of
  23: the supported signing routes (see §3) AND committed the resulting
  24: GitHub Secrets to the repository's secret store.
  25: 
  26: The post-sign verification step in the workflow runs the daemon's
  27: own W2.1b chain validator against the freshly signed artefact, so
  28: a misconfigured cert (untrusted root, missing intermediate, expired,
  29: revoked) fails the workflow before the artefact uploads to the
  30: GitHub release.
  31: 
  32: ## 3) Supported Signing Routes
  33: 
  34: ### 3.1 PFX File on Disk (simplest, baseline)
  35: 
  36: A code-signing certificate exported as a `.pfx` (PKCS#12) file with
  37: a passphrase. Acceptable for non-production / staging signing AND
  38: for production signing IF the PFX is sourced from a hardware-token-
  39: backed export (HSM-issued key, PFX-wrapped for transport).
  40: 
  41: **NOT** acceptable: a soft-key PFX generated by `openssl req` and
  42: self-signed. Such a key fails W2.1b's `WinVerifyTrust` check
  43: (`CERT_E_UNTRUSTEDROOT`) by design.
  44: 
  45: **Setup:**
  46: 
  47: 1. Acquire a code-signing cert from a Microsoft-trusted CA (DigiCert,
  48:    Sectigo, GlobalSign, etc.). The certificate MUST chain to a root
  49:    in the default Windows root store.
  50: 2. Export to PFX with a strong passphrase (minimum 32 random bytes,
  51:    stored only in a password manager + the GitHub Secrets store).
  52: 3. Base64-encode the PFX:
  53:    ```bash
  54:    base64 -w0 release.pfx > release.pfx.b64
  55:    ```
  56: 4. Configure the GitHub Secrets in the repository (Settings → Secrets
  57:    and variables → Actions → New repository secret):
  58:    - `RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_BASE64` = contents of `release.pfx.b64`
  59:    - `RUSTYNET_SIGNING_PFX_PASSWORD` = the PFX passphrase
  60: 5. Optional: `RUSTYNET_SIGNING_TIMESTAMP_URL` = your preferred RFC
  61:    3161 timestamp authority. Defaults to
  62:    `http://timestamp.digicert.com` if unset.
  63: 
  64: The release workflow verifies BOTH secrets are non-empty BEFORE
  65: attempting any sign step; missing secrets fail the job loud.
  66: 
  67: ### 3.2 Azure Key Vault (recommended for production)
  68: 
  69: The signing key never leaves Azure Key Vault. The release workflow
  70: authenticates to Key Vault via OIDC federation + retrieves a
  71: short-lived token, then either:
  72: - exports a sign-only PFX session token (NOT supported by signtool
  73:   today; requires a wrapper like AzureSignTool), OR
  74: - (recommended) uses `AzureSignTool` (https://github.com/vcsjones/AzureSignTool)
  75:   which fetches the cert reference from Key Vault and signs without
  76:   ever materialising a PFX on the runner.
  77: 
  78: Setting up AzureSignTool is OUT OF SCOPE for the v1 runbook (the
  79: PFX flow above is what the workflow currently exercises). Tracked
  80: as a follow-up in
  81: [documents/operations/active/SecurityHardeningAudit_2026-04-28.md](active/SecurityHardeningAudit_2026-04-28.md)
  82: under a future "release signing route hardening" entry.
  83: 
  84: ### 3.3 Hardware Token (Yubikey, SafeNet eToken)
  85: 
  86: Same PFX flow as §3.1 but the PFX is exported from the hardware
  87: token's PKCS#11 / PKCS#12 interface as a *transport* PFX (the
  88: private key still lives on the token; only the cert + a wrapped
  89: export are in the PFX).
  90: 
  91: Operationally identical to §3.1 from the workflow's perspective.
  92: 
  93: ## 4) Release Tag Convention
  94: 
  95: The workflow triggers on tags matching `v*.*.*` (e.g. `v0.1.0`,
  96: `v0.2.3-rc1`). A `git push origin v0.1.0` after `git tag -a v0.1.0`
  97: runs the release-signing job exactly once.
  98: 
  99: Manual `workflow_dispatch` invocation supports a `dry_run` input
 100: (default `true`) that builds without signing — used for path-
 101: validation testing on a branch that does not yet have signing
 102: secrets configured.
 103: 
 104: ## 5) Verification (post-release)
 105: 
 106: A consumer of a Rustynet release MUST verify the signed binary's
 107: chain before installing. Two independent verification paths:
 108: 
 109: 1. Built-in: install the binary, then run
 110:    ```
 111:    "C:\Program Files\RustyNet\rustynetd.exe" windows-authenticode-check
 112:    ```
 113:    The W2.1b chain validator returns `overall_ok=true` only when
 114:    `WinVerifyTrust` reports `Verified` end-to-end.
 115: 
 116: 2. Out-of-band: PowerShell
 117:    ```powershell
 118:    Get-AuthenticodeSignature C:\Path\To\rustynetd.exe
 119:    ```
 120:    Status MUST be `Valid`. Any other status (`UnknownError`,
 121:    `NotSigned`, `HashMismatch`, `NotTrusted`) is fail-closed and
 122:    the binary MUST NOT be installed.
 123: 
 124: The release workflow ships a `rustynetd.exe.sha256` alongside the
 125: signed binary; consumers SHOULD also verify the SHA-256 against the
 126: published release notes' expected hash before running the
 127: Authenticode check.
 128: 
 129: ## 6) Rollback Procedure
 130: 
 131: If a signed release ships and is later found to contain a defect
 132: that requires recall:
 133: 
 134: 1. **Do NOT revoke the signing certificate** unless the private key
 135:    is suspected compromised. Revocation invalidates ALL prior
 136:    signed releases, breaking every deployed install.
 137: 2. Publish a higher-version release with the fix. The W2.1b
 138:    validator does not pin to a specific version; consumers updating
 139:    to the new release pass the chain validator on the new artefact.
 140: 3. Mark the bad release in the GitHub Releases UI as deprecated
 141:    with a clear "do not install — see CVE-XXXX" notice in the
 142:    release notes.
 143: 
 144: If the private key IS suspected compromised:
 145: 
 146: 1. Revoke the certificate at the issuing CA.
 147: 2. Wait for revocation to propagate to CRL/OCSP responders (24-48h
 148:    typically).
 149: 3. The W2.1b validator's `WTD_REVOCATION_CHECK_CHAIN_EXCLUDE_ROOT`
 150:    posture surfaces revoked-cert binaries as
 151:    `CERT_E_REVOKED`/`CRYPT_E_REVOKED` after propagation; deployed
 152:    installs will refuse to restart with the revoked-signed binary.
 153: 4. Re-issue the cert from the CA, re-configure the GitHub Secrets,
 154:    and ship a new release with the fresh cert chain.
 155: 
 156: ## 7) Threat Model Notes
 157: 
 158: - **PFX exfiltration from GitHub Secrets**: Mitigated by the OIDC /
 159:   Key Vault upgrade path in §3.2 (recommended for production). The
 160:   v1 PFX-on-disk flow trusts GitHub's secret-store integrity.
 161: - **Workflow log leakage of signing material**: The helper script
 162:   reads the PFX password from a *named env var* rather than from
 163:   the command line, so the password does not appear in CI logs.
 164:   Workflow steps that reference the PFX/password DO have the
 165:   secret values masked by GitHub Actions' secret-redaction layer.
 166: - **Replay of an old signed binary**: Mitigated by the daemon's
 167:   own integrity verification (the chain validator confirms the
 168:   certificate is still valid + not revoked at runtime, on every
 169:   daemon start). An attacker who replays an old signed binary with
 170:   a since-revoked cert gets `CERT_E_REVOKED` at startup.
 171: - **Misconfigured timestamp authority**: A signed binary without a
 172:   countersigned timestamp expires when the signing cert expires
 173:   (typically 1-3 years). The helper script's `signtool /tr` flag
 174:   is REQUIRED (the script rejects an empty timestamp URL); a
 175:   countersigned timestamp lets the binary remain valid past the
 176:   signing cert's own expiry. Defaults to DigiCert's public RFC
 177:   3161 endpoint.
 178: 
 179: ## 8) Cross-References
 180: 
 181: - W2.1a presence verifier: [crates/rustynetd/src/windows_authenticode.rs](../../crates/rustynetd/src/windows_authenticode.rs)
 182: - W2.1b chain validator: same file + [crates/rustynet-windows-native/src/lib.rs](../../crates/rustynet-windows-native/src/lib.rs)
 183:   (`verify_authenticode_chain`)
 184: - W2.1 plan entry: [documents/operations/active/OsAgnosticOrchestratorAndWindowsPeerDeltaPlan_2026-04-27.md](active/OsAgnosticOrchestratorAndWindowsPeerDeltaPlan_2026-04-27.md)
 185:   §10 W2.1
 186: - Bootstrap trust anchor (membership owner key): [documents/SecurityMinimumBar.md](../SecurityMinimumBar.md)
 187:   §6.B (sister concept — the membership owner key is the trust
 188:   anchor for signed *state*; the Authenticode signing cert is the
 189:   trust anchor for signed *binaries*).

===== /documents/operations/RustynetdServiceHardening.md =====

   1: # Rustynetd Systemd Hardening Profile
   2: 
   3: Status correction (verified 2026-03-05):
   4: - Legacy requirement text that expects a persistent plaintext passphrase file is stale for current Linux hardened runtime.
   5: - Runtime passphrase custody is credential-only via encrypted systemd credential blob (`LoadCredentialEncrypted=wg_key_passphrase:/etc/rustynet/credentials/wg_key_passphrase.cred`).
   6: - Security risk truth: documenting plaintext passphrase files as required can lead to weaker key handling than current code policy.
   7: - When decrypting signing credentials outside unit-injected `%d/...` paths, use explicit credential-name pinning for portability:
   8:   `systemd-creds decrypt --name=signing_key_passphrase /etc/rustynet/credentials/signing_key_passphrase.cred <output>`.
   9: 
  10: ## Purpose
  11: Define a production-safe service profile for `rustynetd` with least privilege, fail-closed behavior, and predictable restart semantics.
  12: 
  13: ## Service Files
  14: - Source: `scripts/systemd/rustynetd.service`
  15: - Install helper: `scripts/systemd/install_rustynetd_service.sh` (compatibility wrapper to `rustynet ops install-systemd`)
  16: - Privileged helper unit: `scripts/systemd/rustynetd-privileged-helper.service`
  17: - Trust refresh unit: `scripts/systemd/rustynetd-trust-refresh.service`
  18: - Trust refresh timer: `scripts/systemd/rustynetd-trust-refresh.timer`
  19: - Trust refresh service executes Rust directly: `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/rustynet ops refresh-trust`, then triggers daemon signed-state apply via `ExecStartPost=/usr/local/bin/rustynet state refresh`
  20: - Assignment refresh unit: `scripts/systemd/rustynetd-assignment-refresh.service`
  21: - Assignment refresh timer: `scripts/systemd/rustynetd-assignment-refresh.timer`
  22: - Assignment refresh service executes Rust directly: `ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/rustynet ops refresh-assignment`, then triggers daemon signed-state apply via `ExecStartPost=/usr/local/bin/rustynet state refresh`
  23: 
  24: Implementation note (runtime shell removal):
  25: - Trust/assignment refresh runtime paths are now direct Rust service execution (`ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/rustynet ops ...`) with binary-custody preflight (`ops verify-runtime-binary-custody`).
  26: - The install helper remains a compatibility wrapper to `rustynet ops install-systemd`, but now pins `/usr/local/bin/rustynet` and runs `ops verify-runtime-binary-custody` before dispatch. Alternate `RUSTYNET_BIN` overrides are rejected fail-closed.
  27: 
  28: ## Hardening Controls (Daemon)
  29: - `NoNewPrivileges=true`
  30: - `ProtectSystem=strict`
  31: - `ProtectHome=true`
  32: - `PrivateTmp=true`
  33: - `PrivateDevices=true`
  34: - `ProtectControlGroups=true`
  35: - `ProtectKernelTunables=true`
  36: - `ProtectKernelModules=true`
  37: - `ProtectKernelLogs=true`
  38: - `MemoryDenyWriteExecute=true`
  39: - `LockPersonality=true`
  40: - `RestrictSUIDSGID=true`
  41: - `RestrictRealtime=true`
  42: - `SystemCallArchitectures=native`
  43: - `CapabilityBoundingSet=` (empty)
  44: - `AmbientCapabilities=` (empty)
  45: - `ReadWritePaths=/run/rustynet /var/lib/rustynet /etc/rustynet`
  46: - `UMask=0077`
  47: - `EnvironmentFile=-/etc/default/rustynetd` with validated daemon/runtime values
  48: 
  49: ## Hardening Controls (Privileged Helper)
  50: - `NoNewPrivileges=true`
  51: - `ProtectSystem=strict`
  52: - `ProtectHome=true`
  53: - `PrivateTmp=true`
  54: - `PrivateDevices=true`
  55: - `ProtectKernelTunables=false` (required for controlled sysctl writes)
  56: - `CapabilityBoundingSet=CAP_NET_ADMIN CAP_NET_RAW CAP_CHOWN CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE CAP_SYS_ADMIN`
  57: - `AmbientCapabilities=CAP_NET_ADMIN CAP_NET_RAW CAP_CHOWN CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE CAP_SYS_ADMIN`
  58: - `ReadWritePaths=/run/rustynet /proc/sys/net/ipv4 /proc/sys/net/ipv6`
  59: 
  60: ## Hardening Controls (Trust Refresh)
  61: - Timer-driven one-shot refresh runs via `rustynetd-trust-refresh.service`.
  62: - Uses `ProtectSystem=full`, `NoNewPrivileges=true`, and only `CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE` + `CAP_CHOWN` to access strict daemon-owned runtime paths and preserve trust evidence owner/group permissions.
  63: - Reads encrypted signer key from `RUSTYNET_TRUST_SIGNER_KEY` and uses explicit passphrase input (`RUSTYNET_TRUST_SIGNING_KEY_PASSPHRASE_FILE`) loaded via `LoadCredentialEncrypted`.
  64: - Enforces signer key ownership/mode guardrails (root-owned, owner-only) plus passphrase file ownership/mode checks.
  65: - Encrypted signing artifacts under `/etc/rustynet` require parent directory mode `0750` (`root:<daemon-group>`) and file mode `0600`.
  66: - Uses daemon-group-readable trust evidence (`root:<daemon-group>`, mode `0640`) when daemon group exists.
  67: - Startup/migration cleanup paths for trust/signing artifacts use scrub+remove semantics (best-effort overwrite before unlink).
  68: 
  69: ## Hardening Controls (Assignment Refresh)
  70: - Timer-driven one-shot refresh runs via `rustynetd-assignment-refresh.service`.
  71: - Auto-refresh remains fail-closed: stale/invalid signed assignment bundles are still rejected at daemon reconcile.
  72: - Requires explicit enable (`RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_AUTO_REFRESH=true`) and root-owned refresh config (`/etc/rustynet/assignment-refresh.env`).
  73: - Reads encrypted signing secret from `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_SIGNING_SECRET` with explicit passphrase input (`RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_SIGNING_SECRET_PASSPHRASE_FILE`) loaded via `LoadCredentialEncrypted`.
  74: - Enforces root ownership/strict mode checks on both encrypted signing secret and passphrase source.
  75: - Encrypted signing artifacts under `/etc/rustynet` require parent directory mode `0750` (`root:<daemon-group>`) and file mode `0600`.
  76: - Reissues signed bundle with bounded TTL and rewrites artifacts atomically:
  77:   - `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.assignment` (`0640 root:<daemon-group>`)
  78:   - `/etc/rustynet/assignment.pub` (`0644 root:root`)
  79: - Legacy encrypted-key migration cleanup uses scrub+remove semantics (best-effort overwrite before unlink).
  80: 
  81: ## Reliability Controls
  82: - `Restart=on-failure`
  83: - `RestartSec=2s`
  84: - `StartLimitBurst=5`
  85: - `StartLimitIntervalSec=60`
  86: - `RuntimeDirectory=rustynet` with mode `0700`
  87: - `StateDirectory=rustynet` with mode `0700`
  88: - Trust refresh timer cadence:
  89:   - `OnBootSec=45s`
  90:   - `OnUnitActiveSec=60s`
  91:   - `RandomizedDelaySec=10s`
  92:   - `Persistent=true`
  93: - Assignment refresh timer cadence:
  94:   - `OnBootSec=45s`
  95:   - `OnUnitActiveSec=60s`
  96:   - `RandomizedDelaySec=10s`
  97:   - `Persistent=true`
  98: 
  99: ## Required Runtime Files
 100: - `/etc/rustynet` directory (`0750`, `root:<daemon-group>`) for verifier + encrypted signing artifacts
 101: - `/etc/rustynet/credentials` directory (`0700`, `root:root`) for encrypted credential blobs
 102: - `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.key.enc` (`0600`, encrypted at rest)
 103: - `/etc/rustynet/credentials/wg_key_passphrase.cred` (`0600`, encrypted credential blob for passphrase custody)
 104: - `/etc/rustynet/credentials/signing_key_passphrase.cred` (`0600`, encrypted credential blob for signing-key passphrase custody)
 105: - `/run/rustynet/wireguard.key` (`0600`, runtime-decrypted key material)
 106: - `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.pub` (`0644`)
 107: - `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.trust` (`0640`, integrity-checked trust evidence)
 108: - `/etc/rustynet/trust-evidence.pub` (pinned trust verifier key)
 109: - `/etc/rustynet/trust-evidence.key` (`0600`, encrypted signer key; required only when trust auto-refresh is enabled)
 110: - `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.assignment` (`0640`, signed auto-tunnel bundle)
 111: - `/etc/rustynet/assignment.pub` (`0644`, assignment verifier key)
 112: - `/etc/rustynet/assignment.signing.secret` (`0600`, encrypted assignment signer secret; required only when assignment auto-refresh is enabled)
 113: - `/etc/rustynet/assignment-refresh.env` (`0600`, root-owned assignment refresh input map)
 114: - `/var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.passphrase` should be absent in hardened Linux runtime (persistent plaintext passphrase files are rejected by preflight).
 115: 
 116: ## Verification
 117: 1. `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`
 118: 2. `sudo ./scripts/systemd/install_rustynetd_service.sh`
 119: 3. `sudo systemctl --no-pager --full status rustynetd.service`
 120: 4. `sudo systemctl --no-pager --full status rustynetd-privileged-helper.service`
 121: 5. If `RUSTYNET_TRUST_AUTO_REFRESH=true`: `sudo systemctl --no-pager --full status rustynetd-trust-refresh.timer`
 122: 6. Trigger one refresh cycle: `sudo systemctl start rustynetd-trust-refresh.service`
 123: 7. If `RUSTYNET_ASSIGNMENT_AUTO_REFRESH=true`: `sudo systemctl --no-pager --full status rustynetd-assignment-refresh.timer`
 124: 8. Trigger one assignment refresh cycle: `sudo systemctl start rustynetd-assignment-refresh.service`
 125: 9. `RUSTYNET_DAEMON_SOCKET=/run/rustynet/rustynetd.sock cargo run -p rustynet-cli -- status`
