===== /documents/operations/SecurityRegressionLessons_2026-03-07.md =====

   1: # Security Regression Lessons and Test Enforcement (2026-03-07)
   2: 
   3: ## Objective
   4: Translate known exploited VPN/overlay/network-control weaknesses into **Rustynet-specific, continuously enforced tests** so security posture cannot silently regress.
   5: 
   6: ## External Vulnerability Lessons (Applied)
   7: 
   8: 1. Route-level VPN bypass / split-tunnel abuse (`TunnelVision`, CVE-2024-3661)
   9: - Public references:
  10:   - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-3661
  11:   - https://www.tunnelvisionbug.com/faq
  12: - Lesson:
  13:   - Route-based VPNs can be bypassed when route-control trust boundaries are weak or manipulated by hostile local network control-plane inputs.
  14: - Rustynet enforcement direction:
  15:   - Keep fail-closed route enforcement and deny unauthorized route mutation for non-admin roles.
  16:   - Keep auto-tunnel enforcement route mutation constrained to explicit policy exceptions only.
  17: 
  18: 2. Encrypted-overlay downgrade/race issues leading to unencrypted forwarding
  19: - Public references:
  20:   - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-28250
  21:   - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-32793
  22: - Lesson:
  23:   - Policy/redirect races can create temporary cleartext paths.
  24: - Rustynet enforcement direction:
  25:   - Preserve deterministic reconcile ordering and fail-closed fallback.
  26:   - Keep replay/watermark protection for signed assignment/traversal artifacts.
  27: 
  28: 3. Privilege escalation via insecure local custody (writable or symlinked trusted paths)
  29: - Public references:
  30:   - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2018-10204
  31:   - https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2018-9105
  32: - Lesson:
  33:   - Local privilege boundaries are frequently broken by weak filesystem custody assumptions.
  34: - Rustynet enforcement direction:
  35:   - Validate **parent directory custody**, not just file ownership/mode.
  36:   - Reject symlink parent directories for sensitive daemon artifacts.
  37: 
  38: ## Implemented in This Pass
  39: 
  40: ### Runtime hardening
  41: - Added parent-directory security validation for sensitive daemon files in preflight path:
  42:   - parent must exist,
  43:   - parent must be a non-symlink directory,
  44:   - parent must not be group/other writable (`mode & 0o022 == 0`),
  45:   - parent owner must match runtime uid (or root when explicitly allowed).
  46: - Enforcement point:
  47:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs` (`validate_file_security` now calls parent-directory validator).
  48: - Added dataplane firewall generation-handoff ordering hardening:
  49:   - fail-closed table handoff now applies the new generation rules first and only then prunes the previous generation table,
  50:   - stale generation state is not reused across generation changes,
  51:   - pre-handoff pruning keeps both target and currently-active owned tables to avoid deleting active fail-closed state.
  52: - Enforcement point:
  53:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs` (`ensure_failclosed_table`, `prune_owned_tables`, `apply_firewall_killswitch`).
  54: 
  55: ### New regression tests
  56: - `daemon::tests::validate_file_security_rejects_group_writable_parent_directory`
  57: - `daemon::tests::validate_file_security_rejects_symlink_parent_directory`
  58: - `phase10::tests::firewall_generation_handoff_deletes_previous_table_only_after_new_rules_apply`
  59: - `phase10::tests::prune_owned_tables_preserves_active_and_target_generation_tables`
  60: - `daemon::tests::read_command_rejects_oversized_payload`
  61: - `daemon::tests::read_command_rejects_null_byte_payload`
  62: - `daemon::tests::node_role_command_matrix_is_fail_closed`
  63: - `daemon::tests::role_auth_matrix_runtime_is_exhaustive_and_fail_closed`
  64: - `daemon::tests::traversal_adversarial_gate_rejects_forged_stale_wrong_signer_and_nonce_replay`
  65: - `daemon::tests::daemon_runtime_netcheck_rejects_forged_traversal_hint_fail_closed`
  66: - `privileged_helper::tests::validate_request_rejects_too_many_arguments`
  67: - `privileged_helper::tests::validate_request_rejects_argument_over_max_bytes`
  68: - `traversal::tests::adversarial_gate_nat_mismatch_blocks_unauthorized_direct_and_keeps_safe_relay_fallback`
  69: - `ops_phase9::tests::read_json_object_rejects_oversized_source`
  70: - `ops_phase9::tests::read_utf8_regular_file_with_max_bytes_rejects_oversized_source`
  71: - `ops_phase9::tests::release_provenance_verification_rejects_tampered_artifact`
  72: - `ops_phase9::tests::release_provenance_verification_rejects_unsigned_document`
  73: - `key_material::tests::remove_file_if_present_rejects_directory`
  74: - `key_material::tests::remove_file_if_present_removes_symlink_without_following_target`
  75: - `tests::secure_remove_file_rejects_directory` (`rustynet-cli`)
  76: - `tests::secure_remove_file_removes_target_file` (`rustynet-cli`)
  77: - `tests::create_secure_temp_file_sets_owner_only_mode` (`rustynet-cli`)
  78: - `scripts/ci/no_leak_dataplane_gate.sh` + `scripts/e2e/real_wireguard_no_leak_under_load.sh` (root Linux high-assurance no-leak gate)
  79: - `scripts/ci/secrets_hygiene_gates.sh` (plaintext-artifact/log-argv/tmp/secure-delete hygiene gate)
  80: - `scripts/ci/role_auth_matrix_gates.sh` (exhaustive role x command x mode x hop allow/deny matrix, including blind_exit least-knowledge restrictions)
  81: - `scripts/ci/traversal_adversarial_gates.sh` (forged/stale/wrong-signer/replay traversal-hint rejection + NAT-mismatch relay safety)
  82: - `scripts/ci/supply_chain_integrity_gates.sh` (cargo audit/deny + SBOM + signed attestation verification + unsigned/tampered binary rejection)
  83: 
  84: These tests prevent regressions where sensitive artifact validation would accept hostile parent-directory custody.
  85: The phase10 handoff test prevents regressions that could reintroduce transient cleartext forwarding windows during generation rollover.
  86: The traversal adversarial tests enforce fail-closed behavior for forged/stale/wrong-signer/replayed traversal hints and block direct-path planning under NAT-mismatch relay-only conditions.
  87: 
  88: ## Continuous Enforcement Path
  89: - The new tests are part of `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`.
  90: - Phase gates (for example Phase10) already execute workspace tests, so this hardening is enforced in CI/release gate paths.
  91: - A dedicated gate bundle now enforces high-value anti-regression tests:
  92:   - `scripts/ci/security_regression_gates.sh`
  93:   - invoked by `scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh`.
  94: - Traversal adversarial checks are part of that gate bundle (`scripts/ci/traversal_adversarial_gates.sh`) and fail closed on:
  95:   - forged/tampered hint signatures,
  96:   - wrong-signer hints,
  97:   - stale hints,
  98:   - nonce replay/rollback hints,
  99:   - NAT mismatch relay-only direct-path denial.
 100: - A dedicated secrets hygiene gate is now part of the regression bundle:
 101:   - `scripts/ci/secrets_hygiene_gates.sh`
 102:   - asserts:
 103:     - no runtime plaintext key artifacts at rest in repo/workspace paths,
 104:     - no inline secret argv flags in source paths,
 105:     - no secret-like leaks in generated artifact/log payloads,
 106:     - strict mode/owner and secure-delete regression tests stay green,
 107:     - shell tmp secret materialization paths enforce `chmod 600` + secure-delete cleanup.
 108: - A dedicated role/auth matrix gate is now part of the regression bundle:
 109:   - `scripts/ci/role_auth_matrix_gates.sh`
 110:   - asserts:
 111:     - exhaustive `role x command x mode x hop` authorization outcomes,
 112:     - fail-closed deny-reason precedence (`role` -> `restricted-safe` -> `auto-tunnel`),
 113:     - blind-exit least-knowledge status invariants (`exit_node=none`, `serving_exit_node=true`, `lan_access=off`).
 114: - Real dataplane no-leak gate is integrated into security regression flow with strict control:
 115:   - `RUSTYNET_SECURITY_RUN_NO_LEAK_GATE=auto` (default): run when host is root Linux.
 116:   - `RUSTYNET_SECURITY_REQUIRE_NO_LEAK_GATE=1`: fail if gate cannot run on current host.
 117:   - CI can enforce this gate by setting `RUSTYNET_SECURITY_REQUIRE_NO_LEAK_GATE=1`.
 118: - Optional real Linux netns leak test is supported via:
 119:   - `RUSTYNET_SECURITY_RUN_REAL_NETNS_E2E=1 ./scripts/ci/security_regression_gates.sh`
 120:   - fails closed if host is not Linux or lacks root privileges.
 121: - Supply-chain integrity gate is now enforced in both release-assurance and regression paths:
 122:   - `scripts/ci/phase8_gates.sh` invokes `scripts/ci/supply_chain_integrity_gates.sh`
 123:   - `scripts/ci/security_regression_gates.sh` invokes `scripts/ci/supply_chain_integrity_gates.sh`
 124:   - Gate requirements:
 125:     - `cargo audit --deny warnings` with advisory DB bootstrap
 126:     - `cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories`
 127:     - SBOM generation + digest (`scripts/release/generate_sbom.sh`)
 128:     - signed release provenance generation (`rustynet ops sign-release-artifact`)
 129:     - fail-closed attestation verify (`rustynet ops verify-release-artifact`)
 130:     - negative checks requiring rejection of unsigned and tampered release artifacts.
 131: 
 132: ## Additional High-Value Backlog Tests (Next)
 133: 1. Role/Auth matrix expansion
 134: - Extend matrix assertions to include membership-health variants (active/revoked/quarantined) and ensure authz outcomes remain deterministic across each role/mode/hop cell.
 135: - Add coverage for additional mutating commands introduced in future CLI/daemon revisions so matrix gates remain complete by default.
 136: 
 137: 2. Reconcile race/fail-closed invariant expansion
 138: - Extend deterministic handoff tests to include NAT/table handoff sequencing and rollback-injected failures.
 139: - Assert fail-closed guarantees across firewall + NAT + route updates as a single transaction boundary.
 140: 
 141: 3. Artifact size and parser abuse limits
 142: - Add maximum input size guards + tests for trust/assignment/traversal artifact parsing to prevent local DoS via oversized artifacts.
 143: - Status update: completed in current security-regression gates (`artifact_limitgate_*`, `artifact_fuzzgate_*`).
 144: 
 145: 4. Socket and local IPC abuse hardening tests
 146: - Add explicit tests for socket ownership/mode drift and peer credential rejection on unauthorized UID access.
 147: 
 148: ## Acceptance Standard for New Security Tests
 149: - Every new security-sensitive behavior must include:
 150:   - a positive test (works when secure),
 151:   - a negative test (fails closed when violated),
 152:   - gate inclusion (workspace or phase gate path).

===== /documents/operations/VulnerabilityResponse.md =====

   1: # Rustynet Vulnerability Response Workflow
   2: 
   3: ## Intake
   4: 1. Collect reports from internal testing, advisories, and disclosure channels.
   5: 2. Assign severity (`critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low`) and affected components.
   6: 3. Open a tracked incident record with owner, discovery time, and patch target.
   7: 
   8: ## SLA Enforcement
   9: - `critical`: mitigation or patched build within 48 hours.
  10: - `high`: patched build within 7 calendar days.
  11: - `medium`: patched build within 30 calendar days.
  12: - `low`: remediation planned in regular hardening cycle.
  13: 
  14: ## Execution
  15: 1. Reproduce and scope impact.
  16: 2. Add regression tests before patching.
  17: 3. Patch root cause and rerun security/phase gates.
  18: 4. Prepare emergency release if severity is `critical` or active exploitation exists.
  19: 
  20: ## Disclosure
  21: 1. Publish advisory summary with affected versions and upgrade guidance.
  22: 2. Record remediation and verification evidence in release artifacts.
  23: 3. Update patch-SLA tracker in `artifacts/security/patch_sla_tracker.json`.
  24: 
  25: ## Staged Release Tracks
  26: 1. Promote to `unstable`.
  27: 2. Promote to `canary` after canary verification.
  28: 3. Promote to `stable` only after all security gates pass.

===== /documents/operations/WindowsWorkingNodeBringUpRunbook.md =====

   1: # Windows Working-Node Bring-Up Runbook
   2: 
   3: Last updated: 2026-04-28
   4: 
   5: ## 1) Mission
   6: 
   7: This runbook walks an operator from "fresh Windows 11 host" to
   8: "daemon running on the `windows-wireguard-nt` backend, ready to
   9: join a RustyNet mesh." It composes the verifier + install +
  10: distribution surface that landed under the OS-Agnostic Orchestrator
  11: + Windows-Peer delta plan and the WindowsWorkingNodePlan.
  12: 
  13: Prerequisite: this runbook assumes the operator has the membership
  14: owner public key delivered out-of-band per
  15: [`SecurityMinimumBar.md` §6.B](../SecurityMinimumBar.md). Without
  16: the trust anchor, no signed-state bundle can be ingested.
  17: 
  18: ## 2) High-Level Flow
  19: 
  20: ```
  21: [1] Run the RustyNet bootstrap (winget installs WireGuard + Git + PS7 + rustup)
  22: [2] Sync the Rustynet source tree to the Windows guest
  23: [3] Build rustynetd.exe inside the guest
  24: [4] Run windows-backend-readiness-check (confirms WG ended up installed)
  25: [5] Run Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1 (auto-detects WG)
  26: [6] Run windows-runtime-acls-check + the W2.x security validators
  27: [7] Distribute signed bundles (membership + assignment + traversal + DNS zone)
  28: [8] Verify the daemon ingested state via windows-mesh-status-check
  29: ```
  30: 
  31: ## 3) Step-By-Step
  32: 
  33: ### 3.1 Run the bootstrap (auto-installs WireGuard for Windows)
  34: 
  35: The `Bootstrap-RustyNetWindows.ps1` helper runs `winget configure`
  36: against `RustyNetBootstrap.winget.yml`, which declares every
  37: prerequisite the working-node bring-up depends on:
  38: 
  39: - `Git.Git` — source sync
  40: - `Microsoft.PowerShell` (PS 7) — modern non-interactive scripting
  41: - `Rustlang.Rustup` — toolchain management for the build phase
  42: - **`WireGuard.WireGuard`** — installs the official WireGuard for
  43:   Windows package, providing
  44:   `C:\Program Files\WireGuard\wireguard.exe`,
  45:   `C:\Program Files\WireGuard\wg.exe`, and the `WireGuardManager`
  46:   tunnel-management service
  47: 
  48: Invoking it (orchestrator-driven path, from a Linux/macOS
  49: workstation):
  50: 
  51: ```bash
  52: ./target/release/rustynet-cli ops vm-lab-bootstrap-phase \
  53:     --phase prepare-transport \
  54:     --vm windows-utm-1 \
  55:     --inventory documents/operations/active/vm_lab_inventory.json \
  56:     --ssh-identity-file ~/.ssh/rustynet_lab_ed25519
  57: ```
  58: 
  59: After winget reports success, `Assert-RustyNetWingetDependenciesInstalled`
  60: double-checks every package landed at its canonical path. If
  61: WireGuard, Rustup, or Git is missing post-winget the bootstrap
  62: fails LOUD with a precise list — preventing a downstream install
  63: helper from silently falling back to `windows-unsupported` because
  64: WireGuard wasn't actually installed.
  65: 
  66: To verify the WireGuard install signature out-of-band:
  67: 
  68: ```powershell
  69: Get-AuthenticodeSignature 'C:\Program Files\WireGuard\wireguard.exe'
  70: ```
  71: 
  72: Status MUST be `Valid`. (The winget package source is itself
  73: signature-verified, but operators on regulated networks may want
  74: the explicit confirmation.)
  75: 
  76: To opt out of the WireGuard install (staging hosts that should
  77: stay on the fail-closed `windows-unsupported` backend), an
  78: operator skips Step 3.4's auto-detection by passing
  79: `-ForceUnsupportedBackend` to the install helper. The daemon
  80: will refuse to start until a future install-helper run flips the
  81: env file.
  82: 
  83: ### 3.2 Sync source + build
  84: 
  85: The orchestrator's `vm-lab-bootstrap-phase --phase build-release`
  86: flow does this for VM-lab guests; an operator bringing up a Windows
  87: host outside the lab can use the equivalent SSH-based path. The
  88: build produces `target\release\rustynetd.exe` inside the
  89: `C:\Rustynet\` source root.
  90: 
  91: ### 3.3 Confirm backend prerequisites are present
  92: 
  93: Before flipping the install helper to `windows-wireguard-nt` mode,
  94: run the daemon's own readiness check:
  95: 
  96: ```powershell
  97: & 'C:\Rustynet\target\release\rustynetd.exe' windows-backend-readiness-check
  98: ```
  99: 
 100: Expected output: `overall_ok: true` with all three reviewed paths
 101: (`wireguard.exe`, `wg.exe`, `netsh.exe`) reporting
 102: `present: true, probed: true`. If any entry is missing, the install
 103: helper will fall back to `windows-unsupported` even on the next
 104: run, so resolve missing prerequisites first.
 105: 
 106: ### 3.4 Install the RustyNet service
 107: 
 108: ```powershell
 109: powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive `
 110:     -ExecutionPolicy Bypass `
 111:     -File 'C:\Rustynet\scripts\bootstrap\windows\Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1' `
 112:     -OutputPath 'C:\Rustynet\.tmp\install-report.json'
 113: ```
 114: 
 115: The helper:
 116: - Validates `-ServiceName`, `-InstallRoot`, `-StateRoot` parameters
 117:   (defense-in-depth W2.5b validators rejecting metacharacters /
 118:   unreviewed paths)
 119: - Probes for WireGuard for Windows
 120:   (`Test-WireGuardDriverPresence`) and writes `--backend
 121:   windows-wireguard-nt` to the env file when detected, else
 122:   `--backend windows-unsupported` for fail-closed
 123: - Installs the daemon binary at `C:\Program Files\RustyNet\rustynetd.exe`,
 124:   locks down the binary's ACL (W2.2: SYSTEM + Administrators full,
 125:   service identity RX-only), creates the runtime ACL'd state tree,
 126:   configures the service via `New-Service` with reviewed startup +
 127:   failure-action policy, and starts the daemon
 128: 
 129: The console output advertises the chosen backend label so the
 130: operator can confirm at a glance which path was taken.
 131: 
 132: To pin the install to fail-closed mode regardless of WG presence
 133: (staging hosts, dry-run validation):
 134: 
 135: ```powershell
 136: ... -ForceUnsupportedBackend
 137: ```
 138: 
 139: ### 3.5 Run the W2.x security validators
 140: 
 141: After install, run every reviewed daemon-side validator to confirm
 142: the host posture matches the security minimum bar:
 143: 
 144: ```powershell
 145: $exe = 'C:\Program Files\RustyNet\rustynetd.exe'
 146: & $exe windows-runtime-acls-check
 147: & $exe windows-service-hardening-check
 148: & $exe windows-key-custody-check
 149: & $exe windows-authenticode-check
 150: & $exe windows-dns-failclosed-check
 151: & $exe windows-backend-readiness-check
 152: ```
 153: 
 154: Each must report `overall_ok: true`. The orchestrator-side
 155: `vm-lab-validate-windows-security` subcommand drives the same set
 156: remotely over SSH; running them locally is the operator's
 157: in-the-loop verification.
 158: 
 159: If `windows-authenticode-check` fails with `TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE`,
 160: the daemon binary is unsigned. Production deployments require a
 161: signed binary built by the release pipeline
 162: (`.github/workflows/release-windows.yml`); the W2.1b chain
 163: validator gates daemon startup against the cert.
 164: 
 165: ### 3.6 Distribute signed-state bundles
 166: 
 167: From the orchestrator host (Linux/macOS, where the rustynet-cli
 168: tooling builds), push each signed bundle to the Windows guest. The
 169: 4 helpers in `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs` are:
 170: 
 171: ```rust
 172: run_distribute_windows_membership_stage(...)
 173: run_distribute_windows_assignment_stage(...)
 174: run_distribute_windows_traversal_stage(...)
 175: run_distribute_windows_dns_zone_stage(...)
 176: ```
 177: 
 178: Each takes the local-filesystem path of the corresponding signed
 179: bundle and pushes via SCP + atomic `Move-Item -Force` + watermark
 180: clear. Order matters:
 181: 
 182: 1. **membership** first — the daemon's peer table can't reconcile
 183:    without a current membership snapshot.
 184: 2. **assignment** — exit / role assignment per peer.
 185: 3. **traversal** — STUN / relay traversal coordination.
 186: 4. **dns-zone** — magic-DNS records.
 187: 
 188: The orchestrator subcommand surface that exposes these helpers
 189: (`ops vm-lab-distribute-windows-state` or similar) is a follow-up;
 190: today the helpers are callable directly from any orchestrator
 191: code path that wires up the Linux-side bundle-pull + Windows-side
 192: bundle-push.
 193: 
 194: ### 3.7 Confirm daemon ingestion
 195: 
 196: ```powershell
 197: & 'C:\Program Files\RustyNet\rustynetd.exe' windows-mesh-status-check
 198: ```
 199: 
 200: Expected output: `overall_ok: true` with `load_status: ok` and a
 201: non-empty `peer_ids` list reflecting the distributed membership.
 202: 
 203: If `load_status: missing`, the daemon hasn't yet refreshed since
 204: the bundle was pushed; the watermark-clear in the distribution
 205: helpers forces re-ingestion on the next refresh tick. The default
 206: refresh cadence is documented in `crates/rustynetd/src/fetcher.rs`
 207: (`RefreshScheduler`).
 208: 
 209: ## 4) Troubleshooting
 210: 
 211: ### 4.1 Daemon refuses to start with `windows-runtime-backend-explicitly-unsupported`
 212: 
 213: Cause: install helper wrote `--backend windows-unsupported` to the
 214: env file (either WireGuard for Windows wasn't installed when the
 215: helper ran, or `-ForceUnsupportedBackend` was passed).
 216: 
 217: Fix:
 218: 1. Install WireGuard for Windows (§3.1).
 219: 2. Re-run the install helper without `-ForceUnsupportedBackend`.
 220: 3. Confirm via `Get-Content C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\config\rustynetd.env`
 221:    that the `RUSTYNETD_DAEMON_ARGS_JSON` line contains
 222:    `windows-wireguard-nt`.
 223: 4. `Restart-Service RustyNet`.
 224: 
 225: ### 4.2 `windows-authenticode-check` fails with `TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE`
 226: 
 227: Cause: daemon binary is an unsigned local build.
 228: 
 229: Fix: download a signed release artefact from the GitHub Release
 230: (produced by `.github/workflows/release-windows.yml` after a tag
 231: push). Verify per
 232: [`ReleaseSigningRunbook.md`](./ReleaseSigningRunbook.md) §5
 233: (`Get-AuthenticodeSignature` Status = `Valid`, SHA-256 matches the
 234: release notes) before installing.
 235: 
 236: ### 4.3 `windows-mesh-status-check` reports `load_status: missing`
 237: 
 238: Cause 1: distribution helpers haven't run yet, or were interrupted
 239: mid-flight. Re-run the distribution sequence (§3.6).
 240: 
 241: Cause 2: the membership.snapshot's signature failed verification
 242: against the membership-owner public key. Confirm
 243: `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\membership.owner.key.pub` matches
 244: the operator's published thumbprint per SecurityMinimumBar §6.B.
 245: 
 246: Cause 3: the watermark file wasn't cleared (concurrent operator
 247: runs, or manual operator intervention). Delete:
 248: - `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\membership\membership.watermark`
 249: - `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.assignment.watermark`
 250: - `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.traversal.watermark`
 251: - `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\rustynetd.dns-zone.watermark`
 252: 
 253: then `Restart-Service RustyNet`. The daemon will re-ingest on next
 254: refresh.
 255: 
 256: ### 4.4 Service install succeeds but tunnels never come up
 257: 
 258: Confirm:
 259: - `Get-Service WireGuardManager` reports `Running`
 260: - `& 'C:\Program Files\WireGuard\wg.exe' show all` lists the
 261:   expected interfaces
 262: - The daemon's log (under
 263:   `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\logs\rustynetd.log` once that path is
 264:   wired up) reports successful `WindowsWireguardBackend::start`
 265: 
 266: If the daemon log shows `install_tunnel_service` failing, the WG
 267: installer's user account / service-control permissions may have
 268: been altered; reinstall WireGuard for Windows.
 269:

 103: ## Document Status: CRITICAL SECURITY REFERENCE
 104: This document defines the complete, production-grade architecture for establishing secure cross-network tunnels between Rustynet nodes across the Internet. Every implementation choice must be traceable to a security requirement or threat mitigation in this document.
 105: 
 106: **Implementation Tracking:** Use the checklist markers `[ ]` throughout this document to track completion. Mark items `[x]` only when implemented + verified with test evidence.
 107: 
 108: ## 1. Objective
 109: Deliver Tailscale-like remote exit-node behavior for Rustynet:
 110: - a device on one network can securely use an authorized Rustynet exit node on a different network,
 111: - direct UDP is used when NAT conditions allow,
 112: - encrypted relay is used when direct UDP cannot be established,
 113: - fail-closed behavior is preserved for traffic, DNS, routing, and control-plane trust.
 114: 
 115: This document is implementation-oriented. It starts from the repository's current state and defines the remaining work in phases.
 116: 
 117: ## 2. Document Relationship and Precedence
 118: This plan extends, but does not replace:
 119: - [Requirements.md](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/documents/Requirements.md)
 120: - [SecurityMinimumBar.md](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/documents/SecurityMinimumBar.md)
 121: - [phase10.md](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/documents/phase10.md)
 122: - [UdpHolePunchingAndRelayTraversalPlan_2026-03-07.md](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/documents/operations/active/UdpHolePunchingAndRelayTraversalPlan_2026-03-07.md)
 123: - [UdpHolePunchingHP2IngestionPlan_2026-03-07.md](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/documents/operations/active/UdpHolePunchingHP2IngestionPlan_2026-03-07.md)
 124: 
 125: If any conflict exists, the stricter security interpretation wins.
 126: 
 127: ## 3. User Outcome
 128: The target user experience is:
 129: 1. A user enrolls a device on network A.
 130: 2. Another enrolled device on network B is authorized as an exit node.
 131: 3. The client selects that remote exit node.
 132: 4. Rustynet establishes the tunnel automatically:
 133:    - direct UDP if possible,
 134:    - encrypted relay if direct UDP is not possible.
 135: 5. Full-tunnel traffic and managed DNS flow through the selected remote exit node without manual consumer-router port forwarding.
 136: 
 137: The phrase "from anywhere" is not acceptable as a claim until the direct path and relay path are both proven under real cross-network conditions.
 138: 
 139: ## 3A. The One Hardened Path Principle (MANDATORY)
 140: 
 141: **Core Philosophy:** Every security-sensitive operation has EXACTLY ONE implementation path. That path is hardened, tested, and enforced at runtime. No legacy branches, no fallback modes, no "temporary" insecure alternatives.
 142: 
 143: ### 3A.1 What This Means in Practice
 144: 
 145: **✅ CORRECT: One Secure Path**
 146: ```rust
 147: fn apply_endpoint_update(peer: PeerId, endpoint: SocketAddr) -> Result<()> {
 148:     // STEP 1: Verify signed traversal bundle (MANDATORY, NO BYPASS)
 149:     let traversal = self.verify_signed_traversal(peer)?;
 150:     
 151:     // STEP 2: Verify endpoint in candidate set (MANDATORY, NO BYPASS)
 152:     if !traversal.candidates.contains(&endpoint) {
 153:         return Err(Error::UnauthorizedEndpoint);
 154:     }
 155:     
 156:     // STEP 3: Apply to backend (ONLY path)
 157:     self.backend.set_peer_endpoint(peer, endpoint)?;
 158:     Ok(())
 159: }
 160: ```
 161: 
 162: **❌ FORBIDDEN: Multiple Paths / Legacy Branches**
 163: ```rust
 164: fn apply_endpoint_update(peer: PeerId, endpoint: SocketAddr) -> Result<()> {
 165:     // WRONG: Has fallback to weaker path
 166:     if let Some(traversal) = self.try_verify_signed_traversal(peer) {
 167:         // Modern secure path
 168:         if traversal.candidates.contains(&endpoint) {
 169:             self.backend.set_peer_endpoint(peer, endpoint)?;
 170:         }
 171:     } else if self.config.legacy_mode {  // ❌ FORBIDDEN
 172:         // "Legacy" unsecured path - NEVER DO THIS
 173:         warn!("Using legacy endpoint update");
 174:         self.backend.set_peer_endpoint(peer, endpoint)?;
 175:     }
 176:     Ok(())
 177: }
 178: ```
 179: 
 180: ### 3A.2 Mandatory Enforcement Rules
 181: 
 182: **RULE 1: No Runtime Branch Selection for Security-Critical Operations**
 183: 
 184: Security-critical operations include:
 185: - Endpoint mutation (direct/relay path changes)
 186: - Route installation (exit-node, LAN access, bypass routes)
 187: - DNS configuration (managed zone, fail-closed mode)
 188: - Firewall rule management (kill-switch, ACL enforcement)
 189: - Key material handling (generation, storage, loading, zeroization)
 190: - Trust state verification (signature checks, freshness, anti-replay)
 191: - Privileged helper invocation (argv construction, validation)
 192: 
 193: For these operations:
 194: - ✅ ONE hardened implementation
 195: - ❌ NO `if legacy_mode` branches
 196: - ❌ NO `if feature_flag_enabled` for security controls
 197: - ❌ NO `try_secure_path().or_else(|| insecure_fallback())`
 198: 
 199: **RULE 2: Migration Strategy Must Remove Old Paths**
 200: 
 201: When migrating from less secure to more secure implementation:
 202: 
 203: ```rust
 204: // WRONG: Keeps both paths
 205: fn apply_route(route: IpNet) -> Result<()> {
 206:     if self.config.use_new_route_engine {
 207:         self.new_signed_route_engine.apply(route)  // Secure
 208:     } else {
 209:         self.old_shell_route_engine.apply(route)   // ❌ Insecure, but still present
 210:     }
 211: }
 212: 
 213: // CORRECT: Old path removed, only secure path exists
 214: fn apply_route(route: IpNet) -> Result<()> {
 215:     // Old shell-based implementation has been DELETED
 216:     // Only signed route engine exists
 217:     self.signed_route_engine.apply(route)
 218: }
 219: ```
 220: 
 221: **Migration Process:**
 222: 1. Implement new secure path with tests
 223: 2. Verify new path meets all security requirements
 224: 3. Add migration gate that enforces new path usage
 225: 4. **DELETE old implementation** (not just deprecate)
 226: 5. Remove any configuration flags that selected old path
 227: 
 228: **RULE 3: Feature Flags for Capability, NOT Security**
 229: 
 230: ```rust
 231: // ✅ CORRECT: Feature flag for capability
 232: if self.config.enable_relay {
 233:     // Relay is a feature - can be enabled/disabled
 234:     self.attempt_relay_connection(peer)?;
 235: }
 236: 
 237: // ❌ FORBIDDEN: Feature flag for security control
 238: if self.config.enforce_signed_traversal {  // ❌ NO!
 239:     // Security controls are NOT optional
 240:     self.verify_signature()?;
 241: }
 242: ```
 243: 
 244: **Security controls are ALWAYS enforced, never behind feature flags.**
 245: 
 246: **RULE 4: No Graceful Degradation for Security**
 247: 
 248: ```rust
 249: // ❌ FORBIDDEN: Graceful degradation
 250: fn establish_connection(peer: PeerId) -> Result<Connection> {
 251:     if let Ok(conn) = self.try_secure_connection(peer) {
 252:         return Ok(conn);
 253:     }
 254:     // WRONG: Falls back to less secure
 255:     warn!("Falling back to insecure connection");
 256:     self.insecure_connection(peer)
 257: }
 258: 
 259: // ✅ CORRECT: Fail closed
 260: fn establish_connection(peer: PeerId) -> Result<Connection> {
 261:     // Either secure connection succeeds, or we fail
 262:     self.secure_connection(peer)
 263:     // No fallback, no degradation
 264: }
 265: ```
 266: 
 267: ### 3A.3 Code Review Rejection Criteria
 268: 
 269: Any pull request MUST be rejected if it:
 270: 
 271: 1. **Adds a second implementation path** for security-critical operations
 272: 2. **Adds `if legacy_mode` or `if insecure_mode`** branches
 273: 3. **Weakens existing security checks** to improve compatibility
 274: 4. **Adds optional security enforcement** via feature flags
 275: 5. **Implements "temporary" bypass** for debugging/testing that could reach production
 276: 6. **Adds graceful degradation** that falls back to weaker security
 277: 
 278: **Code Review Checklist:**
 279: - [ ] Does this PR add a new code path for an existing security-critical operation?
 280:   - If YES → Reject unless old path is deleted in same PR
 281: - [ ] Does this PR add a feature flag that disables security enforcement?
 282:   - If YES → Reject unconditionally
 283: - [ ] Does this PR add error recovery that bypasses security checks?
 284:   - If YES → Reject unless it fails closed
 285: - [ ] Does this PR keep deprecated/legacy security code "just in case"?
 286:   - If YES → Reject, require deletion
 287: 
 288: ### 3A.4 Runtime Enforcement
 289: 
 290: The daemon MUST enforce one-path at runtime:
 291: 
 292: ```rust
 293: // Example: Runtime assertion that no legacy branches exist
 294: #[cfg(test)]
 295: mod one_path_verification {
 296:     #[test]
 297:     fn no_legacy_endpoint_mutation_path() {
 298:         // Verify only one code path exists for endpoint mutation
 299:         let config = Config::default();
 300:         
 301:         // There should be NO configuration option to enable legacy behavior
 302:         assert!(!config.has_field("legacy_endpoint_mode"));
 303:         assert!(!config.has_field("insecure_mode"));
 304:         assert!(!config.has_field("bypass_signature_checks"));
 305:     }
 306:     
 307:     #[test]
 308:     fn all_security_controls_mandatory() {
 309:         let daemon = Daemon::new_test_instance();
 310:         
 311:         // Security controls CANNOT be disabled
 312:         assert!(daemon.signature_verification_enabled());  // Must be true
 313:         assert!(daemon.replay_protection_enabled());       // Must be true
 314:         assert!(daemon.fail_closed_mode_active());         // Must be true
 315:         
 316:         // These should not even be functions - they should be const true
 317:     }
 318: }
 319: ```
 320: 
 321: ### 3A.5 Examples: One Hardened Path Applied
 322: 
 323: **Endpoint Mutation:**
 324: - ❌ OLD: Unsigned endpoint changes allowed "for debugging"
 325: - ✅ NEW: ONLY signed traversal bundles trigger endpoint changes
 326: - 🗑️ DELETED: Debug mode that bypassed signature checks
 327: 
 328: **Route Installation:**
 329: - ❌ OLD: Shell script that parsed user input with `sh -c`
 330: - ✅ NEW: Rust argv array builder with strict validation
 331: - 🗑️ DELETED: Shell-based route management entirely
 332: 
 333: **DNS Configuration:**
 334: - ❌ OLD: Falls back to system DNS if managed DNS unavailable
 335: - ✅ NEW: Fails closed with SERVFAIL if managed DNS state invalid
 336: - 🗑️ DELETED: System DNS fallback code path
 337: 
 338: **Relay Authentication:**
 339: - ❌ OLD: Variable-time string comparison
 340: - ✅ NEW: Constant-time HMAC verification only
 341: - 🗑️ DELETED: Any non-constant-time comparison code
 342: 
 343: **Key Storage:**
 344: - ❌ OLD: Plaintext key file as fallback if keychain unavailable
 345: - ✅ NEW: OS keychain or encrypted file with startup permission check
 346: - 🗑️ DELETED: Plaintext fallback code
 347: 
 348: ### 3A.6 Verification: Proving One Path
 349: 
 350: Every security-critical module MUST have these tests:
 351: 
 352: ```rust
 353: #[cfg(test)]
 354: mod one_path_verification_tests {
 355:     use super::*;
 356: 
 357:     #[test]
 358:     fn only_one_endpoint_mutation_function() {
 359:         // Use reflection/compile-time checks to verify
 360:         // only ONE public function exists for endpoint mutation
 361:         let module = std::module_path!();
 362:         let endpoint_mutation_fns = get_public_functions_matching(
 363:             module,
 364:             "endpoint|peer_endpoint|set_peer"
 365:         );
 366:         
 367:         // Should be exactly ONE function
 368:         assert_eq!(endpoint_mutation_fns.len(), 1,
 369:             "Found multiple endpoint mutation paths: {:?}",
 370:             endpoint_mutation_fns
 371:         );
 372:     }
 373:     
 374:     #[test]
 375:     fn no_config_flags_for_security() {
 376:         let config_schema = Config::schema();
 377:         
 378:         // These fields should NOT exist
 379:         assert!(!config_schema.has_field("insecure_mode"));
 380:         assert!(!config_schema.has_field("skip_signature_verification"));
 381:         assert!(!config_schema.has_field("allow_unsigned_endpoints"));
 382:         assert!(!config_schema.has_field("legacy_route_engine"));
 383:     }
 384:     
 385:     #[test]
 386:     fn security_functions_have_no_optional_behavior() {
 387:         // verify_signature() should not take "skip_if_unavailable" parameter
 388:         // apply_route() should not take "fallback_to_shell" parameter
 389:         // etc.
 390:         
 391:         // This is verified at compile time by function signatures
 392:     }
 393: }
 394: ```
 395: 
 396: ### 3A.7 Benefits of One Hardened Path
 397: 
 398: 1. **Reduced Attack Surface:** No legacy code paths to exploit
 399: 2. **Simplified Auditing:** Only one path to review and verify
 400: 3. **Easier Testing:** No combinatorial explosion of path combinations
 401: 4. **Clearer Reasoning:** Behavior is deterministic and predictable
 402: 5. **No Accidental Bypass:** Cannot accidentally fall back to insecure path
 403: 6. **Better Performance:** No runtime checks for which path to use
 404: 7. **Confident Deployment:** No "what if legacy mode is still enabled?" worries
 405: 
 406: ### 3A.8 Exception: Crypto Agility (Planned, Future)
 407: 
 408: The ONE exception to one-path rule is cryptographic agility for algorithm migration:
 409: 
 410: ```rust
 411: // ALLOWED: Multiple crypto algorithms for migration
 412: enum CipherSuite {
 413:     ChaCha20Poly1305,  // Current
 414:     AesGcm256,         // Future post-quantum hybrid
 415: }
 416: 
 417: // BUT: Only ONE algorithm active per session
 418: // AND: Downgrade attacks prevented by protocol negotiation
 419: // AND: Weak algorithms removed after migration complete
 420: ```
 421: 
 422: This is acceptable because:
 423: - Crypto algorithms need to be upgraded over time
 424: - Each algorithm is still fully secure (no "weak" option)
 425: - Migration is protocol-negotiated, not runtime-configurable
 426: - Old algorithms are DELETED after migration period
 427: 
 428: **This is NOT an excuse for:**
 429: - ❌ Having both "secure" and "insecure" mode
 430: - ❌ Allowing downgrade attacks
 431: - ❌ Keeping deprecated crypto "just in case"
 432:

 462: ## 5. Complete Encryption Architecture
 463: 
 464: This section defines the **complete end-to-end encryption model** for all cross-network traffic. Every byte transmitted between Rustynet nodes across the Internet must be protected according to this specification.
 465: 
 466: ### 5.1 Encryption Layer Model
 467: 
 468: Rustynet employs a **defense-in-depth encryption architecture** with three independent protection layers:
 469: 
 470: ```
 471: ┌───┐
 472: │ Layer 3: Application Payload (User Data)                       │
 473: │   - User's actual network traffic (TCP/UDP/ICMP)               │
 474: │   - DNS queries                                                 │
 475: │   - Already protected by end-application TLS where applicable   │
 476: └───┘
 477:                               ▼
 478: ┌───┐
 479: │ Layer 2: WireGuard Tunnel Encryption (MANDATORY, ALWAYS ON)    │
 480: │   Protocol: WireGuard (RFC-draft, Noise Protocol Framework)    │
 481: │   Cipher: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 8439)                    │
 482: │   Key Exchange: Curve25519 (RFC 7748)                          │
 483: │   Hash: BLAKE2s                                                 │
 484: │   Authentication: Per-packet AEAD tag                          │
 485: │   Anti-Replay: 64-bit counter-based                            │
 486: │   Perfect Forward Secrecy: Automatic key rotation every 2 min  │
 487: │   Confidentiality: 256-bit effective security                  │
 488: └───┘
 489:                               ▼
 490: ┌───┐
 491: │ Layer 1: Transport Path (Direct UDP OR Relay)                  │
 492: │   DIRECT PATH:                                                  │
 493: │     - Raw UDP packets containing WireGuard ciphertext           │
 494: │     - NAT traversal via STUN/ICE-like probing                  │
 495: │     - No additional encryption (WireGuard is sufficient)        │
 496: │                                                                 │
 497: │   RELAY PATH (when direct UDP fails):                          │
 498: │     - Nested encryption model (see Section 5.3)                │
 499: │     - Relay cannot decrypt Layer 2 (WireGuard) traffic         │
 500: │     - Relay-specific session encryption prevents correlation   │
 501: └───┘
 502: ```
 503: 
 504: ### 5.2 Direct Path Encryption (Peer-to-Peer)
 505: 
 506: **[ ] 5.2.1 WireGuard Protocol Enforcement**
 507: 
 508: When nodes communicate via direct UDP path:
 509: 
 510: 1. **Protocol:** WireGuard 1.0 specification (noise-ik-psk pattern)
 511: 2. **Implementation:** `rustynet-backend-wireguard` crate wraps kernel WireGuard or userspace wireguard-rs
 512: 3. **Cipher Suite:** ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (non-negotiable, no cipher downgrade)
 513: 4. **Key Material:**
 514:    - Static Curve25519 keypair per node (generated at enrollment, stored in OS keychain)
 515:    - Ephemeral session keys derived via Noise protocol handshake
 516:    - Pre-shared key (PSK) support for post-quantum hardening (OPTIONAL, future Phase 11)
 517: 5. **Handshake:**
 518:    - 1-RTT handshake using Noise_IK pattern
 519:    - Identity hiding: responder identity is encrypted
 520:    - No handshake amplification (protects against DDoS)
 521: 6. **Packet Protection:**
 522:    - Every packet authenticated with Poly1305 MAC (128-bit tag)
 523:    - Counter-based replay protection (64-bit counter, sliding window)
 524:    - Padding to conceal packet lengths (optional, configurable per-flow)
 525: 7. **Key Rotation:**
 526:    - Automatic session rekey every 2 minutes
 527:    - Automatic rekey after 2^64-1 packets (never reached in practice)
 528:    - Perfect forward secrecy: compromise of long-term key doesn't decrypt old sessions
 529: 
 530: **Security Properties:**
 531: - ✅ Confidentiality: AES-256 equivalent (ChaCha20 uses 256-bit keys)
 532: - ✅ Authenticity: Unforgeable MACs (Poly1305)
 533: - ✅ Integrity: AEAD prevents tampering
 534: - ✅ Anti-Replay: Sliding window prevents packet replay
 535: - ✅ Perfect Forward Secrecy: Session keys rotated, not derivable from static keys
 536: - ✅ Identity Privacy: Responder identity encrypted in handshake
 537: 
 538: **Verification Tests:**
 539: ```bash
 540: # Verify WireGuard encryption is always active on direct paths
 541: cargo test -p rustynetd phase10::tests::direct_path_requires_wireguard_handshake_success
 542: 
 543: # Verify no plaintext packets are ever sent
 544: cargo test -p rustynetd phase10::tests::direct_path_never_sends_cleartext
 545: 
 546: # Verify replay protection
 547: cargo test -p rustynetd phase10::tests::direct_path_rejects_replayed_packets
 548: ```
 549: 
 550: **[ ] 5.2.2 Key Distribution and Trust Model**
 551: 
 552: - **Key Generation:** Each node generates its own Curve25519 keypair at enrollment time
 553: - **Public Key Distribution:** Control plane distributes public keys via signed "assignment bundles"
 554: - **Trust Anchor:** Control plane's signing key is the root of trust
 555: - **Key Verification:** Nodes MUST verify signature on assignment bundle before accepting peer public keys
 556: - **No Key Escrow:** Control plane never sees private keys (zero-trust model)
 557: 
 558: **Implementation Location:**
 559: - Key generation: `crates/rustynet-crypto/src/keypair.rs`
 560: - Assignment bundle verification: `crates/rustynetd/src/assignment.rs`
 561: - Backend integration: `crates/rustynet-backend-wireguard/src/peer_config.rs`
 562: 
 563: **[ ] 5.2.3 Direct Path Endpoint Mutation Security**
 564: 
 565: Critical constraint: **Only signed traversal bundles may trigger endpoint changes.**
 566: 
 567: ```rust
 568: // Pseudocode enforcement pattern
 569: fn apply_endpoint_change(peer_id: NodeId, new_endpoint: SocketAddr) -> Result<()> {
 570:     // STEP 1: Require signed traversal bundle (MANDATORY)
 571:     let traversal = self.get_verified_traversal_bundle(peer_id)?
 572:         .ok_or(Error::NoSignedTraversal)?;
 573:     
 574:     // STEP 2: Verify signature and freshness
 575:     traversal.verify_signature(&self.control_plane_public_key)?;
 576:     traversal.verify_fresh(MAX_TRAVERSAL_AGE)?;
 577:     traversal.verify_nonce_not_replayed(&self.nonce_store)?;
 578:     
 579:     // STEP 3: Verify endpoint is in allowed candidate set
 580:     if !traversal.candidates.contains(&new_endpoint) {
 581:         return Err(Error::EndpointNotInCandidateSet);
 582:     }
 583:     
 584:     // STEP 4: Only now may we mutate backend
 585:     self.backend.update_peer_endpoint(peer_id, new_endpoint)?;
 586:     
 587:     // STEP 5: Record nonce to prevent replay
 588:     self.nonce_store.record_used(traversal.nonce)?;
 589:     
 590:     Ok(())
 591: }
 592: ```
 593: 
 594: **Attack Mitigations:**
 595: - **Unsigned endpoint injection:** Blocked by signature verification
 596: - **Replay attacks:** Blocked by nonce tracking
 597: - **Rollback attacks:** Blocked by watermark/epoch counters
 598: - **Stale traversal:** Blocked by TTL enforcement (MAX_TRAVERSAL_AGE = 60 seconds)
 599: 
 600: **Verification Tests:**
 601: ```bash
 602: # Verify unsigned endpoint changes are rejected
 603: cargo test -p rustynetd traversal::tests::unsigned_endpoint_mutation_rejected
 604: 
 605: # Verify replay protection
 606: cargo test -p rustynetd traversal::tests::replayed_traversal_bundle_rejected
 607: 
 608: # Verify stale traversal rejection
 609: cargo test -p rustynetd traversal::tests::stale_traversal_bundle_rejected
 610: ```
 611: 
 612: ### 5.3 Relay Path Encryption (Zero-Trust Relay Model)
 613: 
 614: **[ ] 5.3.1 Architectural Principle: Zero-Knowledge Relay**
 615: 
 616: When direct UDP is impossible (hard NAT, firewall), Rustynet uses encrypted relay:
 617: 
 618: **Core Principle:** Relay infrastructure is **zero-trust**. Relay operators:
 619: - ❌ Cannot decrypt WireGuard traffic (Layer 2 remains encrypted)
 620: - ❌ Cannot see user application data
 621: - ❌ Cannot correlate flows beyond session lifetime
 622: - ✅ Can only forward opaque ciphertext between authenticated sessions
 623: 
 624: **Encryption Model: Nested Protection**
 625: 
 626: ```
 627: User Data
 628:    └─> WireGuard Encrypted (ChaCha20-Poly1305)
 629:        └─> Relay Session Encrypted (TLS 1.3 or Noise)
 630:            └─> TCP/QUIC Transport
 631:                └─> Internet
 632: ```
 633: 
 634: **Why Nested?**
 635: 1. **Defense in Depth:** Even if relay is compromised, WireGuard layer protects data
 636: 2. **Traffic Analysis Resistance:** Relay-layer encryption prevents correlation by external observers
 637: 3. **Session Isolation:** Relay session keys are ephemeral, distinct from WireGuard keys
 638: 
 639: **[ ] 5.3.2 Relay Session Establishment Protocol**
 640: 
 641: When a node needs relay service:
 642: 
 643: 1. **Client → Control Plane:** Request relay allocation
 644:    ```json
 645:    {
 646:      "request_type": "relay_allocation",
 647:      "source_node_id": "node-abc123",
 648:      "target_node_id": "node-xyz789",
 649:      "signed_request": "<signature over (timestamp, node_ids, nonce)>"
 650:    }
 651:    ```
 652: 
 653: 2. **Control Plane → Client:** Return signed relay credential
 654:    ```json
 655:    {
 656:      "relay_url": "relay.rustynet.example.com:443",
 657:      "relay_public_key": "<relay's X25519 public key>",
 658:      "session_token": "<opaque session identifier>",
 659:      "session_auth_key": "<HMAC key for session authentication>",
 660:      "ttl": 300,
 661:      "signed_bundle": "<control plane signature over entire payload>"
 662:    }
 663:    ```
 664: 
 665: 3. **Client → Relay:** Establish encrypted session
 666:    - Protocol: TLS 1.3 with relay's certificate (pinned public key)
 667:    - OR: Noise_XX handshake for more control
 668:    - Session bound to `session_token`
 669:    - Every relay packet includes `HMAC-SHA256(session_auth_key, packet_data)` for authentication
 670: 
 671: 4. **Relay Behavior:**
 672:    - Relay maintains **two** concurrent encrypted sessions (client A ↔ relay ↔ client B)
 673:    - Relay decrypts relay-layer envelope, extracts session_token, forwards to peer session
 674:    - Relay **never** decrypts WireGuard layer (doesn't have keys)
 675:    - Relay enforces rate limits, abuse detection, and session TTL
 676: 
 677: **[ ] 5.3.3 Relay Transport Protocol Specification**
 678: 
 679: **Option A: TLS 1.3-Based Relay (Recommended for MVP)**
 680: 
 681: ```
 682: Client                    Relay                    Target
 683:   |                         |                         |
 684:   |--- TLS 1.3 Handshake -->|                         |
 685:   |<-- Server Certificate --|                         |
 686:   |    (pin relay pubkey)   |                         |
 687:   |                         |--- TLS 1.3 Handshake -->|
 688:   |                         |<-- Server Certificate --|
 689:   |                         |                         |
 690:   |-- Relay Frame --------->|                         |
 691:   |   [session_token]       |                         |
 692:   |   [HMAC tag]            |                         |
 693:   |   [WireGuard ciphertext]|-- Relay Frame --------->|
 694:   |                         |   [WireGuard ciphertext]|
 695: ```
 696: 
 697: **Relay Frame Format:**
 698: ```
 699: +----------------+----------------+------------------+-----------------+
 700: | session_token  | sequence_num   | hmac_sha256      | wireguard_data  |
 701: |   (16 bytes)   |   (8 bytes)    |   (32 bytes)     | (variable)      |
 702: +----------------+----------------+------------------+-----------------+
 703: ```
 704: 
 705: - **session_token:** Opaque identifier from control plane
 706: - **sequence_num:** Anti-replay counter (per-session)
 707: - **hmac_sha256:** HMAC-SHA256(session_auth_key, session_token || sequence_num || wireguard_data)
 708: - **wireguard_data:** Encrypted WireGuard packet (relay cannot decrypt)
 709: 
 710: **Security Properties:**
 711: - ✅ Confidentiality: TLS 1.3 encryption (AES-128-GCM or ChaCha20-Poly1305)
 712: - ✅ Relay Authentication: Certificate pinning prevents MitM
 713: - ✅ Frame Authentication: HMAC prevents tampering
 714: - ✅ Anti-Replay: Sequence numbers + HMAC binding
 715: - ✅ Session Isolation: Each relay session has unique auth keys
 716: 
 717: **Constant-Time Comparison Requirement:**
 718: ```rust
 719: // MANDATORY: Prevents timing attacks on session_token validation
 720: fn verify_hmac(computed: &[u8; 32], provided: &[u8; 32]) -> bool {
 721:     use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
 722:     computed.ct_eq(provided).into()
 723: }
 724: ```
 725: 
 726: **Implementation References:**
 727: - Relay server: `crates/rustynet-relay/src/server.rs`
 728: - Relay client: `crates/rustynetd/src/relay_client.rs`
 729: - HMAC validation: `crates/rustynet-crypto/src/hmac.rs`
 730: 
 731: **Verification Tests:**
 732: ```bash
 733: # Verify relay cannot decrypt WireGuard layer
 734: cargo test -p rustynet-relay relay::tests::relay_cannot_decrypt_payload
 735: 
 736: # Verify constant-time HMAC comparison
 737: cargo test -p rustynet-crypto hmac::tests::hmac_verification_constant_time
 738: 
 739: # Verify anti-replay protection
 740: cargo test -p rustynet-relay relay::tests::replayed_sequence_rejected
 741: ```
 742: 
 743: **[ ] 5.3.4 Relay Abuse Protections**
 744: 
 745: To prevent relay from becoming an attack vector:
 746: 
 747: 1. **Rate Limiting:**
 748:    - Per-session: 10 MB/s sustained, 50 MB/s burst
 749:    - Per-source-IP: 50 new sessions/minute
 750:    - Global: Configurable capacity ceiling
 751: 
 752: 2. **Session Lifecycle:**
 753:    - Max TTL: 300 seconds (5 minutes)
 754:    - Idle timeout: 60 seconds without traffic
 755:    - Automatic cleanup on expiry
 756: 
 757: 3. **Authentication Failures:**
 758:    - 3 consecutive HMAC failures → session terminated
 759:    - Source IP banned for 60 seconds after 10 failed authentications/minute
 760: 
 761: 4. **Resource Bounds:**
 762:    - Bounded session table (max 10,000 concurrent sessions)
 763:    - Bounded queue depth per session (max 100 packets)
 764:    - Memory limits enforced via bounded allocators
 765: 
 766: **Implementation:** `crates/rustynet-relay/src/abuse_prevention.rs`
 767: 
 768: ### 5.4 Encryption Continuity During Path Transitions
 769: 
 770: **[ ] 5.4.1 Direct ↔ Relay Failover Without Re-keying**
 771: 
 772: Critical security property: **WireGuard session keys NEVER change during path transitions.**
 773: 
 774: ```
 775: Time:  T0              T1              T2              T3
 776:        |               |               |               |
 777: Path:  Direct UDP ---> Relay --------> Direct UDP
 778:        |               ↑               ↑
 779: Keys:  [WG Session 1]  |               |
 780:                        [same keys]     [same keys]
 781:                        
 782: Effect: User experiences path change, but encryption is continuous
 783: ```
 784: 
 785: **Why This Matters:**
 786: - No brief window of unencrypted traffic during failover
 787: - No re-handshake latency
 788: - No risk of handshake failure during network instability
 789: 
 790: **Implementation Approach:**
 791: 1. WireGuard session established once during initial peer connection
 792: 2. Traversal controller changes **transport path only** (UDP socket vs relay connection)
 793: 3. WireGuard backend continues using same session keys regardless of transport
 794: 
 795: **Code Path:**
 796: ```rust
 797: // Pseudocode
 798: fn transition_to_relay(peer_id: NodeId) -> Result<()> {
 799:     // Get current WireGuard session state (DON'T destroy it)
 800:     let wg_session = self.backend.get_session(peer_id)?;
 801:     
 802:     // Establish relay connection
 803:     let relay_conn = self.relay_client.connect(peer_id).await?;
 804:     
 805:     // Redirect WireGuard packets to relay transport
 806:     self.backend.set_transport(peer_id, Transport::Relay(relay_conn))?;
 807:     
 808:     // WireGuard session continues unchanged
 809:     // No re-handshake, no key rotation
 810:     Ok(())
 811: }
 812: ```
 813: 
 814: **Verification Tests:**
 815: ```bash
 816: # Verify no re-handshake during failover
 817: cargo test -p rustynetd phase10::tests::direct_to_relay_transition_preserves_session
 818: 
 819: # Verify no packet loss window
 820: cargo test -p rustynetd phase10::tests::failover_continuous_traffic_no_gap
 821: 
 822: # Verify same session keys before/after
 823: cargo test -p rustynetd phase10::tests::failover_session_key_unchanged
 824: ```
 825: 
 826: **[ ] 5.4.2 Path Transition Security Invariants**
 827: 
 828: During any path transition (direct→relay, relay→direct, relay A→relay B):
 829: 
 830: 1. **Encryption MUST remain active** - no cleartext packets ever sent
 831: 2. **ACL enforcement MUST remain active** - policy not bypassed during transition
 832: 3. **DNS fail-closed MUST remain active** - no DNS leaks during transition
 833: 4. **Kill-switch MUST remain active** - no underlay bypass during transition
 834: 5. **Traversal state MUST be signed** - no unsigned path changes
 835: 
 836: **Live Lab Test:**
 837: ```bash
 838: # TunnelCrack-style bypass test during transition
 839: scripts/e2e/live_linux_transition_leak_test.sh
 840: ```
 841: 
 842: ### 5.5 Cryptographic Parameter Choices and Rationale
 843: 
 844: **[ ] 5.5.1 Algorithm Selection**
 845: 
 846: | Component | Algorithm | Rationale |
 847: |-----------|-----------|-----------|
 848: | Symmetric Encryption | ChaCha20 | Faster than AES on ARM, constant-time, no timing side-channels |
 849: | Authentication | Poly1305 | Fast, provably secure, pairs with ChaCha20 |
 850: | Key Exchange | Curve25519 | Industry standard, fast, side-channel resistant |
 851: | Hash Function | BLAKE2s | Faster than SHA-256, cryptographically secure |
 852: | Signature (Control Plane) | Ed25519 | Small keys, fast verification, deterministic |
 853: 
 854: **No Custom Cryptography:** All algorithms are **proven, standardized, audited implementations**:
 855: - WireGuard: Extensively audited, formally verified in some implementations
 856: - ChaCha20-Poly1305: RFC 8439, IETF standard
 857: - Curve25519: RFC 7748, widely deployed (Signal, TLS 1.3)
 858: - Ed25519: RFC 8032, NIST recommended
 859: 
 860: **[ ] 5.5.2 Key Lengths and Security Levels**
 861: 
 862: | Key Type | Length | Security Level | Post-Quantum Resistant? |
 863: |----------|--------|----------------|-------------------------|
 864: | WireGuard Static Key | 256 bits | 128-bit security | ❌ No (Curve25519) |
 865: | WireGuard Session Key | 256 bits | 128-bit security | ❌ No |
 866: | Control Plane Signing Key | 256 bits | 128-bit security | ❌ No (Ed25519) |
 867: | Relay Session Auth Key | 256 bits | 128-bit security | ✅ Symmetric |
 868: | PSK (Optional) | 256 bits | 256-bit security | ✅ Yes |
 869: 
 870: **Post-Quantum Strategy:**
 871: - Current: Pre-shared key (PSK) mode adds post-quantum protection (future Phase 11)
 872: - Future: Hybrid key exchange (Curve25519 + Kyber) when WireGuard spec stabilizes
 873: 
 874: **[ ] 5.5.3 Cryptographic Implementation Hygiene**
 875: 
 876: **MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS:**
 877: 
 878: 1. **Memory Zeroization:**
 879:    ```rust
 880:    use zeroize::{Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop};
 881:    
 882:    #[derive(Zeroize, ZeroizeOnDrop)]
 883:    struct PrivateKey([u8; 32]);
 884:    
 885:    // Automatically zeroed when dropped
 886:    ```
 887: 
 888: 2. **Constant-Time Comparison:**
 889:    ```rust
 890:    use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
 891:    
 892:    fn compare_macs(a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> bool {
 893:        a.ct_eq(b).into()
 894:    }
 895:    ```
 896: 
 897: 3. **No Key Logging:**
 898:    ```rust
 899:    // NEVER do this
 900:    println!("Private key: {:?}", private_key); // ❌ FORBIDDEN
 901:    
 902:    // Use redacted debug
 903:    #[derive(Debug)]
 904:    struct PrivateKey {
 905:        #[debug("<redacted>")]
 906:        key: [u8; 32]
 907:    }
 908:    ```
 909: 
 910: 4. **Secure Random Number Generation:**
 911:    ```rust
 912:    use rand::rngs::OsRng;
 913:    
 914:    let mut key = [0u8; 32];
 915:    OsRng.fill_bytes(&mut key); // Use OS entropy
 916:    ```
 917: 
 918: **Verification Tests:**
 919: ```bash
 920: # Verify no secret logging
 921: cargo test -p rustynet-control operations::tests::structured_logger_never_writes_cleartext_secrets
 922: 
 923: # Verify zeroization
 924: cargo test -p rustynet-crypto keypair::tests::private_key_zeroized_on_drop
 925: 
 926: # Verify constant-time operations
 927: cargo test -p rustynet-crypto constant_time::tests::no_timing_leaks
 928: ```
 929: 
 930: ### 5.6 Control Plane Transport Security
 931: 
 932: **[ ] 5.6.1 TLS 1.3 Enforcement**
 933: 
 934: All communication between nodes and control plane MUST use TLS 1.3:
 935: 
 936: - **Minimum Version:** TLS 1.3 (no fallback to 1.2 or earlier)
 937: - **Cipher Suites:** 
 938:   - `TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` (preferred)
 939:   - `TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` (acceptable)
 940: - **Certificate Validation:** Full chain validation + hostname verification
 941: - **Certificate Pinning:** Optional for high-security deployments
 942: 
 943: **Why TLS 1.3 Only:**
 944: - ✅ Eliminates downgrade attacks
 945: - ✅ Mandatory perfect forward secrecy
 946: - ✅ Encrypts more handshake data
 947: - ✅ Faster handshake (1-RTT)
 948: 
 949: **[ ] 5.6.2 Signed State Bundle Verification**
 950: 
 951: Every control plane response (assignment, traversal, DNS, trust) MUST be signed:
 952: 
 953: ```rust
 954: struct SignedBundle {
 955:     payload: Vec<u8>,           // JSON-serialized state
 956:     signature: [u8; 64],        // Ed25519 signature
 957:     signing_key_id: String,     // Which key signed this
 958:     timestamp: u64,             // Unix timestamp
 959:     nonce: [u8; 16],            // Anti-replay nonce
 960: }
 961: 
 962: fn verify_bundle(bundle: &SignedBundle, trusted_key: &Ed25519PublicKey) -> Result<()> {
 963:     // 1. Verify signature
 964:     let message = [&bundle.payload, &bundle.timestamp.to_le_bytes(), &bundle.nonce].concat();
 965:     trusted_key.verify(&message, &bundle.signature)?;
 966:     
 967:     // 2. Verify freshness (max 60 seconds old)
 968:     if SystemTime::now() - bundle.timestamp > Duration::from_secs(60) {
 969:         return Err(Error::Stale);
 970:     }
 971:     
 972:     // 3. Verify nonce not replayed
 973:     if nonce_store.seen(&bundle.nonce)? {
 974:         return Err(Error::Replay);
 975:     }
 976:     nonce_store.record(&bundle.nonce)?;
 977:     
 978:     Ok(())
 979: }
 980: ```
 981: 
 982: **Anti-Replay Strategy:**
 983: - Nonce store: In-memory LRU cache (last 10,000 nonces)
 984: - Persistence: Write-ahead log for crash recovery
 985: - Cleanup: Automatic expiry after 120 seconds (2x max bundle age)
 986: 
 987: ## 6. Known Vulnerability Classes and Mitigations
 988: 
 989: This section catalogs **known attacks against VPN systems** and Rustynet's specific defenses. This is **MANDATORY reading** before implementing any cross-network feature.
 990: 
 991: ### 6.1 TunnelCrack (2023) - LocalNet and ServerIP Bypass
 992: 
 993: **Vulnerability:** Attackers create bypass routes that leak traffic outside VPN tunnel.
 994: 
 995: **Attack Vectors:**
 996: 1. **LocalNet Attack:** Attacker controls local router, injects routes for victim's destination IPs via local gateway
 997: 2. **ServerIP Attack:** Traffic to VPN server IP itself bypasses tunnel, attacker observes DNS/control traffic
 998: 
 999: **Rustynet Mitigations:**
1000: 
1001: **[ ] 6.1.1 Strict Route Ownership**
1002: - ALL routes managed by Rustynet MUST be explicitly added via signed route advertisements
1003: - No automatic "trust local gateway" behavior
1004: - Operating system bypass routes ONLY for narrow control-plane IPs (exact /32 or /128)
1005: 
1006: **Implementation:**
1007: ```rust
1008: // crates/rustynetd/src/routing.rs
1009: fn apply_bypass_route(destination: IpAddr) -> Result<()> {
1010:     // ONLY allow /32 (IPv4) or /128 (IPv6) - NO subnet bypass
1011:     if !is_host_route(destination) {
1012:         return Err(Error::BroadBypassNotAllowed);
1013:     }
1014:     
1015:     // ONLY allow control plane IPs
1016:     if !self.control_plane_ips.contains(&destination) {
1017:         return Err(Error::UnauthorizedBypass);
1018:     }
1019:     
1020:     // Add route
1021:     self.route_table.add_bypass(destination)?;
1022:     Ok(())
1023: }
1024: ```
1025: 
1026: **Verification Tests:**
1027: ```bash
1028: # Verify broad bypasses rejected
1029: cargo test -p rustynetd routing::tests::subnet_bypass_rejected
1030: 
1031: # Live lab test
1032: scripts/e2e/live_linux_server_ip_bypass_test.sh
1033: ```
1034: 
1035: **[ ] 6.1.2 Network Namespace Isolation (Linux)**
1036: 
1037: On Linux, use network namespaces for strongest isolation:
1038: - Rustynet interface in separate namespace
1039: - Only authorized sockets can access VPN namespace
1040: - Physical interface isolated from VPN namespace
1041: 
1042: **Future Enhancement:** Phase 11 namespace hardening
1043: 
1044: ### 6.2 TunnelVision (CVE-2024-3661) - DHCP Option 121 Injection
1045: 
1046: **Vulnerability:** Attacker on local network sends DHCP option 121 (classless static routes) that bypass VPN.
1047: 
1048: **Attack Vector:**
1049: ```
1050: Attacker DHCP server → Client
1051:   Option 121: 0.0.0.0/0 via attacker_gateway
1052:   
1053: Result: All traffic bypasses VPN, routes via attacker's gateway
1054: ```
1055: 
1056: **Rustynet Mitigations:**
1057: 
1058: **[ ] 6.2.1 Kill-Switch Route Lock**
1059: 
1060: When VPN is active in protected mode:
1061: 1. Install iptables/nftables rules BEFORE configuring interface
1062: 2. Default DENY all traffic except through VPN interface
1063: 3. DHCP changes cannot override iptables rules
1064: 
1065: **Implementation:**
1066: ```rust
1067: // crates/rustynetd/src/firewall.rs
1068: fn enable_killswitch(vpn_interface: &str) -> Result<()> {
1069:     // 1. Block all output by default
1070:     nftables::add_rule("output", "policy drop")?;
1071:     
1072:     // 2. Allow only through VPN interface
1073:     nftables::add_rule("output", &format!("oifname {} accept", vpn_interface))?;
1074:     
1075:     // 3. Allow localhost
1076:     nftables::add_rule("output", "oifname lo accept")?;
1077:     
1078:     // 4. Allow DHCP/DNS for bootstrap (narrow)
1079:     nftables::add_rule("output", "udp dport 67-68 accept")?;
1080:     
1081:     Ok(())
1082: }
1083: ```
1084: 
1085: **Verification Tests:**
1086: ```bash
1087: # Verify DHCP option 121 cannot bypass
1088: cargo test -p rustynetd dataplane::tests::dhcp_option_121_bypass_blocked
1089: 
1090: # Live lab test with malicious DHCP server
1091: scripts/e2e/live_linux_dhcp_injection_test.sh
1092: ```
1093: 
1094: **[ ] 6.2.2 Network Namespace Alternative (Strongest)**
1095: 
1096: - Place WireGuard interface in dedicated network namespace
1097: - DHCP runs in default namespace, cannot affect VPN namespace
1098: - Physical isolation prevents option 121 from affecting VPN
1099: 
1100: ### 6.3 Tailscale TS-2025-008 - Missing State Fail-Open
1101: 
1102: **Vulnerability:** When trust state files are missing (deleted, corrupted, unmounted), system fails OPEN instead of fail-closed.
1103: 
1104: **Attack Vector:**
1105: ```
1106: 1. Attacker compromises system
1107: 2. Attacker deletes /var/lib/tailscale/tailnet-lock.json
1108: 3. System boots without trust verification
1109: 4. Attacker can now push malicious config
1110: ```
1111: 
1112: **Rustynet Mitigations:**
1113: 
1114: **[ ] 6.3.1 Mandatory Trust State Verification**
1115: 
1116: ```rust
1117: // crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs
1118: fn initialize_runtime() -> Result<RuntimeState> {
1119:     // 1. Load trust state (signed membership/assignment)
1120:     let trust_state = match TrustState::load()? {
1121:         Some(state) => state,
1122:         None => {
1123:             // CRITICAL: Missing state is FAIL-CLOSED
1124:             warn!("Trust state missing - entering restricted safe mode");
1125:             return Ok(RuntimeState::RestrictedSafeMode);
1126:         }
1127:     };
1128:     
1129:     // 2. Verify signature and freshness
1130:     trust_state.verify_signature(&self.control_plane_key)?;
1131:     trust_state.verify_not_stale(MAX_TRUST_AGE)?;
1132:     
1133:     // 3. Only now allow normal operation
1134:     Ok(RuntimeState::Normal(trust_state))
1135: }
1136: ```
1137: 
1138: **Verification Tests:**
1139: ```bash
1140: cargo test -p rustynetd daemon::tests::daemon_runtime_enters_restricted_safe_mode_without_trust_evidence
1141: ```
1142: 
1143: ### 6.4 Tailscale TS-2026-001 - Shell Injection to Root
1144: 
1145: **Vulnerability:** Passing unsanitized input to shell commands allows privilege escalation.
1146: 
1147: **Attack Vector:**
1148: ```bash
1149: # Vulnerable code (DON'T DO THIS)
1150: command = format!("ip route add {} via {}", user_input, gateway);
1151: system(command);  // ❌ Shell injection if user_input = "; rm -rf /"
1152: ```
1153: 
1154: **Rustynet Mitigations:**
1155: 
1156: **[ ] 6.4.1 Argv-Only Command Execution**
1157: 
1158: **MANDATORY RULE:** ALL privileged helper invocations MUST use argv arrays, NEVER shell construction.
1159: 
1160: ```rust
1161: // ✅ CORRECT
1162: fn add_route(destination: IpNet, gateway: IpAddr) -> Result<()> {
1163:     let output = Command::new("/sbin/ip")
1164:         .arg("route")
1165:         .arg("add")
1166:         .arg(destination.to_string())
1167:         .arg("via")
1168:         .arg(gateway.to_string())
1169:         .output()?;
1170:     
1171:     if !output.status.success() {
1172:         return Err(Error::CommandFailed);
1173:     }
1174:     Ok(())
1175: }
1176: 
1177: // ❌ FORBIDDEN
1178: fn add_route_wrong(destination: &str, gateway: &str) -> Result<()> {
1179:     let command = format!("ip route add {} via {}", destination, gateway);
1180:     system(&command)?;  // NEVER DO THIS
1181:     Ok(())
1182: }
1183: ```
1184: 
1185: **[ ] 6.4.2 Input Validation Schema**
1186: 
1187: ALL external inputs MUST be validated against strict schemas:
1188: 
1189: ```rust
1190: fn validate_cidr(input: &str) -> Result<IpNet> {
1191:     // Reject shell metacharacters
1192:     if input.contains(&[';', '&', '|', '$', '`', '\n', '\r']) {
1193:         return Err(Error::InvalidInput);
1194:     }
1195:     
1196:     // Parse as IP network (strict)
1197:     let net: IpNet = input.parse()
1198:         .map_err(|_| Error::InvalidCidr)?;
1199:     
1200:     Ok(net)
1201: }
1202: ```
1203: 
1204: **Verification Tests:**
1205: ```bash
1206: cargo test -p rustynetd privileged_helper::tests::fuzzgate_rejects_unknown_tokens_and_shell_metacharacters
1207: ```
1208: 
1209: ### 6.5 Tailscale TS-2024-005 - Exit Node Inbound Filtering Bypass
1210: 
1211: **Vulnerability:** Exit node forwards inbound internet traffic into mesh, not just outbound.
1212: 
1213: **Attack Vector:**
1214: ```
1215: 1. Client enables exit node
1216: 2. Attacker on internet sends packets to exit node's public IP
1217: 3. Packets forwarded into Rustynet mesh
1218: 4. Client receives unrequested traffic from internet
1219: ```
1220: 
1221: **Rustynet Mitigations:**
1222: 
1223: **[ ] 6.5.1 Strict Inbound Filtering on Exit Nodes**
1224: 
1225: ```rust
1226: // crates/rustynetd/src/exit_node.rs
1227: fn configure_exit_nat(interface: &str) -> Result<()> {
1228:     // 1. Enable forwarding
1229:     sysctl("net.ipv4.ip_forward", "1")?;
1230:     
1231:     // 2. NAT outbound only (SNAT)
1232:     nftables::add_rule("nat", "postrouting", 
1233:         &format!("oifname {} masquerade", interface))?;
1234:     
1235:     // 3. CRITICAL: Block inbound forwarding from internet
1236:     nftables::add_rule("filter", "forward",
1237:         &format!("iifname {} oifname rustynet-* drop", interface))?;
1238:     
1239:     // 4. Allow outbound forwarding from mesh to internet
1240:     nftables::add_rule("filter", "forward",
1241:         &format!("iifname rustynet-* oifname {} accept", interface))?;
1242:     
1243:     Ok(())
1244: }
1245: ```
1246: 
1247: **Verification Tests:**
1248: ```bash
1249: cargo test -p rustynetd phase10::tests::exit_node_blocks_inbound_internet_to_mesh
1250: 
1251: # Live lab: External host tries to reach mesh via exit node
1252: scripts/e2e/live_linux_exit_inbound_filter_test.sh
1253: ```
1254: 
1255: ### 6.6 WireGuard Endpoint Mobility Attack
1256: 
1257: **Vulnerability:** WireGuard accepts endpoint changes from any source IP (by design for NAT roaming).
1258: 
1259: **Attack Vector:**
1260: ```
1261: 1. Attacker observes WireGuard handshake (knows public keys)
1262: 2. Attacker sends spoofed handshake from attacker's IP
1263: 3. WireGuard changes endpoint to attacker's IP
1264: 4. Traffic now routes through attacker (MitM)
1265: ```
1266: 
1267: **Rustynet Mitigations:**
1268: 
1269: **[ ] 6.6.1 Signed Endpoint Hints Only**
1270: 
1271: Rustynet **adds an authorization layer on top of WireGuard:**
1272: 
1273: ```rust
1274: fn process_wireguard_handshake(peer_id: NodeId, source_ip: IpAddr) -> Result<()> {
1275:     // 1. WireGuard will accept handshake (we can't prevent this)
1276:     
1277:     // 2. BUT: Check if source_ip is in our signed candidate set
1278:     let traversal = self.get_verified_traversal(peer_id)?
1279:         .ok_or(Error::NoTraversal)?;
1280:     
1281:     if !traversal.candidates.contains(&source_ip) {
1282:         // 3. Endpoint changed to unauthorized IP - REJECT
1283:         warn!("Handshake from unauthorized endpoint: {}", source_ip);
1284:         
1285:         // 4. Restore last-known-good endpoint
1286:         self.backend.reset_endpoint(peer_id, traversal.last_verified_endpoint)?;
1287:         
1288:         return Err(Error::UnauthorizedEndpoint);
1289:     }
1290:     
1291:     // 5. Authorized endpoint - allow change
1292:     Ok(())
1293: }
1294: ```
1295: 
1296: **Detection:** Monitor WireGuard endpoint changes via netlink/status API
1297: 
1298: **Verification Tests:**
1299: ```bash
1300: # Live lab: Attacker sends handshake from unexpected IP
1301: scripts/e2e/live_linux_endpoint_hijack_test.sh
1302: ```
1303:

1327: ## 7. Non-Negotiable Security Invariants
1328: 
1329: These must hold throughout every phase:
1330: 
1331: 1. **[ ] One hardened path only for endpoint mutation.**
1332:    - `verified signed traversal state -> deterministic controller decision -> backend apply`
1333:    
1334: 2. **[ ] No unsigned endpoint mutation.**
1335:    - All endpoint changes MUST have corresponding signed traversal bundle
1336:    - Verification: Lines in code + test paths
1337:    
1338: 3. **[ ] No silent fallback to weaker path logic.**
1339:    - No "legacy" runtime branches
1340:    - No "temporary" insecure fallbacks
1341:    
1342: 4. **[ ] No plaintext visibility at the relay.**
1343:    - Relay sees only WireGuard ciphertext
1344:    - Verification: Relay server tests + adversarial audit
1345:    
1346: 5. **[ ] No unprotected egress if no valid direct or relay path exists.**
1347:    - Kill-switch enforced in protected mode
1348:    - Fail-closed on trust state loss
1349:    
1350: 6. **[ ] Replay, rollback, stale-state, and wrong-signer artifacts must fail closed.**
1351:    - Nonce tracking prevents replay
1352:    - Watermark/epoch prevents rollback
1353:    - TTL enforcement prevents stale acceptance
1354:    - Signature verification prevents wrong-signer
1355:    
1356: 7. **[ ] Route and DNS protections must survive direct/relay transitions.**
1357:    - No leak window during failover
1358:    - Continuous kill-switch enforcement
1359:    
1360: 8. **[ ] Exit-node selection must never widen LAN or underlay access beyond explicit policy.**
1361:    - Exit node advertising MUST be signed
1362:    - Route ACLs strictly enforced
1363:    
1364: 9. **[ ] Local control surfaces remain Unix-socket or root-only system integration surfaces.**
1365:    - No HTTP API on localhost (prevents DNS rebinding)
1366:    - No LAN-accessible management ports
1367:    
1368: 10. **[ ] Every new cross-network behavior must land with measured gate evidence.**
1369:     - Not just unit tests
1370:     - Live lab validation required
1371: 
1372: ## 8. Minimum Functional Definition of Done
1373: 
1374: Rustynet can claim cross-network remote exit-node support only when all of the following are true:
1375: 
1376: **[ ] 8.1 Direct Path Capabilities**
1377: 1. A client behind NAT can use a remote exit node behind a different NAT via direct UDP when NAT conditions allow.
1378: 2. WireGuard encryption active end-to-end (ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD verified).
1379: 3. Signed traversal bundle required for initial connection and all endpoint changes.
1380: 4. Anti-replay, anti-rollback, and freshness protections operational.
1381: 
1382: **[ ] 8.2 Relay Path Capabilities**
1383: 1. A client can use the same remote exit node via encrypted relay when direct UDP does not work.
1384: 2. Nested encryption: WireGuard layer + relay session layer both active.
1385: 3. Relay cannot decrypt WireGuard payload (zero-trust relay verified).
1386: 4. Relay authentication uses constant-time comparison.
1387: 5. Relay abuse protections enforced (rate limits, session TTL, bounded resources).
1388: 
1389: **[ ] 8.3 Path Transition Safety**
1390: 1. Direct-to-relay and relay-to-direct transitions preserve:
1391:    - WireGuard session keys (no re-handshake)
1392:    - ACL enforcement
1393:    - Kill-switch behavior
1394:    - DNS fail-closed behavior
1395:    - Narrow server-IP bypass semantics (only /32 or /128 for control plane)
1396: 2. No packet loss or cleartext window during transition.
1397: 3. Continuous encryption verified during failover.
1398: 
1399: **[ ] 8.4 Security Properties**
1400: 1. All known vulnerability classes from Section 6 mitigated and tested:
1401:    - TunnelCrack (LocalNet/ServerIP bypass)
1402:    - TunnelVision (DHCP option 121 injection)
1403:    - Tailscale fail-open bugs (TS-2025-008)
1404:    - Tailscale shell injection (TS-2026-001)
1405:    - Tailscale exit filtering (TS-2024-005)
1406:    - WireGuard endpoint mobility attacks
1407: 2. Adversarial test suite passes (forged/replayed/stale traversal rejected).
1408: 3. No secret leakage in logs, metrics, or error messages.
1409: 
1410: **[ ] 8.5 Operational Resilience**
1411: 1. System remains functional after endpoint roaming (IP address change).
1412: 2. System survives control plane temporary unavailability (uses cached signed state).
1413: 3. System fails closed when trust state is missing/corrupted/expired.
1414: 
1415: **[ ] 8.6 Measured Evidence**
1416: 1. Live validation artifacts exist and pass on a multi-network Linux lab.
1417: 2. All artifacts follow schema in CrossNetworkRemoteExitArtifactSchema_2026-03-16.md.
1418: 3. Evidence is commit-bound, not stale, and reproducible.
1419: 
1420: ## 7. Gap Summary
1421: The remaining work falls into four technical gaps:
1422: 1. Candidate acquisition:
1423:    - Rustynet needs real public/reflexive candidate discovery, not just signed endpoint hints carrying static or pre-known addresses.
1424: 2. WAN simultaneous-open behavior:
1425:    - Rustynet needs shared-socket, real NAT traversal behavior rather than only one-sided bounded probe logic.
1426: 3. Relay transport:
1427:    - Rustynet needs a real ciphertext relay service and client integration.
1428: 4. Cross-network exit-path validation:
1429:    - Rustynet needs measured live evidence that full-tunnel routing and DNS remain secure across direct and relay paths.
1430: 
1431: ## 8. Implementation Phases
1432: ### Phase 0: Truth Lock and Threat Model Baseline
1433: Goal:
1434: - Align all remaining work under one current-state plan and stop overstating completion.
1435: 
1436: Tasks:
1437: 1. Keep current docs explicit that WAN simultaneous-open and production relay are still open.
1438: 2. Maintain the exploit-comparison and live-auditing skill outputs as release inputs for traversal and relay work.
1439: 3. Treat HP2 and HP3 as release-blocking for cross-network remote-exit claims.
