1626: ## 8A. Comprehensive Rust Testing Requirements
1627: 
1628: This section defines MANDATORY testing requirements for all cross-network functionality. Every feature must have multi-layered test coverage before it can be considered complete.
1629: 
1630: ### 8A.1 Test Pyramid Structure
1631: 
1632: Rustynet follows a strict test pyramid:
1633: 
1634: ```
1635:                     ▲
1636:                    ╱ ╲
1637:                   ╱   ╲
1638:                  ╱ E2E ╲         10% - Live Lab Tests (hours)
1639:                 ╱───╲
1640:                ╱         ╲
1641:               ╱Integration╲      20% - Integration Tests (minutes)
1642:              ╱───╲
1643:             ╱               ╲
1644:            ╱   Unit Tests    ╲   70% - Unit & Property Tests (seconds)
1645:           ╱___________________╲
1646: ```
1647: 
1648: **Ratios:**
1649: - **70% Unit Tests:** Fast, isolated, deterministic
1650: - **20% Integration Tests:** Multi-component, in-process
1651: - **10% E2E Tests:** Full system, live network
1652: 
1653: ### 8A.2 Unit Test Requirements (Rust)
1654: 
1655: #### 8A.2.1 Core Principles
1656: 
1657: Every Rust module MUST have:
1658: 
1659: ```rust
1660: #[cfg(test)]
1661: mod tests {
1662:     use super::*;
1663:     
1664:     // REQUIRED: Test module for every implementation module
1665: }
1666: ```
1667: 
1668: **Coverage Requirements:**
1669: - **Minimum:** 80% line coverage for security-critical modules
1670: - **Target:** 90% line coverage for all modules
1671: - **Mandatory:** 100% coverage for crypto/signature verification code
1672: 
1673: **Tools:**
1674: ```bash
1675: # Generate coverage report
1676: cargo tarpaulin --out Html --output-dir coverage/
1677: 
1678: # Enforce minimum coverage in CI
1679: cargo tarpaulin --fail-under 80
1680: ```
1681: 
1682: #### 8A.2.2 Signature Verification Tests
1683: 
1684: Every function that verifies signatures MUST have these tests:
1685: 
1686: ```rust
1687: #[cfg(test)]
1688: mod signature_tests {
1689:     use super::*;
1690:     
1691:     #[test]
1692:     fn valid_signature_accepted() {
1693:         let (public_key, secret_key) = generate_test_keypair();
1694:         let payload = b"test payload";
1695:         let signature = sign(payload, &secret_key);
1696:         
1697:         assert!(verify_signature(payload, &signature, &public_key).is_ok());
1698:     }
1699:     
1700:     #[test]
1701:     fn invalid_signature_rejected() {
1702:         let (public_key, _) = generate_test_keypair();
1703:         let payload = b"test payload";
1704:         let bad_signature = [0u8; 64]; // Wrong signature
1705:         
1706:         assert!(verify_signature(payload, &bad_signature, &public_key).is_err());
1707:     }
1708:     
1709:     #[test]
1710:     fn wrong_key_signature_rejected() {
1711:         let (public_key1, secret_key1) = generate_test_keypair();
1712:         let (public_key2, _) = generate_test_keypair();
1713:         let payload = b"test payload";
1714:         let signature = sign(payload, &secret_key1);
1715:         
1716:         // Signed with key1, verified with key2 -> reject
1717:         assert!(verify_signature(payload, &signature, &public_key2).is_err());
1718:     }
1719:     
1720:     #[test]
1721:     fn modified_payload_rejected() {
1722:         let (public_key, secret_key) = generate_test_keypair();
1723:         let original = b"original payload";
1724:         let modified = b"modified payload";
1725:         let signature = sign(original, &secret_key);
1726:         
1727:         assert!(verify_signature(modified, &signature, &public_key).is_err());
1728:     }
1729:     
1730:     #[test]
1731:     fn empty_signature_rejected() {
1732:         let (public_key, _) = generate_test_keypair();
1733:         let payload = b"test payload";
1734:         let empty_sig = [];
1735:         
1736:         assert!(verify_signature(payload, &empty_sig, &public_key).is_err());
1737:     }
1738: }
1739: ```
1740: 
1741: #### 8A.2.3 Anti-Replay Tests
1742: 
1743: Every nonce/replay protection mechanism MUST have:
1744: 
1745: ```rust
1746: #[cfg(test)]
1747: mod replay_protection_tests {
1748:     use super::*;
1749:     
1750:     #[test]
1751:     fn fresh_nonce_accepted() {
1752:         let mut store = NonceStore::new();
1753:         let nonce = generate_nonce();
1754:         
1755:         assert!(store.check_and_record(&nonce).is_ok());
1756:     }
1757:     
1758:     #[test]
1759:     fn replayed_nonce_rejected() {
1760:         let mut store = NonceStore::new();
1761:         let nonce = generate_nonce();
1762:         
1763:         // First use: OK
1764:         assert!(store.check_and_record(&nonce).is_ok());
1765:         
1766:         // Second use: REJECTED
1767:         assert!(store.check_and_record(&nonce).is_err());
1768:     }
1769:     
1770:     #[test]
1771:     fn expired_nonce_cleaned_up() {
1772:         let mut store = NonceStore::new();
1773:         let nonce = generate_nonce();
1774:         
1775:         store.check_and_record(&nonce).unwrap();
1776:         
1777:         // Fast-forward time past expiry
1778:         store.advance_time(Duration::from_secs(121)); // 2x max age
1779:         
1780:         // Cleanup should remove old nonces
1781:         store.cleanup_expired();
1782:         
1783:         // Old nonce is gone, but we still reject to be safe
1784:         assert!(store.check_and_record(&nonce).is_err());
1785:     }
1786:     
1787:     #[test]
1788:     fn concurrent_nonce_recording_safe() {
1789:         use std::sync::Arc;
1790:         use std::thread;
1791:         
1792:         let store = Arc::new(Mutex::new(NonceStore::new()));
1793:         let nonce = Arc::new(generate_nonce());
1794:         
1795:         // Two threads try to use same nonce
1796:         let handles: Vec<_> = (0..2).map(|_| {
1797:             let store = Arc::clone(&store);
1798:             let nonce = Arc::clone(&nonce);
1799:             thread::spawn(move || {
1800:                 store.lock().unwrap().check_and_record(&nonce)
1801:             })
1802:         }).collect();
1803:         
1804:         let results: Vec<_> = handles.into_iter()
1805:             .map(|h| h.join().unwrap())
1806:             .collect();
1807:         
1808:         // Exactly ONE should succeed, ONE should fail
1809:         let successes = results.iter().filter(|r| r.is_ok()).count();
1810:         assert_eq!(successes, 1, "Concurrent nonce check failed atomicity");
1811:     }
1812: }
1813: ```
1814: 
1815: #### 8A.2.4 Constant-Time Operation Tests
1816: 
1817: All timing-sensitive operations MUST have constant-time verification:
1818: 
1819: ```rust
1820: #[cfg(test)]
1821: mod constant_time_tests {
1822:     use super::*;
1823:     use std::time::Instant;
1824:     
1825:     #[test]
1826:     fn hmac_verification_constant_time() {
1827:         let key = [42u8; 32];
1828:         let correct_hmac = compute_hmac(&key, b"test data");
1829:         let wrong_hmac = [0u8; 32];
1830:         
1831:         // Measure timing for correct HMAC
1832:         let start = Instant::now();
1833:         for _ in 0..1000 {
1834:             let _ = verify_hmac(&correct_hmac, &correct_hmac, &key);
1835:         }
1836:         let correct_duration = start.elapsed();
1837:         
1838:         // Measure timing for wrong HMAC
1839:         let start = Instant::now();
1840:         for _ in 0..1000 {
1841:             let _ = verify_hmac(&wrong_hmac, &correct_hmac, &key);
1842:         }
1843:         let wrong_duration = start.elapsed();
1844:         
1845:         // Timing difference should be negligible (< 5%)
1846:         let ratio = if correct_duration > wrong_duration {
1847:             correct_duration.as_nanos() as f64 / wrong_duration.as_nanos() as f64
1848:         } else {
1849:             wrong_duration.as_nanos() as f64 / correct_duration.as_nanos() as f64
1850:         };
1851:         
1852:         assert!(ratio < 1.05, 
1853:             "HMAC verification has timing leak: ratio={}", ratio);
1854:     }
1855:     
1856:     #[test]
1857:     fn token_comparison_constant_time() {
1858:         use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
1859:         
1860:         let token1 = [1u8; 16];
1861:         let token2 = [2u8; 16];
1862:         
1863:         // This should compile (uses constant-time comparison)
1864:         let _ = token1.ct_eq(&token2);
1865:         
1866:         // This should NOT compile if we've forbidden variable-time comparison
1867:         // (enforced via clippy lint)
1868:         // let _ = token1 == token2;  // Should trigger clippy::op_ref_non_const_eq
1869:     }
1870: }
1871: ```
1872: 
1873: #### 8A.2.5 Memory Safety Tests
1874: 
1875: Sensitive data MUST be zeroized:
1876: 
1877: ```rust
1878: #[cfg(test)]
1879: mod memory_safety_tests {
1880:     use super::*;
1881:     use zeroize::Zeroize;
1882:     
1883:     #[test]
1884:     fn private_key_zeroized_on_drop() {
1885:         let key_ptr: *const u8;
1886:         let key_value: u8;
1887:         
1888:         {
1889:             let key = PrivateKey::generate();
1890:             let key_bytes = key.as_bytes();
1891:             key_ptr = key_bytes.as_ptr();
1892:             key_value = key_bytes[0];
1893:             
1894:             // Key exists and has non-zero value
1895:             assert_ne!(key_value, 0);
1896:         }
1897:         // Key dropped here - should be zeroized
1898:         
1899:         // SAFETY: This is a test verification that zeroization occurred
1900:         // In production, this memory may be reallocated
1901:         unsafe {
1902:             let potentially_zeroized = std::ptr::read(key_ptr);
1903:             // Note: This test is best-effort, as memory may have been reused
1904:             // Better approach: Use memory sanitizers in CI
1905:         }
1906:     }
1907:     
1908:     #[test]
1909:     fn session_keys_not_in_debug_output() {
1910:         let session = Session::new_test();
1911:         let debug_output = format!("{:?}", session);
1912:         
1913:         // Debug output should NOT contain raw key bytes
1914:         assert!(!debug_output.contains("key"));
1915:         assert!(debug_output.contains("<redacted>") || 
1916:                 debug_output.contains("***"));
1917:     }
1918:     
1919:     #[test]
1920:     fn no_key_material_in_error_messages() {
1921:         let key = PrivateKey::generate();
1922:         let result: Result<(), _> = Err(Error::InvalidKey(key));
1923:         
1924:         let error_message = format!("{}", result.unwrap_err());
1925:         
1926:         // Error message should NOT expose key material
1927:         assert!(!error_message.contains(&format!("{:?}", key.as_bytes())));
1928:     }
1929: }
1930: ```
1931: 
1932: #### 8A.2.6 Property-Based Testing (Mandatory for Parsers)
1933: 
1934: Use `proptest` for all parsing/validation code:
1935: 
1936: ```rust
1937: #[cfg(test)]
1938: mod property_tests {
1939:     use super::*;
1940:     use proptest::prelude::*;
1941:     
1942:     proptest! {
1943:         #[test]
1944:         fn parse_cidr_never_panics(s in "\\PC*") {
1945:             // Any string input should not panic
1946:             let _ = parse_cidr(&s);
1947:         }
1948:         
1949:         #[test]
1950:         fn valid_cidr_roundtrips(ip in any::<IpAddr>(), prefix_len in 0u8..=128) {
1951:             let cidr = format!("{}/{}", ip, prefix_len);
1952:             if let Ok(parsed) = parse_cidr(&cidr) {
1953:                 assert_eq!(parsed.to_string(), cidr);
1954:             }
1955:         }
1956:         
1957:         #[test]
1958:         fn signature_verification_never_panics(
1959:             payload in proptest::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..1024),
1960:             signature in proptest::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..128),
1961:         ) {
1962:             let (public_key, _) = generate_test_keypair();
1963:             
1964:             // Should never panic, even with garbage input
1965:             let _ = verify_signature(&payload, &signature, &public_key);
1966:         }
1967:         
1968:         #[test]
1969:         fn nonce_check_never_panics(
1970:             nonce in proptest::collection::vec(any::<u8>(), 0..32)
1971:         ) {
1972:             let mut store = NonceStore::new();
1973:             let _ = store.check_and_record(&nonce);
1974:         }
1975:     }
1976: }
1977: ```
1978: 
1979: #### 8A.2.7 Fuzzing Requirements
1980: 
1981: Security-critical parsers MUST have fuzz tests:
1982: 
1983: ```rust
1984: // fuzz/fuzz_targets/traversal_bundle_parser.rs
1985: #![no_main]
1986: use libfuzzer_sys::fuzz_target;
1987: use rustynet_control::TraversalBundle;
1988: 
1989: fuzz_target!(|data: &[u8]| {
1990:     // Should never panic or crash
1991:     let _ = TraversalBundle::parse(data);
1992: });
1993: ```
1994: 
1995: **Fuzzing commands:**
1996: ```bash
1997: # Install cargo-fuzz
1998: cargo install cargo-fuzz
1999: 
2000: # Run fuzzer for 10 minutes minimum
2001: cargo fuzz run traversal_bundle_parser -- -max_total_time=600
2002: 
2003: # Run all fuzzers in CI
2004: cargo fuzz list | xargs -I {} cargo fuzz run {} -- -max_total_time=60
2005: ```

2090: 
2091: Every test MUST generate structured evidence:
2092: 
2093: ```rust
2094: // In test code
2095: #[test]
2096: fn signature_verification_blocks_invalid() {
2097:     let test_id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4();
2098:     let evidence_path = PathBuf::from(format!(
2099:         "artifacts/test_evidence/{}.json",
2100:         test_id
2101:     ));
2102:     
2103:     // Run test
2104:     let result = verify_signature(/* invalid */);
2105:     assert!(result.is_err());
2106:     
2107:     // Generate evidence
2108:     let evidence = TestEvidence {
2109:         test_id: test_id.to_string(),
2110:         test_name: "signature_verification_blocks_invalid",
2111:         timestamp: SystemTime::now(),
2112:         result: "pass",
2113:         git_commit: env!("GIT_COMMIT"),
2114:         details: json!({
2115:             "verification_result": "rejected",
2116:             "error_type": "InvalidSignature",
2117:         }),
2118:     };
2119:     
2120:     std::fs::create_dir_all(evidence_path.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
2121:     std::fs::write(evidence_path, serde_json::to_string_pretty(&evidence).unwrap()).unwrap();
2122: }
2123: ```

2125: ## 9. Mandatory Test and Gate Contract for "Connect From Anywhere"
2126: This is release-blocking. Rustynet must not claim cross-network remote-exit capability until all required tests and gates below exist and pass on the target commit.
2127: 
2128: ### 9.1 Required test classes
2129: 1. Unit and property tests
2130:    - signed candidate parsing and verification
2131:    - replay, rollback, stale-state, wrong-signer rejection
2132:    - bounded simultaneous-open scheduling
2133:    - relay session token/auth validation
2134:    - constant-time auth/token comparison for relay control surfaces
2135:    - route and DNS fail-closed transitions during path changes
2136: 2. Local integration tests
2137:    - backend endpoint rotation on valid traversal decision only
2138:    - direct-path establishment success when handshake evidence advances
2139:    - safe fallback to relay when direct cannot be proven
2140:    - safe failback from relay to direct when direct becomes healthy
2141:    - exit-node routing and DNS enforcement under path transitions
2142: 3. Live multi-network lab tests
2143:    - direct remote-exit success across different networks
2144:    - relay-backed remote-exit success across different networks
2145:    - relay-to-direct failback after reprobe
2146:    - endpoint roaming recovery
2147:    - reboot recovery while remote-exit path remains policy-safe
2148: 4. Adversarial live tests
2149:    - forged traversal state during active session
2150:    - stale traversal state during active session
2151:    - replayed traversal state during active session
2152:    - rogue endpoint injection
2153:    - route-bypass / TunnelCrack-style leak attempts during path change
2154:    - control-surface exposure checks while cross-network exit path is active
2155: 5. Soak and resilience tests
2156:    - long-running direct session across networks
2157:    - long-running relay session across networks
2158:    - repeated direct/relay flaps without policy leak
2159:

2212: 5. Extend the Rustynet security auditor skill so coverage promotion only happens when those measured reports pass schema validation and required checks.
2213: 
2214: ### 9.5 Failure policy
2215: If any required test or artifact fails:
2216: 1. Rustynet must not claim "connect from anywhere".
2217: 2. Coverage remains `partially_covered`.
2218: 3. Release readiness must fail closed.
2219: 4. The fix must land with a regression test or measured validator that proves the failure class is covered.
2220: 
2221: ### 9.6 Security interpretation of pass/fail
2222: - A passing direct-path test without relay proof is insufficient.
2223: - A passing relay-path test without direct-path proof is insufficient.
2224: - A passing happy-path test without adversarial rejection proof is insufficient.
2225: - A passing unit/integration suite without measured live evidence is insufficient.
2226: 
2227: ## 10. Recommended Build Order
2228: The correct implementation order from the current repo state is:
2229: 1. Finish candidate acquisition and signed traversal input completeness.
2230: 2. Finish true WAN simultaneous-open behavior in HP2.
2231: 3. Implement real relay transport in HP3.
2232: 4. Bind exit-node full-tunnel semantics to those paths.
2233: 5. Add live measured evidence and gate enforcement.
2234: 
2235: This order matters. Shipping relay before the direct-path controller is secure enough would multiply trust surfaces unnecessarily. Shipping direct-path claims before live cross-network validation would overstate the feature and weaken release integrity.
2236: 
2237: ## 11. What Must Not Be Done
2238: 1. Do not add a second endpoint mutation path.
2239: 2. Do not accept unsigned or locally guessed external endpoints.
2240: 3. Do not rely on manual port forwarding as the product correctness path.
2241: 4. Do not treat a public-IP exit node as proof that hole punching is complete.
2242: 5. Do not add "temporary" raw shell fallbacks for relay or traversal control.
2243: 6. Do not claim "works from anywhere" until live multi-network evidence exists.
2244: 
2245: ## 12. Immediate Next Code Work
2246: The highest-value next code steps are:
2247: 1. Finish the candidate acquisition side for real public/reflexive candidates.
2248: 2. Complete shared-socket simultaneous-open behavior in the traversal engine and backend integration.
2249: 3. Begin the real ciphertext relay transport implementation in `rustynet-relay`.
2250: 4. Define the cross-network remote-exit measured artifact schemas and readiness checks before implementation claims start to drift.
2251: 
2252: ## 13. Exit Criteria for This Plan
2253: This plan is complete only when:
2254: 1. Rustynet can securely connect a client on one network to an exit node on another network without manual port forwarding when direct NAT traversal is possible.
2255: 2. The same workflow securely succeeds via relay when direct traversal is not possible.
2256: 3. The measured live artifacts and Phase 10 gates prove that behavior on the current commit.
2257: 4. The required cross-network remote-exit tests and adversarial gates in Section 9 pass without weakening any release checks.

2654: ## APPENDIX B: Quick Reference - Security Decision Tree
2655: 
2656: Use this when making implementation decisions:
2657: 
2658: ```
2659: ┌───┐
2660: │ "Should I implement feature X in way Y?"                    │
2661: └───┘
2662:                               │
2663:                               ▼
2664:         ┌───┐
2665:         │ Does it require unsigned state mutation?│
2666:         └───┘
2667:            YES │                     │ NO
2668:                │                     ▼
2669:          ❌ REJECT            Does it bypass existing
2670:                              signed-state requirements?
2671:                                      │
2672:                           YES │            │ NO
2673:                               │            ▼
2674:                         ❌ REJECT   Does it add shell
2675:                                    command construction?
2676:                                             │
2677:                                  YES │           │ NO
2678:                                      │           ▼
2679:                                ❌ REJECT   Does it weaken
2680:                                           fail-closed behavior?
2681:                                                    │
2682:                                         YES │            │ NO
2683:                                             │            ▼
2684:                                       ❌ REJECT   Does it expose
2685:                                                  plaintext at relay?
2686:                                                           │
2687:                                                YES │           │ NO
2688:                                                    │           ▼
2689:                                              ❌ REJECT   Does it have
2690:                                                         measured evidence?
2691:                                                                  │
2692:                                                       NO │            │ YES
2693:                                                          │            ▼
2694:                                                    ❌ DEFER    ✅ PROCEED
2695:                                                    (Block on    (Implement with
2696:                                                     evidence)    test coverage)
2697: ```

2701: ## APPENDIX C: Cryptographic Algorithm Quick Reference
2702: 
2703: | Purpose | Algorithm | Key Size | Standard | Rationale |
2704: |---------|-----------|----------|----------|-----------|
2705: | **Symmetric Encryption** | ChaCha20 | 256-bit | RFC 8439 | Faster than AES on ARM, constant-time |
2706: | **Authentication (AEAD)** | Poly1305 | 256-bit | RFC 8439 | Fast, provably secure, pairs with ChaCha20 |
2707: | **Key Exchange** | Curve25519 | 256-bit | RFC 7748 | Industry standard, fast, side-channel resistant |
2708: | **Hash Function** | BLAKE2s | 256-bit | RFC 7693 | Faster than SHA-256, cryptographically secure |
2709: | **Digital Signature** | Ed25519 | 256-bit | RFC 8032 | Small keys, fast verification, deterministic |
2710: | **HMAC** | HMAC-SHA256 | 256-bit | RFC 2104 | Standard, secure, widely supported |
2711: | **Random Number Generation** | OS-provided (`OsRng`) | N/A | N/A | Uses kernel entropy sources |
2712: 
2713: **Security Level:** All algorithms provide at least 128-bit security (equivalent to AES-256 against quantum computers).
2714: 
2715: **Post-Quantum Status:** Current algorithms are vulnerable to quantum computers. Future Phase 11 will add hybrid key exchange (Curve25519 + Kyber) and optional PSK mode.

2719: ## APPENDIX D: Common Implementation Pitfalls
2720: 
2721: ### ❌ **DON'T: Shell Construction**
2722: ```rust
2723: // WRONG - allows injection
2724: let cmd = format!("ip route add {} via {}", user_dest, gateway);
2725: std::process::Command::new("sh").arg("-c").arg(&cmd).spawn()?;
2726: ```
2727: 
2728: ### ✅ **DO: Argv Arrays**
2729: ```rust
2730: // CORRECT - no injection possible
2731: std::process::Command::new("ip")
2732:     .arg("route")
2733:     .arg("add")
2734:     .arg(user_dest)
2735:     .arg("via")
2736:     .arg(gateway)
2737:     .spawn()?;
2738: ```
2739: 
2740: ### ❌ **DON'T: Variable-Time Comparison**
2741: ```rust
2742: // WRONG - timing attack possible
2743: if computed_hmac == provided_hmac {
2744:     return Ok(());
2745: }
2746: ```
2747: 
2748: ### ✅ **DO: Constant-Time Comparison**
2749: ```rust
2750: // CORRECT - no timing leakage
2751: use subtle::ConstantTimeEq;
2752: if computed_hmac.ct_eq(&provided_hmac).into() {
2753:     return Ok(());
2754: }
2755: ```
2756: 
2757: ### ❌ **DON'T: Logging Secrets**
2758: ```rust
2759: // WRONG - leaks key to logs
2760: debug!("Private key: {:?}", private_key);
2761: ```
2762: 
2763: ### ✅ **DO: Redacted Debug**
2764: ```rust
2765: // CORRECT - key not visible in logs
2766: #[derive(Debug)]
2767: struct PrivateKey {
2768:     #[debug("<redacted>")]
2769:     key: [u8; 32],
2770: }
2771: ```
2772: 
2773: ### ❌ **DON'T: Fail-Open on Missing State**
2774: ```rust
2775: // WRONG - allows bypass when state file deleted
2776: let trust_state = TrustState::load().unwrap_or_default();
2777: ```
2778: 
2779: ### ✅ **DO: Fail-Closed on Missing State**
2780: ```rust
2781: // CORRECT - enters safe mode when state missing
2782: let trust_state = match TrustState::load()? {
2783:     Some(s) => s,
2784:     None => return Ok(RuntimeState::RestrictedSafeMode),
2785: };
2786: ```

 333: ## 6) macOS Built-in Security Features to Use
 334: - Keychain (`Security.framework`) for secret custody instead of disk passphrase files.
 335: - `launchd` for service lifecycle hardening (daemon/helper supervision).
 336: - PF anchors (`pfctl -a`) for scoped fail-closed firewall ownership and cleanup.
 337: - Absolute-path, root-owned binary validation for privileged command execution.
 338: - Unix-domain socket peer credential checks for helper authorization.

 374: ## 10) Threat Model Snapshots by Gap
 375: 
 376: ### GAP-01 Threat: startup secret-source confusion
 377: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 378:   - Operator error or inconsistent env leads to failed daemon startup.
 379:   - Team adds insecure compatibility fallback to "fix startup quickly".
 380: - Security impact:
 381:   - Availability loss or accidental reintroduction of plaintext secret handling.
 382: - Required control:
 383:   - One explicit passphrase source contract on macOS launch path, enforced at startup.
 384: 
 385: ### GAP-02 Threat: user-owned tool binary injection
 386: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 387:   - User-space writable `wg` or `wireguard-go` binary can be swapped/tampered.
 388: - Security impact:
 389:   - Privileged network operations can execute attacker-controlled code.
 390: - Required control:
 391:   - Root-owned, immutable-path privileged tools only; no non-admin fallback.
 392: 
 393: ### GAP-03 Threat: DNS exfiltration when tunnel assumptions fail
 394: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 395:   - DNS traffic escapes protected tunnel path while tunnel is down/degraded.
 396: - Security impact:
 397:   - Domain leakage, policy bypass, potential active redirection.
 398: - Required control:
 399:   - PF-enforced DNS fail-closed rules with positive assertions and negative tests.
 400: 
 401: ### GAP-04 Threat: IPv6 bypass on partial dual-stack enforcement
 402: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 403:   - IPv4 route forced through tunnel while IPv6 path remains open.
 404: - Security impact:
 405:   - Silent traffic leakage and policy non-compliance.
 406: - Required control:
 407:   - Capability truthfulness and enforced IPv6 block/route parity.
 408: 
 409: ### GAP-05 Threat: weak privileged process lifecycle on macOS
 410: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 411:   - launchd unit/plist or environment drift causes degraded privileged lifecycle guarantees.
 412: - Security impact:
 413:   - Firewall/tunnel state desynchronization and weaker trust in runtime posture.
 414: - Required control:
 415:   - launchd-managed daemon/helper lifecycle with deterministic startup/restart.
 416: 
 417: ### GAP-06 Threat: unsafe manual operations due to ops parity gaps
 418: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 419:   - Operators use direct ad-hoc shell commands on macOS for missing menu actions.
 420: - Security impact:
 421:   - Inconsistent validation/audit controls and accidental unsafe peer mutation.
 422: - Required control:
 423:   - Same validated IPC-driven admin paths on both OS families.
 424: 
 425: ### GAP-07 Threat: undetected macOS dataplane regressions
 426: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 427:   - Security behavior breaks in deeper macOS runtime paths not covered by current smoke-level checks.
 428: - Security impact:
 429:   - Vulnerable releases reach users.
 430: - Required control:
 431:   - Mandatory macOS dataplane security gates in CI.
 432: 
 433: ### GAP-08 Threat: documentation drift causes unsafe assumptions
 434: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 435:   - Users rely on docs that overstate support guarantees.
 436: - Security impact:
 437:   - Misconfigured deployments with weaker security than expected.
 438: - Required control:
 439:   - One support matrix and synchronized docs.
 440: 
 441: ### GAP-09 Threat: persistent passphrase-at-rest exposure on macOS
 442: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 443:   - Local file disclosure, backup leak, or post-exploitation file scraping.
 444: - Security impact:
 445:   - Compromise of encrypted key material unlocking path.
 446: - Required control:
 447:   - Keychain-backed secret custody, disk plaintext elimination.
 448: 
 449: ### GAP-10 Threat: monolithic installer regression blast radius
 450: - Attacker/Failure mode:
 451:   - Cross-OS edits accidentally affect Debian hardening path.
 452: - Security impact:
 453:   - Security regression introduced outside intended scope.
 454: - Required control:
 455:   - OS-modular script layout and path-specific tests.

 622: ## 13) Target Secure Architecture (macOS parity without Linux regression)
 623: 
 624: ```mermaid
 625: flowchart TD
 626:     A["start.sh (OS dispatcher)"] --> B["macOS launcher module"]
 627:     A --> C["Linux launcher module"]
 628:     B --> D["launchd: rustynetd"]
 629:     B --> E["launchd: privileged helper"]
 630:     D --> F["Unix socket IPC (strict peer checks)"]
 631:     F --> E
 632:     E --> G["PF anchor rules (fail-closed tunnel + DNS)"]
 633:     D --> H["Keychain secret retrieval"]
 634:     C --> I["systemd rustynetd + credentials"]
 635:     I --> J["nft/ip/sysctl fail-closed policy"]
 636: ```
 637: 
 638: Security properties this architecture must preserve:
 639: - Secrets are sourced from OS-secure storage mechanisms by default.
 640: - Privileged operations remain behind explicit validated boundary.
 641: - Fail-closed network posture is enforced at OS firewall layer on both platforms.
 642: - Linux and macOS startup/lifecycle are deterministic and auditable.

  60: ## 3) Findings + next steps
  61: 
  62: ### 3.1) Orchestrator dispatch hang — FIXED
  63: 
  64: **Root cause:** `execute_utm_remote_powershell_capture` in
  65: `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs` always called
  66: `pull_windows_local_utm_guest_file_with_retry` even when the
  67: `utm_exec_windows_raw` step had already failed (e.g. when utmctl
  68: returned OSStatus -1743 from a sandboxed parent). The pull-retry
  69: loop's `max_attempts = timeout.as_secs().max(10)` meant up to
  70: 86,400 attempts × 1s sleep = 24 hours of futile retrying for a
  71: result file that was never written.
  72: 
  73: **Fix:** added an early-Err guard after `utm_exec_windows_raw`
  74: that returns immediately when the host_status is Err — triggering
  75: the existing SSH fallback in `resolve_local_utm_capture_result`
  76: instead of the doomed pull-retry loop. Cleanup of any partial
  77: local + remote artifacts happens before the early return.
  78: 
  79: **Live evidence post-fix:** the same `vm-lab-validate-windows-security
  80: --skip-access-bootstrap --skip-install` invocation now completes
  81: in <30 seconds and writes a typed JSON report.
  82: [`windows_utm_1_validate_2026-04-28.json`](./windows_utm_1_validate_2026-04-28.json):
  83: 
  84: ```
  85: bootstrap_windows_host:           pass
  86: validate_windows_client_install:  fail (RustyNet service is Stopped)
  87: validate_windows_runtime_acls:    skipped (cascade)
  88: validate_windows_service_hardening: skipped
  89: validate_windows_key_custody:     skipped
  90: validate_windows_authenticode:    skipped
  91: validate_windows_dns_failclosed:  skipped
  92: distribute_*:                     skipped (4 stages)
  93: validate_windows_mesh_join:       skipped
  94: ```
  95: 
  96: The cascade-skip is honest fail-closed behavior — the rest of the
  97: chain depends on a Running service and the service refuses to start
  98: because the daemon ships on `--backend windows-unsupported`.
  99: 
 100: ### 3.2) Stale binary + missing WireGuard for Windows on `windows-utm-1`
 101: 
 102: Two findings stack:
 103: 
 104: 1. **Stale daemon binary.** The deployed daemon (2026-04-27 22:38)
 105:    predates the `windows-dns-failclosed-check` and
 106:    `windows-backend-readiness-check` subcommands added this
 107:    session. Direct probes of those two subcommands return the
 108:    help-text dump (unknown subcommand) — visible in the live run
 109:    evidence above.
 110: 
 111: 2. **WireGuard for Windows not installed.** Probe via SSH:
 112:    ```
 113:    Test-Path "C:\Program Files\WireGuard\wireguard.exe" → False
 114:    Test-Path "C:\Program Files\WireGuard\wg.exe"        → False
 115:    Get-Service WireGuardManager                          → not present
 116:    ```
 117:    The install helper's `Resolve-ReviewedBackendLabel` auto-
 118:    detection therefore wrote
 119:    `RUSTYNETD_DAEMON_ARGS_JSON=["--backend","windows-unsupported"]`
 120:    to the env file. The daemon honors this and refuses to start
 121:    (Event Log: SCM EventID 7023 "service terminated with %%1").
 122: 
 123: **Next-step (operator action required, can't be done from sandbox):**
 124: 1. Install WireGuard for Windows on `windows-utm-1` (either via
 125:    the bootstrap winget config or manually from
 126:    `https://www.wireguard.com/install/`).
 127: 2. Re-run `Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1` on the guest. The
 128:    helper's auto-detect will switch the env file to
 129:    `--backend windows-wireguard-nt`.
 130: 3. Verify `Get-Service RustyNet | Status` is `Running`.
 131: 4. Re-run `vm-lab-validate-windows-security` — the validator chain
 132:    should reach `validate_windows_mesh_join` (which will still
 133:    honestly report "state snapshot missing" until the daemon has
 134:    actually joined a mesh, but every other stage should
 135:    pass / fail with meaningful drift rather than skip-cascade).
 136: 
 137: ### 3.3) Five Debian VMs offline

 411: ## 5. Non-Negotiable Security Rules For The Remaining Delta
 412: - Keep one hardened execution path per security-sensitive workflow.
 413: - Fail closed on missing, invalid, stale, malformed, unauthorized, or unproven state.
 414: - Do not create a daemon-owned or helper-owned side socket.
 415: - Do not treat same-local-port behavior as authoritative transport identity.
 416: - Do not silently downgrade `linux-wireguard-userspace-shared` to `linux-wireguard`.
 417: - Do not move long-lived transport ownership into the helper.
 418: - Do not fake route or exit-mode success to satisfy the lab.
 419: - Do not widen macOS or Windows capability claims from Linux-only work.
 420: - Do not soften `cargo audit`, `cargo deny`, `phase10_gates`, `membership_gates`, or `phase10_cross_network_exit_gates`.

 101: 
 102: ## 0) Purpose
 103: 
 104: Define a single hardened design for Rustynet Magic DNS so node names and admin-assigned aliases are distributed as signed control-plane state, enforced fail-closed, and resolved only through trusted local DNS handling.
 105: 
 106: This document is a schema and runtime contract. It is not a relaxed UX sketch.
 107: 
 108: ## 1) Precedence and Constraints
 109: 
 110: - [Requirements.md](../../Requirements.md) is normative.
 111: - [SecurityMinimumBar.md](../../SecurityMinimumBar.md) is release-blocking.
 112: - [Phase4.md](../../Phase4.md) and [phase10.md](../../phase10.md) define functional and runtime expectations.
 113: - If this document conflicts with a higher-precedence source, the stricter security interpretation wins.
 114: 
 115: Non-negotiable constraints for this design:
 116: 
 117: - one hardened path for DNS record mutation and distribution
 118: - default deny for record visibility
 119: - fail closed when signed DNS state is missing, invalid, stale, replayed, or mismatched
 120: - no unsigned local hostname overrides
 121: - no public-domain interception by default
 122: - no raw shell fallback in runtime DNS control paths
 123: 
 124: ## 2) Security Goals
 125: 
 126: The design must prevent these failure classes:
 127: 
 128: 1. Unsigned local spoofing
 129: - a node must not be able to invent or persist its own name-to-IP mappings
 130: 
 131: 2. Replay and rollback
 132: - old zone bundles must not be re-applied after newer zone state exists
 133: 
 134: 3. Record-to-rogue-IP injection
 135: - a signed record must not be able to point at arbitrary underlay or internet IPs unless policy explicitly allows a future service-IP mode
 136: 
 137: 4. Topology overexposure
 138: - a client should not automatically learn every node and alias in the network if policy does not require it
 139: 
 140: 5. DNS leak/fail-open behavior
 141: - protected DNS mode must not silently fall back to insecure external resolution for managed Rustynet names
 142: 
 143: 6. Alias collision ambiguity
 144: - duplicate or conflicting labels must resolve deterministically before runtime
 145: 
 146: ## 3) Design Position
 147: 
 148: Rustynet Magic DNS should be implemented as:
 149: 
 150: - a centrally issued signed DNS zone artifact
 151: - optionally filtered per target node for least-knowledge visibility
 152: - resolved against signed node identity and signed assignment state
 153: - served locally by a trusted authoritative resolver only for the managed Rustynet zone
 154: 
 155: It should not be implemented as:
 156: 
 157: - a local mutable `/etc/hosts`-style database
 158: - per-node self-registration
 159: - arbitrary public-domain override
 160: - unsigned CLI hostname mutation
 161: 
 162: ## 4) Naming Scope
 163: 
 164: Version 1 scope:
 165: 
 166: - one private zone suffix only, for example `rustynet`
 167: - records only for Rustynet-managed names under that suffix
 168: - supported record types: `A` and `AAAA`
 169: - alias support allowed only as additional labels under the same managed zone
 170: 
 171: Version 1 exclusions:
 172: 
 173: - `CNAME`
 174: - wildcard records
 175: - `TXT`, `SRV`, `MX`, `NS`
 176: - public-domain interception such as `github.com`
 177: - unsigned local alias files
 178: 
 179: These exclusions are deliberate. They keep the first secure implementation small and auditable.
 180: 
 181: ## 5) Artifact Model
 182: 
 183: The recommended artifact is a per-target-node signed bundle:
 184: 
 185: - one bundle is issued for one consuming node
 186: - the bundle contains only the records that node is authorized to learn
 187: 
 188: This is preferred over one global zone file because:
 189: 
 190: - it reduces topology leakage
 191: - it fits the project's existing signed-assignment pattern
 192: - it keeps least-privilege visibility aligned with the control plane
 193: 
 194: Recommended files:
 195: 
 196: - bundle: `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.dns-zone`
 197: - verifier key: `/etc/rustynet/dns-zone.pub`
 198: - watermark: `/var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.dns-zone.watermark`
 199: 
 200: Recommended custody:
 201: 
 202: - bundle: `0640 root:<daemon-group>`
 203: - verifier key: `0644 root:root`
 204: - watermark: `0640 root:<daemon-group>`
 205: 
 206: ## 6) Bundle Schema
 207: 
 208: Top-level artifact:
 209: 
 210: ```json
 211: {
 212:   "schema_version": 1,
 213:   "artifact_type": "signed_dns_zone_bundle",
 214:   "zone_name": "rustynet",
 215:   "subject_node_id": "client-1",
 216:   "generated_at_unix": 1773000000,
 217:   "expires_at_unix": 1773000300,
 218:   "membership_epoch": 5,
 219:   "assignment_generation": 42,
 220:   "dns_policy_generation": 7,
 221:   "nonce_hex": "6f9e8f4c...",
 222:   "records": [
 223:     {
 224:       "label": "nas",
 225:       "fqdn": "nas.rustynet",
 226:       "rr_type": "A",
 227:       "ttl_secs": 60,
 228:       "target_node_id": "node-nas-1",
 229:       "target_addr_kind": "mesh_ipv4",
 230:       "expected_ip": "100.100.10.10",
 231:       "aliases": ["storage", "backup"]
 232:     }
 233:   ],
 234:   "signature": {
 235:     "algorithm": "ed25519",
 236:     "key_id": "dns-zone-root-2026q1",
 237:     "signature_hex": "ab12..."
 238:   }
 239: }
 240: ```
 241: 
 242: ### 6.1 Top-Level Fields
 243: 
 244: - `schema_version`
 245:   - integer
 246:   - required
 247:   - must equal `1` for the first implementation
 248: 
 249: - `artifact_type`
 250:   - string
 251:   - required
 252:   - must equal `signed_dns_zone_bundle`
 253: 
 254: - `zone_name`
 255:   - string
 256:   - required
 257:   - lower-case DNS suffix
 258:   - must match the configured managed zone exactly
 259: 
 260: - `subject_node_id`
 261:   - string
 262:   - required
 263:   - node that is authorized to consume this bundle
 264:   - runtime must reject bundles for a different local node
 265: 
 266: - `generated_at_unix`
 267:   - integer
 268:   - required
 269:   - signing time
 270: 
 271: - `expires_at_unix`
 272:   - integer
 273:   - required
 274:   - hard expiration
 275:   - runtime must reject expired bundles
 276: 
 277: - `membership_epoch`
 278:   - integer
 279:   - required
 280:   - binds DNS state to a signed membership view
 281: 
 282: - `assignment_generation`
 283:   - integer
 284:   - required
 285:   - binds DNS resolution to the signed assignment generation used to validate node address ownership
 286: 
 287: - `dns_policy_generation`
 288:   - integer
 289:   - required
 290:   - monotonically increasing zone-policy/version counter
 291: 
 292: - `nonce_hex`
 293:   - string
 294:   - required
 295:   - anti-replay nonce
 296: 
 297: - `records`
 298:   - array
 299:   - required
 300:   - bounded size
 301: 
 302: - `signature`
 303:   - object
 304:   - required
 305:   - detached or embedded signature payload metadata
 306: 
 307: ### 6.2 Record Fields
 308: 
 309: - `label`
 310:   - relative label under `zone_name`
 311:   - lower-case canonical form only
 312:   - no wildcard
 313:   - each label component must be 1-63 chars
 314: 
 315: - `fqdn`
 316:   - canonical fully-qualified name
 317:   - must exactly equal `label + "." + zone_name`
 318:   - runtime should re-derive and compare, not trust blindly
 319: 
 320: - `rr_type`
 321:   - enum
 322:   - allowed in v1: `A`, `AAAA`
 323: 
 324: - `ttl_secs`
 325:   - integer
 326:   - required
 327:   - bounded, recommended range `30..=300`
 328:   - default recommendation `60`
 329: 
 330: - `target_node_id`
 331:   - required
 332:   - binds record to Rustynet node identity
 333: 
 334: - `target_addr_kind`
 335:   - enum
 336:   - v1 allowed values:
 337:     - `mesh_ipv4`
 338:     - `mesh_ipv6`
 339: 
 340: - `expected_ip`
 341:   - required
 342:   - must match the target node's signed assignment-derived mesh address for the selected address kind
 343:   - runtime must reject mismatch
 344: 
 345: - `aliases`
 346:   - optional array
 347:   - alias labels under the same zone only
 348:   - each alias is subject to the same label restrictions as `label`
 349: 
 350: ## 7) Canonical Validation Rules
 351: 
 352: Runtime must validate all of these before loading the bundle:
 353: 
 354: 1. schema and artifact type are known
 355: 2. signature verifies against the pinned verifier key
 356: 3. artifact is fresh and unexpired
 357: 4. watermark/nonce is not replayed or rolled back
 358: 5. `subject_node_id` matches the local node
 359: 6. `zone_name` matches configured managed zone
 360: 7. every `fqdn` canonicalizes exactly from `label`
 361: 8. every `target_node_id` exists in current signed membership
 362: 9. every `target_node_id` is not revoked
 363: 10. every `expected_ip` matches current signed assignment state for that node
 364: 11. no record points outside authorized Rustynet address space
 365: 12. no duplicate `fqdn`
 366: 13. no alias collides with another primary label or alias
 367: 14. record count, alias count, and label lengths stay within hard bounds
 368: 
 369: If any validation fails:
 370: 
 371: - do not partially load
 372: - preserve the last known valid zone if still fresh
 373: - otherwise fail closed for managed zone resolution
 374: 
 375: ## 8) Hard Bounds
 376: 
 377: Recommended initial bounds:
 378: 
 379: - max bundle size: `256 KiB`
 380: - max records per bundle: `1024`
 381: - max aliases per record: `8`
 382: - max total labels including aliases: `2048`
 383: - max TTL: `300`
 384: - min TTL: `30`
 385: - max zone name length: `64`
 386: 
 387: The goal is to prevent memory abuse, parser abuse, and oversized signed artifacts.
 388: 
 389: ## 9) Watermark and Replay Protection
 390: 
 391: DNS should use the same strict watermark philosophy already used elsewhere in Rustynet.
 392: 
 393: Recommended watermark file fields:
 394: 
 395: ```text
 396: version=2
 397: generation=7
 398: payload_digest_hex=<sha256 of canonical bundle bytes>
 399: generated_at_unix=1773000000
 400: ```
 401: 
 402: Rules:
 403: 
 404: - lower generation than current watermark is rejected
 405: - equal generation with different digest is rejected
 406: - equal generation with same digest is allowed
 407: - legacy watermark versions are rejected fail-closed
 408: 
 409: This prevents stale-bundle replay and same-generation tampering.
 410: 
 411: ## 10) Resolver Runtime Contract
 412: 
 413: The runtime resolver should behave as follows.
 414: 
 415: For names inside the managed zone:
 416: 
 417: - if bundle is valid and loaded:
 418:   - answer authoritatively from signed records
 419: - if bundle is missing, stale, invalid, or mismatched:
 420:   - return `SERVFAIL` for managed names
 421:   - do not forward the query to external DNS
 422: 
 423: For names outside the managed zone:
 424: 
 425: - forward only through the protected upstream DNS path
 426: - keep existing DNS fail-closed behavior from protected mode
 427: 
 428: This distinction matters:
 429: 
 430: - `SERVFAIL` for managed-zone state failure preserves fail-closed semantics
 431: - forwarding managed-zone misses externally would create namespace leakage and trust confusion
 432: 
 433: ## 11) Authorization Model
 434: 
 435: Record visibility must be least-knowledge.
 436: 
 437: Preferred model:
 438: 
 439: - control plane computes visible DNS names for each target node
 440: - zone bundle is filtered to only those records
 441: 
 442: Minimum authorization rules for v1:
 443: 
 444: - a node may see its own record
 445: - a node may see records for peers it is authorized to communicate with under signed assignment/policy state
 446: - a node may see exit-node names it is authorized to select
 447: - a node must not automatically see unrelated aliases or nodes outside its allowed graph
 448: 
 449: This is stricter than many consumer VPNs. That is intentional.
 450: 
 451: ## 12) Collision Handling
 452: 
 453: Collisions must be resolved centrally, not at daemon runtime.
 454: 
 455: Recommended issuer behavior:
 456: 
 457: - normalize labels to lower-case LDH form
 458: - assign first claimant the base label
 459: - assign later collisions deterministic suffixes:
 460:   - `nas`
 461:   - `nas-2`
 462:   - `nas-3`
 463: 
 464: Runtime should still validate uniqueness, but it should not invent new labels locally.
 465: 
 466: Why:
 467: 
 468: - central deterministic issuance is auditable
 469: - local renaming would create inconsistent views across nodes
 470: 
 471: ## 13) Why Raw Hostname-to-IP Overrides Are Not Acceptable
 472: 
 473: A naive design would let an admin or node submit:
 474: 
 475: - `custom_url -> raw_ip`
 476: 
 477: That is not the right default in Rustynet.
 478: 
 479: Problems:
 480: 
 481: - raw IPs can point at rogue underlay or internet endpoints
 482: - names become detached from signed node identity
 483: - stale records survive assignment changes
 484: - local operators can accidentally create unsafe split-brain behavior
 485: 
 486: The secure design is:
 487: 
 488: - `custom label -> target_node_id -> signed assignment-derived address`
 489: 
 490: That keeps naming bound to trust state.
 491: 
 492: ## 14) Future Extension Points
 493: 
 494: These can be added later, but should not be in v1:
 495: 
 496: - service-scoped virtual IP records
 497: - signed `SRV` records for service discovery
 498: - policy-gated public-zone override for verified-owned domains
 499: - DoH/DoT upstream transport
 500: - DNSSEC-style authenticated negative responses inside the managed zone
 501: 
 502: Each of these expands trust surface and should be staged separately.
 503: 
 504: ## 15) Recommended CLI Surface
 505: 
 506: Not for immediate implementation, but this is the right shape:
 507: 
 508: ```bash
 509: rustynet dns zone issue \
 510:   --zone rustynet \
 511:   --subject-node-id client-1 \
 512:   --records-manifest /path/to/zone.records.manifest \
 513:   --signing-secret /etc/rustynet/dns-zone.signing.secret \
 514:   --signing-secret-passphrase-file /run/credentials/.../dns_zone_signing_passphrase \
 515:   --output /tmp/client-1.dns-zone \
 516:   --verifier-key-output /tmp/dns-zone.pub
 517: 
 518: rustynet dns zone verify \
 519:   --bundle /var/lib/rustynet/rustynetd.dns-zone \
 520:   --verifier-key /etc/rustynet/dns-zone.pub
 521: 
 522: rustynet dns inspect
 523: ```
 524: 
 525: Mutation should remain signer-backed and centrally issued. There should be no local unsigned `dns set` command.
 526: 
 527: ## 16) Enforcement Points
 528: 
 529: Recommended enforcement mapping:
 530: 
 531: - `rustynet-control`
 532:   - canonical schema types
 533:   - signing and verification
 534:   - collision validation
 535: 
 536: - `rustynet-cli`
 537:   - issuance and verification commands
 538:   - no local unsigned mutation path
 539: 
 540: - `rustynetd`
 541:   - secure bundle loading
 542:   - watermark enforcement
 543:   - resolver runtime
 544:   - `dns inspect`
 545: 
 546: - dataplane/DNS manager
 547:   - managed-zone authoritative answers
 548:   - protected upstream forwarding for non-managed names
 549:   - fail-closed behavior when DNS state is invalid
 550: 
 551: ## 17) Required Tests
 552: 
 553: Unit tests:
 554: 
 555: - canonical label normalization
 556: - deterministic collision handling
 557: - invalid label rejection
 558: - duplicate alias rejection
 559: - record-to-assignment IP mismatch rejection
 560: - replay/rollback rejection
 561: - subject-node mismatch rejection
 562: 
 563: Integration tests:
 564: 
 565: - node resolves authorized peer name through local authoritative resolver
 566: - node cannot resolve unauthorized peer name
 567: - managed-zone query returns `SERVFAIL` when bundle is stale or invalid
 568: - external DNS remains protected and fail-closed on tunnel/DNS failure
 569: - signed zone update rotates records without stale-cache confusion
 570: 
 571: Adversarial tests:
 572: 
 573: - forged signature
 574: - same-generation different-digest tamper
 575: - alias collision injection
 576: - record pointing to underlay IP
 577: - revoked-node record retention
 578:

 656: ## 19) Bottom Line
 657: 
 658: The correct Rustynet Magic DNS schema is:
 659: 
 660: - signed
 661: - per-target-node
 662: - node-identity-bound
 663: - assignment-cross-checked
 664: - replay-protected
 665: - private-zone-only
 666: - fail-closed for managed names
 667: 
 668: That keeps naming inside the same security model as the rest of Rustynet instead of introducing a weaker side channel.

 134: 
 135: ## TRACK A — NAT Traversal and Production Relay Transport
 136: 
 137: **Owner area:** `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs`, `crates/rustynet-relay/`, `crates/rustynet-backend-api/`
 138: 
 139: **Why this matters:** The whole point of Rustynet is to connect devices "from anywhere" without manual port forwarding. Without HP-3 (real relay transport) and the remaining HP-2 (simultaneous-open WAN traversal), the relay path is just a routing label — no actual packets are relayed. Direct connection only works when both sides happen to have reachable IPs.
 140: 
 141: **Safe to run in parallel with:** Track C, Track D, and Track B (WS-1/WS-3 only).
 142: 
 143: **Conflicts with:** Track B (WS-2) — both touch `traversal.rs`. Coordinate so they are not editing the same functions simultaneously.

 176: 
 177: **A1-b: Simultaneous-Open Coordination**
 178: 
 179: Currently, only the client side sends probe packets. True simultaneous-open requires both sides to start sending at approximately the same time so that both NAT tables have entries before the first packet arrives.
 180: 
 181: Files to modify:
 182: - `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs` — add simultaneous-open orchestration
 183: - `crates/rustynet-control/` — add traversal coordination signal (both sides need to start probing at the same time)
 184: 
 185: Implementation:
 186: ```
 187: 1. Add a TraversalCoordinationRecord issued by control containing:
 188:    - session_id: [u8; 16]  (random, shared between both peers)
 189:    - probe_start_unix: u64 (Unix timestamp, both sides begin at this time)
 190:    - peer_a: NodeId
 191:    - peer_b: NodeId
 192:    - signed by control key, short TTL (30s max)
 193: 
 194: 2. In rustynetd traversal engine:
 195:    - receive coordination record
 196:    - wait until probe_start_unix (bounded wait, max 10s)
 197:    - at that moment, send UDP probe packets to all of peer's candidates
 198:    - simultaneously, peer does the same
 199:    - first handshake observed = direct path established
 200: 
 201: 3. Bounded retry policy:
 202:    - max 5 simultaneous-open rounds
 203:    - 500ms between rounds
 204:    - if no handshake within rounds*spacing + grace, declare direct failed
 205:    - fall through to relay (A2)
 206: 
 207: 4. Record transition reason:
 208:    - PathMode::Direct { reason: DirectReason::SimultaneousOpen }
 209:    - PathMode::Relay { reason: RelayReason::DirectFailed { rounds: N } }
 210: ```
 211: 
 212: Tests required:
 213: - Unit test: coordination record with future probe_start waits, then fires; past probe_start fires immediately
 214: - Unit test: expired coordination record (> 30s old) is rejected
 215: - Unit test: after N failed rounds, transitions to relay decision — no additional attempts
 216: - Integration test (two netns with iptables NAT): verify two nodes establish direct path through simulated NAT using simultaneous-open
 217: 
 218: **Status (A1-b):** Implemented. Traversal coordination record validation, signature verification, freshness, nonce anti-replay window, wait-for-probe_start behaviour, simultaneous probe executor, and fallback to relay after configured rounds are implemented in `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs`. Unit tests were added.

 225: ### A2 — HP-3: Production Relay Transport Service
 226: 
 227: **Status:** Implemented in code (relay transport/session/rate-limit modules and unit tests), with live cross-network evidence still pending lab execution.
 228: 
 229: **What needs to be built:**
 230: 
 231: This is the most substantial remaining code item in the entire project. The relay service must:
 232: 1. Accept authenticated node sessions over a control channel
 233: 2. Forward encrypted WireGuard UDP packets between two authenticated sessions
 234: 3. Never decrypt — only forward ciphertext
 235: 4. Apply per-node rate limits and abuse controls
 236: 5. Integrate with regional relay selection from `rustynet-relay`
 237: 
 238: **A2-a: Relay Session Protocol**
 239: 
 240: Files to create/modify:
 241: - `crates/rustynet-relay/src/transport.rs` (new) — session auth and packet forwarding
 242: - `crates/rustynet-relay/src/session.rs` (new) — per-session state
 243: - `crates/rustynet-relay/src/rate_limit.rs` (new) — per-node rate and abuse controls
 244: - `crates/rustynet-relay/src/lib.rs` — wire everything together
 245: 
 246: Protocol design (keep it minimal and auditable):
 247: ```
 248: Client → Relay: RelayHello {
 249:     node_id: NodeId,          // who is connecting
 250:     peer_node_id: NodeId,     // who they want to reach
 251:     session_token: [u8; 32],  // short-lived token from control plane, signed
 252:     nonce: [u8; 16],          // replay prevention
 253: }
 254: 
 255: Relay → Client: RelayHelloAck {
 256:     session_id: [u8; 16],     // assigned session id
 257:     allocated_port: u16,      // UDP port for this session on relay
 258: } | RelayHelloReject { reason: RejectReason }
 259: 
 260: Client → Relay: RelayPacket { session_id, payload: [u8] }  // ciphertext only
 261: Relay → Client: RelayPacket { session_id, payload: [u8] }  // forwarded from peer
 262: ```
 263: 
 264: Security requirements:
 265: - Session token must be validated against control key signature before session is accepted (no unsigned sessions)
 266: - Session token must have a short TTL (≤ 120s from issuance)
 267: - session_token must include the peer_node_id in its signed payload — cannot be reused to reach a different peer
 268: - Reject immediately if session_token is stale, signature invalid, or nonce replayed
 269: - Relay never reads payload bytes for routing — only session_id determines forwarding destination
 270: - After session auth: relay matches two sessions (A→B and B→A) by (node_id, peer_node_id) pair, then bidirectionally forwards packets
 271: 
 272: Rate limiting per session:
 273: - max packet rate: 10,000 pps (configurable)
 274: - max bandwidth: 100 Mbps (configurable)
 275: - max concurrent sessions per node: 8 (configurable)
 276: - on limit exceeded: drop packets silently (not RST/reject — avoid amplification)
 277: 
 278: Implementation steps:
 279: ```
 280: 1. Add relay session token type to rustynet-control:
 281:    - RelaySessionToken { node_id, peer_node_id, relay_id, issued_at_unix, expires_at_unix, nonce }
 282:    - signed by control key (same signer as traversal hints)
 283:    - issued on demand when a node needs a relay session
 284: 
 285: 2. Add relay server binary or integrate into rustynetd:
 286:    - binds UDP port for relay traffic
 287:    - binds TCP control port for session auth
 288:    - session lifecycle: Hello → verify token → allocate → active → timeout/teardown
 289: 
 290: 3. Integrate into rustynetd relay path:
 291:    - when TraversalDecision::Relay is made, daemon contacts relay control port
 292:    - sends RelayHello with token
 293:    - receives allocated UDP port
 294:    - programs WireGuard peer endpoint to relay_addr:allocated_port
 295:    - sets up keepalive to maintain relay session
 296: 
 297: 4. Session cleanup:
 298:    - idle sessions (no packets for 30s) are torn down
 299:    - on WireGuard peer removal, tear down associated relay session
 300:    - relay server garbage collects half-open sessions
 301: ```
 302: 
 303: Tests required:
 304: - Unit test: invalid session token (bad signature) → rejected, no session allocated
 305: - Unit test: expired session token → rejected
 306: - Unit test: replayed nonce → rejected
 307: - Unit test: session token for wrong peer → rejected
 308: - Unit test: two matching sessions (A→B, B→A) correctly pair and forward packets bidirectionally
 309: - Unit test: rate limit enforcement — packets above limit are silently dropped, session not terminated
 310: - Unit test: session idle timeout — session is cleaned up after idle period
 311: - Integration test: two nodes in separate netns with direct UDP blocked by iptables; verify they can exchange WireGuard packets through relay, decrypt successfully on the other side
 312: 
 313: ---

 316: 
 317: Files to modify:
 318: - `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs` — add relay session establishment
 319: - `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs` — integrate relay session into path controller
 320: - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs` — add relay session state tracking
 321: 
 322: Implementation:
 323: ```
 324: 1. When TraversalDecision::Relay:
 325:    a. Request relay session token from control (or load pre-issued token)
 326:    b. Connect to relay control port, send RelayHello
 327:    c. Receive allocated port (relay_addr:allocated_port)
 328:    d. Update WireGuard peer endpoint to relay_addr:allocated_port
 329:    e. Record: PathMode::Relay { relay_addr, relay_session_id, established_at }
 330: 
 331: 2. Relay session keepalive:
 332:    - send keepalive packet every 25s to prevent idle timeout
 333:    - on keepalive failure (relay unreachable), re-establish or fail-closed

 336:    - when direct path is re-established (failback):

 344: ```

 353: ### A3 — HP-4: Seamless Path Controller Completion
 354: 
 355: **Status:** Implemented for controller logic and unit coverage (`Phase10Controller` hysteresis and fail-closed bypass), with live handoff-under-load evidence still pending Debian lab execution.
 356: 
 357: **What is needed:**
 358: 
 359: **A3-a: Hysteresis for Direct→Relay and Relay→Direct transitions**
 360: 
 361: Without hysteresis, a flapping network causes rapid path switching that can disrupt active connections. Hysteresis requires a path to be stable for a minimum duration before committing.
 362: 
 363: Files to modify:
 364: - `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs` — add hysteresis policy to path controller
 365: - `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs` — expose stability window
 366: 
 367: Implementation:
 368: ```
 369: Add to Phase10Controller:
 370:   direct_stability_window_ms: u64    // how long direct must be healthy before committing (default: 3000)
 371:   relay_stability_window_ms: u64     // how long relay must be healthy before committing (default: 5000)
 372:   last_path_change_at: Option<Instant>
 373:   pending_path_mode: Option<PathMode>  // candidate mode not yet committed
 374: 
 375: Path change logic:
 376:   fn consider_path_change(&mut self, candidate: PathMode) {
 377:       if candidate == self.current_path { return; }
 378:       if self.pending_path_mode != Some(candidate) {
 379:           // New candidate — start stability window
 380:           self.pending_path_mode = Some(candidate);
 381:           self.pending_since = Instant::now();
 382:           return;
 383:       }
 384:       // Existing candidate — check if stability window elapsed
 385:       let stability_window = match candidate {
 386:           PathMode::Direct => self.direct_stability_window_ms,
 387:           PathMode::Relay  => self.relay_stability_window_ms,
 388:       };
 389:       if self.pending_since.elapsed() >= Duration::from_millis(stability_window) {
 390:           self.commit_path_change(candidate);  // one hardened commit path
 391:       }
 392:   }
 393: ```
 394: 
 395: Tests required:
 396: - Unit test: path does not switch when candidate flaps within stability window
 397: - Unit test: path switches after candidate is stable for full window duration
 398: - Unit test: fail-closed transition bypasses hysteresis (security > stability)
 399: - Integration test: induce flapping NAT condition, verify path changes < 3 times in 60s window

 507: ### B1 — WS-1: Control-Plane Reachability Independence
 508: 
 509: **Goal:** The daemon must not depend on the operator's current underlay network to stay alive. It fetches signed state independently over the Rustynet control channel.
 510: 
 511: **B1-a: Pull-Based Signed State Fetch Channel (WS1-01)**
 512: 
 513: Currently: the daemon loads signed state from disk at startup and on explicit IPC command. There is no autonomous outbound fetch.
 514: 
 515: Files to modify:
 516: - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs` — add `StateFetcher` component
 517: - `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs` — wire fetcher into refresh flow
 518: 
 519: Implementation:
 520: ```rust
 521: // New component: StateFetcher
 522: struct StateFetcher {
 523:     control_endpoint: Url,          // https endpoint of control plane
 524:     tls_trust_roots: RootCertStore, // pinned trust roots, not system roots
 525:     node_identity: Ed25519Keypair,  // for mTLS client auth
 526:     watermarks: WatermarkStore,     // tracks last-seen watermarks per bundle type
 527: }
 528: 
 529: impl StateFetcher {
 530:     /// Fetch one signed bundle from control. Verifies signature + watermark before returning.
 531:     fn fetch_assignment(&self) -> Result<SignedAssignmentBundle, FetchError> {
 532:         let raw = self.http_get("/v1/assignment")?;       // HTTP GET with mTLS
 533:         let bundle = parse_signed_assignment_bundle(&raw)
 534:             .map_err(FetchError::ParseError)?;
 535:         bundle.verify(&self.assignment_verifier_key)       // signature check
 536:             .map_err(FetchError::SignatureInvalid)?;
 537:         self.watermarks.advance_assignment(&bundle.watermark) // anti-replay
 538:             .map_err(FetchError::WatermarkRejected)?;
 539:         bundle.check_freshness(SystemTime::now(), MAX_CLOCK_SKEW) // freshness
 540:             .map_err(FetchError::Stale)?;
 541:         Ok(bundle)
 542:     }
 543: 
 544:     // Same pattern for: fetch_traversal, fetch_trust, fetch_dns_zone
 545:     // Each has its own verifier key and watermark namespace
 546: }
 547: ```
 548: 
 549: Important security constraints:
 550: - TLS trust roots must be pinned at install time, not loaded from system CA store
 551: - mTLS client certificate derived from node's identity key (same key as WireGuard identity)
 552: - If fetch fails (network unreachable, cert invalid, signature bad), return `Err` — never return stale state
 553: - Watermark store persisted atomically to disk with strict permissions (0600)
 554: 
 555: Tests required:
 556: - Unit test: valid bundle returned from mock server → parsed, verified, watermark advanced → Ok
 557: - Unit test: invalid signature from server → `FetchError::SignatureInvalid`, watermark not advanced
 558: - Unit test: stale bundle (expired freshness) → `FetchError::Stale`, watermark not advanced
 559: - Unit test: replayed watermark (watermark ≤ current) → `FetchError::WatermarkRejected`
 560: - Unit test: network unreachable → `FetchError::Network`, existing on-disk state unchanged
 561: - Unit test: two concurrent fetches → second fetch sees watermark already advanced by first, rejects (idempotency via watermark)
 562: 
 563: ---
 564: 
 565: **B1-b: Node-Side Periodic Refresh (WS1-02)**
 566: 
 567: The daemon needs a background loop that periodically refreshes signed state before it expires.
 568: 
 569: Files to modify:
 570: - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs` — add refresh scheduler to daemon event loop
 571: 
 572: Implementation:
 573: ```rust
 574: struct RefreshScheduler {
 575:     assignment_ttl_secs: u64,    // from current bundle
 576:     traversal_ttl_secs: u64,
 577:     trust_ttl_secs: u64,
 578:     pre_expiry_margin_secs: u64, // default: 120s before expiry
 579:     jitter_max_secs: u64,        // default: 30s (prevent thundering herd)
 580: }
 581: 
 582: impl RefreshScheduler {
 583:     fn next_refresh_at(&self, bundle_expires_at: SystemTime) -> Instant {
 584:         let margin = Duration::from_secs(self.pre_expiry_margin_secs);
 585:         let jitter = Duration::from_secs(rand::random::<u64>() % self.jitter_max_secs);
 586:         let target = bundle_expires_at - margin + jitter;
 587:         // Never schedule in the past
 588:         let now = SystemTime::now();
 589:         if target <= now {
 590:             Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5)  // fire soon
 591:         } else {
 592:             Instant::now() + target.duration_since(now).unwrap()
 593:         }
 594:     }
 595: }
 596: 
 597: // In daemon event loop:
 598: loop {
 599:     select! {
 600:         _ = assignment_refresh_timer => {
 601:             match fetcher.fetch_assignment() {
 602:                 Ok(bundle) => {
 603:                     controller.apply_signed_assignment(bundle)?; // one hardened apply path
 604:                     assignment_refresh_timer.reset(scheduler.next_refresh_at(bundle.expires_at));
 605:                 }
 606:                 Err(e) => {
 607:                     log::warn!("assignment refresh failed: {e}");
 608:                     // Do NOT fail-closed on first failure — retry with backoff
 609:                     assignment_refresh_timer.reset(Instant::now() + RETRY_BACKOFF);
 610:                     // If expiry passes without successful refresh → fail-closed
 611:                     if SystemTime::now() > current_assignment.expires_at {
 612:                         controller.transition_fail_closed("assignment expired without refresh");
 613:                     }
 614:                 }
 615:             }
 616:         }
 617:         // Same for traversal, trust, dns_zone timers
 618:     }
 619: }
 620: ```
 621: 
 622: Tests required:
 623: - Unit test: refresh fires at `expires_at - margin + jitter`, not after `expires_at`
 624: - Unit test: jitter is bounded (never exceeds `jitter_max_secs`)
 625: - Unit test: on failed refresh, daemon retries without fail-closing immediately
 626: - Unit test: if refresh fails and bundle expires, daemon transitions to fail_closed
 627: - Unit test: successful refresh resets timer to new bundle's expiry window
 628: - Integration test: daemon with short-TTL bundle (10s), verify refresh fires before expiry, daemon never enters fail_closed

 640: Implementation:
 641: 
 642: [IN_PROGRESS — started 2026-03-23T18:45Z] Evidence: added a minimal StateFetcher implementation (crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs) and unit tests (crates/rustynetd/tests/state_fetcher.rs). CLI/IPC wiring already routes `state refresh` to daemon; the fetch-path is currently conservative: network-unreachable or unset endpoints fall back to secure disk-based verification; cryptographic verification failures will surface as errors and prevent apply. Full verification and Debian test-run pending.

 644: 
 645: ```rust
 646: // In ipc.rs — command is already parsed, handler needs completion:
 647: IpcCommand::StateRefresh { target: RefreshTarget } => {
 648:     // Verify caller credential (SO_PEERCRED)
 649:     let cred = get_peer_credential(&stream)?;
 650:     if !is_authorized_for_refresh(&cred) {
 651:         return Ok(IpcResponse::Denied { reason: "insufficient privilege" });
 652:     }
 653:     // Dispatch to daemon
 654:     daemon_tx.send(DaemonMessage::TriggerStateRefresh { target })?;
 655:     // Wait for result (bounded timeout)
 656:     match daemon_rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(30)) {
 657:         Ok(DaemonMessage::StateRefreshComplete { result }) => {
 658:             IpcResponse::StateRefreshResult { result }
 659:         }
 660:         Ok(_) | Err(_) => IpcResponse::Error { message: "refresh timed out" }
 661:     }
 662: }
 663: 
 664: // In daemon.rs — the actual refresh:
 665: fn handle_state_refresh(&mut self, target: RefreshTarget) -> RefreshResult {
 666:     // ONE path: fetch → verify → apply
 667:     // Never applies unverified state even if caller is root
 668:     match target {
 669:         RefreshTarget::All => {
 670:             self.refresh_assignment()?;
 671:             self.refresh_traversal()?;
 672:             self.refresh_trust()?;
 673:             self.refresh_dns_zone()?;
 674:         }
 675:         RefreshTarget::Assignment => self.refresh_assignment()?,
 676:         // etc.
 677:     }
 678:     // If any refresh fails → return Err, caller gets failure reason
 679:     // Daemon stays in current state (does not partially apply)
 680:     RefreshResult::Success
 681: }
 682: ```

 693: ### B2 — WS-2: Endpoint Mobility and Re-establishment
 694: 
 695: **Goal:** When the daemon's underlay IP changes (interface up/down, DHCP renewal, VPN reconnect), it automatically detects this and issues updated traversal hints so peers can reach it at the new address.

 699: **B2-a: Endpoint Change Detection (WS2-01)**
 700: 
 701: Files to modify:
 702: - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs` — add netlink watcher or poll-based monitor
 703: - `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs` — add endpoint change notification type
 704: 
 705: Implementation:
 706: ```rust
 707: // Option 1: poll-based (simpler, Linux + macOS compatible)
 708: struct EndpointMonitor {
 709:     last_seen_addrs: BTreeMap<String, Vec<IpAddr>>, // interface → addresses
 710:     poll_interval: Duration,                         // default: 5s
 711: }
 712: 
 713: impl EndpointMonitor {
 714:     fn poll(&mut self) -> Option<EndpointChangeEvent> {
 715:         let current = get_all_interface_addresses()?; // reads /proc/net/if_inet6 + getifaddrs
 716:         for (iface, addrs) in &current {
 717:             if self.last_seen_addrs.get(iface) != Some(addrs) {
 718:                 // Change detected
 719:                 let event = EndpointChangeEvent {
 720:                     interface: iface.clone(),
 721:                     old_addrs: self.last_seen_addrs.get(iface).cloned().unwrap_or_default(),
 722:                     new_addrs: addrs.clone(),
 723:                     detected_at: SystemTime::now(),
 724:                 };
 725:                 self.last_seen_addrs = current;
 726:                 return Some(event);
 727:             }
 728:         }
 729:         None
 730:     }
 731: }
 732: 
 733: // Option 2: netlink (Linux-only, lower latency)
 734: // Subscribe to RTM_NEWADDR / RTM_DELADDR netlink events
 735: // On event: extract new address, compare to last known, emit EndpointChangeEvent
 736: ```
 737: 
 738: Security constraint: the endpoint monitor must filter out:
 739: - The `rustynet0` WireGuard interface itself (IP changes on the tunnel are not underlay changes)
 740: - Loopback (`127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`)
 741: - Link-local addresses (`169.254.0.0/16`, `fe80::/10`) — these are not routable
 742: 
 743: Tests required:
 744: - Unit test: interface address added → EndpointChangeEvent emitted with correct old/new
 745: - Unit test: interface goes down (all addresses removed) → event emitted
 746: - Unit test: `rustynet0` address change → no event emitted (filtered)
 747: - Unit test: loopback address change → no event emitted
 748: - Unit test: debounce — multiple events within 1s window coalesced into one
 749: 
 750: ---
 751: 
 752: **B2-b: Traversal Re-Issue After Endpoint Change (WS2-02)**
 753: 
 754: When an endpoint change is detected, the daemon must immediately issue new signed traversal hints and distribute to peers.
 755: 
 756: Files to modify:
 757: - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs` — wire EndpointChangeEvent to traversal re-issue
 758: - `crates/rustynet-control/` — ensure traversal hint issuance API accepts refresh trigger
 759: 
 760: Implementation:
 761: ```
 762: On EndpointChangeEvent:
 763: 1. Gather fresh candidates with new IP (+ re-run STUN if available)
 764: 2. Request new signed traversal hint bundle from control
 765:    (or: if node is its own control, self-sign with local key)
 766: 3. Verify the new bundle (signature, freshness, watermark) before applying
 767: 4. Distribute to all active peers via the control channel
 768: 5. Re-run traversal probe with new candidates
 769: 6. Log: "endpoint change detected on {iface}: {old} → {new}, traversal re-issued"
 770: ```
 771: 
 772: Security constraint: fresh traversal hints must be issued with a new nonce and a watermark that advances past the previous bundle. Old bundle must not be re-distributed.
 773: 
 774: Tests required:
 775: - Unit test: endpoint change → traversal re-issue triggered within 10s
 776: - Unit test: re-issued bundle has higher watermark than previous bundle
 777: - Unit test: unsigned re-issued bundle rejected (signature check still applies even on self-trigger)
 778: - Integration test: change IP on client interface → verify exit node receives updated endpoint within 30s
 779:

 812: ### B3 — WS-3: Traversal Freshness Hardening
 813: 
 814: **B3-a: Proactive Traversal Refresh (WS3-01)**
 815: 
 816: **Status:** Implemented in `traversal.rs` and `daemon.rs` with pre-expiry refresh scheduling, telemetry counters, fail-closed alarm behavior, and unit coverage; live soak evidence remains under Track E.
 817: 
 818: Files to modify:
 819: - `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs` — add TTL-driven refresh scheduling
 820: - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs` — wire traversal refresh timer
 821: 
 822: Implementation:
 823: ```rust
 824: // In TraversalEngineConfig:
 825: pub struct TraversalEngineConfig {
 826:     // existing fields...
 827:     pub pre_expiry_refresh_margin_secs: u64,  // default: 60 (refresh 60s before TTL)
 828:     pub pre_expiry_jitter_max_secs: u64,      // default: 15
 829: }
 830: 
 831: // In traversal engine loop:
 832: fn schedule_proactive_refresh(expires_at: SystemTime, config: &TraversalEngineConfig) -> Instant {
 833:     let margin = Duration::from_secs(config.pre_expiry_refresh_margin_secs);
 834:     let jitter_secs = rand::random::<u64>() % config.pre_expiry_jitter_max_secs;
 835:     let jitter = Duration::from_secs(jitter_secs);
 836:     let target_system_time = expires_at - margin + jitter;
 837:     // Convert to Instant safely
 838:     match target_system_time.duration_since(SystemTime::now()) {
 839:         Ok(d) => Instant::now() + d,
 840:         Err(_) => Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(5), // already past — fire soon
 841:     }
 842: }
 843: 
 844: // On proactive refresh trigger:
 845: match fetcher.fetch_traversal() {
 846:     Ok(bundle) => {
 847:         controller.apply_signed_traversal_update(bundle); // ONE apply path, same as always
 848:         schedule_proactive_refresh(bundle.expires_at, config);
 849:     }
 850:     Err(e) => {
 851:         warn!("proactive traversal refresh failed: {e}, will retry");
 852:         // Retry at shorter interval, but do NOT fail-closed immediately
 853:         // Fail-closed only when expiry passes
 854:     }
 855: }
 856: ```
 857: 
 858: Tests required:
 859: - Unit test: `schedule_proactive_refresh` fires before `expires_at`, never after
 860: - Unit test: jitter is within `[0, jitter_max_secs)`
 861: - Unit test: proactive refresh applies bundle via same path as reactive (no bypass)
 862: - Unit test: failed proactive refresh → retry scheduled, fail_closed only after expiry
 863: - Integration test: short-TTL traversal (20s), verify proactive refresh fires at ~10s remaining, daemon never enters fail_closed
 864:

 937: 
 938: ## TRACK C — Membership System (M0–M8)
 939: 
 940: **Owner area:** `crates/rustynet-control/src/membership/`
 941: 
 942: **Why this matters:** Node add/remove/revoke operations currently happen through signed assignment bundles. The membership system adds quorum governance — a threshold of admin keys must sign any membership change. This prevents a single compromised admin key from adding a rogue node.
 943: 
 944: **Safe to run fully in parallel with:** All other tracks. Membership code lives entirely in `rustynet-control` and `rustynet-policy`. Only M4 touches `rustynetd`.
 945: 
 946: ---
