 948: ### C1 — M0: Foundations and Schema Lock
 949: 
 950: [DONE — evidence: scripts/ci/membership_gates.sh, documents/operations/MembershipGovernanceRunbook.md, commit: 53dfb70]
 951: 
 952: 
 953: Files to modify:
 954: - `crates/rustynet-control/src/membership/schema.rs` (new or extend)
 955: 
 956: Tasks:
 957: ```
 958: 1. Define canonical membership schema types:
 959:    - MembershipState { epoch: u64, state_root: [u8; 32], members: BTreeMap<NodeId, MemberRecord> }
 960:    - MemberRecord { node_id, public_key, status: Active|Revoked, added_at_unix, updated_at_unix }
 961:    - MembershipUpdate { update_id: [u8; 16], prev_state_root: [u8; 32], operation: Operation,
 962:                         expires_at_unix: u64, approvals: Vec<Approval> }
 963:    - Operation: AddNode | RemoveNode | RevokeNode | RotateKey | UpdateApproverSet
 964:    - Approval { approver_id: NodeId, signature: Ed25519Signature }
 965: 
 966: 2. Choose canonical encoding: CBOR (use ciborium crate) or canonical JSON (use serde_json with
 967:    sorted keys + no extra whitespace). Decision: canonical JSON is simpler to audit, use that.
 968: 
 969: 3. Define root hash computation:
 970:    - Serialize MembershipState to canonical JSON
 971:    - SHA-256 of the bytes = state_root
 972:    - This is deterministic: same state always → same root
 973: 
 974: 4. Add schema version constant: MEMBERSHIP_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1
 975:    - Updates with unknown schema version are rejected with MembershipError::UnknownSchemaVersion
 976: 
 977: 5. Add golden test vectors:
 978:    - Known state → known canonical JSON → known root hash
 979:    - These vectors must be committed and never change without a schema version bump
 980: ```
 981: 
 982: Tests required:
 983: - Unit test: known state serializes to exact expected JSON bytes
 984: - Unit test: known JSON computes to exact expected SHA-256 root hash
 985: - Unit test: state with unknown schema version → rejected
 986: - Unit test: two states with same members but different order → same root hash (canonical ordering)

 990: ### C2 — M1: State Root and Update Engine
 991: 
 992: Files to modify:
 993: - `crates/rustynet-control/src/membership/engine.rs` (new)
 994: 
 995: Tasks:
 996: ```rust
 997: // Pure deterministic reducer (no side effects, pure function):
 998: fn apply_update(state: &MembershipState, update: &MembershipUpdate)
 999:     -> Result<MembershipState, MembershipError>
1000: {
1001:     // Anti-replay check
1002:     if state.applied_update_ids.contains(&update.update_id) {
1003:         return Err(MembershipError::DuplicateUpdateId);
1004:     }
1005: 
1006:     // Freshness check
1007:     if SystemTime::now() > SystemTime::UNIX_EPOCH + Duration::from_secs(update.expires_at_unix) {
1008:         return Err(MembershipError::UpdateExpired);
1009:     }
1010: 
1011:     // Rollback protection: prev_state_root must match current root
1012:     if update.prev_state_root != state.state_root {
1013:         return Err(MembershipError::StateRootMismatch {
1014:             expected: update.prev_state_root,
1015:             actual: state.state_root
1016:         });
1017:     }
1018: 
1019:     // Apply operation
1020:     let mut new_state = state.clone();
1021:     match &update.operation {
1022:         Operation::AddNode(record) => {
1023:             if new_state.members.contains_key(&record.node_id) {
1024:                 return Err(MembershipError::NodeAlreadyExists(record.node_id));
1025:             }
1026:             new_state.members.insert(record.node_id, record.clone());
1027:         }
1028:         Operation::RemoveNode(node_id) => {
1029:             if !new_state.members.contains_key(node_id) {
1030:                 return Err(MembershipError::NodeNotFound(*node_id));
1031:             }
1032:             new_state.members.remove(node_id);
1033:         }
1034:         Operation::RevokeNode(node_id) => {
1035:             let member = new_state.members.get_mut(node_id)
1036:                 .ok_or(MembershipError::NodeNotFound(*node_id))?;
1037:             member.status = MemberStatus::Revoked;
1038:         }
1039:         // ... other operations
1040:     }
1041: 
1042:     // Advance epoch and recompute root
1043:     new_state.epoch += 1;
1044:     new_state.applied_update_ids.insert(update.update_id);
1045:     new_state.state_root = compute_state_root(&new_state)?;
1046: 
1047:     Ok(new_state)
1048: }
1049: ```
1050: 
1051: Tests required:
1052: - Unit test: AddNode valid → new state has member, epoch+1, new root
1053: - Unit test: AddNode duplicate → MembershipError::NodeAlreadyExists
1054: - Unit test: RemoveNode unknown → MembershipError::NodeNotFound
1055: - Unit test: wrong prev_state_root → MembershipError::StateRootMismatch
1056: - Unit test: expired update → MembershipError::UpdateExpired
1057: - Unit test: replayed update_id → MembershipError::DuplicateUpdateId
1058: - Unit test: epoch is strictly increasing
1059:

1062: ### C3 — M2: Quorum Signature Verification
1063: 
1064: Files to modify:
1065: - `crates/rustynet-control/src/membership/quorum.rs` (new)
1066: 
1067: Tasks:
1068: ```rust
1069: fn verify_quorum(
1070:     update: &MembershipUpdate,
1071:     state: &MembershipState,   // current state contains approver set + threshold
1072: ) -> Result<(), QuorumError> {
1073:     let canonical_payload = canonical_json(update.operation_payload())?;
1074: 
1075:     let mut valid_signers: BTreeSet<NodeId> = BTreeSet::new();
1076: 
1077:     for approval in &update.approvals {
1078:         // Check approver is active in current state
1079:         let approver = state.approvers.get(&approval.approver_id)
1080:             .ok_or(QuorumError::UnknownApprover(approval.approver_id))?;
1081: 
1082:         if approver.status != ApproverStatus::Active {
1083:             return Err(QuorumError::ApproverNotActive(approval.approver_id));
1084:         }
1085: 
1086:         // Verify signature over exact canonical payload bytes
1087:         let verifying_key = VerifyingKey::from_bytes(&approver.public_key)
1088:             .map_err(|_| QuorumError::InvalidApproverKey)?;
1089: 
1090:         verifying_key.verify_strict(&canonical_payload, &approval.signature)
1091:             .map_err(|_| QuorumError::InvalidSignature(approval.approver_id))?;
1092: 
1093:         // Enforce uniqueness (duplicate approver_id = attack attempt)
1094:         if !valid_signers.insert(approval.approver_id) {
1095:             return Err(QuorumError::DuplicateSigner(approval.approver_id));
1096:         }
1097:     }
1098: 
1099:     // Check threshold
1100:     let threshold = state.quorum_threshold; // e.g. 2 out of 3
1101:     if valid_signers.len() < threshold as usize {
1102:         return Err(QuorumError::InsufficientSignatures {
1103:             got: valid_signers.len(),
1104:             required: threshold as usize
1105:         });
1106:     }
1107: 
1108:     Ok(())
1109: }
1110: ```
1111: 
1112: Tests required:
1113: - Unit test: 2-of-3 quorum with 2 valid signatures → Ok
1114: - Unit test: 2-of-3 quorum with 1 valid signature → InsufficientSignatures
1115: - Unit test: duplicate signer → DuplicateSigner
1116: - Unit test: inactive approver → ApproverNotActive
1117: - Unit test: unknown approver → UnknownApprover
1118: - Unit test: bad signature (payload modified) → InvalidSignature
1119: - Unit test: modifying payload bytes after signing → InvalidSignature (not a different error)

1123: ### C4 — M3: Persistence and Integrity
1124: 
1125: Files to modify:
1126: - `crates/rustynet-control/src/membership/persistence.rs` (new)
1127: 
1128: Tasks:
1129: ```
1130: Snapshot file: /var/lib/rustynet/membership.snapshot
1131:   - Canonical JSON of MembershipState
1132:   - mode: 0600, owner: rustynet user
1133: 
1134: Log file: /var/lib/rustynet/membership.log
1135:   - Append-only, one MembershipUpdate per line (JSON)
1136:   - mode: 0600, owner: rustynet user
1137: 
1138: Startup integrity verification:
1139: 1. Load snapshot → decode → compute root hash
1140: 2. Replay each log entry through apply_update()
1141: 3. Compute final root hash
1142: 4. Compare to snapshot root hash + all applied updates
1143: 5. If mismatch → enter restricted-safe mode (no peer/route apply until resolved)
1144: 
1145: Atomic write strategy:
1146: 1. Write to snapshot.tmp
1147: 2. fsync
1148: 3. rename snapshot.tmp → snapshot
1149: 4. This ensures no partial-write corruption
1150: 
1151: Log integrity metadata (per entry):
1152: - entry_hash: SHA-256 of (prev_entry_hash || update_json)
1153: - This forms a hash chain — any tampering breaks the chain
1154: ```
1155: 
1156: Tests required:
1157: - Unit test: valid snapshot + valid log → replays to correct state
1158: - Unit test: tampered snapshot (byte flip) → detected at startup → restricted-safe
1159: - Unit test: tampered log entry → hash chain broken → detected → restricted-safe
1160: - Unit test: atomic write — if process killed during write, snapshot is uncorrupted
1161: - Unit test: strict permissions enforced on all written files (0600)

===== /documents/operations/active/OsAgnosticOrchestratorAndWindowsPeerDeltaPlan_2026-04-27.md =====

   1: # OS-Agnostic Orchestrator + Windows-Peer Delta Plan
   2: 
   3: Date: 2026-04-27
   4: Owner: Rustynet engineering
   5: Status: active delta ledger
   6: Branch baseline at creation: `main` @ `52372a7` (all local branches and `origin/main` aligned at `f838a76` ancestor; no divergent worktree work to recover)
   7: 
   8: ## 0) Mission
   9: 
  10: Make `vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab` accept any 5 UTM guests as equal first-class
  11: peers in the live-lab mesh, regardless of guest OS, **without weakening any
  12: existing security control**. Today the orchestrator only accepts five Linux
  13: guests, with Windows bolted on as a sidecar that runs after Linux stages
  14: finish. This plan turns Windows into a real peer that can fill any slot and
  15: keeps Mac/iOS/Android scaffolding in place for later turn-on.
  16: 
  17: The orchestrator's security responsibility — enforcing a single hardened
  18: execution path per security-sensitive workflow on every node — is the load-
  19: bearing requirement. Cross-OS support that lowers the bar is rejected.
  20: 
  21: ## 1) Scope And Non-Scope
  22: 
  23: In scope:
  24: 
  25: - Replace the Linux-only live-lab gate with a per-stage capability-aware
  26:   dispatcher that can drive Linux or Windows nodes in any of the five lab
  27:   roles (`exit`, `client`, `entry`/`relay`, `aux`, `extra`).
  28: - Close the Windows security-parity gaps the orchestrator currently relies on
  29:   the Linux unit/path/DNS toolchain to enforce.
  30: - Land a `StageOrchestrator` abstraction in Rust so each live-lab stage can
  31:   dispatch on `VmPlatformProfile` instead of shelling to one bash script.
  32: - Keep macOS / iOS / Android variants of the abstractions as `Unsupported`
  33:   stubs with clear blocker text and negative tests asserting the rejection,
  34:   so future work has a stable target.
  35: - Stay aligned with `documents/Requirements.md` and
  36:   `documents/SecurityMinimumBar.md`.
  37: 
  38: Not in scope (this delta):
  39: 
  40: - macOS guest implementation. Daemon path on Darwin is untested; tracked
  41:   separately. Stubs only.
  42: - iOS / Android guest implementation.
  43: - Replacing the Linux bash orchestrator wholesale. Linux remains the
  44:   reference implementation; the dispatcher wraps it during transition.
  45: - Promoting Windows out of `runtime-host-capable only` posture in the
  46:   release matrix. That promotion is gated on the broader work tracked in
  47:   [WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md](./WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md)
  48:   and remains untouched by this plan.
  49: 
  50: ## 2) Source-Of-Truth Cross-References
  51: 
  52: This delta is layered on top of, and must not contradict, these documents.
  53: When this plan disagrees with one of them, fix this plan, not the other.
  54: 
  55: - [WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md](./WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md)
  56:   — Windows daemon backend / runtime-host posture. Owns "what Windows must
  57:   prove before it counts as working." This delta does not relax that bar; it
  58:   only adds the orchestrator-side dispatch and parity stages that let a
  59:   Windows guest be tested in a peer slot once the backend exists.
  60: - [WindowsVmLabAccessOrchestrationRecoveryPlan_2026-04-16.md](./WindowsVmLabAccessOrchestrationRecoveryPlan_2026-04-16.md)
  61:   — Windows UTM access / SSH / callback bootstrapping. This delta consumes
  62:   whatever guest-access path that plan stabilizes; it does not replace it.
  63: - [CrossPlatformSecurityGapRemediationPlan_2026-03-05.md](./CrossPlatformSecurityGapRemediationPlan_2026-03-05.md)
  64:   — historical cross-platform gap analysis. Treat as background context.
  65: - [ShellToRustMigrationPlan_2026-03-06.md](./ShellToRustMigrationPlan_2026-03-06.md)
  66:   — bash→Rust migration of `start.sh` privileged subflows and evidence
  67:   pipelines. The orchestrator-stage dispatch work in this delta is the next
  68:   natural step after that plan; it migrates the **live-lab orchestration
  69:   shell** itself out of pure bash.
  70: - [MasterWorkPlan_2026-03-22.md](./MasterWorkPlan_2026-03-22.md) and
  71:   [PlugAndPlayTraversalRelayDeltaPlan_2026-03-29.md](./PlugAndPlayTraversalRelayDeltaPlan_2026-03-29.md)
  72:   — broader execution ledgers. Add a back-link to this delta in their next
  73:   routine update.
  74: - `documents/operations/active/UTMVirtualMachineInventory_2026-03-31.md` and
  75:   `documents/operations/active/vm_lab_inventory.json` — VM inventory truth.
  76: - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs` — current orchestrator
  77:   implementation; primary code under change.
  78: 
  79: ## 3) Current State Snapshot (2026-04-27)
  80: 
  81: Captured from a fresh repo + agent walk; verify against current code if
  82: anything below looks off.
  83: 
  84: ### 3.1 Live-lab orchestrator
  85: - CLI: `vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab` in `crates/rustynet-cli/src/main.rs`,
  86:   with `--windows-vm <alias>` sidecar flag.
  87: - Stage runner is largely a Rust wrapper around
  88:   `scripts/e2e/live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh` (~109 lines of Linux-only
  89:   shell: `systemctl`, `/etc/...`, `apt`/`dnf`, `systemd-resolved`,
  90:   `nft`/`ip route`, `tc`/`netem`).
  91: - Hard gate: `ensure_live_lab_profile_linux_only()` at
  92:   `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs:5445` rejects any non-Linux node
  93:   with `requires platform=linux remote_shell=posix
  94:   guest_exec_mode=linux_bash service_manager=systemd`.
  95: - Windows sidecar runs after Linux stages finish:
  96:   `run_windows_orchestration_stages()` at
  97:   `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs:4954-5138`. Three stages only:
  98:   `bootstrap_windows_host`, `validate_windows_client_install`,
  99:   `validate_windows_mesh_join` (deferred / unimplemented).
 100: 
 101: ### 3.2 Existing platform abstractions (unused by stages)
 102: Defined in `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs`:
 103: - `VmGuestPlatform` (~line 500): Linux, Macos, Windows, Ios, Android.
 104: - `VmRemoteShell` (~line 575): Posix, Powershell, Unsupported.
 105: - `VmGuestExecMode` (~line 602): LinuxBash, MacosPosix, WindowsPowershell,
 106:   Unsupported.
 107: - `VmServiceManager` (~line 632): Systemd, Launchd, WindowsService,
 108:   Unsupported.
 109: - `VmPlatformProfile` (~line 660) bundles all four; `default_platform_profile()`
 110:   (~line 675) maps each OS to correct defaults.
 111: 
 112: These types exist and parse correctly. **Stages do not dispatch on them.**
 113: 
 114: ### 3.3 Daemon cross-platform status
 115: - Linux: production target, well-evidenced.
 116: - Windows: `rustynetd --windows-service --env-file …` runs;
 117:   `windows-unsupported` and opt-in `windows-wireguard-nt` backend labels
 118:   exist behind the backend abstraction; no reviewed Windows backend ships
 119:   yet (see [WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md](./WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md)
 120:   §"Current Repo Truth"). Windows runtime paths under
 121:   `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\…`, DPAPI passphrase custody, named-pipe IPC, and
 122:   service-installer ACL repair already landed in Phase 2.
 123: - macOS daemon: builds POSIX but is untested as a guest. Out of scope here.
 124: - iOS / Android: out of scope.
 125: 
 126: ### 3.4 VM inventory
 127: - `debian-headless-1` … `debian-headless-5` cover the five Linux peer roles.
 128: - `windows-utm-1` is `include_in_all=false`, `lab_role=windows_client`,
 129:   sidecar-only today.

 141: ## 4) Non-Negotiable Constraints
 142: 
 143: These come from `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `documents/SecurityMinimumBar.md`,
 144: and the existing related plans. They override every choice in this plan.
 145: 
 146: 1. **One hardened execution path per security-sensitive workflow.** No
 147:    runtime fallback, downgrade, or legacy branch in production paths. The
 148:    dispatcher selects an OS-specific implementation; once selected it is the
 149:    only path.
 150: 2. **Default-deny.** ACL, routes, DNS, trust state. The dispatcher must not
 151:    relax this on any OS.
 152: 3. **Fail closed** when trust/security state is missing, invalid, stale,
 153:    replayed, or unauthorized. A stage that cannot verify its security
 154:    guarantee on a given OS must refuse to run on that OS rather than skip
 155:    the check.
 156: 4. **No custom crypto, no custom VPN protocol invention.** WireGuard remains
 157:    a backend adapter. Cross-OS work does not get to invent shortcuts.
 158: 5. **No WireGuard / OS specifics leaking into protocol-agnostic crates.** OS
 159:    adapters live behind the backend / orchestrator abstractions.
 160: 6. **Argv-only privileged exec.** No `cmd.exe /c …` and no PowerShell string
 161:    interpolation with untrusted input on Windows. No shell construction
 162:    with untrusted values on Linux.
 163: 7. **Strict key custody.** OS keystore (DPAPI on Windows; OS keystore on
 164:    Linux when available) else encrypted-at-rest fallback with strict
 165:    permissions and startup permission checks. Never log key material.
 166: 8. **No TODO/FIXME/placeholders in completed deliverables.**
 167: 9. **Each implemented security control has both an enforcement point in
 168:    code and a verification method** (unit test, integration test, negative
 169:    test, or gate check). Negative tests are mandatory for every fail-closed
 170:    claim.
 171: 10. **macOS / iOS / Android stubs must reject explicitly with a clear
 172:     blocker reason.** No silent "no-op success" branches.
 173: 11. **Linux behavior must not regress.** All existing Linux gates pass on
 174:     every increment.
 175: 12. **Mandatory gates** (CLAUDE.md §7) run for every substantial increment:
 176:     `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -D warnings`, `cargo check`,
 177:     `cargo test`, `cargo audit --deny warnings`,
 178:     `cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories`, plus any
 179:     scope-specific gate scripts.
 180: 
 181: ## 5) Security-Parity Matrix (Windows-First)
 182: 
 183: For each existing Linux orchestrator-enforced control, list the Windows
 184: equivalent that must exist before a Windows guest can fill any of the five
 185: peer slots. Mac/iOS/Android entries are intentionally `Stub only — out of
 186: scope this delta`.
 187: 
 188: | # | Control (Linux today) | Windows equivalent required | Status today |
 189: |---|---|---|---|
 190: | 1 | Service hardening: systemd unit with `NoNewPrivileges`, `ProtectSystem=strict`, `ReadOnlyPaths`, etc. | Windows Service running under restricted virtual SID; binary path ACL'd to SYSTEM+Admins; no interactive desktop; recovery action defined; service-image-path drift detection | Service exists (`crates/rustynetd/src/windows_service.rs`); hardening profile + verifier still needed |
 191: | 2 | Privileged exec: argv-only, no shell construction | `CreateProcess` with explicit argv; never `cmd.exe /c`; never PowerShell string concat with untrusted input; helper exec audited end-to-end | Recent commit `f838a76` hardened helper exec; full audit pending |
 192: | 3 | Config dir perms: `/etc/rustynet` 0700, owner check at startup | `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\` ACL: SYSTEM + Administrators full, Users denied; startup ACL verifier; fail-closed if drift; orchestrator stage that re-verifies on the live guest | Phase 2 installer repairs ACLs; explicit startup verifier + orchestrator stage missing |
 193: | 4 | Key custody: OS keystore else encrypted-at-rest with permission check | DPAPI machine scope (or CNG NCrypt) for runtime passphrase; encrypted-at-rest fallback with same ACL check; no plaintext key on disk; orchestrator stage validates the live state | DPAPI passphrase custody landed (Phase 2); orchestrator-side validation stage missing |
 194: | 5 | DNS fail-closed in protected mode | NRPT rules + interface-bound resolver; orchestrator stage applies, validates, and runs a negative test that proves bypass is impossible | Stage missing on Windows |
 195: | 6 | Default-deny ACL applied + verified by traffic test | Same protocol layer (daemon-enforced); traffic-test probe must run from a Windows node and confirm denies | Probe harness Linux-shell-only today |
 196: | 7 | Signed trust state + anti-replay before mutation | Protocol-layer, daemon-side; cross-platform if the Windows daemon takes the same code path | Verify the Windows daemon takes the shared path and not a parallel branch |
 197: | 8 | Wrapper-script hygiene: shell wrappers must dispatch to Rust only and fail closed | Same rule on Windows: no PowerShell wrapper that does anything beyond dispatch; argv-only | Audit pending |
 198: | 9 | Binary integrity at install (signed release artifact + checksum) | Authenticode signature verification on the Windows binary before service registration; reject unsigned | Not enforced today |
 199: | 10 | Membership and assignment distribution under owner-checked dir | Same on Windows under `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\membership` and `\trust`, with the same ownership/ACL invariants | Path layout exists; stage that distributes membership/assignment to a Windows peer missing |
 200: 
 201: Each row, when implemented, must produce: (a) enforcement code, (b) an
 202: orchestrator stage that verifies it on a live Windows guest, (c) a negative
 203: test that proves it fails closed.
 204: 
 205: ## 6) Architecture Plan
 206: 
 207: ### 6.1 `StageOrchestrator` trait
 208: New trait in `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/`:
 209: 
 210: - One method per live-lab stage (or a single `execute_stage(stage_id,
 211:   &[RemoteTarget])` enum-driven entry, to be decided at first impl).
 212: - Two real impls land in P1:
 213:   - `LinuxBashOrchestrator`: wraps the existing
 214:     `scripts/e2e/live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh` for back-compat. Used when
 215:     every node in a stage's target set is Linux.
 216:   - `RustOrchestrator`: dispatches per-target on `VmPlatformProfile`
 217:     (service manager, remote shell, paths). Used when any node is non-Linux,
 218:     or when invoked under an explicit migration flag for a Linux-only run.
 219: - Stage outputs converge on a single typed report. No "which orchestrator
 220:   ran" branching downstream.
 221: 
 222: ### 6.2 Capability-based stage gating
 223: Replace `ensure_live_lab_profile_linux_only` with per-stage capability
 224: declarations. Each stage declares:
 225: 
 226: - required capabilities (e.g. `requires_capability(NetemImpairment)`),
 227: - supported OS variants and the specific reason any unsupported variant is
 228:   rejected.
 229: 
 230: A stage that cannot run on a given target's OS skips with an explicit
 231: recorded reason. A stage whose security guarantee cannot be verified on a
 232: target's OS does **not** skip — it fails the run. Distinguish these two
 233: cases in the report.
 234: 
 235: ### 6.3 Per-OS adapters
 236: - `ServiceManager` adapter trait: systemd | windows-service | launchd
 237:   (stub) | unsupported. Operations: install, enable, start, stop, status,
 238:   uninstall.
 239: - `RuntimePaths` adapter trait: returns canonical config / membership /
 240:   trust / logs / secrets roots per OS. Linux + Windows real, macOS stub.
 241: - `RemoteExec` adapter: argv-only command dispatch over the configured
 242:   remote-shell channel (POSIX SSH, WinRM/SSH+PowerShell). Already partially
 243:   exists for Windows sidecar; consolidate.
 244: - `DaemonProbe` adapter: typed daemon-reported state (mesh join, ACL
 245:   effective set, DNS resolver state). Cross-platform because it is
 246:   daemon-driven, not host-shell-driven.
 247: 
 248: ### 6.4 Test harness moves to daemon-driven probes where possible
 249: Replace shell `nc` / `ping` / `curl` traffic checks with daemon-issued probes
 250: that report typed results. Removes the per-OS shell divergence and gives
 251: one hardened parser path per check (consistent with the wider Phase G
 252: direction in `ShellToRustMigrationPlan_2026-03-06.md`).
 253: 
 254: ### 6.5 Linux-only capabilities stay Linux-only
 255: Examples: `tc`/`netem` cross-network impairment, `nftables` forwarding
 256: introspection. These are kernel-feature-bound; declare them as
 257: Linux-capability stages and skip-with-reason when the target is Windows.
 258: Do not fake or simulate them.
 259: 
 260: ## 7) Phased Plan
 261: 
 262: Each phase ends with: code change, code-side verifier, negative test, gate
 263: re-run, doc status update in this file.
 264: 
 265: ### Phase W0 — Doc + capture baseline (this plan)
 266: - Land this delta plan and index it. **(in progress)**
 267: - Capture an evidence baseline: current `vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab`
 268:   stage list, current Linux-only gate, current Windows sidecar surface, with
 269:   exact file:line refs (already inline in §3).
 270: 
 271: Exit: this document is committed and indexed.
 272: 
 273: ### Phase W1 — Security parity gates 1 (config dir + DNS fail-closed)
 274: Closes matrix rows 3 and 5.
 275: 
 276: - W1.1 Implement Windows runtime-dir startup ACL verifier in `rustynetd`
 277:   Windows path. SYSTEM + Administrators only, deny Users, deny Everyone.
 278:   Daemon refuses to start if drifted. Negative test: drift the ACL, expect
 279:   startup refusal with exact error code.
 280: - W1.2 Implement orchestrator stage `validate_windows_runtime_acls` that
 281:   runs the verifier against a live guest and reports per-path results.
 282: - W1.3 Implement Windows DNS fail-closed enforcement (NRPT + interface-bound
 283:   resolver) in the runtime path. Daemon-side enforcement; orchestrator
 284:   applies and validates.
 285: - W1.4 Implement orchestrator stage `validate_windows_dns_failclosed`. Must
 286:   include a negative test that attempts a bypass (e.g. setting a rogue DNS
 287:   server on the test interface) and confirms the daemon shuts the path down.
 288: - W1.5 Run mandatory gates plus any Windows-specific gate scripts.
 289: 
 290: Exit: a Windows guest can pass the same DNS-fail-closed and config-dir-ACL
 291: guarantees the Linux nodes pass. Status of each item recorded inline in
 292: §10.
 293: 
 294: ### Phase W2 — Security parity gates 2 (key custody + binary integrity + exec audit)
 295: Closes matrix rows 1, 2, 4, 8, 9.
 296: 
 297: - W2.1 Authenticode signature verification on the Windows binary before
 298:   service registration in the bootstrap provider. Reject unsigned. Negative
 299:   test with a tampered binary.
 300: - W2.2 Service hardening profile verifier (restricted SID, no interactive
 301:   desktop, image-path pin, recovery action). Daemon-side verifier and
 302:   orchestrator stage `validate_windows_service_hardening`.
 303: - W2.3 Audit every Windows `CreateProcess` / shell-out call site for
 304:   argv-only discipline. Add lints / tests where feasible to prevent
 305:   reintroduction.
 306: - W2.4 Daemon-side validator that confirms key material is DPAPI-protected
 307:   at rest and not present in plaintext. Orchestrator stage
 308:   `validate_windows_key_custody`.
 309: - W2.5 Wrapper-hygiene audit (no PowerShell wrapper does anything beyond
 310:   argv-only dispatch).
 311: - W2.6 Run mandatory gates.
 312: 
 313: Exit: Windows guest passes the matrix rows 1, 2, 4, 8, 9 with code +
 314: verifier + negative test for each.
 315: 
 316: ### Phase W3 — Orchestrator dispatcher (`StageOrchestrator` trait)
 317: - W3.1 Define `StageOrchestrator` trait + `LinuxBashOrchestrator` impl that
 318:   wraps the existing bash script. Behavior unchanged for pure-Linux runs.
 319: - W3.2 Define `ServiceManager`, `RuntimePaths`, `RemoteExec`, `DaemonProbe`
 320:   adapter traits with Linux + Windows real impls and macOS / iOS / Android
 321:   `Unsupported` stubs. Negative tests assert each stub rejects with a clear
 322:   blocker reason.
 323: - W3.3 Land `RustOrchestrator` impl that dispatches per-target on
 324:   `VmPlatformProfile`. For pure-Linux node sets, it must produce
 325:   byte-identical (or behaviorally equivalent — to be defined precisely
 326:   before the swap) reports to the bash impl. No silent divergence.
 327: - W3.4 Run mandatory gates plus the full Linux live-lab gate to prove no
 328:   regression on the reference path.
 329: 
 330: Exit: dispatcher exists and Linux runs are unaffected. Windows runs still
 331: go through the sidecar path until Phase W4.
 332: 
 333: ### Phase W4 — Per-stage capability gating + Windows mesh-join
 334: - W4.1 Replace `ensure_live_lab_profile_linux_only` with per-stage
 335:   capability checks. Stages that require kernel features unavailable on
 336:   Windows (e.g. `tc`/`netem`) skip-with-reason; stages that enforce
 337:   security guarantees that have no Windows verifier yet **fail** the run
 338:   rather than skip.
 339: - W4.2 Implement Windows mesh-join stage (currently deferred at
 340:   `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs:5132`). Membership + assignment
 341:   ingestion via the existing Windows IPC path, with the same signed-state
 342:   + anti-replay guarantees.
 343: - W4.3 Implement Windows traffic-test peer participation. Daemon-driven
 344:   probes in/out of the Windows node confirm default-deny and selected
 345:   allows. Negative tests for both directions.
 346: - W4.4 Implement Windows route + DNS lifecycle stages within the lab
 347:   orchestrator (consume rather than re-implement the daemon-side route/DNS
 348:   truth from [WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md](./WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md)
 349:   §"Route And DNS Runtime Truth").
 350: - W4.5 Run mandatory gates plus a 4×Linux + 1×Windows live-lab run as the
 351:   first heterogeneous proof. Capture artifacts under
 352:   `artifacts/orchestrator_w4/<UTC-timestamp>/`.
 353: 
 354: Exit: any one of the five peer slots can be Windows. The orchestrator
 355: stops gating on `platform=linux` and gates on per-stage capability
 356: declarations instead.
 357: 
 358: ### Phase W5 — Stretch: 5×Windows and mixed-arrangement matrices
 359: - W5.1 5×Windows live-lab run. Likely requires extra Windows guests in the
 360:   inventory; track that ask in `vm_lab_inventory.json` updates.
 361: - W5.2 Random arrangements (e.g. Windows as exit; Windows as relay; two
 362:   Windows + three Linux) covered by a matrix runner.
 363: - W5.3 Promote Windows posture in the release matrix only after this
 364:   evidence exists **and** the [WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md](./WindowsWorkingNodePlan_2026-04-17.md)
 365:   §"Definition Of Done" has independently been met.
 366: 
 367: Exit: heterogeneous topology evidence is current and reproducible.
 368: 
 369: ### Stub-only (kept for future)
 370: - `ServiceManager::Launchd` stub returning `Unsupported("macos
 371:   orchestration not yet implemented")`.
 372: - `RuntimePaths` macOS stub returning `Unsupported(...)`.
 373: - iOS / Android: `VmGuestPlatform` variants stay; no provider; tests assert
 374:   rejection.
 375: - A future delta will fill these in. Do not delete the variants in this
 376:   delta even if they are unused.

 384: - `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features`
 385: - `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features`
 386: - `cargo audit --deny warnings`
 387: - `cargo deny check bans licenses sources advisories`
 388: 
 389: Scope-specific:
 390: 
 391: - `./scripts/ci/phase9_gates.sh`
 392: - `./scripts/ci/phase10_gates.sh`
 393: - `./scripts/ci/membership_gates.sh`
 394: - Active-phase gate scripts as they emerge under the Windows / orchestrator
 395:   scope.
 396: 
 397: Live-lab evidence (capture under `artifacts/`):
 398: 
 399: - pre-change baseline: 5×Linux live-lab run on the current main, archive the
 400:   report;
 401: - per-phase: re-run 5×Linux to prove no regression;
 402: - W4 milestone: 4×Linux + 1×Windows live-lab run, archive report and the
 403:   per-stage capability decisions;
 404: - W5 milestone: heterogeneous matrix runs.
 405: 
 406: Negative tests are mandatory for every fail-closed claim. A stage that
 407: cannot demonstrate fail-closed on the live guest does not count as
 408: complete.
 409: 
 410: ## 9) Rollback Strategy
 411: 
 412: - Use git history for rollback; do not keep parallel active orchestrator
 413:   paths in tree.
 414: - During W3, the `LinuxBashOrchestrator` impl preserves byte-/behavior-
 415:   level parity with the current bash script. If `RustOrchestrator` shows
 416:   divergence on a Linux-only run, revert the dispatcher selection (still
 417:   one path) rather than running both side by side.
 418: - The Linux-only gate is removed only at W4.1, after W1, W2, W3 are
 419:   complete and all Linux gates still pass on the dispatcher path. Until
 420:   then, Windows continues to run as the sidecar.

 574: - [x] W1.3 Windows DNS fail-closed verifier (verifier-side; runtime
 575:       enforcement gated on working Windows backend)
 576:   - Changed files:
 577:     - `crates/rustynetd/src/windows_dns_failclosed.rs` (new) — typed
 578:       `WindowsInterfaceDnsEntry`, `WindowsNrptRule`,
 579:       `WindowsDnsFailclosedSnapshot`, `WindowsDnsFailclosedReport`
 580:       (schema_version=1). Pure aggregator
 581:       `evaluate_windows_dns_failclosed_snapshot` walks the snapshot
 582:       once and returns every drift reason in one pass. The reviewed
 583:       RustyNet contract: (a) every host network interface has either
 584:       an empty DNS server list or loopback servers only
 585:       (`127.0.0.0/8` for IPv4, `::1` for IPv6) — anything else is a
 586:       bypass route; (b) at least one NRPT rule covers the root
 587:       namespace (`.`) with name servers that are all loopback, so
 588:       unqualified lookups also stay on the daemon resolver; (c) every
 589:       captured NRPT rule's name-server set is a subset of loopback
 590:       addresses — a single non-loopback NRPT entry would let a
 591:       crafted name leak past the daemon. Cross-platform:
 592:       `cfg(windows)` collector
 593:       `collect_windows_dns_failclosed_snapshot` shells to a static
 594:       PowerShell probe script that calls `Get-DnsClientServerAddress`
 595:       + `Get-DnsClientNrptRule` and emits typed JSON. The script body
 596:       is a hardcoded `&str` constant with zero runtime-data
 597:       interpolation, so the privileged-boundary argv-only / no-shell-
 598:       construction discipline still holds. Off-Windows the collector
 599:       returns a `requires a Windows runtime host` blocker error so
 600:       the verifier still fails closed without fabricating a passing
 601:       snapshot. The probe script tolerates `Get-DnsClientNrptRule`
 602:       being absent on certain SKUs by falling back to an empty rule
 603:       list — the evaluator then surfaces the missing-NRPT drift, so
 604:       the contract still gates rather than silently passing.
 605:     - `crates/rustynetd/src/lib.rs` — exposed the new module.

 609:       dispatch). `--no-fail-on-drift` is report-only for diagnostics
 610:       against a known-incomplete state (e.g. before runtime

 742: ### Phase W2 (Security parity gates 2: key custody + binary integrity + exec audit)
 743: - [x] W2.1 Authenticode signature **presence** verification (W2.1a)
 744:   - Changed files:
 745:     - `crates/rustynetd/src/windows_authenticode.rs` (new) — pure-Rust PE
 746:       parser (no `unsafe`, no external crates). Walks the DOS header → PE
 747:       header → COFF header → optional header (PE32 or PE32+) → data
 748:       directories → Certificate Table directory entry, then iterates
 749:       `WIN_CERTIFICATE` entries with 8-byte alignment. Recognises
 750:       revision=0x0200 (`WIN_CERT_REVISION_2_0`) + type=0x0002
 751:       (`WIN_CERT_TYPE_PKCS_SIGNED_DATA`) as a valid Authenticode entry.
 752:       Typed `WindowsAuthenticodeReport` (schema_version=1, binary_path,
 753:       binary_size_bytes, overall_ok, signature_present,
 754:       certificate_table_offset, certificate_table_size, certificates,
 755:       drift_reasons). Public `inspect_authenticode_signature(path)` that
 756:       reads the binary and returns the report.
 757:     - `crates/rustynetd/src/lib.rs` — exposed the new module.
 758:     - `crates/rustynetd/src/main.rs` — added subcommand
 759:       `windows-authenticode-check [--binary-path <path>] [--no-fail-on-drift]`.
 760:       Default binary path = `C:\Program Files\RustyNet\rustynetd.exe`.
 761:       Default behavior is fail-closed.
 762:     - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs` — added live-lab stage
 763:       `validate_windows_authenticode` between
 764:       `validate_windows_key_custody` and the deferred
 765:       `validate_windows_mesh_join`. Stage skips when an earlier stage
 766:       didn't pass; otherwise dispatches the new subcommand and parses the
 767:       typed JSON report. Pure parser/evaluator extracted as
 768:       `evaluate_windows_authenticode_report` for direct unit testing.
 769:       Raw report archived under
 770:       `report_dir/logs/validate_windows_authenticode.log`.

 785:       +6 evaluator tests covering: signed payload accept w/ identity-rich

 793:   - Residual risk:
 794:     - **Presence check only.** This slice rejects unsigned binaries and
 795:       malformed signatures, but does NOT validate the PKCS#7 SignedData
 796:       payload, the certificate chain, the file-hash binding via
 797:       `spcIndirectData`, or timestamp validity. An attacker who can
 798:       produce a self-signed Authenticode entry will pass this gate. Full
 799:       chain validation requires Win32 `WinVerifyTrust` (W2.1b — adds
 800:       `Win32_Security_WinTrust` feature to `windows-sys` deps and a
 801:       safe wrapper in `rustynet-windows-native`). **Closed by W2.1b
 802:       below.**
 803:     - The PE parser is targeted at well-formed PE32+ binaries. It bounds-
 804:       checks every read, but unusual layouts (overlapping cert table and
 805:       sections, etc.) may fail to parse. That's still fail-closed
 806:       behavior; the daemon refuses to start.
 807:     - The orchestrator stage assumes the installed binary lives at
 808:       `C:\Program Files\RustyNet\rustynetd.exe`. Same constant
 809:       reconciliation note as W1.2b / W2.2.
 810: - [x] W2.1b Full Authenticode chain validation via `WinVerifyTrust`
 811:   - Changed files:
 812:     - `crates/rustynet-windows-native/Cargo.toml` — added
 813:       `Win32_Security_WinTrust` to the windows-sys feature list so
 814:       the FFI types (`WINTRUST_DATA`, `WINTRUST_FILE_INFO`,
 815:       `WINTRUST_ACTION_GENERIC_VERIFY_V2`, etc.) are available on
 816:       the Windows target.
 817:     - `crates/rustynet-windows-native/src/lib.rs` — added the
 818:       `AuthenticodeChainOutcome` public enum (`Verified` |
 819:       `Untrusted { reason, hresult }`) and the
 820:       `verify_authenticode_chain(path)` wrapper. Off-Windows the fn
 821:       returns an `Err` blocker. On Windows the fn calls
 822:       `WinVerifyTrust` with `WINTRUST_ACTION_GENERIC_VERIFY_V2`,
 823:       `WTD_REVOCATION_CHECK_CHAIN_EXCLUDE_ROOT` (root certs
 824:       typically self-signed; checking everything below the root is
 825:       the canonical Authenticode posture), `WTD_UI_NONE` (no UI), and
 826:       always pairs the verify call with a follow-up
 827:       `WTD_STATEACTION_CLOSE` cleanup so verifier state never leaks
 828:       into subsequent calls. Non-zero HRESULTs are mapped to the
 829:       canonical Win32 label set (`TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE`,
 830:       `CERT_E_UNTRUSTEDROOT`, `CERT_E_REVOKED`, `TRUST_E_BAD_DIGEST`,
 831:       etc.) so the orchestrator-side log is human-readable rather
 832:       than a hex code. Cross-target check
 833:       (`cargo check -p rustynet-windows-native --target
 834:       x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) clean.
 835:     - `crates/rustynetd/src/windows_authenticode.rs` — extended
 836:       the report shape: new `WindowsAuthenticodeChainStatus` enum
 837:       (`Verified` | `Untrusted { reason, hresult }` |
 838:       `NotEvaluated { reason }`) with serde tag `outcome`; new
 839:       `chain_status` field on `WindowsAuthenticodeReport`; module
 840:       header rewritten to reflect the two-stage (presence + chain)
 841:       verification posture.
 842:       `inspect_authenticode_signature` now runs both stages and
 843:       tightens `overall_ok` to require BOTH `signature_present` AND
 844:       `chain_status == Verified`. The chain stage is *skipped* when
 845:       the presence stage already rejected the binary (running
 846:       WinVerifyTrust on a malformed PE adds no information). Chain-
 847:       stage outcomes are mirrored into `drift_reasons` so callers
 848:       that grep `drift_reasons` only still see the chain-side
 849:       rejection. Off-Windows the chain stage surfaces as
 850:       `NotEvaluated` and `overall_ok` is false — fail-closed when
 851:       the trust state cannot be observed.
 852:     - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs` — orchestrator-side
 853:       `evaluate_windows_authenticode_report` now double-checks
 854:       that `overall_ok=true` implies `chain_status=Verified`
 855:       (rejects a stale or crafted JSON payload that claims
 856:       overall_ok with a weaker chain status). Success summary
 857:       updated to `"Windows Authenticode signature + chain
 858:       verified"` so downstream tooling can grep for the new posture
 859:       (W2.1a's summary said "signature present"). Test fixture
 860:       updated to set `chain_status: { outcome: 'verified' }` in the
 861:       reviewed-payload helper.
 862:   - Verification:
 863:     - `cargo fmt -p rustynetd -p rustynet-cli -p rustynet-windows-native -- --check` clean.
 864:     - `cargo check -p rustynet-windows-native --target
 865:       x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` clean (FFI compiles against
 866:       `Win32_Security_WinTrust`).
 867:     - `cargo test -p rustynetd` — 441 lib + 52 bin + 3 integration
 868:       pass (was 439 lib + 52 + 3). +2 new lib tests for the
 869:       report's new chain_status variants:
 870:       `report_round_trips_chain_status_untrusted_variant`,
 871:       `report_round_trips_chain_status_not_evaluated_variant`.
 872:     - `cargo test -p rustynet-cli --bin rustynet-cli` — 450 / 450
 873:       pass (was 447). +3 new evaluator tests:
 874:       `evaluate_windows_authenticode_report_rejects_overall_ok_true_with_untrusted_chain`,
 875:       `evaluate_windows_authenticode_report_rejects_overall_ok_true_with_not_evaluated_chain`,
 876:       `evaluate_windows_authenticode_report_accepts_payload_with_verified_chain`.
 877:   - Residual risk:
 878:     - `WinVerifyTrust` does network I/O for revocation checks
 879:       (CRL/OCSP fetch). On a fully air-gapped Windows host the
 880:       revocation check returns `CRYPT_E_REVOCATION_OFFLINE` and the
 881:       chain stage rejects. This is fail-closed by design; an
 882:       operator deploying RustyNet to an air-gapped network should
 883:       pre-cache the revocation responses or pre-validate the
 884:       release artefact's trust chain at build time and ship a
 885:       signed-attestation alongside the binary.
 886:     - The chain validation is gated behind a presence-stage pass.
 887:       An attacker could in principle craft a PE that the presence
 888:       parser accepts but `WinVerifyTrust` would also reject — that
 889:       case lands in the `Untrusted` branch and `overall_ok` is
 890:       still false. The skip-on-presence-fail behavior is purely a
 891:       no-info-gain optimisation, not a security relaxation.
 892:     - Live evidence on the actual `windows-utm-1` UTM guest is
 893:       pending — the Windows VM's installed binary is an unsigned
 894:       `cargo build --release` artefact, so the chain stage will
 895:       report `Untrusted { TRUST_E_NOSIGNATURE }` (or skip with
 896:       `NotEvaluated` if presence stage's pure-Rust parser rejects
 897:       first). Real signed-binary evidence requires the production
 898:       release-signing workflow to ship and is tracked separately
 899:       under `documents/operations/active/Phase5ReleaseReadinessChecklist_2026-04-12.md`.

 905:       returns every drift reason in one pass, `build_windows_service_hardening_report`
 906:       wrapper, best-effort `parse_windows_image_path_argv` for the SCM
 907:       `ImagePath` string, and a `cfg(windows)` snapshot collector that
 908:       queries the live SCM via the existing `windows-service` crate

 986: - [x] W2.3 Argv-only audit for Windows exec sites
 987:   - Findings:
 988:     - All `Command::new("ssh"|"scp"|"git"|"cargo"|"bash"|utmctl)` sites in
 989:       `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/` use Rust's `Command::arg(...)` /
 990:       `args(...)` API, which builds `argv` arrays and passes them to
 991:       `execve` with no shell interpretation. No `cmd.exe /c` or
 992:       shell-string constructions found in active production paths.
 993:     - PowerShell script bodies that get sent over the SSH channel are
 994:       built by `build_windows_helper_command` and similar helpers in
 995:       `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs`, which run every
 996:       interpolated path / value through `powershell_quote` (single-quoted
 997:       PS literal w/ proper `'` → `''` escape) and pre-flight every
 998:       string with `ensure_no_control_chars`. Long flags matching
 999:       `--[A-Za-z0-9-]+` pass through unquoted (PS parser treats them as
1000:       tokens). Short / value args always get quoted. The whole script
1001:       body is then base64-encoded and dispatched as
1002:       `powershell.exe -EncodedCommand <b64>` — the encoding step makes
1003:       the SSH-layer transport oblivious to PS quoting concerns.
1004:     - The Windows service host registration path
1005:       (`crates/rustynetd/src/windows_service.rs`) uses the
1006:       `windows-service` crate's typed `ServiceManager::create_service`
1007:       API, which passes the binary path and args through Win32 SCM
1008:       structs (no shell). Audit confirmed via cargo-source review at
1009:       `~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-…/windows-service-0.8.0`.
1010:   - Hardening landed in this slice:
1011:     - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs` — extracted shared builder
1012:       `build_windows_security_check_invocation(subcommand, extra_args)`.
1013:       The builder rejects subcommands that are empty or contain anything
1014:       other than ASCII-alphanumeric + hyphen (so a future caller cannot
1015:       sneak a metacharacter through), runs every value-arg through
1016:       `powershell_quote` w/ `ensure_no_control_chars`, lets well-formed
1017:       `--long-flag` tokens pass unquoted, and emits a
1018:       single-quoted-literal `& 'C:\Program Files\RustyNet\rustynetd.exe'
1019:       <subcommand> --no-fail-on-drift [...]`. All four W1.2/W2.2/W2.4/
1020:       W2.1 stage helpers now route through this builder instead of
1021:       hand-rolled `format!` — single audit point.
1022:     - 6 new unit tests in `vm_lab::tests` covering: well-formed
1023:       invocation shape (quoted exe path + subcommand + fail-closed flag);
1024:       rejection of subcommands carrying `;`, backticks, `$`, spaces,
1025:       apostrophes, or empty string; apostrophe in a value arg gets
1026:       doubled (`'` → `''`) and the resulting script keeps its
1027:       single-quote count even (balanced literal); control-byte arg
1028:       rejected; long-flag passes unquoted; positional / short arg gets
1029:       quoted.

1635:         3. SSH + PowerShell atomic install: `Move-Item -Force

1643:            Mirrors the bash orchestrator's
1644:            `distribute_membership_worker` semantics on Linux peers
1645:            (`root install` + `rm -f watermark`).
1646:       Every PowerShell-boundary value (canonical paths, watermark
1647:       path, staging filename) is wrapped through `powershell_quote`
1648:       so the boundary is the same audited single-quoted-PS-literal
1649:       pattern the W2.x security validators use.

1678:       is correct and ready — the file is in the daemon-expected
1679:       location, with the daemon-expected ACL inherited from the
1680:       W1.1-reviewed `membership\` root, with the watermark cleared
1681:       so the next refresh tick re-ingests. When the Windows backend
1682:       ships, this code is the unblocker for live mesh-join evidence
1683:       on the W4.2 verifier.
1684:     - **Membership-only this slice.** Assignment, traversal, and
1685:       DNS-zone bundles follow the same scp + atomic-install
1686:       pattern but each lands in their own canonical Windows path
1687:       (`C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\trust\`,
1688:       `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet\…assignment`, etc. per
1689:       `crates/rustynetd/src/windows_paths.rs`). Each is a
1690:       mechanical follow-up to this slice; the orchestrator's
1691:       distribution code path does not need re-architecting.
1692:     - **Not yet wired into orchestrator stage sequence.** The
1693:       helper is exported as a `pub fn` callable from the
1694:       orchestrator code path but is not yet referenced from
1695:       `run_windows_orchestration_stages_with_options`. Wiring it
1696:       into the heterogeneous live-lab orchestration sequence is
1697:       W4.3/W4.5 territory (the live-lab run that pulls a snapshot
1698:       from the Linux exit and pushes to the Windows peer end-to-
1699:       end). The CLI subcommand surface that exposes the helper to
1700:       operators (`ops vm-lab-distribute-windows-membership` or
1701:       similar) is also a follow-up.
1702:     - **Multi-snapshot collision window.** If two operators
1703:       simultaneously distribute a snapshot to the same Windows
1704:       guest, the staging filenames collide with negligible
1705:       probability (32-hex u128) but the canonical-path Move-Item
1706:       could race between the second SCP and the first install.
1707:       The reviewed Move-Item is `-Force` so it overwrites
1708:       atomically; the second operator's snapshot wins. Operators
1709:       who need strict serialisation should coordinate via the
1710:       existing membership-owner lock (out of orchestrator scope).

   1: # Phase 3 Dependency And Policy Cleanup Checklist
   2: 
   3: Prepared: 2026-04-12

  43:   Evidence:
  44:   - code: `crates/rustynet-cli/src/main.rs`
  45:   - code: `crates/rustynet-cli/src/ops_e2e.rs`
  46:   - code: `crates/rustynet-cli/src/ops_install_systemd.rs`
  47:   - code: `crates/rustynet-cli/src/ops_phase9.rs`
  48:   - code: `crates/rustynet-control/src/lib.rs`
  49:   - code: `crates/rustynet-relay/src/session.rs`
  50:   - code: `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs`
  51: 
  52: - [x] Phase 3 rationale is written down with rejected alternatives
  53:   Evidence:
  54:   - rationale: this document, “Decision And Rationale”
  55: 
  56: ## Decision And Rationale
  57: 
  58: ### Exact `paste` path
  59: 
  60: The unmaintained `paste` crate was not coming from the Rustynet workspace directly. It entered through the Linux userspace-shared backend path:
  61: 
  62: - `rustynet-backend-wireguard`
  63: - `tun-rs`
  64: - `netconfig-rs` and its route-management helpers
  65: - `paste`
  66: 
  67: That path was removed by replacing `tun-rs` with a narrow in-repo crate, `third_party/rustynet-tun`, which implements only the Linux `/dev/net/tun` behavior that the active backend actually needs.
  68: 
  69: ### Chosen result
  70: 
  71: The accepted Phase 3 result has three parts:
  72: 
  73: 1. Replace `tun-rs` with the in-repo `rustynet-tun` crate for the active Linux userspace-shared path.
  74: 2. Narrow the active `boringtun` dependency surface to an in-repo vendored copy that excludes the policy-blocking license set which was not needed for Rustynet’s active use.
  75: 3. Upgrade direct workspace `rand` usage from `0.8.5` to `0.9.3` and make `OsRng` failure explicit instead of treating it as infallible.
  76: 
  77: This is better for security and maintainability than the previous state because:
  78: 
  79: - it removes the unmaintained `paste` path entirely instead of tolerating it
  80: - it preserves the single hardened userspace-shared execution path instead of adding a fallback
  81: - it avoids policy exceptions, ignore files, or advisory allowlists
  82: - it shrinks the active dependency surface to the minimum code Rustynet actually uses
  83: - it improves failure semantics around OS entropy by making those failure points explicit
  84: 
  85: ### Alternatives considered and rejected
  86: 
  87: - Keep `tun-rs` and add advisory or license exceptions.
  88:   Rejected because it widens policy instead of fixing the dependency path.
  89: 
  90: - Keep upstream `boringtun` as-is and add license-policy exceptions.
  91:   Rejected because the blocked crates were outside the minimal surface Rustynet actually needs, and an exception would preserve unnecessary exposure.
  92: 
  93: - Replace the full userspace-shared backend or the full WireGuard engine in Phase 3.
  94:   Rejected because it is much higher-risk churn than needed to eliminate the actual blockers.
  95: 
  96: - Introduce a non-cryptographic or custom fallback RNG path to avoid `OsRng` failure handling changes.
  97:   Rejected because it would soften the security model. The chosen implementation fails closed instead.
  98: 
  99: ## Validation Evidence
 100: 
 101: - [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check`
 102: - [x] `cargo check -p rustynet-backend-wireguard --offline`
 103: - [x] `cargo test -p rustynet-backend-wireguard --offline`
 104: - [x] `cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --offline`
 105: - [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --offline -- -D warnings`
 106: - [x] `cargo test --workspace --all-targets --all-features --offline`
 107: - [x] `cargo audit --deny warnings`
 108: - [x] `cargo deny check advisories bans licenses sources`

  38:   - Canonical pass reports no longer accept under-specified path evidence; shared-transport identity must be authoritative.
  39:   - Extended-soak evidence no longer allows fallback/drift to hide behind coarse aggregate counters.

 112: ## 1. Executive Summary
 113: This document is the delta plan for making Rustynet behave like a plug-and-play mesh VPN across unrelated networks.
 114: 
 115: The key conclusion is simple:
 116: - **Direct UDP hole punching is necessary but not sufficient.**
 117: - **Ciphertext-only relay fallback is mandatory for robust plug-and-play behavior.**
 118: - **Manual router port forwarding may remain an optional power-user optimization, but it must not be the baseline correctness path.**
 119: 
 120: The repository already contains significant traversal and relay groundwork, but it is not yet a finished, user-transparent transport system. The highest-value remaining work is:
 121: 1. correct public candidate acquisition using the right socket and the right mapped port,
 122: 2. full WAN simultaneous-open behavior on the active runtime path,
 123: 3. real relay runtime integration and live relay transport,
 124: 4. measured evidence and gates for both direct and relay outcomes.
 125: 
 126: ## 2. What This Document Resolves
 127: This document exists because the repository contains both real implementation progress and stale or optimistic status text.
 128: 
 129: Current authoritative truth must come from:
 130: 1. `documents/Requirements.md`
 131: 2. `documents/SecurityMinimumBar.md`
 132: 3. `documents/phase10.md`
 133: 4. current runtime evidence
 134: 5. lower-precedence active plans only insofar as they still match code reality
 135: 
 136: Supporting implementation plan for the remaining production shared-transport delta:
 137: - [ProductionTransportOwningWireGuardBackendPlan_2026-03-31.md](./ProductionTransportOwningWireGuardBackendPlan_2026-03-31.md)
 138: 
 139: Where documents conflict:
 140: - [README.md](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/README.md) and [phase10.md](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/documents/phase10.md) currently state that full production WAN simultaneous-open and full relay transport are still open work.
 141: - some lower-precedence active traversal notes claim more completion than current live evidence supports.
 142: - this document resolves those conflicts in favor of the stricter, runtime-proven interpretation.
 143: 
 144: ## 3. Product Outcome We Are Targeting
 145: The target user experience is:
 146: 1. user installs Rustynet,
 147: 2. user joins a Rustynet using accepted credentials,
 148: 3. another authorized node is selected as an exit,
 149: 4. Rustynet automatically establishes transport:
 150:    - direct UDP if possible,
 151:    - relay if direct is not proven quickly,
 152: 5. traffic routes through the exit node securely,
 153: 6. the user never has to manually configure a home router or understand NAT.
 154: 
 155: The user should not need to know whether the transport is:
 156: - direct to exit, or
 157: - relayed to exit.
 158: 
 159: Diagnostics may expose that distinction, but the baseline UX must not depend on user networking knowledge.
 160: 
 161: ## 4. Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules
 162: 1. **Exit node and relay are different roles.**
 163:    - exit node terminates the encrypted tunnel and forwards internet/LAN traffic,
 164:    - relay only forwards ciphertext packets to help two peers reach each other.
 165: 2. **Relay is not optional for plug-and-play.**
 166:    - some real user networks will never support direct P2P reliably.
 167: 3. **Direct path is an optimization; relay is the correctness fallback.**
 168: 4. **NAT-PMP/PCP/UPnP are opportunistic only.**
 169: 5. **No unsigned endpoint mutation.**
 170: 6. **No programmed-vs-live confusion in status or gates.**
 171: 7. **One hardened path only.**
 172:    - `verified traversal state -> deterministic controller decision -> transport/backend apply`
 173: 8. **Allocated-port relay demux is the chosen production fallback design for this scope.**
 174:    - authenticated-framing relay transport is explicitly out of scope for the current implementation plan.
 175: 
 176: ## 5. External Standards and Primary References
 177: These references define the network reality and security expectations that Rustynet must respect:
 178: 
 179: - RFC 8445 (ICE): candidate gathering, candidate pairs, connectivity checks, nomination, consent model
 180:   - https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8445
 181: - RFC 5389 (STUN): server reflexive discovery primitives
 182:   - https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5389
 183: - RFC 8656 (TURN): relay allocation and relayed transport model
 184:   - https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8656
 185: - RFC 7675 (STUN Consent Freshness): ongoing consent/liveness requirements on an active 5-tuple
 186:   - https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7675
 187: - RFC 4787: NAT UDP behavior variability and mapping/filtering constraints
 188:   - https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc4787
 189: - RFC 5128: P2P across NATs, including when UDP hole punching fails
 190:   - https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5128
 191: - RFC 6887 (PCP): optional port mapping as an optimization, not a universal solution
 192:   - https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6887
 193: - Tailscale engineering write-up on NAT traversal: practical direct-first plus relay fallback operating model
 194:   - https://tailscale.com/blog/how-nat-traversal-works
 195: - Tailscale DERP documentation: public relay fleet behavior, encrypted relay semantics, directory-distributed region selection
 196:   - https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/derp-servers
 197: 
 198: Primary implications for Rustynet:
 199: - direct success depends on NAT behavior and cannot be guaranteed,
 200: - server-reflexive candidates must represent the actual socket/port pair that will later exchange peer traffic,
 201: - relaying is a standard, necessary fallback for hard NAT cases,
 202: - auto port mapping can help but cannot be the main connectivity design,
 203: - active paths need a consent/liveness mechanism that is bound to the actual transport 5-tuple,
 204: - best-in-class systems use relay as a transparent correctness fallback and upgrade to direct only after measured proof.
 205:

 259: - the policy plane is not the blocker,
 260: - the transport plane is the blocker,
 261: - direct WAN traversal is not yet robust in the tested topology,
 262: - relay fallback is still not live enough to recover when direct fails,

 270: ## 8. Critical Current Defects That Must Be Fixed First
 271: These are not optional improvements. They are correctness bugs or architectural gaps.
 272: 
 273: ### 8.1 STUN Candidate Port Is Currently Guessed, Not Discovered
 274: **Files:**
 275: - [crates/rustynetd/src/stun_client.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/stun_client.rs)
 276: - [crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs)
 277: 
 278: **Current behavior:**
 279: - `StunClient::query_stun_server(...)` binds `0.0.0.0:0`, i.e. an ephemeral port.
 280: - `gather_public_ips()` returns only `IpAddr`, not full mapped `SocketAddr`.
 281: - `poll_stun_results()` later reconstructs srflx candidates by attaching `self.wg_listen_port` to the discovered public IP.
 282: 
 283: **Why this is wrong:**
 284: - the NAT mapping observed by STUN is for the ephemeral STUN socket, not necessarily the WireGuard socket,
 285: - the NAT may not preserve the local port,
 286: - attaching `wg_listen_port` to the public IP is a guess, not a measured mapped endpoint,
 287: - this can produce false srflx candidates and failed direct probes.
 288: 
 289: **Required fix:**
 290: - STUN gathering must return the full mapped public `SocketAddr`, not just IP,
 291: - the STUN probe must use the same UDP socket or the same bound local port that later carries peer traffic,
 292: - candidate publication must stop assuming the public port equals `wg_listen_port`.
 293: 
 294: **Minimum implementation direction:**
 295: 1. redesign [crates/rustynetd/src/stun_client.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/stun_client.rs) to return `Vec<SocketAddr>` or richer candidate structs,
 296: 2. stop using `SocketAddr::new(ip, self.wg_listen_port)` in daemon runtime,
 297: 3. tie candidate discovery to the active transport socket semantics.
 298: 
 299: ### 8.2 Relay Client Binds a Separate Ephemeral Socket Despite Its Own Security Comment
 300: **Files:**
 301: - [crates/rustynetd/src/relay_client.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/relay_client.rs)
 302: - [crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs)
 303: 
 304: **Current behavior:**
 305: - `RelayClient::bind(...)` documentation says it should use the same socket as WireGuard traffic so NAT mappings are shared.
 306: - `load_relay_client(...)` currently binds `UdpSocket::bind(..., 0)`, i.e. another ephemeral socket.
 307: 
 308: **Why this is wrong:**
 309: - relay session establishment occurs on a different socket identity than the socket used for actual peer traffic,
 310: - NAT bindings and public source tuples will diverge,
 311: - relay hello/session allocation may not correspond to the transport socket that later sends packets.
 312: 
 313: **Required fix:**
 314: - relay session establishment and relay transport usage must share the active transport socket identity,
 315: - or the backend must be explicitly redesigned so the same socket handles both direct and relay transport.
 316: 
 317: ### 8.3 `rustynet-relay` Main Binary Is Still a Placeholder, Not a Production Relay Service
 318: **Files:**
 319: - [crates/rustynet-relay/src/main.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynet-relay/src/main.rs)
 320: - [crates/rustynet-relay/src/lib.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynet-relay/src/lib.rs)
 321: - [crates/rustynet-relay/src/transport.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynet-relay/src/transport.rs)
 322: 
 323: **Current behavior:**
 324: - the `main.rs` binary only selects a relay from an in-memory fleet and prints a startup line,
 325: - it does not bind a public UDP port,
 326: - it does not deserialize `RelayHello`, manage live sockets, or forward packets between actual peers.
 327: 
 328: **Required fix:**
 329: - implement a real relay daemon binary with public UDP listener(s), hello/ack wire handling, session table, transport forwarding loop, metrics, config, and clean shutdown.
 330: 
 331: ### 8.4 Relay Runtime Exists But Is Not Yet the Product-Correct Fallback Path
 332: **Files:**
 333: - [crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs)
 334: - [crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs)
 335: - [crates/rustynetd/src/relay_client.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/relay_client.rs)
 336: 
 337: **Current symptom:**
 338: - live runs end in `relay_programmed` / `relay_session_disabled` or otherwise unproven relay state instead of `relay_active` with liveness proof.
 339: 
 340: **Required fix:**
 341: - a relay candidate must be backed by a real reachable relay server,
 342: - a relay path must only be considered live when:
 343:   - session token is valid,
 344:   - relay session is established,
 345:   - traffic or fresh handshake proof exists through the relay,
 346:   - no policy or kill-switch invariant is bypassed.
 347: 
 348: ### 8.5 Relay Data-Plane Demultiplexing and On-Wire Session Semantics Are Still Underspecified
 349: **Files:**
 350: - [crates/rustynet-relay/src/transport.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynet-relay/src/transport.rs)
 351: - [crates/rustynet-relay/src/session.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynet-relay/src/session.rs)
 352: - [crates/rustynet-relay/src/main.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynet-relay/src/main.rs)
 353: - [crates/rustynetd/src/relay_client.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynetd/src/relay_client.rs)
 354: 
 355: **Current behavior:**
 356: - `RelayTransport::forward_packet(...)` expects the caller to already know which `session_id` owns an incoming datagram.
 357: - `RelaySession` tracks identity, peer, allocation, and expiry metadata, but not the full live ingress/egress UDP dispatch contract for a running server.
 358: - `main.rs` does not yet define how incoming UDP packets are mapped to sessions on the public listener.
 359: 
 360: **Why this is a problem:**
 361: - the relay wire model is not yet specific enough for an implementation agent to safely fill in the missing pieces without guessing,
 362: - a guessed demultiplexing scheme risks creating multiple transport paths, inconsistent NAT behavior, or a security bug in packet attribution,
 363: - without an explicit dispatch contract, it is easy to accidentally build an open proxy or a session-confusion bug.
 364: 
 365: **Required fix:**
 366: - define one hardened relay data-plane contract and implement only that contract.
 367: - for this scope, the chosen contract is **allocated-port relay demultiplexing**.
 368: - the contract must specify, at minimum:
 369:   1. which UDP port(s) receive hello/auth traffic,
 370:   2. which UDP port(s) receive relayed ciphertext traffic,
 371:   3. how an inbound datagram is attributed to exactly one authenticated relay session by allocated relay port,
 372:   4. how the server distinguishes pre-allocation control traffic from post-allocation ciphertext forwarding traffic,
 373:   5. how the server binds a session to the observed peer transport tuple and refreshes or rejects tuple changes,
 374:   6. how replay, spoofing, stale tuple reuse, and session cross-talk are rejected.
 375: 
 376: **Implementation constraint:**
 377: - implement allocated-port demultiplexing only in production paths for this scope.
 378: - do not add authenticated per-packet relay framing as a second production path.
 379: - if authenticated-framing is ever explored later, it must be introduced only by a new design/change document with separate security review and tests.
 380: 
 381: ## 9. Desired End-State Architecture
 382: ### 9.1 User-Visible Model
 383: The user model must be:
 384: - join network,
 385: - select exit,
 386: - Rustynet connects,
 387: - traffic works.
 388: 
 389: The user must not be asked to:
 390: - configure router port forwards,
 391: - understand STUN, NAT, ICE, TURN, or relays,
 392: - paste public IPs,
 393: - manually choose direct vs relay.
 394: 
 395: ### 9.2 Runtime Transport State Machine
 396: The runtime should converge through a single deterministic controller.
 397: 
 398: Required logical states:
 399: - `direct_programmed`
 400: - `direct_active`
 401: - `relay_programmed`
 402: - `relay_active`
 403: - `mixed_active` only if strictly necessary during transitions and never as a persistent ambiguity
 404: - `fail_closed`
 405: 
 406: Required transition rules:
 407: 1. start with signed traversal authority only,
 408: 2. gather fresh local candidates,
 409: 3. attempt direct via candidate pairs,
 410: 4. if direct is not proven within bounded policy, establish relay,
 411: 5. once relay is live, route via relay,
 412: 6. keep reprobeing direct in the background,
 413: 7. fail back to direct only after fresh proof,
 414: 8. close stale relay sessions after successful direct recovery,
 415: 9. fail closed if neither trusted direct nor trusted relay is available.
 416: 
 417: Active-path liveness requirement:
 418: - Rustynet must maintain ongoing proof that the currently selected path is still permitted and live.
 419: - If Rustynet adopts STUN consent freshness directly, it must follow a request/response model bound to the active 5-tuple.
 420: - If Rustynet instead uses a WireGuard-native or Rustynet-native liveness mechanism, the implementation must document and test why that mechanism is equivalent in security outcome for continuing to send traffic.
 421: - In all cases, the implementation must stop transmitting on an unproven path within a bounded timeout.
 422: 
 423: ### 9.3 Candidate Model
 424: Required candidate classes:
 425: - `host`
 426: - `srflx`
 427: - `relay`
 428: 
 429: Candidate requirements:
 430: - bounded count
 431: - bounded serialized size
 432: - no duplicates
 433: - no RFC1918/CGNAT relay transport candidates for public relay use
 434: - no guessed port numbers
 435: - freshness-bounded signed publication
 436: - no endpoint mutation from unsigned or stale candidate sets
 437: 
 438: ### 9.4 Relay Model
 439: Relay is **not** the exit node.
 440: Relay is a ciphertext forwarder between client and exit.
 441: 
 442: Path options:
 443: - direct: `client <-> exit`
 444: - relayed: `client <-> relay <-> exit`
 445: 
 446: Security requirements:
 447: - relay sees ciphertext only,
 448: - relay never decrypts or rewrites inner payloads,
 449: - relay is token-scoped to specific node pairs and relay IDs,
 450: - relay is not an open proxy,
 451: - relay is bounded and rate-limited.
 452: 
 453: Chosen v1 relay data-plane design:
 454: - post-authentication forwarding uses an **allocated relay UDP port** returned by the relay server,
 455: - the client/backend targets `relay_ip:allocated_port` as the relay endpoint for ciphertext transport,
 456: - the relay attributes inbound ciphertext datagrams to sessions by allocated relay port and session ownership rules,
 457: - authenticated per-packet outer relay framing is **not** part of the v1 production design.
 458: 
 459: Why this choice is correct for the product:
 460: - it matches the current repo shape (`allocated_port` already exists in session and ack models),
 461: - it minimizes custom transport invention,
 462: - it reduces per-packet complexity and MTU overhead,
 463: - it is easier to integrate with the current backend endpoint model,
 464: - it is operationally sufficient for the intended residential/small-network scale.
 465:

 803: ## 13. Security Requirements for the Final Design
 804: ### 13.1 Direct Path Security
 805: - all endpoint hints signed and freshness-bounded
 806: - anti-replay watermarks
 807: - no mutation from assignment `peer.N.endpoint` once enforced traversal mode is active
 808: - bounded probe fanout and timing
 809: - no shell-built probe logic
 810: 
 811: ### 13.2 Relay Security
 812: - ciphertext-only forwarding
 813: - signed session tokens
 814: - constant-time auth comparisons
 815: - nonce replay rejection
 816: - relay binding (`relay_id`)
 817: - peer binding (`node_id`, `peer_node_id`)
 818: - strict scope (`forward_ciphertext_only`)
 819: - rate limits, session caps, idle expiry, max packet bounds
 820: - relay never acts as generic open UDP proxy
 821: - session attribution is deterministic and cannot be confused across peers or tuples
 822: - allocated relay ports are bound to exactly one live authorized session at a time
 823: - expired or cleaned-up relay ports are never reused without clearing prior attribution state
 824: 
 825: ### 13.3 Transition Security
 826: During direct<->relay transitions:
 827: - no cleartext packet escape
 828: - no ACL bypass
 829: - no DNS leak
 830: - no kill-switch disable window
 831: - no unsigned path switch
 832: - no status optimism without proof
 833: 
 834: ### 13.4 Active Path Consent / Liveness Security
 835: - the selected path must have a bounded-expiry proof that the remote side is still willing and able to receive traffic,
 836: - liveness/consent state must be tied to the actual 5-tuple or transport identity in use,
 837: - if consent/liveness expires, Rustynet must stop sending on that path and either fail over or fail closed,
 838: - refresh transactions, if any, must not expose reusable transaction identifiers or secrets to untrusted control-plane or scripting inputs.
 839: 
 840: ## 14. What Correct and Working Looks Like
 841: ### 14.1 Direct Success Case
 842: A correct direct success looks like:
 843: - both peers gather valid local + srflx candidates,
 844: - signed traversal bundles contain correct tuples,
 845: - traversal probe picks a direct pair,
 846: - backend handshake becomes fresh,
 847: - `path_mode=direct_active`,
 848: - `path_live_proven=true`,
 849: - relay not required.
 850: 
 851: ### 14.2 Relay Fallback Case
 852: A correct relay fallback looks like:
 853: - direct probing fails or is denied by NAT profile reality,
 854: - runtime establishes relay session automatically,
 855: - backend sends encrypted traffic through relay endpoint,
 856: - relay forwards ciphertext only,
 857: - traffic flows,
 858: - `path_mode=relay_active`,
 859: - `relay_session_state=live`,
 860: - `path_live_proven=true`.
 861: 
 862: ### 14.3 Failback Case
 863: A correct failback looks like:
 864: - direct path becomes healthy later,
 865: - runtime proves fresh direct handshake,
 866: - transport switches back without policy/leak regression,
 867: - relay session is closed or retained safely until no longer needed,
 868: - status changes honestly to `direct_active`.
 869: 
 870: ## 15. What To Avoid
 871: Do **not** do any of the following:
 872: - do not require manual consumer-router port forwarding for baseline connectivity,
 873: - do not claim “works from anywhere” based only on direct-friendly home NATs,
 874: - do not guess public ports,
 875: - do not use separate ephemeral sockets where transport identity must be shared,
 876: - do not treat relay fleet-selection code as a real relay service,
 877: - do not mark `relay_programmed` as success,
 878: - do not reintroduce assignment-endpoint fallback as runtime authority,
 879: - do not create a second unsigned mutation path,
 880: - do not introduce authenticated per-packet relay framing into the production path for this scope,
 881: - do not add TODO/FIXME markers instead of finishing in-scope work.
 882:
