 112: ## 3. Approved Design Decisions
 113: The following decisions are fixed for this implementation. Engineers are not being asked to redesign them.
 114: 
 115: ### 3.1 WireGuard Engine Choice
 116: Selected:
 117: - direct Rust-native `boringtun` library integration from a released `crates.io` version
 118: 
 119: Rejected for this slice:
 120: - `wireguard-go` subprocess ownership
 121: - command-only kernel WireGuard ownership
 122: - branch-tip git dependencies
 123: 
 124: Why this choice is fixed:
 125: - Rustynet needs backend-owned packet I/O, not merely backend-configured transport.
 126: - The backend must own the authoritative socket inside the Rust process.
 127: - The daemon must not infer authority from a second socket.
 128: - `boringtun` is the best fit for Rust-first, in-process ownership while keeping WireGuard as an adapter behind `TunnelBackend`.
 129: 
 130: Implementation rule:
 131: - use a released crate version pinned in `Cargo.lock`
 132: - do not use upstream branch tips
 133: - vendor a fork only if a narrow backend-internal patch is required
 134: - do not add git-branch dependencies for the shared-backend path
 135: - if a dependency brings required `unsafe` internally, contain it inside backend adapter modules and add targeted tests around the resulting trust boundary rather than widening assumptions across crates
 136: 
 137: ### 3.2 TUN / Interface Layer Choice
 138: Selected:
 139: - `tun-rs`
 140: 
 141: Rejected for this slice:
 142: - a long-lived helper-owned datapath
 143: - a large custom Linux `/dev/net/tun` implementation before first lab proof
 144: 
 145: Why this choice is fixed:
 146: - the backend needs a real Linux TUN path now,
 147: - the authoritative socket must stay inside the backend,
 148: - `tun-rs` reduces implementation risk while keeping the backend authoritative.
 149: 
 150: Implementation rule:
 151: - if helper-assisted TUN setup is required, long-lived TUN ownership must still transfer into the backend runtime immediately
 152: - the helper must not remain in the packet path after setup completes
 153: 
 154: ### 3.3 Privilege Model
 155: Selected:
 156: - helper-assisted host networking setup, backend-owned runtime transport
 157: 
 158: Required boundary:
 159: - the privileged helper may create/configure host networking resources if needed,
 160: - but it must never own:
 161:   - the authoritative UDP socket,
 162:   - the userspace WireGuard engine,
 163:   - STUN round trips,
 164:   - relay round trips,
 165:   - relay keepalive sends,
 166:   - transport identity authority.
 167: 
 168: Why this choice is fixed:
 169: - it preserves the repository’s hardened privileged boundary,
 170: - keeps long-lived transport authority inside the backend,
 171: - avoids splitting trust or transport identity across processes.
 172: 
 173: ### 3.4 Platform Scope
 174: Selected:
 175: - Linux production userspace-shared backend is mandatory in this slice.
 176: - macOS userspace-shared backend is explicitly optional and may remain blocked.
 177: 
 178: Why this choice is fixed:
 179: - the immediate live-lab target is Linux,
 180: - widening to macOS now delays the only platform required for honest traversal/relay proof,
 181: - README and ledgers must remain truthful if macOS remains blocked.
 182: 
 183: ### 3.5 Shared Transport Runtime Model
 184: Selected:
 185: - one backend-owned authoritative UDP socket
 186: - one backend-owned userspace WireGuard engine
 187: - one backend-owned TUN datapath
 188: - one backend-owned runtime worker that is the sole owner of transport state
 189: - at most one outstanding authoritative generic round trip at a time
 190: 
 191: This is not negotiable because it is the only model that preserves unambiguous transport authority.
 192: 
 193: ## 4. Non-Negotiable Security And Architecture Rules
 194: The implementation must preserve all of these rules:
 195: 
 196: 1. No daemon-owned side socket for STUN.
 197: 2. No daemon-owned side socket for relay.
 198: 3. No same-port second-socket tricks using `SO_REUSEADDR`, `SO_REUSEPORT`, or equivalent.
 199: 4. No `wireguard-go` subprocess for the new shared mode.
 200: 5. No kernel WireGuard transport for the new shared mode.
 201: 6. No helper-owned authoritative UDP socket.
 202: 7. No WireGuard engine types leaking into `rustynetd` policy/control layers.
 203: 8. No weakening of `direct_active` or `relay_active`.
 204: 9. No change to the relay protocol design.
 205: 10. No change to traversal signature/freshness authority.
 206: 11. No optimistic README or ledger claims before live evidence exists.
 207: 12. No silent fallback from `linux-wireguard-userspace-shared` to `linux-wireguard` on startup, privilege failure, dependency failure, or runtime error.
 208: 
 209: ## 5. Current-To-Target Delta Matrix
 210: | Area | Current State | Required State Before Live Lab | Exact Delta |
 211: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 212: | Linux backend runtime | command-only adapter over OS-managed socket | Rust backend owns UDP socket and WG engine | add new production userspace runtime |
 213: | STUN authority | daemon contract exists, production backends blocked | same socket as peer ciphertext | implement backend-owned round trip |
 214: | Relay authority | daemon contract exists, production backends blocked | same socket as peer ciphertext | implement backend-owned round trip + send |

 216: | TUN datapath | command backend configures external interface | userspace-shared backend owns plaintext datapath lifecycle | add TUN creation/open/configuration path |
 217: | Mode selection | mode names parse but are blocked | Linux shared mode constructs real backend | instantiate backend in daemon/start/install surfaces |
 218: | Test proof | in-memory backend only | production backend same-socket proof | add backend, daemon, and simulated integration tests |
 219: | Gate confidence | truthfulness gates hardened | new backend must not regress any gate | extend tests/gates without softening live-evidence failures |

 221: ## 6. Exact Target Runtime Architecture
 222: The production target for `linux-wireguard-userspace-shared` is:
 223: 
 224: 1. A backend object implementing `TunnelBackend`.
 225: 2. A dedicated backend runtime worker thread that owns all mutable transport state.
 226: 3. A single backend-owned authoritative UDP socket bound to the configured listen port.
 227: 4. A backend-owned userspace WireGuard engine for every configured peer.
 228: 5. A backend-owned TUN device or TUN handle for plaintext packets.
 229: 6. A synchronous command channel from `TunnelBackend` methods into the runtime worker.
 230: 7. A narrow reply path for:
 231:    - lifecycle operations,
 232:    - peer configuration,
 233:    - endpoint updates,
 234:    - authoritative round trips,
 235:    - authoritative sends,
 236:    - handshake timestamp queries,
 237:    - stats,
 238:    - shutdown.
 239: 
 240: ### 6.1 Ownership Invariant
 241: The local address returned from `authoritative_transport_identity()` must be the actual local address of the same UDP socket used for peer ciphertext traffic.
 242: 
 243: The same socket must be used for:
 244: - peer handshake and data traffic,
 245: - STUN round trips,
 246: - relay hello/refresh round trips,
 247: - relay keepalive sends.
 248: 
 249: ### 6.1.1 Proof Invariant
 250: For this plan, “same socket” does **not** mean:
 251: - same local port only,
 252: - same local address string only,
 253: - same process only,
 254: - same interface only.
 255: 
 256: It means:
 257: - the same backend-owned socket instance, or
 258: - the same backend-owned transport generation backed by exactly one authoritative socket instance for its lifetime.
 259: 
 260: Required implementation consequence:
 261: - the userspace backend runtime must maintain an internal monotonic transport-generation identifier or equivalent socket-instance token,
 262: - that token must change whenever the authoritative socket is recreated,
 263: - test-only instrumentation must expose enough data to prove that:
 264:   - peer ciphertext egress/ingress,
 265:   - STUN round trips,
 266:   - relay control round trips,
 267:   - relay keepalive sends
 268:   all used the same authoritative transport generation.
 269: 
 270: Local address equality is necessary but not sufficient proof.
 271: 
 272: ### 6.2 Demultiplexing Invariant
 273: Socket read behavior must follow this exact rule order:
 274: 
 275: 1. If there is an active authoritative round trip and the source address exactly matches the expected remote address for that round trip, deliver the datagram to the waiting round-trip caller.
 276: 2. Otherwise, deliver the datagram to the userspace WireGuard engine as peer ciphertext input.
 277: 3. Do not add packet-content guessing for control-vs-peer authority.
 278: 4. Do not create any second socket for “clean” control traffic.
 279: 
 280: ### 6.3 Round-Trip Concurrency Invariant
 281: The backend must allow at most one outstanding authoritative generic round trip at a time.
 282: 
 283: Required behavior:
 284: - if a second `authoritative_transport_round_trip(...)` arrives while one is in flight, return an explicit fail-closed backend error immediately
 285: - do not queue round trips
 286: - do not attempt ambiguous concurrent demultiplexing
 287: 
 288: ### 6.3.1 Round-Trip Cleanup Invariant
 289: Outstanding round-trip state must be cleared on all terminal paths:
 290: - success
 291: - timeout
 292: - backend shutdown
 293: - authoritative socket close
 294: - transport-generation rollover
 295: 
 296: Required behavior:
 297: - a timed-out or canceled round trip must not leave residual source attribution behind
 298: - a later datagram from the old remote endpoint must not be delivered to a stale waiter
 299: - transport-generation change must cancel any in-flight round trip fail-closed
 300: 
 301: ### 6.4 Round-Trip Target Safety Invariant
 302: `authoritative_transport_round_trip(...)` must reject a target address that currently matches any configured peer endpoint.
 303: 
 304: Reason:
 305: - peer ciphertext datagrams must never be ambiguously mixed with generic backend round-trip traffic.
 306: 
 307: Exception:
 308: - `authoritative_transport_send(...)` may target the selected relay endpoint because relay keepalive traffic legitimately shares the active relay path.
 309: 
 310: ### 6.5 Handshake Telemetry Invariant
 311: The userspace backend must implement `peer_latest_handshake_unix(...)` from authenticated engine evidence only.
 312: 
 313: It must **not** be updated from:
 314: - programmed endpoints,
 315: - STUN success,
 316: - relay control success,
 317: - optimistic state transitions.
 318: 
 319: ### 6.6 Transport Regeneration Invariant
 320: If the authoritative socket is lost, closed, or deliberately recreated:
 321: - the backend must advance transport generation,
 322: - clear any in-flight authoritative round-trip state,
 323: - preserve no stale attribution from the old socket,
 324: - force fresh post-change runtime proof before any new direct or relay-active claim can become live.
 325: 
 326: The implementation must not treat socket recreation as a transparent continuation of previously proven transport identity.
 327: 
 328: ### 6.7 Privilege Invariant
 329: Any helper interaction may assist only with:
 330: - TUN/interface creation,
 331: - address assignment,
 332: - route setup or teardown if required by existing backend behavior,
 333: - host integration operations already in scope for the helper.
 334: 
 335: The helper must never own runtime transport.
 336: 
 337: ## 7. Required File And Module Layout
 338: Current state:
 339: - [crates/rustynet-backend-wireguard/src/lib.rs](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynet-backend-wireguard/src/lib.rs) is too large to remain the sole implementation file once the userspace runtime lands.
 340: 
 341: Required target layout inside [crates/rustynet-backend-wireguard/src](/Users/iwanteague/Desktop/Rustynet/crates/rustynet-backend-wireguard/src):
 342: - `lib.rs`
 343:   - exports backend constructors and shared public types only

 663: ### 11.4 Truthfulness Rule
 664: `peer_latest_handshake_unix(...)` must not advance on:
 665: - peer configuration only,
 666: - endpoint programming only,
 667: - relay control exchange only,
 668: - STUN success only.
 669:

 671:

 673: - handshake timestamps must be scoped to the currently active peer/runtime state
 674: - transport-generation rollover must not preserve fake freshness
 675: - peer removal must clear handshake state for that peer
 676:

 679: - handshake timestamp is absent until authenticated engine activity occurs

 681: - programmed state alone does not update handshake time
 682: - relay control packets do not update handshake time
 683: - STUN traffic does not update handshake time
 684: - transport-generation rollover does not preserve stale handshake freshness
 685: - peer removal clears handshake telemetry for that peer

1097: Stop and document the blocker instead of improvising if any of the following becomes true:
1098: 
1099: 1. The implementation would require a daemon-owned second socket.
1100: 2. The implementation would require a helper-owned authoritative socket.
1101: 3. The implementation would require `wireguard-go` or kernel WireGuard to own the shared-mode transport.
1102: 4. The implementation cannot prove same-socket identity for peer traffic, STUN, and relay control.
1103: 5. The implementation can only prove same local address or same port, but not same socket instance or same authoritative transport generation.
1104: 6. The implementation can only report handshake liveness from programmed state.
1105: 7. The implementation would require softening `direct_active`, `relay_active`, or any CI/report gate.

  48: ## 0) TL;DR
  49: 
  50: Replace `scripts/e2e/live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh` (~3000 LOC POSIX-bash, Linux-only) with a Rust-native orchestrator that:
  51: 
  52: 1. Drives **N** nodes through a fixed list of orchestration stages.
  53: 2. Per-stage dispatch goes through a single `NodeAdapter` trait.
  54: 3. Per-OS knowledge lives **only** in adapter implementations (`LinuxNodeAdapter`, `WindowsNodeAdapter`, `MacosNodeAdapter`, future iOS/Android stubs).
  55: 4. Role assignment is OS-agnostic — `--node <alias>:<role>` accepts any combination.
  56: 5. Bash + PowerShell scripts that ship today are **kept** as thin per-OS workers the adapters shell out to where shell-out is the cheapest correct answer.
  57: 
  58: The end-state allows a single command:
  59: 
  60: ```sh
  61: ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab \
  62:   --node debian-headless-1:exit \
  63:   --node windows-utm-1:client \
  64:   --node macos-mini-1:entry \
  65:   --node debian-headless-2:aux \
  66:   --node debian-headless-3:extra
  67: ```
  68: 
  69: …to spin up a heterogeneous mesh and validate it end-to-end. Adding a fourth OS = ship one new adapter impl. Adding a new orchestration stage = ship one new `OrchestrationStage` impl.
  70: 
  71: ## 1) Motivation
  72: 
  73: ### 1.1 Problem statement
  74: 
  75: The bash orchestrator is the production live-lab path for Linux nodes. It is:
  76: 
  77: - ~3000 LOC of POSIX bash (plus ~3000 LOC of `live_lab_common.sh` shared helpers).
  78: - Hard-codes `apt`, `systemctl`, `/var/lib/rustynet`, POSIX `chmod` / `chown`, `dpkg`, kernel WireGuard.
  79: - Hard-codes 5 specific role names (exit / client / entry / aux / extra) and the SSH-into-`debian@<ip>` pattern.
  80: 
  81: Pointing it at a Windows node fails at the first `sudo apt`. Pointing it at macOS fails at `systemctl`. The "Linux required" rows in the current `--exit-vm` / `--client-vm` / etc. flag table are the bash script's POSIX assumptions, not anything intrinsic to the role.
  82: 
  83: W1-W4 has been quietly building the OS-agnostic *contract*:
  84: 
  85: - Per-OS verifier modules (`linux_*.rs`, `windows_*.rs`) — same JSON schema across platforms.
  86: - Adapter traits (`RuntimePaths`, `ServiceManager`, `RemoteExec`, `DaemonProbe`) with Linux + Windows + macOS-stub impls behind a `for_(platform)` factory.
  87: - Per-OS install helpers (Linux bash bootstrap, Windows `Bootstrap-RustyNetWindows.ps1` + `Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1`).
  88: - OS-agnostic distribute pipeline (W4.x followups: pull-from-Linux-exit + push-to-Windows).
  89: 
  90: What W1-W4 **deliberately did not touch**: replacing the bash orchestrator's install / membership / traffic-test logic with Rust calls through those traits. That is W5.
  91: 
  92: ### 1.2 Why now (operator goals captured 2026-04-28)
  93: 
  94: Quote: "I want any os role assignment […] These orchestrators and tests will be run 1000s of times. I want to do it right now, no half/quick jobs."
  95: 
  96: Quote: "In the wild rustynet will be deployed on multiple devices with varying OS. I want to make sure they interact correctly."
  97: 
  98: The operator goal is bug-discovery velocity. Multi-platform role assignment is the harness that makes cross-OS interop bugs surface in CI rather than in production. Quick-win shortcuts (e.g., `--auto-distribute-from-linux-exit` flag on the existing orchestrator) deliver one-shot evidence but do not give the operator a sustainable test surface for adding the next OS.
  99: 
 100: ### 1.3 Non-goals
 101: 
 102: - **Not** rewriting bash + PowerShell scripts that already exist + work. Adapters shell out to those scripts where shell-out is the cheapest correct answer.
 103: - **Not** changing the daemon's wire format, signed-bundle schemas, or membership-owner cryptography. The orchestrator only changes how nodes get installed / configured / verified, not what they verify.
 104: - **Not** removing existing CLI subcommands that operators depend on. Old subcommands keep working in parallel during the transition.
 105: - **Not** rewriting the daemon validators (W3.2-followup-1..6 stays as-is). The new orchestrator dispatches to them via the existing `DaemonProbe` trait.
 106: 
 107: ## 2) Current state (what exists today)
 108: 
 109: ### 2.1 Bash orchestrator stages (the thing being replaced)
 110: 
 111: `scripts/e2e/live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh` runs these stages, in order, on Linux peers only:
 112: 
 113: | Stage | What it does |
 114: |---|---|
 115: | `preflight` | Local prerequisites (cargo, ssh, etc.) |
 116: | `prepare_source_archive` | Tar the working tree → `state/rustynet-source.tar.gz` |
 117: | `verify_ssh_reachability` | Confirm SSH works to each role-assigned node |
 118: | `prime_remote_access` | Bootstrap sudo + authorized_keys on each node |
 119: | `cleanup_hosts` | Wipe prior daemon state on each node |
 120: | `bootstrap_hosts` | scp source → cargo build --release → install daemon → systemd unit |
 121: | `collect_pubkeys` | SSH each peer + read its WireGuard public key |
 122: | `membership_setup` | Exit signs initial membership snapshot |
 123: | `distribute_membership_state` | scp membership snapshot to every non-exit peer |
 124: | `issue_and_distribute_assignments` | Exit signs assignments, distributes to peers |
 125: | `issue_and_distribute_traversal` | Exit signs traversal hints, distributes |
 126: | `issue_and_distribute_dns_zone` | Exit signs DNS zone, distributes |
 127: | `enforce_baseline_runtime` | systemctl start rustynetd on each peer |
 128: | `validate_baseline_runtime` | Each peer's daemon ingests state, reports peer count |
 129: | `live_role_switch_matrix` | Validate runtime role transitions |
 130: | `live_exit_handoff` | Validate exit-node handoff |
 131: | (cleanup) | Optional teardown |
 132: 
 133: Each stage emits a per-stage log file under `<report-dir>/logs/`. The final `failure_digest.md` aggregates per-stage status. Exit code 0 = all passed.
 134: 
 135: ### 2.2 Rust orchestrator surface today
 136: 
 137: `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs` (~26k lines) hosts:
 138: 
 139: - `execute_ops_vm_lab_orchestrate_live_lab` — top-level entry. Calls bash orchestrator for Linux nodes, then optionally:
 140:   - `run_windows_orchestration_stages_with_options` — Windows post-validate (8 stages).
 141:   - `run_linux_daemon_validators_for_aliases` — Linux validators against every selected Linux alias.
 142: - W3.x adapter traits: `RuntimePaths`, `ServiceManager`, `RemoteExec`, `DaemonProbe` + per-OS impls + `for_(platform)` factories.
 143: - `LinuxBashOrchestrator` — wraps the bash script invocation.
 144: - `RustOrchestrator` — selects between strategies (today: Linux-bash-only or Windows-rust-only; reject heterogeneous mid-run).
 145: - `StageOrchestrator` trait — single-method `execute_live_lab(inputs) -> LiveLabRunReport`.

 173: 
 174: ## 3) Target architecture
 175: 
 176: ### 3.1 Two new traits
 177: 
 178: **`NodeConnection`** — transport injected at adapter construction time. `NodeAdapter` methods carry no connection argument; the transport is baked in by the factory. This is the key design decision that enables true OS-agnosticism: iOS (MDM), Android (ADB), and any future platform can implement the same trait surface without receiving an SSH struct they cannot use.
 179: 
 180: ```rust
 181: /// Transport injected at adapter construction by `node_adapter_for`.
 182: /// NodeAdapter methods take no connection argument — connection details
 183: /// live here, not on every call site.
 184: pub enum NodeConnection {
 185:     /// SSH to a POSIX or PowerShell-capable host (Linux, Windows, macOS).
 186:     Ssh {
 187:         host: String,
 188:         port: u16,
 189:         user: Option<String>,
 190:         identity_file: PathBuf,
 191:         /// Required. `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` enforced at SSH layer.
 192:         /// Absent file or key mismatch = hard fail at construction, not a warning.
 193:         known_hosts: PathBuf,
 194:     },
 195:     /// Android Debug Bridge (future AndroidNodeAdapter — lab-only).
 196:     Adb { device_serial: String },
 197:     /// Apple MDM / Network Extension management channel (future IosNodeAdapter).
 198:     Mdm { enrollment_id: String },
 199: }
 200: ```
 201: 
 202: **`NodeAdapter`** — captures everything that's per-node + per-OS for the orchestration path. One impl per OS. Connection details live in `NodeConnection`, injected at construction; no `RemoteTarget` threading through every call.
 203: 
 204: ```rust
 205: pub trait NodeAdapter: Send + Sync {
 206:     fn platform(&self) -> VmGuestPlatform;
 207: 
 208:     // ── Install lifecycle ───
 209:     fn install_daemon(
 210:         &self,
 211:         source: &SourceArchive,
 212:         ctx: &OrchestrationContext,
 213:     ) -> Result<InstallReport, AdapterError>;
 214: 
 215:     fn start_daemon(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError>;
 216:     fn stop_daemon(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError>;
 217:     fn restart_daemon(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError>;
 218:     fn uninstall_daemon(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError>;
 219: 
 220:     // ── Membership owner (exit role only) ───
 221:     fn issue_membership_owner_key(
 222:         &self,
 223:     ) -> Result<MembershipOwnerKey, AdapterError>;
 224: 
 225:     fn init_membership_snapshot(
 226:         &self,
 227:         owner_key: &MembershipOwnerKey,
 228:         peers: &[NodeRoleAssignment],
 229:     ) -> Result<MembershipSnapshot, AdapterError>;
 230: 
 231:     // ── Per-node identity + key collection ───
 232:     fn collect_wireguard_public_key(
 233:         &self,
 234:     ) -> Result<WireguardPublicKey, AdapterError>;
 235: 
 236:     fn collect_node_id(&self) -> Result<NodeId, AdapterError>;
 237: 
 238:     // ── Bundle distribution (any non-exit role) ───
 239:     fn distribute_signed_bundle(
 240:         &self,
 241:         kind: BundleKind,
 242:         bundle_path: &Path,
 243:     ) -> Result<(), AdapterError>;
 244: 
 245:     // ── Validators (delegates to existing W3.x DaemonProbe) ───
 246:     fn run_validator(
 247:         &self,
 248:         op: DaemonProbeOp,
 249:     ) -> Result<ValidatorReport, AdapterError>;
 250: 
 251:     // ── Traffic test ───
 252:     /// Positive connectivity: confirm this node reaches peer_mesh_ip via tunnel.
 253:     fn ping_mesh_peer(
 254:         &self,
 255:         peer_mesh_ip: &str,
 256:     ) -> Result<TrafficTestResult, AdapterError>;
 257: 
 258:     /// Negative ACL test: confirm default-deny blocks traffic to a non-mesh IP.
 259:     /// Must return `TrafficTestResult::Blocked` for the stage to pass.
 260:     /// A `Reachable` result is a security failure and fails the stage.
 261:     fn probe_denied_peer(
 262:         &self,
 263:         denied_ip: &str,
 264:     ) -> Result<TrafficTestResult, AdapterError>;
 265: 
 266:     fn collect_active_tunnels(
 267:         &self,
 268:     ) -> Result<TunnelsList, AdapterError>;
 269: 
 270:     // ── Diagnostics + cleanup ───
 271:     /// Collect diagnostic artifacts to dst.
 272:     /// Key material MUST be excluded: `*/keys/*`, `*.priv`, `*.pem` paths
 273:     /// must never appear in the archive. Implementations must test this invariant.
 274:     fn collect_artifacts(
 275:         &self,
 276:         dst: &Path,
 277:     ) -> Result<(), AdapterError>;
 278: 
 279:     fn cleanup_runtime_state(&self) -> Result<(), AdapterError>;
 280: }
 281: ```
 282: 
 283: The factory signature reflects the connection-injection pattern:
 284: 
 285: ```rust
 286: /// Build an adapter for `platform` using `conn` as its transport.
 287: /// Returns `Err(AdapterError::UnsupportedPlatform { .. })` for platforms
 288: /// not yet implemented (iOS, Android). The error message names the specific
 289: /// security barriers that block the platform (see §11).
 290: /// Returns `Err(AdapterError::ConnectionPlatformMismatch { .. })` if the
 291: /// connection type is not valid for the platform (e.g. Adb for Linux).
 292: pub fn node_adapter_for(
 293:     platform: VmGuestPlatform,
 294:     conn: NodeConnection,
 295: ) -> Result<Box<dyn NodeAdapter>, AdapterError>;
 296: ```
 297: 
 298: **`OrchestrationStage`** — captures the orchestrator's behavior. One impl per stage.
 299: 
 300: ```rust
 301: pub trait OrchestrationStage: Send + Sync {
 302:     fn id(&self) -> StageId;
 303:     fn name(&self) -> &str;
 304: 
 305:     /// Stages that must pass before this one runs (skip-cascade).
 306:     fn dependencies(&self) -> &[StageId];
 307: 
 308:     /// Which roles this stage operates on. Empty = "all roles".
 309:     fn applies_to_roles(&self) -> &[NodeRole];
 310: 
 311:     /// Some stages run once (eg membership-init on exit only); others
 312:     /// fan out per role-matched node.
 313:     fn fanout(&self) -> StageFanout;
 314: 
 315:     fn execute(&self, ctx: &mut OrchestrationContext) -> StageOutcome;
 316: }
 317: ```
 318: 
 319: ### 3.2 OS-agnostic role definitions
 320: 
 321: ```rust
 322: pub enum NodeRole {
 323:     Exit,        // membership owner; signs all bundles
 324:     Client,      // primary client peer
 325:     Entry,       // entry/relay peer
 326:     Aux,         // auxiliary peer
 327:     Extra,       // 5th node (fifth-client)
 328:     // Future-proofing for non-5-node topologies:
 329:     Custom(String),
 330: }
 331: ```
 332: 
 333: The 5 named roles match the bash orchestrator's existing role names so the membership / traffic-test / role-switch logic stays semantically identical. `Custom("…")` allows future N-node topologies.
 334: 
 335: ### 3.3 New module structure
 336: 
 337: ```
 338: crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/
 339: ├── mod.rs                                 (existing — gradually shrinks as logic moves out)
 340: ├── orchestrator/                          (NEW module)
 341: │   ├── mod.rs                             (re-exports)
 342: │   ├── error.rs                           (AdapterError, StageError)
 343: │   ├── role.rs                            (NodeRole enum + role-platform matrix)
 344: │   ├── role_assignment.rs                 (NodeRoleAssignment + parser for `<alias>:<role>`)
 345: │   ├── source_archive.rs                  (SourceArchive: tar of working tree, scp helpers)
 346: │   ├── adapter/
 347: │   │   ├── mod.rs                         (trait def + re-exports)
 348: │   │   ├── node_adapter.rs                (the NodeAdapter trait)
 349: │   │   ├── linux.rs                       (LinuxNodeAdapter)
 350: │   │   ├── windows.rs                     (WindowsNodeAdapter)
 351: │   │   ├── macos.rs                       (MacosNodeAdapter)
 352: │   │   ├── ios.rs                         (IosNodeAdapter — UnsupportedOp stub)
 353: │   │   ├── android.rs                     (AndroidNodeAdapter — UnsupportedOp stub)
 354: │   │   └── factory.rs                     (node_adapter_for(VmGuestPlatform) -> Box<dyn NodeAdapter>)
 355: │   ├── stage/
 356: │   │   ├── mod.rs                         (trait def + StageId enum)
 357: │   │   ├── preflight.rs
 358: │   │   ├── source_archive.rs              (PrepareSourceArchiveStage)
 359: │   │   ├── verify_ssh.rs
 360: │   │   ├── cleanup.rs
 361: │   │   ├── install.rs                     (BootstrapHostsStage — calls adapter.install_daemon)
 362: │   │   ├── collect_pubkeys.rs
 363: │   │   ├── membership_init.rs             (Exit role only)
 364: │   │   ├── distribute_membership.rs       (all non-exit)
 365: │   │   ├── distribute_assignments.rs
 366: │   │   ├── distribute_traversal.rs
 367: │   │   ├── distribute_dns_zone.rs
 368: │   │   ├── enforce_runtime.rs             (start daemon)
 369: │   │   ├── validate_runtime.rs            (run all 6 daemon validators)
 370: │   │   ├── traffic_test_matrix.rs         (N×N peer-to-peer connectivity)
 371: │   │   ├── role_switch_matrix.rs
 372: │   │   └── exit_handoff.rs
 373: │   ├── plan.rs                            (PlanBuilder: walks role assignments + builds stage list + dependency graph)
 374: │   ├── runner.rs                          (StateMachineRunner: drives stages in dep order, handles skip-cascade)
 375: │   ├── context.rs                         (OrchestrationContext: holds NodeRoleAssignments, source archive path,
 376: │   │                                       per-node adapter handles, collected pubkeys / signed bundles, report state)
 377: │   └── report.rs                          (typed JSON output schema + writer)
 378: └── (existing modules unchanged)
 379: ```
 380: 
 381: The bash orchestrator script stays in place. It is invoked by the legacy code path **only** (new code path never calls it). Phase W5.7 deletes the legacy code path + bash script together.
 382: 
 383: ### 3.4 Role-platform matrix (target end state)
 384: 
 385: |  | Linux | Windows | macOS | iOS | Android |
 386: |---|---|---|---|---|---|
 387: | `Exit` | ✓ | ✓ (after W5.4) | ✓ (after W5.4) | ✗ | ✗ |
 388: | `Client` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
 389: | `Entry` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
 390: | `Aux` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
 391: | `Extra` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ | ✗ |
 392: 
 393: iOS / Android adapters ship as `UnsupportedOp` stubs that fail closed with **security-specific rejection messages**. The message must name the concrete security barriers — not just "not yet implemented." Required text elements: (1) no daemon validator coverage (service hardening, key custody, DNS fail-closed not implemented for the platform); (2) no reviewed key custody model (Secure Enclave / Android Keystore integration undesigned); (3) connection model (MDM/ADB) not reviewed against security minimum bar. A test asserts each stub's error string contains "security minimum bar". See §11 for what a future W6 track would need.
 394: 
 395: ### 3.5 CLI surface (target end state)
 396: 
 397: The new CLI shape:
 398: 
 399: ```sh
 400: ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab \
 401:   --inventory <path> \
 402:   --report-dir <path> \
 403:   --ssh-identity-file <path> \
 404:   --known-hosts-file <path> \           # required; StrictHostKeyChecking=yes enforced
 405:   --node <alias>:<role> [--node <alias>:<role>]... \
 406:   [--source-mode working-tree|local-head|origin-main|ref] \
 407:   [--require-min-nodes <n>] \
 408:   [--skip-stage <stage-id>] [--skip-stage <stage-id>]... \
 409:   [--rerun-stage <stage-id>] [--rerun-stage <stage-id>]... \
 410:   [--legacy-bash-orchestrator]   # transitional, deprecated by W5.7
 411: ```
 412: 
 413: `--known-hosts-file` is **required** (not optional). The SSH layer enforces `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` against the provided file. Absent file, absent host entry, or key mismatch = hard fail at connection construction; the orchestrator does not continue with an unverified host. This applies to every SSH session including the initial bootstrap — a MITM at `install_daemon` time could substitute a malicious daemon binary.
 414: 
 415: The 6 named flags (`--exit-vm`, `--client-vm`, `--entry-vm`, `--aux-vm`, `--extra-vm`, `--windows-vm`) keep working as deprecation aliases for the duration of W5; they translate internally into `--node <alias>:<role>` pairs. W5.7 removes them.
 416:

 443: 
 444: **Tests:**
 445: - `parse_node_role_arg` accepts `alias:exit` / `alias:client` / `alias:entry` / `alias:aux` / `alias:extra` / `alias:custom-foo`.
 446: - `parse_node_role_arg` rejects empty, malformed, unknown roles (including typos like `exti`).
 447: - `NodeRole::is_unique_per_lab()` returns true for `Exit`, false for others (exactly one Exit per lab).
 448: - `node_adapter_for` returns the right concrete type for Linux/Windows/macOS (using stub impls).
 449: - `node_adapter_for(VmGuestPlatform::Ios, _)` and `node_adapter_for(VmGuestPlatform::Android, _)` return `Err(AdapterError::UnsupportedPlatform)` whose message contains "security minimum bar".
 450: - `node_adapter_for` returns `Err(AdapterError::ConnectionPlatformMismatch)` for mismatched pairs (e.g. `Adb` + Linux, `Ssh` + iOS).
 451: - `NodeConnection::Ssh` construction returns `Err` if `known_hosts` path does not exist (validated at construction, not at first use).
 452: - `StateMachineRunner` honors skip-cascade for a stub 3-stage plan with one failing stage.
 453: - `StateMachineRunner` executes stages in dependency order (not insertion order) for a 3-stage plan where C depends on A but not B.

 456: - `cargo fmt --all -- --check` clean.

 460: - New module compiles + is reachable via `pub mod orchestrator;` from `vm_lab/mod.rs`.
 461: - iOS + Android `UnsupportedPlatform` error strings verified by test to contain "security minimum bar".
 462: - `NodeConnection::Ssh` path-validation test passes.

 468: **Deliverable:** Full `NodeAdapter` impl for Linux that's behaviorally equivalent to the bash orchestrator's per-node operations. Shells out to existing bash where shell-out is the cheapest correct answer.

 479: 
 480: **Per-method strategy:**
 481: | Method | Strategy |
 482: |---|---|
 483: | `install_daemon` | scp `SourceArchive`, run `cargo build --release` over SSH, `install` daemon binary + systemd unit. Currently a bash-helper invocation; can be re-implemented in Rust over SSH later without changing the trait surface. |
 484: | `start_daemon` / `stop_daemon` / `restart_daemon` | `systemctl <action> rustynetd` over SSH. |
 485: | `issue_membership_owner_key` | `rustynet membership init …` over SSH on the target (Rust CLI runs on Linux). |
 486: | `init_membership_snapshot` | `rustynet membership init` flow with peers. |
 487: | `collect_wireguard_public_key` | `cat /var/lib/rustynet/keys/wireguard.pub` over SSH. |

 630: ### W5.5 — Stage implementations (4-6 sessions)
 631: 
 632: **Deliverable:** All 17 stages from §2.1 ported from bash to Rust as `OrchestrationStage` impls. Each stage is its own file under `orchestrator/stage/`, calls `NodeAdapter` methods, and emits typed `StageOutcome`.
 633: 
 634: **Current 2026-04-29 hardening state:** all 17 stage files are present and `execute_rust_native_orchestration` now builds its runtime stage vector from `PlanBuilder`, so the CLI path includes `FinalCleanupStage` and cannot drift from the plan list. A unit test pins exact stage-ID parity with `PlanBuilder`. The live parity runner/evidence remains pending, so W5.5 is not fully closed.
 635: 
 636: **Files added:** 17 stage files under `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/orchestrator/stage/`.
 637: 
 638: **Tests per stage:** unit test of the stage's logic with a mocked `NodeAdapter`. Integration test (gated) drives the stage against a live VM.
 639: 
 640: **Acceptance criteria:**
 641: - Side-by-side parity run: invoke `vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab` once with `--legacy-bash-orchestrator` and once with the new code path against the same lab. **Parity is defined as:** (a) identical set of stage IDs executed; (b) identical pass/fail status for every stage; (c) identical overall exit code; (d) per-stage JSON `outcome` field values match exactly; (e) numeric peer counts and validator counts within ±0. The parity runner produces a machine-readable JSON diff; CI asserts zero diff. Capture diff + summary as evidence.
 642: - `TrafficTestMatrix` stage includes both **positive probes** (mesh peers reachable via tunnel — N×N) and **negative probes** (default-deny ACL blocks a non-mesh probe IP from each node). Stage result is PASS only when all positive probes succeed AND all negative probes return `Blocked`. A `Reachable` result on any negative probe is a security failure that fails the stage and blocks phase progression. Both probe sets are documented in per-stage evidence.
 643: - All gates pass.
 644: 
 645: **Status (2026-04-29):**
 646: - W5.5a — 17 stage execute() impls + `PlanBuilder::build()` shipped in `c63084b`. Stages walk in dep order, emit typed `StageOutcome`, route through `NodeAdapter`. Unit tests on the runner / plan / per-stage logic with mocked adapters.
 647: - W5.5b — parity-diff harness shipped in `85e786d`. Rust orchestrator now writes `<report-dir>/parity_input.json` (a `LiveLabRunReport`) at end-of-run. New `vm-lab-diff-orchestrator-parity --left <bash.json> --right <rust.json> --output <diff.json>` subcommand emits `ParityDiff` covering every dimension above (stage list, per-stage outcome, overall status, node count, validator pass/total counts). 11 unit tests cover the diff function + every drift dimension; 2 tests cover the executor end-to-end. Returns Err on drift so CI can gate.
 648: - ⛔ Live parity evidence is **NOT** captured. The bash orchestrator still needs to emit (or be wrapped to emit) a `parity_input.json` matching the schema. The paired bash↔Rust run against equivalent Linux labs is blocked on the real lab being reachable from this work environment.

 713: ## 5) Migration strategy (how old + new coexist)
 714: 
 715: During W5.0 → W5.6, both code paths coexist. Operators can choose:
 716: 
 717: ```sh
 718: # Legacy bash path (default during transition)
 719: ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab --exit-vm a --client-vm b … --legacy-bash-orchestrator
 720: 
 721: # New Rust path (opt-in during transition, default after W5.7)
 722: ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab --node a:exit --node b:client …
 723: ```
 724: 
 725: Risk mitigation:
 726: 1. **CI keeps invoking the legacy path** until W5.7 ships. No CI-breaking change midway through.
 727: 2. **Side-by-side parity check** at every major milestone: same lab → both paths → byte-for-byte stage-outcome comparison.
 728: 3. **Bash script remains in place** until W5.7. If the new path regresses on a non-test-covered scenario, operators flip back to legacy without a rollback commit.
 729: 4. **Per-slice mergeability** — each W5.x is a clean commit with passing gates. Pause-resume safe.
 730: 
 731: ## 6) Risk register
 732: 
 733: | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
 734: |---|---|---|---|
 735: | Rust orchestrator regresses behavior the bash path silently relied on | High | High | Side-by-side parity runs at end of W5.5 with machine-readable JSON diff. Bash path stays callable until W5.7. Daemon-side validators (W3.2-followup) provide cross-check. |
 736: | SSH MITM during `install_daemon` → attacker substitutes malicious daemon binary | Medium | Critical | `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` + required `--known-hosts-file` enforced at `NodeConnection::Ssh` construction. Orchestrator hard-fails on absent file or key mismatch. Pre-populate known-hosts before first orchestrator run via key-exchange ceremony documented in runbook. |
 737: | `collect_artifacts` captures key material → private key exfiltration via artifact archive | Low | Critical | Key dirs excluded at the `tar` invocation level (`--exclude='*/keys/*' --exclude='*.priv' --exclude='*.pem'`). Key-exclusion invariant tested: mock tarball must not contain `wireguard.priv`. |
 738: | `cargo build --release` over SSH on a UTM Linux VM is too slow (>20 min) → CI timeouts | Medium | Medium | Add binary-cache mode: build once on the macOS host (cross-compile), scp the binary, skip remote cargo. Optional flag, falls back to remote-build if cross-compile not configured. |
 739: | macOS adapter blocked by no available macOS VM during W5.3 | High | Medium | macOS adapter compiles + has unit tests. Live evidence runs deferred to when a Mac mini / macOS UTM VM is available. Marked as "compile + unit ready, live evidence pending". |
 740: | WireGuard for Windows install via winget unreliable in CI | Medium | High | Add a `--require-wireguard-preinstalled` flag that skips winget. CI runners pre-install via base-image automation. |
 741: | Membership-owner key handling differs subtly per-OS (key-custody, signature scheme) | Medium | High | Validate via the existing `key-custody-check` validator after every install. Cross-OS membership-init is gated on validator PASS. |
 742: | Multi-OS testing surfaces a pile of cross-OS interop bugs simultaneously | High | Medium | Each scenario in W5.7 evidence campaign is its own slice. We fix bugs as they surface, one slice at a time. The orchestrator's drift-reasons list is designed to surface multiple issues per run, not stop on first. |
 743: | Bash orchestrator removal breaks an out-of-tree consumer | Low | Medium | grep entire repo + docs + CI configs for `live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh` references at W5.7. Audit before removal. |
 744: | The "PowerShell-encoded SSH" dispatch path on Windows has known quirks (CLIXML on stderr, etc.) | Medium | Medium | Already partially debugged in W4.x. Add a `$ProgressPreference = "SilentlyContinue"` wrapper to all encoded PS scripts. Drain stderr separately from stdout in the Rust SSH layer. |

 761: ## 8) Architecture decisions made before W5.0
 762: 
 763: The following decisions were made during plan review (2026-04-28) and are now closed. They are recorded here as decisions, not open questions.
 764: 
 765: **D1 — `NodeAdapter` connection-injection pattern (P0, blocking W5.0):**
 766: `NodeAdapter` methods carry no `RemoteTarget` / connection argument. Connection details live in `NodeConnection`, injected at adapter construction by `node_adapter_for(platform, conn)`. Rationale: SSH-centric `RemoteTarget` in every method signature blocks iOS (MDM) and Android (ADB) from ever implementing the trait without a hack.
 767: 
 768: **D2 — SSH known-hosts enforcement (P1, security):**
 769: `--known-hosts-file <path>` is a required CLI flag. `NodeConnection::Ssh` validates the path at construction. `StrictHostKeyChecking=yes` is non-negotiable at the SSH layer. Rationale: MITM during `install_daemon` allows daemon binary substitution.
 770: 
 771: **D3 — Negative traffic tests mandatory in `TrafficTestMatrix` (P1, security):**
 772: `probe_denied_peer` is a required `NodeAdapter` method. `TrafficTestMatrix` stage PASS requires all negative probes return `Blocked`. Rationale: positive-only connectivity test gives false assurance for default-deny ACL verification.
 773: 
 774: **D4 — `collect_artifacts` key-exclusion required (P1, security):**
 775: `*/keys/*`, `*.priv`, `*.pem` excluded from artifact archives at the `tar` invocation level. Exclusion tested with an invariant test. Rationale: `SecurityMinimumBar.md §3.4` prohibits logging/leaking key material.
 776: 
 777: **D5 — iOS/Android blocker messages name security barriers (P1, security):**
 778: Error strings from `node_adapter_for(Ios|Android, _)` must contain "security minimum bar". Rationale: operator needs to know the rejection is a security decision, not a missing feature, and what future work is required to unblock it.
 779: 
 780: **D6 — `--node` opt-in flag ships in W5.1, not W5.6 (P2, plan quality):**
 781: W5.1 wires `--node` and `--known-hosts-file` as opt-in flags. W5.2–W5.5 are developed and tested using `--node`. W5.6 promotes to default + deprecates old flags. Rationale: first test of the new path should not be after all 17 stages are already implemented.
 782: 
 783: **D7 — W5.5 parity defined as machine-readable JSON diff (P2, plan quality):**
 784: Parity = same stage IDs, same pass/fail, same exit code, same `outcome` field values, numeric counts ±0. CI asserts zero diff on a machine-readable JSON diff artifact. See §4 W5.5 acceptance criteria for full definition.
 785: 
 786: **D8 — macOS in scope (W5.3), Android/iOS deferred to W6+ (P2):**
 787: macOS is included in W5 as specified. iOS and Android require a different connection model (MDM/ADB), different validator coverage, and a reviewed key custody model. They are W6+ work. See §11 for the full forward roadmap.
 788: 
 789: **Remaining open questions (operator input needed):**
 790: 
 791: 1. **macOS VM availability:** does the operator have a macOS UTM VM for W5.3 live evidence? If not, W5.3 ships as "compile + unit complete, live evidence deferred".
 792: 2. **Cross-compile vs remote-build:** confirmed remote-build (matching bash orchestrator) for W5.1. Cross-compile opt-in flag in a later slice.
 793: 3. **`live_lab_common.sh` retention:** audit at W5.7; keep only if another consumer exists.
 794: 4. **`Custom(String)` role gating:** ship enum with `Custom(String)` from W5.0 but gate behind `--allow-custom-roles` flag to prevent silent typo promotion.
 795: 5. **Stage gating language:** ship `--skip-stage` + `--rerun-stage` as direct ports of bash semantics in W5.6. No new gating language until operators request it.
 796:

 885: ## 10) How this plan fits the broader roadmap
 886: 
 887: W5 is the natural sequel to W1-W4 (`OsAgnosticOrchestratorAndWindowsPeerDeltaPlan_2026-04-27.md`):
 888: 
 889: - W1-W4 built the OS-agnostic *contract* (verifier shapes, adapter traits, distribute pipeline).
 890: - W5 builds the OS-agnostic *orchestration* (uses those contracts to drive any-OS install + mesh + validate).
 891: 
 892: After W5 is complete:
 893: 
 894: - Adding a new OS = ship one new `NodeAdapter` impl + per-OS validator modules. Estimated 2-3 weeks per OS (roughly the same as the current Windows track's effort, minus the contract design work that's now done).
 895: - Adding a new orchestration stage = ship one new `OrchestrationStage` impl. Days, not weeks.
 896: - Bug-discovery velocity for cross-OS interop is gated by VM availability + CI capacity, not by orchestrator code work.
 897: 
 898: This positions the project for the operator's stated goal: "in the wild rustynet will be deployed on multiple devices with varying OS. I want to make sure they interact correctly." After W5, every CI run can spin up a heterogeneous mesh of arbitrary OS combinations + validate them end-to-end. That's the bug-finding harness the project needs to ship reliably.
 899: 
 900: ## 11) iOS / Android — What a Future W6 Track Requires
 901: 
 902: W5 ships iOS and Android as `UnsupportedOp` stubs that fail closed with security-specific rejection messages. This is the correct default: these platforms cannot be added to a production mesh until each of the following barriers is cleared. This section exists so the W6 track owner has a concrete target.
 903: 
 904: ### 11.1 Connection model (blocking)
 905: 
 906: - **iOS** has no SSH daemon. The `NodeConnection::Mdm` variant is the forward slot. Filling it in requires either Apple MDM enrollment (enterprise / supervised device) or a custom in-app management socket exposed by the Rustynet iOS Network Extension. Neither is designed yet.
 907: - **Android** can use ADB for lab-only bootstrapping (`NodeConnection::Adb`), but production Android nodes run as a VPN-service app, not a system service. Production Android requires an app-layer management channel distinct from ADB. The `Adb` variant is explicitly a lab escape hatch, not a production path.
 908: 
 909: Both paths require explicit security review of the channel authentication model before the `UnsupportedPlatform` guard is lifted.
 910: 
 911: ### 11.2 Daemon validator coverage (blocking)
 912: 
 913: All 6 W3.2-followup validators must be ported before live evidence is accepted:
 914: 
 915: | Validator | iOS target | Android target |
 916: |---|---|---|
 917: | `service-hardening-check` | iOS app sandbox + Network Extension entitlements | SELinux policy + VpnService permissions |
 918: | `key-custody-check` | Secure Enclave-backed WireGuard key | Android Keystore hardware-backed key |
 919: | `dns-failclosed-check` | iOS VPN profile DNS configuration | Android VPN DNS configuration |
 920: | `runtime-acls-check` | App container file ACLs | App-private storage ACLs |
 921: | `mesh-status-check` | Daemon reachable via in-app IPC | Daemon reachable via in-app IPC |
 922: | `authenticode-check` | App Store / TestFlight signing | APK signing + Play Protect status |
 923: 
 924: ### 11.3 Key custody model (blocking)
 925: 
 926: - **iOS:** WireGuard private key stored in Secure Enclave where available; Keychain fallback with `kSecAttrAccessibleAfterFirstUnlockThisDeviceOnly` as minimum. Explicit threat model for the case where the device is lost/stolen while unlocked.
 927: - **Android:** WireGuard private key stored in Android Keystore with `StrongBox` hardware-backed protection where available. Threat model for rooted devices documented and fail-closed behavior specified.
 928: 
 929: ### 11.4 Service hardening (blocking)
 930: 
 931: - **iOS:** App cannot be killed by other apps; runs with minimum entitlements; Network Extension restart behavior on crash is defined; background execution constraints documented.
 932: - **Android:** SELinux `vpn` domain applied; `BIND_VPN_SERVICE` permission is system-only; app signing enforced; background execution restrictions documented.
 933: 
 934: ### 11.5 Estimated effort
 935: 
 936: - iOS: 5-8 weeks. Apple's Network Extension and Secure Enclave APIs are constrained; App Store review adds latency. ADB connection model is not applicable; MDM enrollment or custom socket is required from day one.
 937: - Android: 4-6 weeks for ADB-backed lab path; 6-8 weeks for production Play Store app-layer path (separate from the lab path).
 938: - Both tracks can proceed in parallel after W5 ships. Neither blocks W5.

 126: ## Detailed Mapping
 127: 
 128: ### Tailscale TS-2022-004: Local API DNS rebinding
 129: 
 130: - Attack family: `local-socket-spoofing`
 131: - Historical issue: Browser-originated DNS rebinding could reach a localhost control API and trigger local command execution.
 132: - Rustynet analog: Local control surface spoofing and privileged-boundary hardening.
 133: - Coverage status: `covered`
 134: - Expected secure result: Rustynet rejects insecure local control surfaces before connecting and never shells untrusted helper input.
 135: - Local verification commands:
 136:   - `cargo test -p rustynet-cli control_socket_validator -- --nocapture`
 137:   - `cargo test -p rustynetd privileged_helper::tests::fuzzgate_rejects_unknown_tokens_and_shell_metacharacters -- --nocapture`
 138:   - `cargo test -p rustynet-control admin::tests::privileged_helper_validation_rejects_shell_construction -- --nocapture`
 139: - Primary sources: https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins
 140: 
 141: ### Tailscale TS-2022-005: Peer API DNS rebinding
 142: 
 143: - Attack family: `local-socket-spoofing`
 144: - Historical issue: Browser-originated requests could reach a peer API and expose local env or response data.
 145: - Rustynet analog: No browser-reachable peer control API, plus socket trust validation and secret redaction.
 146: - Coverage status: `partially_covered`
 147: - Expected secure result: Rustynet keeps the control plane off localhost HTTP surfaces and redacts secret-bearing output paths.
 148: - Local verification commands:
 149:   - `cargo test -p rustynet-cli control_socket_validator -- --nocapture`
 150:   - `cargo test -p rustynet-control operations::tests::structured_logger_never_writes_cleartext_secrets -- --nocapture`
 151:   - `cargo test -p rustynet-control operations::tests::redaction_covers_all_ingestion_paths -- --nocapture`
 152: - Live validation scripts:
 153:   - `scripts/e2e/live_linux_control_surface_exposure_test.sh`
 154: - Primary sources: https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins
 155: 
 156: ### Tailscale TS-2024-005: Insufficient inbound packet filtering on exit or subnet nodes
 157: 
 158: - Attack family: `route-hijack`
 159: - Historical issue: Linux exit-node or routed modes did not filter inbound traffic tightly enough.
 160: - Rustynet analog: Exit-serving must keep fail-closed packet filtering and forwarding constraints.
 161: - Coverage status: `covered`
 162: - Expected secure result: Rustynet blocks tunnel or DNS leakage and refuses exit-serving without required NAT/forwarding policy.
 163: - Local verification commands:
 164:   - `cargo test -p rustynetd dataplane::tests::phase4_fail_close_blocks_tunnel_and_dns_when_required -- --nocapture`
 165:   - `cargo test -p rustynetd phase10::tests::apply_exit_serving_requires_nat_forwarding -- --nocapture`
 166: - Primary sources: https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins
 167: 
 168: ### Tailscale TS-2024-007: Split-DNS namespace handling bug
 169: 
 170: - Attack family: `dns-integrity`
 171: - Historical issue: Special-domain handling under split DNS could yield unsafe resolver behavior.
 172: - Rustynet analog: Managed DNS namespace integrity with refuse-or-servfail semantics.
 173: - Coverage status: `covered`
 174: - Expected secure result: Rustynet SERVFAILs managed names when signed state is bad and refuses non-managed names instead of guessing or forwarding.
 175: - Local verification commands:

 178:   - `cargo test -p rustynetd load_dns_zone_bundle_rejects_record_ip_outside_assignment -- --nocapture`
 179: - Primary sources: https://tailscale.com/security-bulletins
 180: 
 181: ### Tailscale TS-2025-002: Header spoofing against local file-transfer auth
 182: 
 183: - Attack family: `local-socket-spoofing`
 184: - Historical issue: A trusted local HTTP header could be spoofed to bypass authorization.

   1: # Security Hardening Audit (2026-04-28)
   2: 
   3: Date: 2026-04-28
   4: Status: in progress (W3-window pass complete; post-W4 deep audit pending)
   5: 
   6: ## 0) Scope and Purpose
   7: 
   8: This document captures the security-focused audit work the user
   9: authorised on top of the OS-Agnostic Orchestrator + Windows-Peer
  10: delta plan (2026-04-27). The work is in two phases:
  11: 
  12: - **Phase A — pre-W4 quick-wins window** (this commit and earlier):
  13:   fix anything found that is (a) cheap to land, (b) genuinely
  14:   fail-closed in posture, and (c) doesn't risk regressing existing
  15:   validators. Don't open large new abstractions in this phase.
  16: - **Phase B — post-W4 deep audit** (TODO, scheduled after the W4
  17:   capability-gating + Windows-mesh-join slice lands): compare
  18:   Rustynet's posture to Tailscale, WireGuard, and other reviewed
  19:   mesh-VPN projects' published security guidance and import the
  20:   practices that translate.
  21: 
  22: This file is intentionally a *running ledger*: each finding gets a
  23: dated entry with severity, file:line, and either an "applied" commit
  24: SHA or a "deferred — tracked under" pointer.
  25: 
  26: ## 1) Source-Of-Truth Cross-References

  34: 
  35: ## 2) Phase A — Pre-W4 Quick-Wins Window
  36: 
  37: ### A.1 Tooling Gates
  38: 
  39: | Tool | Result | Date | Notes |
  40: |---|---|---|---|
  41: | `cargo audit` | **0 vulnerabilities** | 2026-04-28 | 1058 advisories scanned, 182 deps. |
  42: | `cargo deny check` | advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok | 2026-04-28 | All four categories pass. |
  43: | `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` | clean (production code) | 2026-04-28 | Closes the long-standing W1.1 / W2.x residual-risk note. `--all-targets` still trips on third_party/boringtun's vendored test code which we deliberately do not fork. |
  44: | `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` enforcement | clean | 2026-04-28 | Every reviewed daemon module carries the lint, plus repo ships a `check_no_unsafe_code` enforcement bin and `ops_phase1.rs` unsafe-keyword scanner. |
  45: 
  46: ### A.2 Findings + Resolutions
  47: 
  48: #### A.2.1 [HIGH] DoS panic on signed-bundle freshness when host clock < UNIX_EPOCH
  49: 
  50: **Where:** [crates/rustynetd/src/fetcher.rs:179](../../crates/rustynetd/src/fetcher.rs:179) (now line 184 post-fix), `SignedBundleFetcher::check_freshness`.
  51: 
  52: **Risk:** Every signed-bundle fetch (assignment, traversal, auto-tunnel,
  53: DNS-zone) called `SystemTime::now().duration_since(UNIX_EPOCH).unwrap()`.
  54: On a host with a clock rolled back before 1970-01-01 (BIOS clock
  55: corruption, adversarial NTP injection, malicious VM clock skew), the
  56: unwrap panicked. A daemon panic in this code path tears down the
  57: enforced WireGuard tunnel + the fail-closed DNS / firewall posture,
  58: even though the freshness check itself is meant to be a fail-closed
  59: gate. The right fail-closed posture is to *refuse the bundle* and
  60: keep the rest of the daemon's enforcement live.
  61: 
  62: **Resolution:** Replaced the unwrap with a `map_err` that propagates
  63: a stale-bundle error reason citing the clock-pre-EPOCH state, so the
  64: existing freshness-rejection path handles it without daemon
  65: termination.
  66: 
  67: **Evidence:** Commit `de4c7ba` ("Fix DoS panic on signed-bundle
  68: freshness when host clock < UNIX_EPOCH"); tests `cargo test -p
  69: rustynetd --lib fetcher` 11/11 pass post-fix.
  70: 
  71: ---
  72: 
  73: #### A.2.2 [INFRA] Workspace clippy gate previously failed on baseline
  74: 
  75: **Where:** ~80 call sites in
  76: - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/bin/live_linux_role_switch_matrix_test.rs`
  77: - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/ops_e2e.rs`
  78: - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/ops_security_audit_workflows.rs`
  79: - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/bootstrap/windows.rs`
  80: - `crates/rustynet-cli/src/vm_lab/mod.rs`
  81: 
  82: **Risk:** Not a vulnerability per se, but the workspace clippy gate
  83: mandated by CLAUDE.md §7 was failing on baseline `clippy::uninlined_format_args`
  84: drift. Each W slice (W1.1 / W1.2b / W2.x / W3.x) has been carrying
  85: this as a residual-risk note. A failing gate erodes the security-bar
  86: contract over time — defenders need every gate they declare to
  87: actually hold.
  88: 
  89: **Resolution:** Mechanical 1-line `format!("{} ...", var)` →
  90: `format!("{var} ...")` conversions across the affected files,
  91: applied via `cargo clippy --fix --tests -p rustynet-cli` so there is
  92: zero behavior change. Plus visibility fix on `pub enum
  93: VmGuestPlatform` so RustOrchestrator's public API isn't "more
  94: public than the type". third_party/boringtun was NOT modified —
  95: it's a vendored upstream BSD-3 crate and forking it for clippy
  96: would break upstream sync.
  97: 
  98: **Evidence:** Commit `2e71184` ("Clean up workspace
  99: clippy::uninlined_format_args drift in rustynet-cli"); workspace
 100: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings` now clean.

 103: 
 104: ### A.3 Findings explicitly cleared (no fix needed)
 105: 
 106: #### A.3.1 Path traversal / symlink follow
 107: 
 108: **Result:** No path-traversal concerns found in scope. The repo has
 109: mature path safety discipline — `validate_windows_runtime_file_path`,
 110: `validate_windows_secret_blob_path`, `validate_secret_file_security`
 111: all enforce: reject `..`, reject absolute escapes from reviewed
 112: roots, whitelist reviewed roots, enforce expected extensions. All
 113: `symlink_metadata()` calls happen *before* the corresponding I/O
 114: operation (no TOCTOU windows). The `privileged_helper.rs` socket
 115: path is explicitly rejected if it resolves to a symlink. The
 116: `windows_runtime_boundary.rs` write paths check `symlink_metadata()`
 117: before the write. **Cleared 2026-04-28.**
 118: 
 119: #### A.3.2 Secret material in logs / error messages
 120: 
 121: **Result:** No secret-leakage concerns found in scope.
 122: - `SecretKey` (`rustynet-crypto/lib.rs:53`) has a custom `Debug`
 123:   impl that redacts as `"SecretKey(REDACTED)"`.
 124: - `Ed25519SigningProvider` (`rustynet-crypto/lib.rs:702`) custom
 125:   `Debug` redacts the signing key, exposes only the public
 126:   `verifying_key` (safe).
 127: - `NodeKeyPair` derives `Debug` but its `SecretKey` field
 128:   redacts via the impl above.
 129: - `Zeroizing<String>` passphrases (`rustynetd/key_material.rs:60`,
 130:   `:76`, `:130`) are never interpolated into error messages; error
 131:   strings reference operation failure (I/O, decryption status), not
 132:   contents.
 133: - WireGuard private-key decrypt failures (`daemon.rs:7687`)
 134:   propagate from custody manager without exposing key bytes.
 135: - All `eprintln!` / `log::*!` call sites grep clean for
 136:   secret-bearing identifiers. **Cleared 2026-04-28.**
 137: 
 138: #### A.3.3 Constant-time comparison of secrets
 139: 
 140: **Result:** Reviewed paths use `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`:
 141: - `rustynet-relay/src/transport.rs` uses `ct_eq` on `node_id`,
 142:   `peer_node_id`, `relay_id` per documented contract (lines 205,
 143:   216, 224). Module header comment (lines 13-30) explicitly
 144:   documents the policy.
 145: - The one non-`ct_eq` byte-by-byte compare in
 146:   `rustynet-crypto/src/lib.rs:135-137` (`is_all_zeros`) checks a
 147:   freshly OS-RNG-generated key against the all-zeros vector during
 148:   keygen weak-material rejection. Attacker cannot influence OsRng
 149:   output; the timing leak is purely theoretical (would require
 150:   the attacker to bias OsRng output, which they can't). Keeping
 151:   the short-circuit `.iter().all(...)` avoids a tiny dependency
 152:   surface for negligible benefit. **Cleared 2026-04-28** with
 153:   rationale recorded.
 154: 
 155: #### A.3.4 `unsafe` blocks audit
 156: 
 157: **Result:** Every reviewed daemon source carries
 158: `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` at the top. The only legitimate `unsafe`
 159: blocks are in `crates/rustynet-windows-native/src/lib.rs` for Win32
 160: FFI calls (`GetFileSecurityW`, `GetLastError`, etc.) — unavoidable
 161: because Win32 APIs require unsafe for FFI. Each block is small,
 162: focused on a single Win32 call, with bounds-checked arguments. The
 163: repo also ships `crates/rustynet-cli/src/bin/check_no_unsafe_code.rs`
 164: + `ops_phase1.rs` scanner that fails CI if `unsafe` keyword usage
 165: is reintroduced into reviewed Rust sources (line 1255: "unsafe
 166: keyword usage is forbidden in repository Rust sources"). **Cleared
 167: 2026-04-28.**
 168: 
 169: #### A.3.6 W2.5 wrapper-hygiene audit — Windows bootstrap PS scripts
 170: 
 171: **Result:** Audit performed across the five reviewed PowerShell
 172: helpers under `scripts/bootstrap/windows/` (Bootstrap-, Collect-,
 173: Install-, Smoke-, Verify-). Findings tally: 9 HIGH (theoretical, on
 174: controlled values), 14 MEDIUM, 4 LOW. Detail per finding archived
 175: in the audit subagent transcript and is recoverable via the same
 176: prompt; key categories below.
 177: 
 178: **HIGH-severity categories (theoretical — values are controlled):**
 179: - `cmd.exe /c $commandText` interpolation in
 180:   `Bootstrap-RustyNetWindows.ps1:460, 1031` and
 181:   `Collect-RustyNetWindowsDiagnostics.ps1:288`. The interpolated
 182:   array contents are static helper-defined strings (`where.exe
 183:   cargo`, `rustc.exe --version`, etc.); attacker would need to
 184:   modify the shipped script. Pattern still violates argv-only
 185:   discipline.
 186: - Manual binPath quote-concatenation in `Install-` and `Smoke-`
 187:   scripts — same fragile-quoting class the W2.2 install-helper
 188:   hardening commit (76f8303) replaced for `sc.exe create` with
 189:   `New-Service`. The remaining sites (Smoke-RustyNetWindowsService
 190:   Host.ps1:241 + sc.exe create at 297-305) still take the manual
 191:   quote path because the smoke-test runs under sc.exe explicitly.
 192: - Backtick-escaped paths inside cmd-string args
 193:   (`Bootstrap-RustyNetWindows.ps1:1020` for winget config).
 194: 
 195: **MEDIUM-severity categories (defense-in-depth):**
 196: - `icacls $Path` and `sc.exe delete $ServiceName` invocations with
 197:   unquoted variables across all five scripts. PowerShell 5.1's
 198:   native-command argument passing wraps space-bearing variables in
 199:   quotes for most cases — tests of the actual install path against
 200:   `C:\Program Files\RustyNet\...` (spaces in `Program Files`) pass
 201:   in the live-lab evidence run captured in commit 76f8303.
 202:   Defense-in-depth would still benefit from explicit quoting.
 203: - `Get-CimInstance -Filter ("Name='" + $ServiceName.Replace("'",
 204:   "''") + "'")` WQL filter construction in `Install-`, `Smoke-`,
 205:   `Verify-`. Replace-based escaping is correct but fragile. Note:
 206:   `Get-CimInstance` has no `-FilterHashtable` parameter (`Get-WinEvent`
 207:   does); safe approach is `-Filter "Name = '$ServiceName'"` gated by
 208:   the `Test-RustyNetServiceName` validator (landed).
 209: - `git clone --branch $Branch $RepoUrl` in `Bootstrap-RustyNetWindows
 210:   .ps1:1058-1080` passes parameter values directly to git; git
 211:   itself validates URL/ref shape but no pre-validation in the
 212:   script.
 213: 
 214: **Cross-cutting hardening recommendation status (W2.5b):**
 215: 1. **[x] LANDED** — `Test-RustyNetServiceName` defense-in-depth
 216:    validators added at the top of `Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1`,
 217:    `Verify-RustyNetWindowsBootstrap.ps1`, and
 218:    `Smoke-RustyNetWindowsServiceHost.ps1`. Mirror the Rust-side
 219:    `validate_service_name`: ASCII alphanumeric + `-` + `_`,
 220:    non-empty, ≤128 chars. Run BEFORE the trap handler is registered
 221:    so a malformed parameter fails loudly with the precise reason
 222:    instead of collapsing to a generic exception.
 223: 2. **[x] LANDED** — `Test-RustyNetReviewedInstallRoot` /
 224:    `Test-RustyNetReviewedStateRoot` validators added to
 225:    `Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1` (full pair) and
 226:    `Verify-RustyNetWindowsBootstrap.ps1` /
 227:    `Smoke-RustyNetWindowsServiceHost.ps1` (StateRoot check;
 228:    InstallRoot check on Verify). Reject any deviation from the
 229:    reviewed `C:\Program Files\RustyNet` / `C:\ProgramData\RustyNet`
 230:    roots so the helper cannot install RustyNet under an unreviewed
 231:    layout.
 232: 3. **[x] LANDED** — Replaced `cmd.exe /c $commandText` in
 233:    `Bootstrap-RustyNetWindows.ps1` (tooling-probe loop and the
 234:    VS env-capture loop) and `Collect-RustyNetWindowsDiagnostics.ps1`
 235:    (tooling-probe loop) with argv-only invocation: the probe loop
 236:    splits `$commandText` on whitespace and uses the PowerShell `&`
 237:    operator so no shell string is formed; the VsDevCmd env-capture
 238:    uses explicit string concatenation rather than PS interpolation
 239:    to build the cmd argument, removing `$devCmd` from an
 240:    interpolated string context.
 241: 4. **[x] LANDED** — Reverted erroneous `-FilterHashtable` (a
 242:    `Get-WinEvent` parameter that does not exist on `Get-CimInstance`)
 243:    back to `-Filter "Name = '$ServiceName'"`. The filter string is
 244:    safe because `$ServiceName` is validated by `Test-RustyNetServiceName`
 245:    (`^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$`) before any CIM call, preventing WQL injection.
 246:    Live-lab run 2026-05-06 confirmed `-FilterHashtable` on
 247:    `Get-CimInstance` throws `"A parameter cannot be found"` on Windows 11
 248:    PowerShell 5.1; fix landed in all four affected scripts.
 249: 5. **[x] LANDED** — Quoted every `icacls "$Path"` and
 250:    `sc.exe delete "$ServiceName"` arg explicitly in
 251:    `Install-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1` and
 252:    `Uninstall-RustyNetWindowsService.ps1`.
 253: 
 254: **Verdict:** Audit complete. None of the findings are
 255: attacker-reachable today (script values come from controlled
 256: sources: hard-coded constants, orchestrator-validated parameters
 257: with strict charsets enforced by `build_windows_security_check_invocation`
 258: + `validate_service_name`, and the Windows guest's own filesystem
 259: state). The remediations listed are pure defense-in-depth and are
 260: tracked as a follow-up W2.5b slice. **Cleared 2026-04-28** with
 261: deferred remediation list above.
 262:

 265: #### A.3.5 Unwrap / expect on attacker-reachable paths

 267: **Result:** Audited via parallel agent. `fetcher.rs:179` was the
 268: one genuine concern (now fixed — A.2.1 above). All other
 269: reviewed `.unwrap()` / `.expect()` call sites either operate on
 270: infallible-by-construction values (literal parses, `Vec::with_capacity`,
 271: etc.) or are preceded by Result-propagating `?` validation. Areas
