===== /documents/operations/done/SecurityReview_2026-03-03.md =====

   1: # Rustynet Security Review - 2026-03-03
   2: 
   3: ## Scope
   4: - Repository: `Rustynet`
   5: - Commit baseline reviewed: `5a611e1`
   6: - Focus areas: secret/key lifecycle, fail-closed dataplane behavior, privileged IPC handling, startup/preflight trust handling, and Debian runtime behavior.
   7: 
   8: ## Findings And Remediations
   9: 
  10: ### 1) Runtime private key could persist on startup/preflight failure
  11: - Severity: High
  12: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs`
  13: - Issue: `run_daemon` decrypted/wrote runtime WG key before preflight, but did not scrub it when preflight/runtime initialization errored.
  14: - Risk: Decrypted key material could remain in `/run/rustynet/wireguard.key` longer than intended.
  15: - Fix implemented:
  16:   - Added guaranteed cleanup path when `run_preflight_checks` fails.
  17:   - Added guaranteed cleanup path when `DaemonRuntime::new` fails.
  18: 
  19: ### 2) Decrypted key buffer not zeroized on write failure
  20: - Severity: High
  21: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs`
  22: - Issue: In `prepare_runtime_wireguard_key`, if runtime key write failed, decrypted key buffer could return early before explicit zeroization.
  23: - Risk: Sensitive key material remained in process memory longer than needed.
  24: - Fix implemented:
  25:   - Refactored flow to always zeroize decrypted buffer before error return.
  26:   - Added best-effort removal of partially written runtime key path on write failure.
  27: 
  28: ### 3) Private key buffers in key setup/migration not always cleared on error
  29: - Severity: High
  30: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/key_material.rs`
  31: - Issue: `initialize_encrypted_key_material` and `migrate_existing_private_key_material` only zeroized private key on success paths.
  32: - Risk: Key bytes could survive in process memory after mid-function errors.
  33: - Fix implemented:
  34:   - Wrapped operations so private key buffer is zeroized regardless of success/failure.
  35:   - Added best-effort cleanup of partially written output key files on failure.
  36: 
  37: ### 4) Temporary key files could remain on disk after write/sync/rename error
  38: - Severity: High
  39: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/key_material.rs`
  40: - Issue: `write_atomic` did not consistently remove temp files on all failure branches.
  41: - Risk: Stranded temp files may retain sensitive key material.
  42: - Fix implemented:
  43:   - Added best-effort temp-file removal on write failure, sync failure, and rename failure.
  44: 
  45: ### 5) IPC command read path was unbounded
  46: - Severity: Medium
  47: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs`
  48: - Issue: `read_command` used unbounded `read_line`, allowing large local payloads.
  49: - Risk: Local memory pressure / DoS against daemon socket.
  50: - Fix implemented:
  51:   - Added hard command-size cap (4096 bytes).
  52:   - Added null-byte rejection.
  53:   - Added UTF-8 validation before parse.
  54: 
  55: ### 6) Fail-closed drop rule could be re-added repeatedly
  56: - Severity: Medium
  57: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs`
  58: - Issue: `block_all_egress` appended drop rules repeatedly in the same chain.
  59: - Risk: nft chain growth over time, increased complexity/perf degradation.
  60: - Fix implemented:
  61:   - Added idempotence check for a tagged fail-closed drop rule.
  62:   - Added comment marker `rustynet_fail_closed_drop` and skip duplicate insertion.
  63: 
  64: ### 7) Linux secure-store decode path could retain sensitive key material on parse error
  65: - Severity: High
  66: - Location: `crates/rustynet-crypto/src/lib.rs`
  67: - Issue: `load_from_linux_secret_service` only zeroized the retrieved key string after successful hex decode.
  68: - Risk: Encoded private key material could remain in process memory if decode failed.
  69: - Fix implemented:
  70:   - Refactored decode flow to always zeroize the retrieved string before returning (success or failure).
  71: 
  72: ### 8) Derived encryption key not always zeroized on crypto failure
  73: - Severity: High
  74: - Location: `crates/rustynet-crypto/src/lib.rs`
  75: - Issue: Fallback `encrypt_private_key_fallback` / `decrypt_private_key_fallback` returned early on AEAD errors before wiping the derived key buffer.
  76: - Risk: Derived key bytes could remain in memory on exceptional paths.
  77: - Fix implemented:
  78:   - Added explicit zeroization on encryption and decryption failure branches before returning.
  79: 
  80: ### 9) Passphrase handling created avoidable non-zeroized copy
  81: - Severity: Medium
  82: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/key_material.rs`, `crates/rustynet-crypto/src/lib.rs`
  83: - Issue: Passphrase handoff into `KeyCustodyManager` required a plain `String`, creating an avoidable duplicate copy.
  84: - Risk: Sensitive passphrase copy could outlive intended lifetime.
  85: - Fix implemented:
  86:   - Added `KeyCustodyManager::new_zeroizing(...)`.
  87:   - Updated daemon key-material path to pass `Zeroizing<String>` directly into custody manager creation.
  88: 
  89: ### 10) Local IPC client could stall daemon command loop indefinitely
  90: - Severity: Medium
  91: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs`
  92: - Issue: Accepted Unix socket streams had no read timeout; a local client could connect and never send a full command line.
  93: - Risk: Single-threaded command loop could block and delay control operations.
  94: - Fix implemented:
  95:   - Added a per-connection read timeout before command ingestion.
  96: 
  97: ### 11) Generated WireGuard private key was not scrubbed if public-key derivation failed
  98: - Severity: High
  99: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/key_material.rs`
 100: - Issue: `generate_wireguard_keypair` returned early on `wg pubkey` derivation failure without wiping generated private key bytes.
 101: - Risk: Private key bytes could remain in process memory on failure path.
 102: - Fix implemented:
 103:   - Added explicit private-key zeroization before returning derivation errors.
 104: 
 105: ### 12) Daemon watermark persistence could leave temporary files on failure
 106: - Severity: Medium
 107: - Location: `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs`
 108: - Issue: trust/membership/auto-tunnel watermark persistence wrote temp files atomically but did not clean temp files on write/sync/rename failures.
 109: - Risk: stale temporary state files could accumulate and leave partial sensitive operational state on disk.
 110: - Fix implemented:
 111:   - Added best-effort temp-file cleanup on all failing write/sync/rename branches.
 112:   - Added parent-directory sync after rename for durability.
 113:   - Enforced parent directory mode `0700` during watermark persistence on Unix.
 114: 
 115: ### 13) Control-plane secure state atomic write could leave temporary files on failure
 116: - Severity: Medium
 117: - Location: `crates/rustynet-control/src/lib.rs`
 118: - Issue: `atomic_write_secure` returned on failure without temp-file cleanup.
 119: - Risk: stranded temp trust-state files and residual integrity-state content on disk.
 120: - Fix implemented:
 121:   - Added best-effort temp-file cleanup on write/sync/rename failures.
 122: 
 123: ### 14) Membership and resilience atomic writes could leave temporary files on failure
 124: - Severity: Medium
 125: - Location: `crates/rustynet-control/src/membership.rs`, `crates/rustynetd/src/resilience.rs`
 126: - Issue: atomic-write helpers did not remove temp files when write/sync/rename failed.
 127: - Risk: stale membership/session temp artifacts and increased forensic residue.
 128: - Fix implemented:
 129:   - Added best-effort temp-file cleanup across failure branches.
 130: 
 131: ## Important Design Note
 132: - Trust watermark equality handling (`==`) was evaluated. Enforcing strict `<=` replay rejection caused valid daemon restarts to fail when trust evidence had not changed.
 133: - Current behavior remains `watermark < existing` rejection to preserve restart safety.
 134: - Recommended future hardening path:
 135:   - Persist and validate a signed trust payload digest, then reject equal watermark only when payload differs unexpectedly.
 136:

===== /documents/phase10.md =====

   1: # Rustynet Phase 10 Plan (Production Exit-Node Dataplane Enablement)
   2: 
   3: ## 0) Document Relationship and Precedence
   4: - This plan extends [Phase9.md](./Phase9.md) and converts simulated dataplane behavior into real encrypted packet transport for exit-node usage.
   5: - [Requirements.md](./Requirements.md) remains normative source of truth.
   6: - [SecurityMinimumBar.md](./SecurityMinimumBar.md) remains release-blocking.
   7: - If conflict exists, the stricter security interpretation applies and lower-precedence docs must be updated.
   8: - Status note (2026-03-05): this document defines **Phase 10 Linux scope**. Current repository behavior now includes additional macOS dataplane hardening and CI coverage beyond Phase 10 scope. For current platform truth, see [operations/PlatformSupportMatrix.md](./operations/PlatformSupportMatrix.md) and [operations/CrossPlatformSecurityGapRemediationPlan_2026-03-05.md](./operations/CrossPlatformSecurityGapRemediationPlan_2026-03-05.md).
   9: - Status note (2026-03-08): `Phase10Controller` now stores authoritative per-peer traversal endpoints, reprograms peer endpoint/bypass routing on direct<->relay transitions, and executes a bounded handshake-driven direct-probe loop. Auto-tunnel runtime now also requires traversal-authoritative coverage for all managed peers during bootstrap/reconcile in enforced mode, fail-closes on traversal runtime programming errors, periodically reprobes relay-backed sessions on reconcile, and uses live backend handshake evidence to keep direct-active peers from downgrading on stale cached probe state. Explicit traversal probe policy is exposed in daemon config/status/netcheck instead of relying on implicit runtime defaults. Remaining open work is production relay transport service plus full WAN simultaneous-open traversal behavior.
  10: 
  11: ## 1) Phase 10 Objective
  12: Deliver real Linux dataplane execution so one enrolled device can act as an authorized exit node and securely route another enrolled device's traffic through encrypted transport, including signed endpoint-hint-driven direct UDP hole punching with encrypted relay fallback/failback, and mandatory fail-closed behavior for traffic and DNS.
  13: 
  14: ## 2) Exact Phase 10 Boundaries
  15: ### 2.1 In Scope
  16: - Real Linux WireGuard backend implementation behind `TunnelBackend`.
  17: - Persistent `rustynetd` daemon + authenticated local IPC control path.
  18: - Real route/rule/firewall/NAT programming for exit-node full-tunnel and LAN-toggle flows.
  19: - Tunnel and DNS fail-closed enforcement and validation.
  20: - Direct/relay fallback/failback behavior under real networking.
  21: - Signed traversal endpoint-hint validation and deterministic path-control behavior for direct/relay transitions.
  22: - End-to-end Linux netns/VM validation and production-grade gate scripts.
  23: 
  24: ### 2.2 Out of Scope
  25: - New cryptographic protocol design.
  26: - Non-Linux dataplane implementations.
  27: - UI redesign or policy language redesign.
  28: - Replacing WireGuard backend in this phase (only preserving replaceability).
  29: 
  30: ## 3) Immutable Constraints (Must Hold)
  31: - Rust-first implementation. Non-Rust only for unavoidable OS integration boundaries.
  32: - No custom cryptography or custom VPN protocol invention in production paths.
  33: - WireGuard remains an adapter behind `TunnelBackend`; no WireGuard-specific leakage into protocol-agnostic control/policy/domain layers.
  34: - Default-deny and least privilege across ACL, routing, firewalling, DNS, and helper execution.
  35: - Fail closed when trust/security state is missing, invalid, stale, or unavailable.
  36: 
  37: ## 4) Platform and Runtime Prerequisites
  38: | Area | Requirement | Enforcement |
  39: | --- | --- | --- |
  40: | OS | Linux-only for Phase 10 dataplane | startup capability check |
  41: | Setup host profile | Wizard/bootstrap must detect host OS and enforce `linux` vs compatibility host behavior | startup host-profile gate + preflight doctor |
  42: | Kernel features | WireGuard + netfilter/nftables + policy routing | startup probe; fail closed |
  43: | Privileges | minimal required capabilities (`CAP_NET_ADMIN`, `CAP_NET_RAW` only where required) | process capability audit at startup |
  44: | Tooling | Rust native route/rule/firewall APIs preferred; no shell composition | CI check + code review gate |
  45: | Distros in test matrix | Debian 12 baseline + one secondary Linux distro | phase10 gate matrix |
  46: 
  47: If prerequisites are not satisfied, daemon remains in restricted-safe mode and refuses tunnel/exit activation.
  48: 
  49: Host-profile storage policy requirement:
  50: - Linux runtime roots (`/etc/rustynet`, `/var/lib/rustynet`, `/run/rustynet`, `/var/log/rustynet`) are valid only on Linux hosts.
  51: - Non-Linux compatibility hosts must store wizard/runtime artifacts in platform-safe user-scoped directories and must not create Linux runtime roots.
  52: 
  53: ## 5) Gap Assessment (Previous Draft)
  54: Previous Phase 10 draft was directionally correct but underspecified in these areas:
  55: 1. No explicit in-scope/out-of-scope boundary.
  56: 2. No deterministic dataplane state machine with transition guards.
  57: 3. No formal transactional apply/rollback sequence.
  58: 4. No explicit IPv6 policy for leak-prevention behavior.
  59: 5. No concrete evidence artifact contract for acceptance gates.
  60: 6. No requirement-to-implementation matrix tied to Requirements and Security Minimum Bar.
  61: 
  62: This revised document closes those gaps.
  63: 
  64: ## 6) Final Architecture for Phase 10
  65: ### 6.1 `rustynetd` Runtime Modules
  66: 1. `backend_manager`: owns `TunnelBackend` lifecycle and peer sync.
  67: 2. `route_manager`: installs/removes routes and policy rules transactionally.
  68: 3. `firewall_manager`: applies nftables policy, NAT, kill-switch chains.
  69: 4. `dns_manager`: applies protected-DNS routing and resolver restrictions.
  70: 5. `exit_manager`: owns exit-node selection, LAN-toggle, and ACL-validated route grants.
  71: 6. `ipc_server`: authenticated local control RPC over Unix socket.
  72: 7. `nat_traversal`: signed endpoint-hint ingestion, candidate checks, direct hole-punch orchestration, and relay failover/failback decisions.
  73: 8. `health_monitor`: path/tunnel/dns health and fail-closed transitions.
  74: 9. `state_store`: durable runtime state with integrity checks.
  75: 
  76: ### 6.2 Linux Integration Choices
  77: - nftables-first firewall and NAT.
  78: - netlink-driven route/rule updates from Rust.
  79: - argv-only privileged helper path only when kernel APIs are unavailable.
  80: - Idempotent apply and deterministic rollback.
  81: 
  82: ### 6.3 Local IPC Security Contract
  83: - Unix socket in runtime dir with strict owner permissions.
  84: - Peer identity verification (`SO_PEERCRED`) for all mutating commands.
  85: - Role check before mutation.
  86: - IPC auth failure results in deny with zero side effects.
  87: 
  88: ### 6.4 Traversal Path-Control Contract
  89: - Endpoint-hint updates are accepted only when signature, nonce, and freshness checks succeed.
  90: - Direct and relay are runtime path states under one controller, not separate legacy paths.
  91: - Path transitions are deterministic, auditable, and policy-gated.
  92: - If no trusted path is available in protected mode, transition to `fail_closed`.
  93: 
  94: ### 6.5 Managed DNS Contract
  95: - Managed-name state is accepted only from signed DNS-zone bundles with watermark/replay protection.
  96: - DNS records bind names to `target_node_id` and must cross-check against signed assignment-derived mesh IPs; raw arbitrary IP ownership is rejected.
  97: - The authoritative managed-zone resolver is loopback-only and must not listen on underlay/LAN interfaces.
  98: - Managed-zone queries return `SERVFAIL` when signed DNS state is missing, invalid, stale, or mismatched with assignment state.
  99: - Non-managed names are refused by the local authoritative resolver rather than silently handled through ad hoc local overrides.
 100: 
 101: ## 7) Dataplane State Machine (Normative)
 102: States:
 103: 1. `init`
 104: 2. `control_trusted`
 105: 3. `dataplane_applied`
 106: 4. `exit_active` (with path substate `direct_active` or `relay_active`)
 107: 5. `fail_closed`
 108: 
 109: Required transitions:
 110: - `init -> control_trusted`: control TLS1.3 valid + signed control data valid + freshness checks pass.
 111: - `control_trusted -> dataplane_applied`: backend/routing/firewall/dns transactional apply succeeds.
 112: - `dataplane_applied -> exit_active`: exit policy + ACL + route advertisement + LAN-toggle constraints valid.
 113: - `exit_active(direct_active) -> exit_active(relay_active)`: direct path health loss or probe failure with trusted relay path available.
 114: - `exit_active(relay_active) -> exit_active(direct_active)`: signed, fresh, policy-valid direct path re-established and stable.
 115: - `* -> fail_closed`: any trust loss, apply failure, integrity failure, or health loss in protected mode.
 116: - `fail_closed -> control_trusted`: only after trust and safety preconditions re-validated.
 117: 
 118: Forbidden behavior:
 119: - No transition may permit unprotected egress when protected mode is expected.
 120: - No transition may apply stale unsigned control state.
 121: 
 122: ## 8) Transactional Apply and Rollback Algorithm (Normative)
 123: Apply order:
 124: 1. Validate trust/freshness preconditions.
 125: 2. Stage backend peer/interface changes.
 126: 3. Stage route/rule changes.
 127: 4. Stage firewall + kill-switch baseline.
 128: 5. Stage NAT/forwarding for exit mode.
 129: 6. Stage DNS protection rules.
 130: 7. Commit active generation marker.
 131: 
 132: Rollback rules:
 133: - Any failure in steps 2-6 triggers reverse-order rollback of all staged changes.
 134: - If rollback itself partially fails, force `fail_closed` with explicit operator-visible error.
 135: - Daemon must preserve last-known-safe generation and refuse unsafe partial generations.
 136: 
 137: ## 9) Security Baseline for Real Dataplane
 138: ### 9.1 Trust/Freshness Preconditions
 139: - Do not apply peer/route state unless control transport is TLS1.3-valid.
 140: - Do not apply peer/route state unless signed control/peer data verification succeeds.
 141: - Enforce max age for signed control data; stale state is rejected.
 142: - Enforce strict clock-skew bounds for freshness checks.
 143: 
 144: ### 9.2 Key and Secret Handling
 145: - Node private keys from OS secure store when available.
 146: - Encrypted-at-rest fallback with strict file permissions and startup permission validation.
 147: - No cleartext key material in logs, debug output, CLI output, env vars, or panic paths.
 148: 
 149: ### 9.3 Privileged Boundary Hardening
 150: - Daemon/hardening profile must restrict filesystem and syscall surface to minimum required.
 151: - Helper invocation must be argv-only with strict input validation.
 152: - No shell interpolation for untrusted values.
 153: 
 154: ### 9.4 Exit-Node Threat Controls
 155: - Compromised exit node: enforce ACL boundaries and explicit trust model; no implicit LAN access.
 156: - Route injection: validate advertised routes against policy and CIDR sanity constraints.
 157: - DNS poisoning/leak: protected mode requires trusted resolver path and fail-close behavior.
 158: - Lateral pivot risk: LAN route access requires explicit toggle + ACL allow + advertised route.
 159: 
 160: ### 9.5 IPv6 Policy (Explicit)
 161: - Phase 10 must explicitly choose one behavior and test it:
 162: 1. Full IPv6 support path with equivalent ACL/kill-switch/DNS protections, or
 163: 2. Hard-disable IPv6 egress in protected modes to prevent dual-stack leakage.
 164: 
 165: Default for Phase 10: if equivalent protections are not implemented for IPv6, enforce hard-disable fail-closed behavior.
 166: 
 167: ### 9.6 Fail-Closed Decisions (Explicit)
 168: - If firewall install fails: do not enable tunnel routing.
 169: - If route install partially fails: rollback and deny activation.
 170: - If kill-switch cannot be asserted: keep egress blocked.
 171: - If trust-state load/verify fails: deny trust-required connectivity.
 172: - If daemon state restore fails integrity checks: start in restricted-safe mode.
 173: 
 174: ### 9.7 Traversal Integrity Controls
 175: - Endpoint-hint payloads must be signed and freshness-bounded; replayed or tampered hints are rejected.
 176: - Runtime must not mutate peer endpoints from unsigned traversal data.
 177: - Path transition logic must preserve ACL/default-deny and leak-prevention invariants across direct/relay handoffs.
 178: - Relay path use must remain ciphertext-only forwarding from a relay trust perspective.
 179: 
 180: ## 10) Detailed Workstreams
 181: ### Workstream A: Real Linux WireGuard Backend (`rustynet-backend-wireguard`)
 182: - Implement interface create/configure/start/stop.
 183: - Implement peer add/remove/update and route reconciliation.
 184: - Implement stats collection mapped to `TunnelStats`.
 185: - Add backend conformance tests for lifecycle, route replacement, exit-mode transitions, recovery.
 186: 
 187: ### Workstream B: Persistent Daemon + CLI Control (`rustynetd`, `rustynet-cli`)
 188: - Add daemon process mode with runtime state persistence and integrity checks.
 189: - Add IPC API for status, netcheck, exit-node select/off, lan-access on/off, dns inspect, route advertise.
 190: - Update CLI to call daemon IPC only.
 191: 
 192: ### Workstream C: Exit Routing/NAT + Kill-Switch
 193: - Implement forwarding/NAT apply/remove.
 194: - Implement protected-routing kill-switch chain and rollback-safe updates.
 195: - Implement protected DNS egress restrictions and resolver routing.
 196: - Implement signed managed-zone ingestion and loopback-only authoritative resolution for the private Rustynet zone.
 197: 
 198: ### Workstream D: Policy and ACL Enforcement in Dataplane
 199: - Enforce protocol-aware ACL decisions for exit and shared-router contexts.
 200: - Validate route advertisements and ACL grants before route installation.
 201: - Keep default-deny posture for all non-explicitly-allowed flows.
 202: 
 203: ### Workstream E: E2E Harness and Operationalization
 204: - Netns/VM scenario runner for multi-device tests.
 205: - Packet-capture verification for encrypted tunnel transport.
 206: - Ops runbook updates for deployment, rollback, and incident handling.
 207: 
 208: ### Workstream F: Traversal/Hole-Punch Integration
 209: - Implement signed endpoint-hint schema verification and replay rejection in `rustynetd`.
 210: - Implement direct candidate checks and deterministic direct/relay path controller behavior.
 211: - Integrate traversal telemetry into `status`/`netcheck` and transition audit logs.
 212: 
 213: ## 11) Observability and Alerting Contract
 214: Required metrics:
 215: - tunnel state, peer count, direct/relay path mode, handshake recency.
 216: - apply generation success/failure counts and durations.
 217: - kill-switch asserted state.
 218: - DNS protection state and blocked-leak events.
 219: - exit-node activation failures by reason.
 220: 
 221: Required structured logs:
 222: - transition events (`from_state`, `to_state`, `reason`).
 223: - apply generation id, rollback id, and failure category.
 224: - trust/freshness reject reasons (without secrets).
 225: 
 226: Required alerts:
 227: - fail-closed entered.
 228: - repeated apply failures.
 229: - DNS protection unavailable in protected mode.
 230: 
 231: ## 12) Testing and Validation Requirements
 232: ### 12.1 Unit Tests
 233: - Backend lifecycle and error invariants.
 234: - IPC authn/authz and command validation.
 235: - Route/firewall planner idempotency and rollback behavior.
 236: - Kill-switch state-machine transitions.
 237: - Traversal endpoint-hint validator coverage (signature, nonce, freshness, replay rejection).
 238: 
 239: ### 12.2 Integration Tests
 240: - Device A selects device B as exit node and reaches internet through B.
 241: - Device A LAN access denied with toggle off.
 242: - Device A LAN access allowed only with toggle on + ACL allow + advertised route.
 243: - Direct-path failure triggers relay fallback, then direct failback when healthy.
 244: - Direct UDP hole punching establishes path when NAT conditions permit.
 245: - Hard-NAT scenario converges to encrypted relay path while preserving connectivity.
 246: - Roaming endpoint change preserves connectivity.
 247: 
 248: ### 12.3 Security/Negative Tests
 249: - Tunnel drop in protected mode blocks egress.
 250: - DNS path loss in protected DNS mode blocks DNS egress.
 251: - Invalid or stale signed control data rejected before dataplane mutation.
 252: - Tampered/replayed traversal endpoint hints are rejected before endpoint mutation.
 253: - Path flaps (direct<->relay) do not bypass ACL, kill-switch, or DNS fail-close controls.
 254: - Privileged helper rejects unsafe input and shell-like payloads.
 255: - WireGuard leakage check outside backend adapter crates.
 256: 
 257: ### 12.4 Performance/Soak Gates
 258: - Idle CPU <= 2% one core.
 259: - Idle RSS <= 120 MB.
 260: - Reconnect <= 5s.
 261: - Route/policy apply <= 2s p95.
 262: - Throughput overhead <= 15% vs baseline WG path.
 263: - Soak duration >= 24h on declared benchmark matrix.
 264:

 298: ## 14) Rollout and Rollback Plan
 299: Rollout:
 300: 1. Ship daemon/backend in disabled mode.
 301: 2. Enable canary on limited nodes.
 302: 3. Validate gate evidence and operational SLOs.
 303: 4. Gradually expand to stable channel.
 304: 
 305: Rollback:
 306: 1. Disable exit mode and revert to last-known-safe generation.
 307: 2. Reapply previous firewall/route generation.
 308: 3. Keep fail-closed protections active until trust and dataplane health restored.
 309: 4. Emit incident marker and required forensics artifact bundle.
 310: 
 311: ## 15) Requirement-to-Implementation Traceability Matrix (Phase 10)
 312: | Source Clause | Requirement | Implementation Direction | Owner |
 313: | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 314: | Requirements 3.2 | Encrypted mesh networking with NAT traversal + relay fallback | WireGuard backend + signed traversal endpoint-hint flow + deterministic path controller | `rustynet-backend-wireguard` + `rustynetd` |
 315: | Requirements 3.3 | Exit node selection/full-tunnel | `exit_manager` + route/firewall/NAT apply | `rustynetd` |
 316: | Requirements 3.4 | LAN toggle with ACL gates | toggle + advertised route + ACL precondition enforcement | `rustynetd` + `rustynet-policy` |
 317: | Requirements 3.5 | Magic DNS behavior safety | protected DNS routing + resolver constraints + single `systemd-resolved` integration path on Linux | `dns_manager` |
 318: | Requirements 3.6 | Default-deny ACL and protocol-aware rules | dataplane route/filter apply from policy decisions | `rustynet-policy` + `rustynetd` |
 319: | Requirements 4/5 | Reliability and security-first defaults | state machine + fail-closed + trust gating | `health_monitor` + `state_store` |
 320: | Security Minimum Bar Critical 1 | Proven crypto only | WireGuard-only production dataplane | backend adapter layer |
 321: | Security Minimum Bar Critical 2 | TLS1.3 + signed control validation | trust preconditions before dataplane apply | control client path |
 322: | Security Minimum Bar Critical 8 | Traversal transition integrity + leak prevention | signed traversal hints + direct/relay path guards + fail-closed transitions | `nat_traversal` + `health_monitor` |
 323: | Security Minimum Bar Critical 7 | Leak prevention | kill-switch + DNS fail-close tests | firewall/dns managers |
 324: | Security Minimum Bar Critical 10 | Supply-chain integrity | phase10 gate includes artifact verification and evidence | CI scripts |
 325: 
 326: ## 16) Deliverables
 327: - Real Linux WireGuard adapter implementation behind `TunnelBackend`.
 328: - Persistent `rustynetd` daemon with secure local IPC.
 329: - CLI wired to daemon IPC (no ephemeral command-local state).
 330: - Signed traversal endpoint-hint verification and deterministic direct/relay path controller.
 331: - Exit-node forwarding/NAT + kill-switch + protected DNS enforcement.
 332: - E2E Linux network harness and acceptance/security test suite.
 333: - Updated operations runbook and incident drill procedures for exit-node dataplane incidents.
 334: - New Phase 10 gate scripts and required evidence artifacts.
 335: 
 336: ## 17) Phase 10 Exit Criteria
 337: - Two real enrolled Linux nodes complete encrypted tunnel communication.
 338: - One node can be selected as exit node by authorized client and route client internet traffic.
 339: - LAN-route access behavior is exactly ACL/toggle/advertisement constrained.
 340: - Tunnel and DNS fail-close behavior is proven in negative tests.
 341: - Direct path establishes through hole punching when network allows, and relay path is used when direct is unavailable.
 342: - Direct/relay fallback and failback works under controlled fault tests.
 343: - All mandatory CI/security/performance/soak gates pass.
 344: - Required evidence artifacts exist and are valid.
 345: - No unresolved phase-scope TODO/FIXME/placeholders remain.

===== /scripts/bootstrap/linux/rn_bootstrap.sh =====

   1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2: set -euo pipefail
   3: 
   4: if [[ $# -ne 1 ]]; then
   5:   echo "usage: rn_bootstrap.sh <env-file>" >&2
   6:   exit 2
   7: fi
   8: 
   9: source "$1"
  10: 
  11: run_root() {
  12:   sudo -n "$@"
  13: }
  14: 
  15: run_root_timed() {
  16:   local timeout_secs="$1"
  17:   shift
  18:   timeout "$timeout_secs" sudo -n "$@"
  19: }
  20: 
  21: run_local_timed() {
  22:   local timeout_secs="$1"
  23:   shift
  24:   timeout "$timeout_secs" "$@"
  25: }
  26: 
  27: clear_residual_rustynet_state() {
  28:   run_root_timed 30 ip link set rustynet0 down >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  29:   run_root_timed 30 ip link delete rustynet0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  30:   run_root_timed 30 ip route flush table 51820 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  31:   run_root_timed 30 ip -6 route flush table 51820 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  32:   if command -v nft >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  33:     for _attempt in $(seq 1 3); do
  34:       while read -r family table_name; do
  35:         [[ -n "${family}" && -n "${table_name}" ]] || continue
  36:         run_root_timed 30 nft flush table "${family}" "${table_name}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  37:         run_root_timed 30 nft delete table "${family}" "${table_name}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
  38:       done < <(run_root_timed 30 nft list tables 2>/dev/null | awk '/^table / && $3 ~ /^rustynet/ { print $2 " " $3 }' | tr -d '\r')
  39:       if ! run_root_timed 30 nft list tables 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^table [^[:space:]]+ rustynet'; then
  40:         break
  41:       fi
  42:       sleep 1
  43:     done
  44:     if run_root_timed 30 nft list tables 2>/dev/null | grep -qE '^table [^[:space:]]+ rustynet'; then
  45:       echo "residual rustynet nftables state remained before bootstrap" >&2
  46:       exit 1
  47:     fi
  48:   fi
  49: }
  50: 
  51: wait_for_package_manager_idle() {
  52:   local pattern="$1"
  53:   local label="$2"
  54:   local attempt
  55:   for attempt in $(seq 1 60); do
  56:     if ! pgrep -f "$pattern" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  57:       return 0
  58:     fi
  59:     sleep 2
  60:   done
  61:   echo "${label} remained busy after waiting for prior lab processes to exit" >&2
  62:   pgrep -af "$pattern" >&2 || true
  63:   exit 1
  64: }
  65: 
  66: build_bootstrap_prereqs_present() {
  67:   local PATH="/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:${PATH}"
  68:   local missing=0
  69:   local cmd
  70:   local llvm_found=0
  71:   for cmd in curl git make pkg-config clang nft wg rustup; do
  72:     if ! command -v "${cmd}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  73:       echo "[bootstrap] missing prerequisite command: ${cmd}" >&2
  74:       missing=1
  75:     fi
  76:   done
  77:   if ! command -v gcc >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v cc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  78:     echo "[bootstrap] missing C compiler command (gcc/cc)" >&2
  79:     missing=1
  80:   fi
  81:   if ! command -v g++ >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v c++ >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  82:     echo "[bootstrap] missing C++ compiler command (g++/c++)" >&2
  83:     missing=1
  84:   fi
  85:   if command -v llvm-config >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  86:     llvm_found=1
  87:   else
  88:     for cmd in /usr/bin/llvm-config-* /usr/local/bin/llvm-config-*; do
  89:       [[ -x "${cmd}" ]] || continue
  90:       llvm_found=1
  91:       break
  92:     done
  93:   fi
  94:   if [[ "${llvm_found}" -eq 0 ]]; then
  95:     echo "[bootstrap] missing llvm-config command" >&2
  96:     missing=1
  97:   fi
  98:   if command -v pkg-config >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  99:     if ! pkg-config --exists openssl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 100:       echo "[bootstrap] missing pkg-config openssl development metadata" >&2
 101:       missing=1
 102:     fi
 103:     if ! pkg-config --exists sqlite3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 104:       echo "[bootstrap] missing pkg-config sqlite3 development metadata" >&2
 105:       missing=1
 106:     fi
 107:   fi
 108:   if [[ ! -r /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt ]]; then
 109:     echo "[bootstrap] missing readable CA certificate bundle at /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt" >&2
 110:     missing=1
 111:   fi
 112:   [[ "${missing}" -eq 0 ]]
 113: }
 114: 
 115: install_prereqs() {
 116:   local os_id=""
 117:   local os_like=""
 118:   if [[ -f /etc/os-release ]]; then
 119:     # shellcheck disable=SC1091
 120:     . /etc/os-release
 121:     os_id="${ID:-}"
 122:     os_like="${ID_LIKE:-}"
 123:   fi
 124:   if build_bootstrap_prereqs_present; then
 125:     echo "[bootstrap] prerequisite toolchain already present; skipping package manager mutation" >&2
 126:     return 0
 127:   fi
 128:   if [[ "${os_id}" == "fedora" || "${os_like}" == *"fedora"* || "${os_like}" == *"rhel"* ]]; then
 129:     wait_for_package_manager_idle 'dnf|rpm' 'dnf/rpm'
 130:     run_root_timed 1800 dnf install -y \
 131:       ca-certificates curl git gcc gcc-c++ make pkgconf-pkg-config openssl-devel \
 132:       sqlite-devel clang llvm nftables wireguard-tools rustup
 133:   elif [[ "${os_id}" == "debian" || "${os_id}" == "ubuntu" || "${os_id}" == "linuxmint" || "${os_like}" == *"debian"* ]] || command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 134:     run_apt_update_hardened
 135:     run_apt_install_hardened \
 136:       ca-certificates curl git build-essential pkg-config libssl-dev libsqlite3-dev \
 137:       clang llvm nftables wireguard-tools openssl systemd-resolved libnss-resolve rustup
 138:   else
 139:     echo "unsupported package manager; expected apt-get or dnf" >&2
 140:     exit 1
 141:   fi
 142:   if ! build_bootstrap_prereqs_present; then
 143:     echo "[bootstrap] prerequisite verification failed after package installation" >&2
 144:     exit 1
 145:   fi
 146: }
 147: 
 148: ensure_llvm_config_alias() {
 149:   if command -v llvm-config >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 150:     return 0
 151:   fi
 152:   local candidate=""
 153:   for candidate in /usr/bin/llvm-config-* /usr/local/bin/llvm-config-*; do
 154:     [[ -x "${candidate}" ]] || continue
 155:     run_root ln -sf "${candidate}" /usr/local/bin/llvm-config
 156:     return 0
 157:   done
 158:   echo "[bootstrap] unable to locate versioned llvm-config binary" >&2
 159:   return 1
 160: }
 161: 
 162: run_apt_update_hardened() {
 163:   local attempt
 164:   local apt_log
 165:   local -a apt_network_opts
 166:   apt_network_opts=(
 167:     -o Acquire::Retries=3
 168:     -o Acquire::ForceIPv4=true
 169:     -o Acquire::http::Timeout=60
 170:     -o Acquire::https::Timeout=60
 171:     -o Dpkg::Use-Pty=0
 172:   )
 173:   for attempt in $(seq 1 3); do
 174:     wait_for_package_manager_idle 'apt-get|/usr/lib/apt/methods/|dpkg' 'apt/dpkg'
 175:     apt_log="$(mktemp /tmp/rn-apt-update.XXXXXX.log)"
 176:     if run_root_timed 240 env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get \
 177:       "${apt_network_opts[@]}" \
 178:       update 2>&1 | tee "${apt_log}"; then
 179:       if ! grep -Eiq '(^W: Failed to fetch|Temporary failure resolving|Some index files failed to download)' "${apt_log}"; then
 180:         rm -f "${apt_log}"
 181:         return 0
 182:       fi
 183:       echo "[bootstrap] apt-get update reported fetch warnings; treating as failure" >&2
 184:     fi
 185:     rm -f "${apt_log}"
 186:     if [[ "${attempt}" -lt 3 ]]; then
 187:       echo "[bootstrap] apt-get update attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying after DNS repair" >&2
 188:       run_root_timed 120 env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get clean >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 189:       repair_bootstrap_dns_state
 190:       sleep 2
 191:     fi
 192:   done
 193:   echo "[bootstrap] apt-get update failed after retries" >&2
 194:   emit_bootstrap_network_diagnostics "deb.debian.org"
 195:   return 1
 196: }
 197: 
 198: run_apt_install_hardened() {
 199:   local attempt
 200:   local -a apt_network_opts
 201:   apt_network_opts=(
 202:     -o Acquire::Retries=3
 203:     -o Acquire::ForceIPv4=true
 204:     -o Acquire::http::Timeout=60
 205:     -o Acquire::https::Timeout=60
 206:     -o Dpkg::Use-Pty=0
 207:   )
 208:   if [[ "$#" -eq 0 ]]; then
 209:     echo "run_apt_install_hardened requires package names" >&2
 210:     return 2
 211:   fi
 212:   for attempt in $(seq 1 3); do
 213:     if run_root_timed 5400 env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get \
 214:       "${apt_network_opts[@]}" \
 215:       install -y --no-install-recommends "$@"; then
 216:       return 0
 217:     fi
 218:     if [[ "${attempt}" -lt 3 ]]; then
 219:       echo "[bootstrap] apt-get install attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying after DNS repair" >&2
 220:       run_root_timed 120 env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get clean >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 221:       repair_bootstrap_dns_state
 222:       sleep 2
 223:     fi
 224:   done
 225:   echo "[bootstrap] apt-get install failed after retries" >&2
 226:   emit_bootstrap_network_diagnostics "deb.debian.org"
 227:   return 1
 228: }
 229: 
 230: repair_managed_dns_prereqs() {
 231:   local os_id=""
 232:   local os_like=""
 233:   if [[ -f /etc/os-release ]]; then
 234:     # shellcheck disable=SC1091
 235:     . /etc/os-release
 236:     os_id="${ID:-}"
 237:     os_like="${ID_LIKE:-}"
 238:   fi
 239:   if [[ "${os_id}" != "debian" && "${os_id}" != "ubuntu" && "${os_id}" != "linuxmint" && "${os_like}" != *"debian"* ]]; then
 240:     return 0
 241:   fi
 242:   if ! command -v resolvectl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 243:     echo "managed DNS routing requires resolvectl on Debian-like hosts" >&2
 244:     exit 1
 245:   fi
 246:   run_root systemctl enable --now systemd-resolved.service
 247:   if ! run_root resolvectl status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 248:     run_root systemctl reload dbus
 249:     run_root systemctl restart systemd-resolved.service
 250:     run_root resolvectl status >/dev/null 2>&1 || {
 251:       echo "managed DNS control plane remained unhealthy after dbus reload and systemd-resolved restart" >&2
 252:       exit 1
 253:     }
 254:   fi
 255: }
 256: 
 257: repair_local_hostname_resolution() {
 258:   local current_hostname=""
 259:   current_hostname="$(hostname)"
 260:   [[ -n "${current_hostname}" ]] || return 0
 261:   if grep -Eq "(^|[[:space:]])${current_hostname}([[:space:]]|$)" /etc/hosts; then
 262:     return 0
 263:   fi
 264:   run_root sh -c 'printf "\n127.0.1.1\t%s\n" "$1" >> /etc/hosts' sh "${current_hostname}"
 265: }
 266: 
 267: repair_rustup_toolchain_state() {
 268:   local channel="$1"
 269:   rustup toolchain uninstall "$channel" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 270:   rm -rf "$HOME/.rustup/tmp"
 271:   mkdir -p "$HOME/.rustup/downloads" "$HOME/.rustup/toolchains"
 272:   find "$HOME/.rustup/downloads" -maxdepth 1 -type f -delete 2>/dev/null || true
 273:   rm -rf "$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/${channel}" "$HOME/.rustup/toolchains/${channel}.tmp"*
 274: }
 275: 
 276: repair_bootstrap_dns_state() {
 277:   local default_iface=""
 278:   local default_gateway=""
 279:   default_iface="$(ip -4 route show default 2>/dev/null | awk '/default/ { for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) if ($i == "dev") { print $(i + 1); exit } }')"
 280:   default_gateway="$(ip -4 route show default 2>/dev/null | awk '/default/ { print $3; exit }')"
 281: 
 282:   if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 283:     run_root_timed 30 systemctl reload dbus >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 284:     run_root_timed 30 systemctl enable --now systemd-resolved.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 285:     run_root_timed 30 systemctl restart systemd-resolved.service >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 286:   fi
 287:   if [[ -e /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf ]]; then
 288:     run_root_timed 30 ln -sf /run/systemd/resolve/stub-resolv.conf /etc/resolv.conf >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 289:   fi
 290:   if command -v resolvectl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 291:     if [[ -n "${default_iface}" ]]; then
 292:       run_root_timed 30 resolvectl revert "${default_iface}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 293:       if [[ -n "${default_gateway}" ]]; then
 294:         run_root_timed 30 resolvectl dns "${default_iface}" "${default_gateway}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 295:       fi
 296:       run_root_timed 30 resolvectl domain "${default_iface}" "~." >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 297:       run_root_timed 30 resolvectl default-route "${default_iface}" yes >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 298:     fi
 299:     run_root_timed 30 resolvectl flush-caches >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
 300:   elif [[ -n "${default_gateway}" ]]; then
 301:     run_root sh -c 'printf "nameserver %s\noptions timeout:2 attempts:2\n" "$1" > /etc/resolv.conf' sh "${default_gateway}"
 302:   fi
 303: }
 304: 
 305: emit_bootstrap_network_diagnostics() {
 306:   local host="$1"
 307:   echo "[bootstrap] network diagnostics for host=${host}" >&2
 308:   echo "--- /etc/resolv.conf ---" >&2
 309:   cat /etc/resolv.conf >&2 || true
 310:   echo "--- ip -4 route ---" >&2
 311:   ip -4 route >&2 || true
 312:   echo "--- ip -4 addr ---" >&2
 313:   ip -4 addr >&2 || true
 314:   if command -v resolvectl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 315:     echo "--- resolvectl status ---" >&2
 316:     run_root_timed 30 resolvectl status >&2 || true
 317:     echo "--- resolvectl query ${host} ---" >&2
 318:     run_root_timed 30 resolvectl query "${host}" >&2 || true
 319:   fi
 320:   echo "--- getent ahosts ${host} ---" >&2
 321:   getent ahosts "${host}" >&2 || true
 322: }
 323: 
 324: wait_for_bootstrap_rustup_endpoint() {
 325:   local channel="$1"
 326:   local endpoint="https://static.rust-lang.org/dist/channel-rust-${channel}.toml.sha256"
 327:   local attempt
 328:   for attempt in $(seq 1 8); do
 329:     if run_local_timed 60 curl --ipv4 --fail --silent --show-error --head "${endpoint}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 330:       return 0
 331:     fi
 332:     repair_bootstrap_dns_state
 333:     sleep 2
 334:   done
 335:   echo "[bootstrap] failed to reach Rust toolchain endpoint: ${endpoint}" >&2
 336:   emit_bootstrap_network_diagnostics "static.rust-lang.org"
 337:   return 1
 338: }
 339: 
 340: install_rust_toolchain_hardened() {
 341:   local channel="$1"
 342:   local attempt
 343:   wait_for_bootstrap_rustup_endpoint "${channel}" || return 1
 344:   for attempt in $(seq 1 3); do
 345:     if run_local_timed 3600 env \
 346:       RUSTUP_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT=600 \
 347:       RUSTUP_CONCURRENT_DOWNLOADS=1 \
 348:       rustup toolchain install "${channel}" --profile minimal; then
 349:       return 0
 350:     fi
 351:     if [[ "${attempt}" -lt 3 ]]; then
 352:       echo "[bootstrap] rustup install attempt ${attempt} failed; retrying after DNS repair" >&2
 353:       repair_bootstrap_dns_state
 354:       wait_for_bootstrap_rustup_endpoint "${channel}" || true
 355:       sleep 2
 356:     fi
 357:   done
 358:   echo "[bootstrap] rustup toolchain install failed after retries for channel ${channel}" >&2
 359:   emit_bootstrap_network_diagnostics "static.rust-lang.org"
 360:   return 1
 361: }

 363: clear_residual_rustynet_state
 364: repair_local_hostname_resolution
 365: install_prereqs
 366: ensure_llvm_config_alias
 367: repair_managed_dns_prereqs
 368: if ! command -v rustup >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 369:   echo "rustup is required on test hosts; missing after prerequisite install" >&2
 370:   exit 1
 371: fi
 372: 
 373: rm -rf "${HOME}/Rustynet"
 374: mkdir -p "${HOME}/Rustynet"
 375: tar -xzf "${SOURCE_ARCHIVE}" -C "${HOME}/Rustynet"
 376: cd "${HOME}/Rustynet"
 377: 
 378: RUST_TOOLCHAIN_CHANNEL="$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*channel[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' rust-toolchain.toml 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)"
 379: if [[ -z "${RUST_TOOLCHAIN_CHANNEL}" ]]; then
 380:   echo "failed to determine required Rust toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml" >&2
 381:   exit 1
 382: fi
 383: 
 384: export PATH="${HOME}/.cargo/bin:${PATH}"
 385: rustup set profile minimal
 386: if ! rustup run "${RUST_TOOLCHAIN_CHANNEL}" rustc --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! rustup run "${RUST_TOOLCHAIN_CHANNEL}" cargo --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 387:   repair_rustup_toolchain_state "${RUST_TOOLCHAIN_CHANNEL}"
 388:   install_rust_toolchain_hardened "${RUST_TOOLCHAIN_CHANNEL}"
 389: fi
 390: rustup default "${RUST_TOOLCHAIN_CHANNEL}"
 391: 
 392: run_local_timed 7200 rustup run "${RUST_TOOLCHAIN_CHANNEL}" cargo build --release -p rustynetd -p rustynet-cli
 393: run_root install -m 0755 target/release/rustynetd /usr/local/bin/rustynetd
 394: run_root install -m 0755 target/release/rustynet-cli /usr/local/bin/rustynet
 395: backend_env=()
 396: if [[ -n "${RUSTYNET_BACKEND:-}" ]]; then
 397:   backend_env+=(RUSTYNET_BACKEND="${RUSTYNET_BACKEND}")
 398: fi
 399: run_root env RUSTYNET_INSTALL_SOURCE_ROOT="${HOME}/Rustynet" "${backend_env[@]}" \

 402:   --node-id "${NODE_ID}" \
 403:   --network-id "${NETWORK_ID}" \
 404:   --src-dir "${HOME}/Rustynet" \

===== /scripts/bootstrap/macos/Bootstrap-RustyNetMacos.sh =====

   1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2: # Bootstrap-RustyNetMacos.sh — macOS parity of scripts/bootstrap/linux/rn_bootstrap.sh
   3: #
   4: # Usage: Bootstrap-RustyNetMacos.sh <env-file>
   5: #
   6: # Env-file variables (set by the Rust orchestrator):
   7: #   ROLE              — client | exit | entry | aux | extra
   8: #   NODE_ID           — unique node identifier
   9: #   NETWORK_ID        — mesh network identifier
  10: #   SSH_ALLOW_CIDRS   — comma-separated CIDRs allowed through the SSH fail-open exception
  11: #   SOURCE_ARCHIVE    — path to the source tarball on the remote host
  12: #
  13: # This script runs as root (called via sudo or as the launchd daemon user).
  14: # It mirrors the structure of rn_bootstrap.sh so the Rust adapter can use
  15: # the same SCP+run pattern for both Linux and macOS.
  16: 
  17: set -euo pipefail
  18: 
  19: if [[ $# -ne 1 ]]; then
  20:   echo "usage: Bootstrap-RustyNetMacos.sh <env-file>" >&2
  21:   exit 2
  22: fi
  23: 
  24: source "$1"
  25: 
  26: # ── Constants ───
  27: RUSTYNETD_BIN="/usr/local/bin/rustynetd"
  28: RUSTYNET_BIN="/usr/local/bin/rustynet"
  29: STATE_ROOT="/usr/local/var/rustynet"
  30: CONFIG_ROOT="/usr/local/etc/rustynet"
  31: KEYS_DIR="${STATE_ROOT}/keys"
  32: LOG_DIR="/usr/local/var/log/rustynet"
  33: LAUNCHDAEMON_DIR="/Library/LaunchDaemons"
  34: PLIST_PATH="${LAUNCHDAEMON_DIR}/com.rustynet.daemon.plist"
  35: PLIST_SCRIPT_DIR="$(dirname "$0")"
  36: BUILD_DIR="/tmp/rustynet-build-$$"
  37: 
  38: # ── Prerequisite check ───
  39: check_prereqs() {
  40:   local missing=0
  41:   for cmd in curl git make rustup wg; do
  42:     if ! command -v "${cmd}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  43:       echo "[bootstrap] missing prerequisite: ${cmd}" >&2
  44:       missing=1
  45:     fi
  46:   done
  47:   if ! command -v cc >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v clang >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  48:     echo "[bootstrap] missing C compiler (cc/clang)" >&2
  49:     missing=1
  50:   fi
  51:   if [[ "${missing}" -ne 0 ]]; then
  52:     echo "[bootstrap] install prerequisites via Homebrew: brew install rust wireguard-tools" >&2
  53:     exit 1
  54:   fi
  55: }
  56: 
  57: # ── User/group setup ───
  58: ensure_rustynetd_user() {
  59:   if ! dscl . -read /Users/rustynetd >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  60:     local uid
  61:     # Find an unused uid in the service range 500-599.
  62:     for candidate in $(seq 500 599); do
  63:       if ! dscl . -search /Users UniqueID "${candidate}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q UniqueID; then
  64:         uid="${candidate}"
  65:         break
  66:       fi
  67:     done
  68:     if [[ -z "${uid:-}" ]]; then
  69:       echo "[bootstrap] could not find a free UID in 500-599 for rustynetd" >&2
  70:       exit 1
  71:     fi
  72:     dscl . -create /Groups/rustynetd
  73:     dscl . -create /Groups/rustynetd RealName "RustyNet Daemon"
  74:     dscl . -create /Groups/rustynetd gid "${uid}"
  75:     dscl . -create /Users/rustynetd
  76:     dscl . -create /Users/rustynetd RealName "RustyNet Daemon"
  77:     dscl . -create /Users/rustynetd UniqueID "${uid}"
  78:     dscl . -create /Users/rustynetd PrimaryGroupID "${uid}"
  79:     dscl . -create /Users/rustynetd UserShell /usr/bin/false
  80:     dscl . -create /Users/rustynetd NFSHomeDirectory /var/empty
  81:     echo "[bootstrap] created rustynetd user/group with uid/gid=${uid}"
  82:   fi
  83: }
  84: 
  85: # ── Directory setup ───
  86: setup_directories() {
  87:   install -d -m 0700 -o rustynetd -g rustynetd "${STATE_ROOT}"
  88:   install -d -m 0700 -o rustynetd -g rustynetd "${KEYS_DIR}"
  89:   install -d -m 0750 -o root      -g rustynetd "${CONFIG_ROOT}"
  90:   install -d -m 0750 -o rustynetd -g rustynetd "${LOG_DIR}"
  91: }
  92: 
  93: # ── Clear residual state ───
  94: clear_residual_state() {
  95:   # Remove stale WireGuard interface if present.
  96:   if networksetup -listallhardwareports 2>/dev/null | grep -q rustynet; then
  97:     ifconfig rustynet0 down 2>/dev/null || true
  98:   fi
  99:   # Stop any existing daemon instance.
 100:   if launchctl print system/com.rustynet.daemon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 101:     launchctl bootout system/com.rustynet.daemon 2>/dev/null || true
 102:     sleep 1
 103:   fi
 104: }
 105: 
 106: # ── Build ───
 107: build_rustynet() {
 108:   mkdir -p "${BUILD_DIR}"
 109:   tar -xzf "${SOURCE_ARCHIVE}" -C "${BUILD_DIR}" --strip-components=1
 110:   pushd "${BUILD_DIR}" >/dev/null
 111:   rustup target add "$(rustc -vV | awk '/^host/ { print $2 }')" 2>/dev/null || true
 112:   cargo build --release --bin rustynetd --bin rustynet
 113:   popd >/dev/null
 114: }
 115: 
 116: # ── Install binaries ───
 117: install_binaries() {
 118:   install -m 0755 -o root -g wheel \
 119:     "${BUILD_DIR}/target/release/rustynetd" "${RUSTYNETD_BIN}"
 120:   install -m 0755 -o root -g wheel \
 121:     "${BUILD_DIR}/target/release/rustynet" "${RUSTYNET_BIN}"
 122:   rm -rf "${BUILD_DIR}"
 123: }
 124: 
 125: # ── WireGuard key generation ───
 126: generate_wireguard_keys() {
 127:   if [[ ! -f "${KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.pub" ]]; then
 128:     local tmp_priv
 129:     tmp_priv="$(mktemp)"
 130:     chmod 600 "${tmp_priv}"
 131:     wg genkey > "${tmp_priv}"
 132:     wg pubkey < "${tmp_priv}" > "${KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.pub"
 133:     # Encrypt the private key using the rustynetd key-custody mechanism.
 134:     "${RUSTYNETD_BIN}" key init --wg-private-key "${tmp_priv}" \
 135:       --wg-encrypted-private-key "${KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.key.enc" 2>/dev/null || \
 136:       cp "${tmp_priv}" "${KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.key.enc"
 137:     rm -f "${tmp_priv}"
 138:     chmod 600 "${KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.key.enc"
 139:     chmod 640 "${KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.pub"
 140:     chown rustynetd:rustynetd "${KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.key.enc" "${KEYS_DIR}/wireguard.pub"
 141:   fi
 142: }
 143: 
 144: # ── Install launchd service ───
 145: install_launchd_service() {
 146:   local install_script="${PLIST_SCRIPT_DIR}/Install-RustyNetMacosService.sh"
 147:   if [[ -f "${install_script}" ]]; then
 148:     bash "${install_script}" \
 149:       --rustynetd-bin "${RUSTYNETD_BIN}" \
 150:       --state-root "${STATE_ROOT}" \
 151:       --log-dir "${LOG_DIR}" \
 152:       --plist-dst "${PLIST_PATH}" \
 153:       --node-id "${NODE_ID}" \
 154:       --node-role "${ROLE}" \
 155:       --network-id "${NETWORK_ID}"
 156:   else
 157:     echo "[bootstrap] Install-RustyNetMacosService.sh not found at ${install_script}" >&2
 158:     exit 1
 159:   fi
 160: }
 161: 
 162: # ── Main ───
 163: echo "[bootstrap] macOS bootstrap starting: node_id=${NODE_ID} role=${ROLE}"
 164: 
 165: check_prereqs
 166: ensure_rustynetd_user
 167: setup_directories
 168: clear_residual_state
 169: build_rustynet
 170: install_binaries
 171: generate_wireguard_keys
 172: install_launchd_service
 173: 
 174: echo "[bootstrap] macOS bootstrap complete"

===== /scripts/bootstrap/macos/Install-RustyNetMacosService.sh =====

   1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2: # Install-RustyNetMacosService.sh — Install the RustyNet launchd service on macOS.
   3: #
   4: # Writes the reviewed com.rustynet.daemon.plist to /Library/LaunchDaemons/,
   5: # applies correct ownership and mode (root:wheel 0644), then loads the
   6: # service via `launchctl bootstrap system`.
   7: #
   8: # Usage:
   9: #   Install-RustyNetMacosService.sh \
  10: #     --rustynetd-bin <path>    (default: /usr/local/bin/rustynetd)
  11: #     --state-root <path>       (default: /usr/local/var/rustynet)
  12: #     --log-dir <path>          (default: /usr/local/var/log/rustynet)
  13: #     --plist-dst <path>        (default: /Library/LaunchDaemons/com.rustynet.daemon.plist)
  14: #     --node-id <id>
  15: #     --node-role <role>
  16: #     --network-id <id>
  17: 
  18: set -euo pipefail
  19: 
  20: # ── Argument parsing ───
  21: RUSTYNETD_BIN="/usr/local/bin/rustynetd"
  22: STATE_ROOT="/usr/local/var/rustynet"
  23: LOG_DIR="/usr/local/var/log/rustynet"
  24: PLIST_DST="/Library/LaunchDaemons/com.rustynet.daemon.plist"
  25: NODE_ID=""
  26: NODE_ROLE=""
  27: NETWORK_ID=""
  28: 
  29: while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  30:   case "$1" in
  31:     --rustynetd-bin) RUSTYNETD_BIN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
  32:     --state-root)    STATE_ROOT="$2";    shift 2 ;;
  33:     --log-dir)       LOG_DIR="$2";       shift 2 ;;
  34:     --plist-dst)     PLIST_DST="$2";     shift 2 ;;
  35:     --node-id)       NODE_ID="$2";       shift 2 ;;
  36:     --node-role)     NODE_ROLE="$2";     shift 2 ;;
  37:     --network-id)    NETWORK_ID="$2";    shift 2 ;;
  38:     *) echo "unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  39:   esac
  40: done
  41: 
  42: if [[ -z "${NODE_ID}" || -z "${NODE_ROLE}" ]]; then
  43:   echo "error: --node-id and --node-role are required" >&2
  44:   exit 2
  45: fi
  46: 
  47: # ── Write plist ───
  48: cat > "${PLIST_DST}" <<PLIST
  49: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
  50: <!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
  51: <plist version="1.0">
  52: <dict>
  53:     <key>Label</key>
  54:     <string>com.rustynet.daemon</string>
  55:     <key>ProgramArguments</key>
  56:     <array>
  57:         <string>${RUSTYNETD_BIN}</string>
  58:         <string>daemon</string>
  59:         <string>--node-id</string>
  60:         <string>${NODE_ID}</string>
  61:         <string>--node-role</string>
  62:         <string>${NODE_ROLE}</string>
  63:         <string>--state</string>
  64:         <string>${STATE_ROOT}/rustynetd.state</string>
  65:         <string>--wg-encrypted-private-key</string>
  66:         <string>${STATE_ROOT}/keys/wireguard.key.enc</string>
  67:         <string>--wg-public-key</string>
  68:         <string>${STATE_ROOT}/keys/wireguard.pub</string>
  69:         <string>--backend</string>
  70:         <string>macos-wireguard</string>
  71:     </array>
  72:     <key>UserName</key>
  73:     <string>rustynetd</string>
  74:     <key>GroupName</key>
  75:     <string>rustynetd</string>
  76:     <key>RunAtLoad</key>
  77:     <true/>
  78:     <key>KeepAlive</key>
  79:     <true/>
  80:     <key>ProcessType</key>
  81:     <string>Background</string>
  82:     <key>AbandonProcessGroup</key>
  83:     <false/>
  84:     <key>StandardOutPath</key>
  85:     <string>${LOG_DIR}/rustynetd.log</string>
  86:     <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
  87:     <string>${LOG_DIR}/rustynetd-error.log</string>
  88:     <key>EnvironmentVariables</key>
  89:     <dict>
  90:         <key>RUSTYNET_NODE_ROLE</key>
  91:         <string>${NODE_ROLE}</string>
  92:         <key>RUSTYNET_NETWORK_ID</key>
  93:         <string>${NETWORK_ID}</string>
  94:     </dict>
  95: </dict>
  96: </plist>
  97: PLIST
  98: 
  99: # ── Apply ownership and mode ───
 100: chown root:wheel "${PLIST_DST}"
 101: chmod 0644 "${PLIST_DST}"
 102: 
 103: # ── Load the service ───
 104: # Unload first if already registered (idempotent re-install).
 105: if launchctl print system/com.rustynet.daemon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
 106:   launchctl bootout system/com.rustynet.daemon || true
 107:   sleep 1
 108: fi
 109: 
 110: launchctl bootstrap system "${PLIST_DST}"
 111: 
 112: echo "[install-service] com.rustynet.daemon loaded via launchctl bootstrap"

===== /scripts/ci/membership_gates.sh =====

   1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2: set -euo pipefail
   3: 
   4: SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
   5: REPO_ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd)"
   6: 
   7: echo "Running membership CI gates..."
   8: 
   9: # Lint and deny warnings
  10: cargo clippy -p rustynet-control -- -D warnings
  11: 
  12: # Run membership unit tests (targeted)
  13: cargo test -p rustynet-control membership -- --nocapture
  14: 
  15: # Run policy coupling tests (M5)
  16: cargo test -p rustynet-policy -- --nocapture
  17: 
  18: # Verify membership evidence artifact exists and is well-formed JSON
  19: MEMBERSHIP_REPORT="${REPO_ROOT}/artifacts/phase10/membership_report.json"
  20: if [[ ! -f "${MEMBERSHIP_REPORT}" ]]; then
  21:     echo "GATE FAIL: artifacts/phase10/membership_report.json is missing" >&2
  22:     exit 1
  23: fi
  24: if ! python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open(sys.argv[1])); assert d.get('status')=='pass', 'status!=pass'" \
  25:         "${MEMBERSHIP_REPORT}" 2>/dev/null; then
  26:     echo "GATE FAIL: artifacts/phase10/membership_report.json schema validation failed" >&2
  27:     exit 1
  28: fi
  29: echo "membership_report.json schema validation: pass"
  30: 
  31: # Run the higher-level ops membership gates (legacy wrapper)
  32: exec cargo run --quiet -p rustynet-cli --bin membership_gates -- "$@"

===== /scripts/ci/security_regression_gates.sh =====

   1: #!/usr/bin/env bash
   2: set -euo pipefail
   3: 
   4: echo "Running security regression gates..."
   5: 
   6: # Run the Rust-based gates
   7: cargo run --quiet -p rustynet-cli --bin security_regression_gates -- "$@"
   8: 
   9: # G1: Grep-based CI gate for secret material equality
  10: echo "Checking for raw equality on secret material..."
  11: if grep -rn --include="*.rs" -E '(token|csrf|session_key|nonce|mac|hmac|session_id)\s*(==|!=)\s' \
  12:   crates/rustynet-relay/src/ crates/rustynet-control/src/ 2>/dev/null | \
  13:   grep -v "// EXCEPTION:" | grep -v "ct_eq"; then
  14:   echo "ERROR: raw equality on secret material detected — use subtle::ConstantTimeEq" >&2
  15:   exit 2
  16: fi
  17: 
  18: # Also check .as_bytes() == patterns
  19: if grep -rn --hidden --no-ignore --glob 'crates/**/*.rs' -E '\\.as_bytes\(\)\s*==\s*|\\.as_slice\(\)\s*==\s*|==.*csrf_token' \
  20:   crates/rustynet-relay/src/ crates/rustynet-control/src/ 2>/dev/null | \
  21:   grep -v "// EXCEPTION:" | grep -v "ct_eq"; then
  22:   echo "ERROR: raw equality on secret material detected — use subtle::ConstantTimeEq" >&2
  23:   exit 2
  24: fi
  25: 
  26: echo "PASS: no raw secret equality detected"
  27: 
  28: # G2a: Fail if sha1 or 3des appear in Cargo.lock (fast, no network)
  29: echo "Checking Cargo.lock for deprecated cryptographic algorithm packages..."
  30: if grep -iE '^name = "(sha1|md-5|des|des3|3des|triple-des)"' Cargo.lock 2>/dev/null; then
  31:   echo "FAIL: deprecated cryptographic algorithm crate found in Cargo.lock" >&2
  32:   echo "FAIL: remove the dependency or disable the feature that pulls in sha1/3des/md5" >&2
  33:   exit 1
  34: fi
  35: echo "PASS: no deprecated crypto algorithm crates in Cargo.lock"
  36: 
  37: # G2b: cargo deny check bans (enforces deny.toml [[bans.deny]] entries)
  38: echo "Running cargo deny check bans for deprecated crypto algorithms..."
  39: if ! cargo deny check bans 2>&1; then
  40:   echo "FAIL: cargo deny check bans failed — check deny.toml for details" >&2
  41:   exit 1
  42: fi
  43: echo "PASS: cargo deny bans check passed"
  44: 
  45: # G2c: Source scan — reject any use statement importing deprecated crypto crates
  46: echo "Scanning source for imports of deprecated cryptographic crates..."
  47: if grep -rn --include="*.rs" -E \
  48:   '^[[:space:]]*(pub[[:space:]]+)?use[[:space:]]+(sha1|md5|md_5|des|des3|triple_des)(::|;| )' \
  49:   crates/ 2>/dev/null | grep -v "// EXCEPTION:"; then
  50:   echo "FAIL: use-import of deprecated crypto crate found in source" >&2
  51:   exit 1
  52: fi
  53: echo "PASS: no imports of deprecated crypto crates in source"
  54: 
  55: echo "All security regression gates passed."
  56: exit 0

===== /scripts/e2e/README.md =====

   1: # Live-Lab Orchestrator Function Reference
   2: 
   3: This directory contains the shell entrypoints that drive the live Linux lab.
   4: The main orchestrator is [`live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh`](./live_linux_lab_orchestrator.sh),
   5: with shared SSH, file, and snapshot helpers in [`live_lab_common.sh`](./live_lab_common.sh).
   6: These shell stages are Linux-runtime specific; Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android
   7: targets must not be routed into `live_linux_*` execution paths.
   8: 
   9: Use this README as a quick map of the orchestration functions, especially the
  10: high-level wrappers that compose many lower-level stages into one operator-facing flow.
  11: 
  12: ## Recommended Live-Lab Workflow
  13: 
  14: Start here when you want to bring up and exercise a local UTM-backed lab end to
  15: end.
  16: 
  17: | Step | Primary wrapper | What it does |
  18: | --- | --- | --- |
  19: | Discover | `ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm-summary` | Finds the local UTM bundles, live IPs, SSH readiness, and the fastest setup summary. Use `ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm` when you need the full JSON report. |
  20: | Setup | `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab` | Generates or validates the live-lab profile, runs the setup-only sequence through baseline validation, and writes a resumable report directory. |
  21: | Link and Test | `ops vm-lab-run-live-lab` | Runs the full live-lab suite, validates the report contract, and automatically continues from a setup-only report directory when setup already completed. |
  22: | Diagnose | `ops vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure` | Collects the first failed stage and packages a stage-aware forensic bundle for triage. |
  23: 
  24: This is the recommended operator path: discover, set up, link and test, then
  25: diagnose if something fails.
  26: 
  27: Automation security posture for this workflow:
  28: 
  29: - SSH host trust is pinned from the operator-supplied `known_hosts` file
  30: - SSH TOFU / `accept-new` is not part of the active wrapper path
  31: - the active wrapper path expects passwordless sudo (`sudo -n`) on automation targets
  32: - unattended runtime passphrase custody remains credential-only; plaintext passphrase files are not part of the live-lab release path
  33: - canonical cross-network pass reports now require a suite-local SSH trust summary proving pinned host-key coverage and `sudo -n` for every participating target
  34: - canonical cross-network pass reports now require daemon path evidence to show `transport_socket_identity_state=authoritative_backend_shared_transport`
  35: - canonical cross-network soak pass now requires the soak to remain direct for the full duration with zero relay/fail-closed/drift samples
  36: 
  37: ## Windows UTM Support Matrix
  38: 
  39: The Rust CLI now treats mixed Linux/Windows inventories as explicit rather than
  40: implicitly Linux-only:
  41: 
  42: These labels describe current Rustynet wrapper support, not general Windows or
  43: macOS platform capability.
  44: 
  45: - Supported for Windows UTM targets: `vm-lab-discover-local-utm`,
  46:   `vm-lab-start`, `vm-lab-restart`, `vm-lab-sync-repo`, and the partial
  47:   Windows bootstrap-phase surface for `sync-source` and `build-release`.
  48: - Windows support here is `bootstrap-capable/scaffolded only`. The Windows
  49:   provider and helper roots are real and platform-aware, but Windows
  50:   `install-release` is still a protective stub, `build-release` remains subject
  51:   to verified MSVC/toolchain preconditions, and `restart-runtime`,
  52:   `verify-runtime`, and `all` are not runtime-capable proof on the current
  53:   branch.
  54: - Intentionally blocked for Windows UTM targets: `vm-lab-validate-live-lab-profile`,
  55:   `vm-lab-setup-live-lab`, `vm-lab-run-live-lab`,
  56:   `vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab`, `vm-lab-iterate-live-lab`,
  57:   `vm-lab-run-suite`, and `vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure`.
  58: - The `scripts/e2e/live_linux_*` stage scripts remain Linux-only until a
  59:   Windows stage implementation exists. Mixed inventories can still live in the
  60:   repo, but the Linux live-lab wrappers fail closed instead of inventing Debian
  61:   shell assumptions for Windows entries. Those wrappers require explicit
  62:   `platform=linux`, `remote_shell=posix`, `guest_exec_mode=linux_bash`, and
  63:   `service_manager=systemd` metadata before execution starts.
  64: - Linux UTM targets continue to use the existing shell orchestrator path.
  65: 
  66: ## Capability Reporting Gap
  67: 
  68: The top-level wrappers still enforce a coarse Linux-only boundary for the live
  69: setup/run/orchestrate flow. That is deliberate and fail-closed, but the wrapper
  70: surface already knows more than it currently reports because several
  71: sub-capabilities are platform-aware or partially implemented.
  72: 
  73: The wrapper-support expectations in this section are separate from the
  74: implementation support matrix in
  75: [`documents/operations/PlatformSupportMatrix.md`](../../documents/operations/PlatformSupportMatrix.md).
  76: 
  77: The documentation target is to move toward explicit capability reporting for
  78: each command and stage, without changing the current support truth:
  79: 
  80: - `supported`
  81: - `partially supported`
  82: - `unsupported`
  83: 
  84: The capability explanation should cover the command, stage or phase, source
  85: mode, platform mix, and the blocking requirements. The proposed machine-readable
  86: artifact is `state/platform_capabilities.json`; a dedicated inspection command
  87: would be a useful follow-up, but it is not required for the current execution
  88: path.
  89: 
  90: Until that reporting layer exists, the existing Linux-only execution guards and
  91: their fail-closed errors remain the source of truth for the operator path.
  92: 
  93: ## How The Orchestrator Works
  94: 
  95: - `run_stage` wraps a stage with logging, summary recording, failure-digest refresh, and optional forensics capture.
  96: - `run_parallel_node_stage` fans a worker across the selected nodes and writes per-node `results.tsv` evidence.
  97: - `run_serial_node_stage` executes a stage one node at a time when a single authority is required.
  98: - Most higher-level helpers are composition wrappers. They do not invent new dataplane behavior; they sequence the existing hardened stages in a consistent order.
  99: 
 100: ## Supporting Shell Wrappers
 101: 
 102: These are useful shell orchestration helpers after the primary workflow above.
 103: 
 104: | Function | What it composes | When to use |
 105: | --- | --- | --- |
 106: | `stage_run_extended_soak` | Pre-soak two-hop validation, exit-handoff validation, LAN toggle validation, reboot recovery, and the managed-DNS refresh steps between them | Long-running resilience and reboot-recovery evidence after the baseline is healthy |
 107: | `stage_run_cross_network_preflight` | Time, process, socket, permissions, DNS, route-policy, signed-state, and discovery-bundle readiness checks | Before any cross-network mutation or soak stage |
 108: | `stage_run_live_role_switch_matrix` | Controlled role-switch validation across the full five-node topology | When you need release-gate role-switch evidence |
 109: | `stage_run_live_exit_handoff` | Live exit failover evidence on a topology with entry and aux peers | When you want handoff proof without the full soak path |
 110: | `stage_run_live_two_hop` | Two-hop proof using entry and aux peers | When you need relay-path validation or a narrower live-path check |
 111: | `stage_run_live_lan_toggle` | Blind-exit / LAN-access toggle proof | When you need to confirm the client can move between the direct and blind-exit path safely |
 112: | `stage_run_live_managed_dns` | Managed-DNS live validation | When you need DNS issuance, refresh, and fail-closed behavior evidence |
 113: | `stage_run_reboot_recovery_report` | Exit reboot, client reboot, post-reboot DNS refresh, and post-reboot path checks | When you need a dedicated recovery artifact without the full soak wrapper |
 114: 
 115: ## Supporting Rust CLI Wrappers
 116: 
 117: The preferred operator-facing entrypoints are in `rustynet-cli`; the shell
 118: orchestrator remains the execution engine behind them.
 119: 
 120: | Command | What it does | When to use |
 121: | --- | --- | --- |
 122: | `ops vm-lab-write-live-lab-profile` | Generates a non-interactive live-lab profile from inventory-backed VM aliases or explicit SSH targets | First step for any repeatable live-lab run |
 123: | `ops vm-lab-validate-live-lab-profile` | Verifies the generated profile is internally consistent and matches the expected backend/source-mode/topology | Before a run when profile or provenance correctness matters |
 124: | `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab` | Drives the setup-only live-lab pipeline, emits structured JSON, and supports `--resume-from` and `--rerun-stage` for setup-stage recovery | Preferred operator entrypoint for repeatable lab setup without immediately running the full suite |
 125: | `ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab` | Discovers selected local UTM VMs, restarts only the aliases that are not execution-ready, reruns discovery, then drives setup, run, and diagnose-on-failure in one report directory. `--stop-after-ready` exits after the readiness gate when you only need VM recovery proof. | Preferred one-shot wrapper when the operator wants recovery plus the standard live-lab workflow without manual branching |
 126: | `ops vm-lab-run-live-lab` | Runs the full live-lab suite, validates required report artifacts, and can continue from an existing setup-only report directory | Preferred operator entrypoint for the full suite after setup is complete |
 127: | `ops vm-lab-iterate-live-lab` | Runs typed local validation, writes the profile, launches the reduced live-lab flow, and prints the first failed stage on error | Narrow iteration loop while debugging a red live-lab stage |
 128: | `ops vm-lab-diff-live-lab-runs` | Compares two report directories and shows the first divergent stage outcome | When a patch moves the blocker and you want a quick regression/progression diff |
 129: | `ops vm-lab-bootstrap-phase --phase all` | Runs the reusable Rust bootstrap pipeline across the selected VM set: sync source, build release, install release, restart runtime, verify runtime. On the current branch, treat this as a Linux-runtime workflow; Windows guests use only the narrower verified `sync-source` and `build-release` phases plus explicit diagnostics. | Fresh-install or rebuild-only workflow when you want provisioning without the full live-lab test suite |
 130: | `ops vm-lab-preflight` | Verifies SSH reachability, sudo, free disk, and required commands | Standalone readiness check before provisioning or a live-lab run |
 131: | `ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm` | Automatically scans the local UTM documents tree, resolves live IPs, and reports SSH port/process readiness for every discovered bundle. `--update-inventory-live-ips` persists the refreshed IPs only when the whole matched set is execution-ready. | Use when you want the full machine-discovered local UTM lab inventory |
 132: | `ops vm-lab-restart --wait-ready` | Restarts the selected local UTM VMs, waits for process presence, live IP resolution, SSH port-open state, and SSH auth readiness, then refreshes the inventory IP fields on success. `--json` and `--report-dir` add machine-readable result and artifact output. | Recovery path when discovery knows the VMs but they are not yet actually reachable over SSH |
 133: | `ops vm-lab-status` | Captures per-node runtime and service status snapshots | Fast point-in-time inspection outside the failure-diagnostics wrapper |
 134: 
 135: The four entries above the fold are the recommended operator path:
 136: `ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm-summary`, `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab`,
 137: `ops vm-lab-run-live-lab`, and `ops vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure`.
 138: 
 139: `ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab` is the optional one-shot wrapper that
 140: automates the common discovery -> restart-if-needed -> setup -> run ->
 141: diagnose-on-failure decision tree.
 142: 
 143: ## Recommended Workflows
 144: 
 145: Use the smallest wrapper set that matches the task:
 146: 
 147: | Goal | Preferred wrapper flow |
 148: | --- | --- |
 149: | Fresh install all selected Linux Rustynet nodes | `ops vm-lab-bootstrap-phase --phase all` |
 150: | Prepare a Windows UTM guest without claiming runtime parity | `ops vm-lab-sync-repo` -> `ops vm-lab-bootstrap-phase --phase sync-source` -> `ops vm-lab-bootstrap-phase --phase build-release` |
 151: | Fresh install plus baseline and the full standard live suite | `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab` -> `ops vm-lab-run-live-lab` |
 152: | One command that recovers unready local UTM VMs and then runs the standard live-lab flow | `ops vm-lab-orchestrate-live-lab` |
 153: | Reduced repeatable debug loop for a failing live-lab stage | `ops vm-lab-iterate-live-lab` |
 154: | Investigate a red run after completion | `ops vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure` and optionally `ops vm-lab-diff-live-lab-runs` |
 155: 
 156: Minimal four-command live-lab path:
 157: 
 158: | Step | Preferred command |
 159: | --- | --- |
 160: | Discover local UTM state and SSH readiness | `ops vm-lab-discover-local-utm-summary` |
 161: | Configure the topology and complete setup-only stages | `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab` |
 162: | Run the full live-lab suite | `ops vm-lab-run-live-lab` |
 163: | Gather a stage-aware forensic bundle after a red run | `ops vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure` |
 164: 
 165: Current usage in this repo:
 166: 
 167: - We now use `ops vm-lab-setup-live-lab` plus `ops vm-lab-run-live-lab` as the primary operator path for the current five-node UTM lab work.
 168: - `ops vm-lab-diagnose-live-lab-failure` is now the preferred post-failure collection path because it packages the failed stage context and targeted diagnostics into one bundle.
 169: - The lower-level profile and preflight helpers still exist when you need tighter control over one slice of the workflow.
 170:
