3596: query_lan_access_status() {
3597:   local status_line selected_exit lan_access
3598:   status_line="$(run_rustynet_cli status 2>/dev/null || true)"
3599:   if [[ -z "${status_line}" ]]; then
3600:     print_err "Unable to query daemon status for LAN access toggle."
3601:     return 1
3602:   fi
3603:   selected_exit="$(extract_status_field "${status_line}" "exit_node")"
3604:   lan_access="$(extract_status_field "${status_line}" "lan_access")"
3605:   case "${lan_access}" in
3606:     on|true) lan_access="on" ;;
3607:     off|false|"") lan_access="off" ;;
3608:     *) lan_access="off" ;;
3609:   esac
3610:   printf '%s|%s\n' "${selected_exit}" "${lan_access}"
3611: }
3612: 
3613: apply_linux_lan_access_coupling() {
3614:   local mode="$1"
3615:   local enable_bool
3616: 
3617:   if ! is_linux_host; then
3618:     print_err "apply_linux_lan_access_coupling is supported on Linux only."
3619:     return 1
3620:   fi
3621:   if ! command -v rustynet >/dev/null 2>&1; then
3622:     print_err "rustynet CLI is required for LAN access coupling operations."
3623:     return 1
3624:   fi
3625: 
3626:   case "${mode}" in
3627:     on) enable_bool="true" ;;
3628:     off) enable_bool="false" ;;
3629:     *)
3630:       print_err "Unsupported LAN access mode '${mode}'."
3631:       return 1
3632:       ;;
3633:   esac
3634: 
3635:   local lan_coupling_cmd=(rustynet ops apply-lan-access-coupling \
3636:     --enable "${enable_bool}" \
3637:     --env-path "${ASSIGNMENT_REFRESH_ENV_PATH}")
3638:   if [[ "${mode}" == "on" || "${mode}" == "off" ]]; then
3639:     lan_coupling_cmd+=(--lan-routes "${DEFAULT_EXIT_LAN_CIDRS}")
3640:   fi
3641:   if ! run_root env \
3642:     RUSTYNET_SOCKET="${SOCKET_PATH}" \
3643:     RUSTYNET_AUTO_TUNNEL_BUNDLE="${AUTO_TUNNEL_BUNDLE_PATH}" \
3644:     RUSTYNET_AUTO_TUNNEL_WATERMARK="${AUTO_TUNNEL_WATERMARK_PATH}" \
3645:     "${lan_coupling_cmd[@]}"; then
3646:     print_err "Signed LAN access coupling failed; setup is fail-closed."
3647:     return 1
3648:   fi
3649:   return 0
3650: }
3651: 
3652: enable_lan_access_for_selected_exit() {
3653:   local status_pair selected_exit lan_access
3654:   if is_blind_exit_role; then
3655:     print_err "LAN access toggles are disabled for blind_exit role."
3656:     return 1
3657:   fi
3658: 
3659:   if ! status_pair="$(query_lan_access_status)"; then
3660:     return 1
3661:   fi
3662:   selected_exit="$(cut -d'|' -f1 <<<"${status_pair}")"
3663:   lan_access="$(cut -d'|' -f2 <<<"${status_pair}")"
3664:   if [[ "${lan_access}" == "on" ]]; then
3665:     print_info "LAN access is already enabled."
3666:     return 0
3667:   fi
3668: 
3669:   if [[ -z "${selected_exit}" || "${selected_exit}" == "none" ]]; then
3670:     print_err "Select an exit node first, then toggle LAN access on."
3671:     return 1
3672:   fi
3673: 
3674:   print_info "Enabling local LAN access through exit node '${selected_exit}'."
3675:   if is_linux_host; then
3676:     if ! apply_linux_lan_access_coupling "on"; then
3677:       return 1
3678:     fi
3679:     print_info "LAN access enabled for ${DEFAULT_EXIT_LAN_CIDRS}."
3680:     return 0
3681:   fi
3682:   if ! run_rustynet_cli lan-access on; then
3683:     return 1
3684:   fi
3685:   print_info "LAN access enabled."
3686:   return 0
3687: }
3688: 
3689: toggle_lan_access() {
3690:   local status_pair lan_access
3691:   if ! status_pair="$(query_lan_access_status)"; then
3692:     return 1
3693:   fi
3694:   lan_access="$(cut -d'|' -f2 <<<"${status_pair}")"
3695:   if [[ "${lan_access}" == "on" ]]; then
3696:     print_info "Disabling exit-node local LAN access."
3697:     if is_linux_host; then
3698:       apply_linux_lan_access_coupling "off"
3699:       return $?
3700:     fi
3701:     run_rustynet_cli lan-access off
3702:     return $?
3703:   fi
3704:   enable_lan_access_for_selected_exit
3705: }
3706: 
3707: enable_lan_access_after_exit_selection() {
3708:   if prompt_yes_no "Enable local LAN access through the selected exit node now?" "n"; then
3709:     if ! enable_lan_access_for_selected_exit; then
3710:       print_warn "Exit selection succeeded, but enabling LAN access failed."
3711:       return 1
3712:     fi
3713:   fi
3714:   return 0
3715: }

3717: probe_selected_exit_tunnel_status() {
3718:   local node_id="$1"
3719:   local peer_public_key="${2:-}"
3720:   local attempt status_line selected state restricted netcheck_line handshake_ts
3721: 
3722:   for attempt in 1 2 3; do
3723:     status_line="$(run_rustynet_cli status 2>/dev/null || true)"
3724:     selected="$(extract_status_field "${status_line}" "exit_node")"
3725:     state="$(extract_status_field "${status_line}" "state")"
3726:     restricted="$(extract_status_field "${status_line}" "restricted_safe_mode")"
3727:     netcheck_line="$(run_rustynet_cli netcheck 2>/dev/null || true)"
3728: 
3729:     if [[ "${selected}" != "${node_id}" ]]; then
3730:       sleep 1
3731:       continue
3732:     fi
3733:     if [[ "${state}" != "ExitActive" ]]; then
3734:       sleep 1
3735:       continue
3736:     fi
3737:     if [[ "${restricted}" == "true" ]]; then
3738:       sleep 1
3739:       continue
3740:     fi
3741:     if [[ "${netcheck_line}" == *"path=fail-closed"* ]]; then
3742:       sleep 1
3743:       continue
3744:     fi
3745: 
3746:     if [[ -n "${peer_public_key}" ]] && command -v wg >/dev/null 2>&1; then
3747:       handshake_ts="$(
3748:         wg show "${WG_INTERFACE}" latest-handshakes 2>/dev/null \
3749:           | awk -v key="${peer_public_key}" '$1 == key { print $2; exit }'
3750:       )"
3751:       if [[ "${handshake_ts}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( handshake_ts > 0 )); then
3752:         printf 'online'
3753:         return 0
3754:       fi
3755:       sleep 1
3756:       continue
3757:     fi
3758: 
3759:     printf 'online'
3760:     return 0
3761:   done
3762: 
3763:   printf 'offline'
3764: }
3765: 
3766: probe_exit_node_readiness() {
3767:   local node_id="$1"
3768:   local peer_public_key="${2:-}"
3769:   local status_line original_exit_node selection_output
3770:   local membership_state="unknown"
3771:   local tunnel_state="offline"
3772:   local readiness="select-failed"
3773: 
3774:   status_line="$(run_rustynet_cli status 2>/dev/null || true)"
3775:   original_exit_node="$(extract_status_field "${status_line}" "exit_node")"
3776:   if [[ "${original_exit_node}" == "none" ]]; then
3777:     original_exit_node=""
3778:   fi
3779: 
3780:   if ! selection_output="$(apply_exit_selection_change "${node_id}" 2>&1)"; then
3781:     if [[ "${selection_output}" == *"not active in membership state"* ]]; then
3782:       membership_state="inactive"
3783:       tunnel_state="skipped"
3784:       readiness="membership-inactive"
3785:     else
3786:       membership_state="unknown"
3787:       tunnel_state="offline"
3788:       readiness="select-failed"
3789:     fi
3790:     if ! restore_exit_selection "${original_exit_node}"; then
3791:       readiness="restore-failed"
3792:     fi
3793:     printf '%s|%s|%s' "${membership_state}" "${tunnel_state}" "${readiness}"
3794:     return 0
3795:   fi
3796: 
3797:   membership_state="active"
3798:   tunnel_state="$(probe_selected_exit_tunnel_status "${node_id}" "${peer_public_key}")"
3799:   if [[ "${tunnel_state}" == "online" ]]; then
3800:     readiness="ready"
3801:   else
3802:     readiness="selected-but-no-tunnel"
3803:   fi
3804: 
3805:   if ! restore_exit_selection "${original_exit_node}"; then
3806:     readiness="restore-failed"
3807:   fi
3808:   printf '%s|%s|%s' "${membership_state}" "${tunnel_state}" "${readiness}"
3809: }
3810: 
3811: print_saved_exit_candidates_with_probe() {
3812:   local records_output name node_id public_key endpoint cidr role probe_result membership_state tunnel_state readiness
3813:   local status_line current_exit_node marker
3814:   if ! records_output="$(peer_store_list_records 2>&1)"; then
3815:     print_err "Unable to read peer store for exit-candidate probe."
3816:     print_err "${records_output}"
3817:     return 1
3818:   fi
3819:   status_line="$(run_rustynet_cli status 2>/dev/null || true)"
3820:   current_exit_node="$(extract_status_field "${status_line}" "exit_node")"
3821:   if [[ "${current_exit_node}" == "none" ]]; then
3822:     current_exit_node=""
3823:   fi
3824:   print_info "Running exit-node readiness probe (membership + tunnel)."
3825:   print_warn "Probe temporarily switches exit selection per candidate, then restores it."
3826:   if [[ -n "${current_exit_node}" ]]; then
3827:     print_info "Current selection: '${current_exit_node}' (marked with '*')."
3828:   else
3829:     print_info "Current selection: none."
3830:   fi
3831:   while IFS='|' read -r name node_id public_key endpoint cidr role _rest; do
3832:     if [[ "${name}" == \#* || -z "${name}" ]]; then
3833:       continue
3834:     fi
3835:     if [[ -z "${node_id}" || -z "${endpoint}" || -z "${cidr}" ]]; then
3836:       continue
3837:     fi
3838:     if [[ -z "${role}" ]]; then
3839:       role="unknown"
3840:     fi
3841: 
3842:     probe_result="$(probe_exit_node_readiness "${node_id}" "${public_key}")"
3843:     membership_state="$(cut -d'|' -f1 <<<"${probe_result}")"
3844:     tunnel_state="$(cut -d'|' -f2 <<<"${probe_result}")"
3845:     readiness="$(cut -d'|' -f3 <<<"${probe_result}")"
3846:     marker=" "
3847:     if [[ -n "${current_exit_node}" && "${node_id}" == "${current_exit_node}" ]]; then
3848:       marker="*"
3849:     fi
3850:     printf '  %s %s (node=%s endpoint=%s cidr=%s role=%s membership=%s tunnel=%s readiness=%s)\n' \
3851:       "${marker}" "${name}" "${node_id}" "${endpoint}" "${cidr}" "${role}" \
3852:       "${membership_state}" "${tunnel_state}" "${readiness}"
3853:   done <<< "${records_output}"
3854: }

3856: select_exit_node() {
3857:   local hop_count first_hop final_hop status_line current_exit_node
3858:   local known_entry known_final
3859:   if is_blind_exit_role; then
3860:     print_err "Exit node selection is disabled for blind_exit role."
3861:     return 1
3862:   fi
3863: 
3864:   sanitize_exit_chain_defaults
3865:   print_saved_exit_candidates_with_probe
3866:   status_line="$(run_rustynet_cli status 2>/dev/null || true)"
3867:   current_exit_node="$(extract_status_field "${status_line}" "exit_node")"
3868:   if [[ "${current_exit_node}" == "none" ]]; then
3869:     current_exit_node=""
3870:   fi
3871: 
3872:   print_info "Current chain mode: $(exit_chain_label)"
3873:   if [[ -n "${current_exit_node}" ]]; then
3874:     print_info "Selecting current exit node '${current_exit_node}' will disconnect and clear selection."
3875:   fi
3876: 
3877:   prompt_default hop_count "Routing depth (1=one-hop, 2=two-hop)" "${EXIT_CHAIN_HOPS}"
3878:   if ! is_valid_exit_chain_hops "${hop_count}"; then
3879:     print_err "Invalid routing depth '${hop_count}'. Expected 1 or 2."
3880:     return 1
3881:   fi
3882: 
3883:   if [[ "${hop_count}" == "1" ]]; then
3884:     prompt_default first_hop "Exit node id to select" "${EXIT_CHAIN_ENTRY_NODE_ID}"
3885:     if [[ -z "${first_hop}" ]]; then
3886:       print_err "Exit node id is required."
3887:       return 1
3888:     fi
3889:     if ! is_valid_node_id_value "${first_hop}"; then
3890:       print_err "Invalid exit node id '${first_hop}'. Allowed characters: letters, numbers, dot, underscore, hyphen."
3891:       return 1
3892:     fi
3893: 
3894:     if [[ -n "${current_exit_node}" && "${first_hop}" == "${current_exit_node}" ]]; then
3895:       if [[ "${EXIT_CHAIN_HOPS}" == "1" && "${EXIT_CHAIN_ENTRY_NODE_ID}" == "${first_hop}" ]]; then
3896:         print_info "Exit node '${first_hop}' is already selected. Disconnecting from exit node."
3897:         if ! disable_exit_selection; then
3898:           return 1
3899:         fi
3900:         finalize_exit_chain_disable
3901:         return $?
3902:       fi
3903:       print_info "Exit node '${first_hop}' is already selected. Updating chain mode to one-hop."
3904:     else
3905:       if ! apply_exit_selection_change "${first_hop}"; then
3906:         return 1
3907:       fi
3908:     fi
3909: 
3910:     EXIT_CHAIN_HOPS="1"
3911:     EXIT_CHAIN_ENTRY_NODE_ID="${first_hop}"
3912:     EXIT_CHAIN_FINAL_NODE_ID=""
3913:     finalize_exit_chain_selection "One-hop exit selected: ${first_hop}"
3914:     return $?
3915:   fi
3916: 
3917:   prompt_default first_hop "First-hop entry relay node id" "${EXIT_CHAIN_ENTRY_NODE_ID}"
3918:   prompt_default final_hop "Final exit node id" "${EXIT_CHAIN_FINAL_NODE_ID}"
3919:   if [[ -z "${first_hop}" || -z "${final_hop}" ]]; then
3920:     print_err "Both first-hop and final exit node ids are required for two-hop mode."
3921:     return 1
3922:   fi
3923:   if ! is_valid_node_id_value "${first_hop}" || ! is_valid_node_id_value "${final_hop}"; then
3924:     print_err "Invalid node id in two-hop chain. Allowed characters: letters, numbers, dot, underscore, hyphen."
3925:     return 1
3926:   fi
3927:   if [[ "${first_hop}" == "${final_hop}" ]]; then
3928:     print_err "Two-hop chain requires distinct first-hop and final exit nodes."
3929:     return 1
3930:   fi
3931: 
3932:   known_entry="$(find_peer_record_by_node_id "${first_hop}" || true)"
3933:   known_final="$(find_peer_record_by_node_id "${final_hop}" || true)"
3934:   if [[ -z "${known_entry}" ]]; then
3935:     print_warn "First-hop node '${first_hop}' is not present in local peer records."
3936:   fi
3937:   if [[ -z "${known_final}" ]]; then
3938:     print_warn "Final exit node '${final_hop}' is not present in local peer records."
3939:   fi
3940: 
3941:   if [[ "${first_hop}" == "${DEVICE_NODE_ID}" ]]; then
3942:     require_admin_role "configure local entry relay chain" || return 1
3943:     print_info "Configuring this node as entry relay with upstream exit '${final_hop}'."
3944:     if ! apply_exit_selection_change "${final_hop}"; then
3945:       return 1
3946:     fi
3947:     if ! run_rustynet_cli route advertise 0.0.0.0/0; then
3948:       print_err "Failed to advertise 0.0.0.0/0 while configuring entry relay mode."
3949:       return 1
3950:     fi
3951:   else
3952:     if [[ -n "${current_exit_node}" \
3953:       && "${current_exit_node}" == "${first_hop}" \
3954:       && "${EXIT_CHAIN_HOPS}" == "2" \
3955:       && "${EXIT_CHAIN_ENTRY_NODE_ID}" == "${first_hop}" \
3956:       && "${EXIT_CHAIN_FINAL_NODE_ID}" == "${final_hop}" ]]; then
3957:       print_info "Two-hop chain '${first_hop} -> ${final_hop}' is already selected. Disconnecting and clearing chain."
3958:       if ! disable_exit_selection; then
3959:         return 1
3960:       fi
3961:       finalize_exit_chain_disable
3962:       return $?
3963:     fi
3964: 
3965:     if [[ "${current_exit_node}" != "${first_hop}" ]]; then
3966:       if ! apply_exit_selection_change "${first_hop}"; then
3967:         return 1
3968:       fi
3969:     else
3970:       print_info "First-hop '${first_hop}' already selected; updating final-hop metadata only."
3971:     fi
3972: 
3973:     print_warn "Two-hop chain metadata recorded: ${first_hop} -> ${final_hop}."
3974:     print_warn "Ensure entry relay '${first_hop}' is configured to use upstream exit '${final_hop}' and advertises 0.0.0.0/0."
3975:   fi
3976: 
3977:   EXIT_CHAIN_HOPS="2"
3978:   EXIT_CHAIN_ENTRY_NODE_ID="${first_hop}"
3979:   EXIT_CHAIN_FINAL_NODE_ID="${final_hop}"
3980:   finalize_exit_chain_selection "Two-hop chain selection saved: ${first_hop} -> ${final_hop}"
3981: }

3990: apply_lan_mode_noninteractive() {
3991:   local mode="$1"
3992:   case "${mode}" in
3993:     on|off)
3994:       if is_linux_host; then
3995:         if apply_linux_lan_access_coupling "${mode}"; then
3996:           print_info "LAN access set to '${mode}'."
3997:         else
3998:           print_warn "Failed to set LAN access to '${mode}'."
3999:         fi
4000:       elif run_rustynet_cli lan-access "${mode}"; then
4001:         print_info "LAN access set to '${mode}'."
4002:       else
4003:         print_warn "Failed to set LAN access to '${mode}'."
4004:       fi
4005:       ;;
4006:     skip|"")
4007:       ;;
4008:     *)
4009:       print_warn "Ignoring unsupported LAN mode '${mode}'."
4010:       ;;
4011:   esac
4012: }

4014: apply_launch_profile() {
4015:   local profile="$1"
4016:   local exit_node_id="${2:-}"
4017:   local lan_mode="${3:-skip}"
4018: 
4019:   if ! is_valid_launch_profile "${profile}"; then
4020:     print_err "Unsupported launch profile '${profile}'."
4021:     return 1
4022:   fi
4023:   if is_blind_exit_role && [[ "${profile}" != "menu" && "${profile}" != "quick-exit-node" ]]; then
4024:     print_err "Launch profile '${profile}' is not permitted for blind_exit role."
4025:     return 1
4026:   fi
4027:   if is_client_role && [[ "${profile}" == "quick-exit-node" || "${profile}" == "quick-hybrid" ]]; then
4028:     print_err "Launch profile '${profile}' is admin-only for serving exit traffic."
4029:     return 1
4030:   fi
4031:   if ! is_valid_lan_mode "${lan_mode}"; then
4032:     print_warn "Invalid LAN mode '${lan_mode}', using 'skip'."
4033:     lan_mode="skip"
4034:   fi
4035: 
4036:   if [[ "${profile}" == "menu" ]]; then
4037:     return 0
4038:   fi
4039: 
4040:   print_info "Applying launch profile '${profile}'."
4041:   start_or_restart_service
4042: 
4043:   case "${profile}" in
4044:     quick-connect)
4045:       if [[ -n "${exit_node_id}" ]]; then
4046:         apply_launch_profile_exit_selection "${exit_node_id}"
4047:       fi
4048:       ;;
4049:     quick-exit-node)
4050:       if is_blind_exit_role; then
4051:         print_info "blind_exit role enforces exit-serving mode without exposing manual route mutation."
4052:       else
4053:         if run_rustynet_cli route advertise 0.0.0.0/0; then
4054:           print_info "Exit route advertised (0.0.0.0/0)."
4055:         else
4056:           print_warn "Failed to advertise exit route. Check auto-tunnel policy restrictions."
4057:         fi
4058:         apply_lan_mode_noninteractive "${lan_mode}"
4059:       fi
4060:       ;;
4061:     quick-hybrid)
4062:       if [[ -n "${exit_node_id}" ]]; then
4063:         apply_launch_profile_exit_selection "${exit_node_id}"
4064:       fi
4065:       if run_rustynet_cli route advertise 0.0.0.0/0; then
4066:         print_info "Exit route advertised (0.0.0.0/0)."
4067:       else
4068:         print_warn "Failed to advertise exit route. Check auto-tunnel policy restrictions."
4069:       fi
4070:       apply_lan_mode_noninteractive "${lan_mode}"
4071:       ;;
4072:   esac
4073: }

4491: if [[ -n "${REQUESTED_EXIT_NODE_ID}" ]]; then
4492:   launch_exit_node_id="${REQUESTED_EXIT_NODE_ID}"
4493: fi
4494: if [[ -n "${REQUESTED_LAN_MODE}" ]]; then
4495:   launch_lan_mode="${REQUESTED_LAN_MODE}"
4496: fi
4497: 
4498: if [[ "${REQUESTED_LAUNCH_PROFILE}" == "auto" ]]; then
4499:   launch_profile="${DEFAULT_LAUNCH_PROFILE}"
4500: elif [[ -n "${REQUESTED_LAUNCH_PROFILE}" ]]; then
4501:   launch_profile="${REQUESTED_LAUNCH_PROFILE}"
4502: elif [[ "${AUTO_LAUNCH_ON_START}" == "1" ]]; then
4503:   launch_profile="${DEFAULT_LAUNCH_PROFILE}"
4504: fi
4505: 
4506: if [[ -n "${launch_profile}" && "${launch_profile}" != "menu" ]]; then
4507:   if ! apply_launch_profile "${launch_profile}" "${launch_exit_node_id}" "${launch_lan_mode}"; then
4508:     if [[ "${AUTO_ONLY_LAUNCH}" == "1" ]]; then
4509:       exit 1
4510:     fi
4511:   fi
4512:   if [[ "${AUTO_ONLY_LAUNCH}" == "1" ]]; then
4513:     exit 0
4514:   fi
4515: fi
4516: 
4517: main_menu

===== /tools/skills/rustynet-security-auditor/SKILL.md =====

   1: ---
   2: name: rustynet-security-auditor
   3: description: Use when the target is specifically the Rustynet repository or a Rustynet live lab: audit Rustynet’s control plane, dataplane, DNS, traversal, and release evidence; run the canonical Rustynet live validators; correlate findings to Rustynet enforcement points; and produce reproducible hardening guidance plus coverage decisions for Rustynet exploit classes.
   4: ---
   5: 
   6: # Rustynet Security Auditor
   7: 
   8: Use this skill only for Rustynet. It is the Rustynet-specific layer above the generic network adversarial hardening workflow.
   9: 
  10: The source of truth for this skill is the version committed in the Rustynet repo under `tools/skills/rustynet-security-auditor/`. If a global installed copy exists under `~/.codex/skills`, keep it synchronized from the repo copy.
  11: 
  12: ## When To Use This Skill
  13: 
  14: Use this skill when the user wants to:
  15: - audit Rustynet specifically for security weaknesses
  16: - run or interpret Rustynet live-lab adversarial validations
  17: - compare Rustynet against historical exploit classes from Tailscale, WireGuard-based clients, OpenVPN, NetBird, and similar systems
  18: - decide whether a Rustynet exploit class is still `partially_covered` or can be promoted to `covered`
  19: - generate Rustynet-specific hardening findings with direct file and gate correlation
  20: 
  21: Do not use this skill for:
  22: - non-Rustynet targets
  23: - offensive activity against any non-lab network
  24: - generic penetration testing without a Rustynet hardening objective
  25: 
  26: ## Required Rustynet Context
  27: 
  28: Before doing substantial work, read:
  29: - `README.md`
  30: - `AGENTS.md`
  31: - `CLAUDE.md`
  32: - `documents/Requirements.md`
  33: - `documents/SecurityMinimumBar.md`
  34: - `documents/phase10.md`
  35: - `references/rustynet-audit-surface-map.md`
  36: 
  37: Load additional references only as needed:
  38: - `references/comparative-vpn-exploit-catalog.md`
  39: - `references/live-lab-correlation-map.md`
  40: - `references/attack-catalog.md`
  41: - `references/lab-playbooks.md`
  42: - `references/audit-checklist.md`
  43: 
  44: ## Rustynet Workflow
  45: 
  46: ### 1. Establish Rustynet Scope
  47: 
  48: Determine whether the task is:
  49: - code audit only
  50: - comparative exploit audit
  51: - live-lab validation
  52: - coverage-promotion decision
  53: 
  54: If the live lab is not explicitly authorized, stop at code audit and comparative analysis.
  55: 
  56: ### 2. Rustynet Comparative Baseline
  57: 
  58: When the user wants exploit comparison or weakness discovery:
  59: 1. run `rustynet ops generate-comparative-exploit-coverage`
  60: 2. if useful, add `--run-local-tests`
  61: 3. inspect every `future_surface_gap` and `partially_covered` item
  62: 4. do not claim `covered` from local tests alone where the comparative mapping still requires live evidence
  63: 
  64: Default output path:
  65: - `documents/operations/RustynetComparativeVpnExploitCoverage_<date>.md`
  66: 
  67: ### 3. Rustynet Live-Lab Validation
  68: 
  69: For Rustynet live-lab work, use one hardened execution path only:
  70: - `rustynet ops run-live-lab-validations`
  71: 
  72: Do not hand-stitch validator runs unless you are debugging the runner itself.
  73: 
  74: The runner is the canonical path because it:
  75: - executes the selected Rustynet validators
  76: - emits canonical JSON reports
  77: - requires a pinned SSH `known_hosts` path and validates host-key presence before any validator starts
  78: - verifies SSH reachability to every targeted host before any validator starts
  79: - verifies the required remote binaries and the `rustynetd.service` unit are present before any validator starts
  80: - validates report schema
  81: - generates prioritized findings
  82: - evaluates whether comparative coverage can be promoted
  83: 
  84: The schema, promotion, matrix, findings, comparative coverage, and live-runner logic now live in `rustynet-cli` ops commands. The older Python entrypoints have been retired from the repo.
  85: 
  86: Default validation set for the currently partially covered exploit classes:
  87: - `control_surface_exposure`
  88: - `server_ip_bypass`
  89: - `endpoint_hijack`
  90: 
  91: ### 4. Rustynet Findings And Correlation
  92: 
  93: After live execution:
  94: 1. read the generated findings markdown from `rustynet ops generate-live-lab-findings`
  95: 2. use `references/live-lab-correlation-map.md`
  96: 3. confirm the likely Rustynet enforcement points in source
  97: 4. check the relevant gates and tests before proposing fixes
  98: 
  99: Never stop at runtime symptoms. Always tie the finding to:
 100: - the failing validator check
 101: - the relevant Rustynet files
 102: - the missing or weakened enforcement point
 103: - the regression test or gate that must prove the fix
 104: 
 105: ### 5. Rustynet Coverage Promotion
 106: 
 107: Only promote a comparative exploit class from `partially_covered` to `covered` if:
 108: - the required Rustynet live validator report exists
 109: - report schema validation passed
 110: - the report status is `pass`
 111: - every mandatory check passed
 112: - the promotion gate `rustynet ops evaluate-live-coverage-promotion` returns success
 113: 
 114: If any of those conditions fail, keep the exploit class at `partially_covered`.
 115: 
 116: ## Required Output
 117: 
 118: For Rustynet work, outputs should be concrete and usually written into repo-visible `.md` artifacts under `documents/operations/` unless the user asks otherwise.
 119: 
 120: Preferred output order:
 121: 1. findings
 122: 2. assumptions or open questions
 123: 3. remediation summary
 124: 4. exact verification path
 125: 
 126: Include:
 127: - affected Rustynet subsystem
 128: - exploit family
 129: - exact failing validator or test
 130: - exact Rustynet files to inspect
 131: - fail-open vs fail-closed result
 132: - remediation with one hardened path only
 133: 
 134: ## Bundled Commands
 135: 
 136: - `rustynet ops generate-comparative-exploit-coverage`
 137:   Generate the Rustynet exploit coverage baseline from historical VPN incidents.
 138: - `rustynet ops run-live-lab-validations`
 139:   Canonical Rustynet live-lab runner.
 140: - `rustynet ops validate-live-lab-reports`
 141:   Enforce the shared Rustynet live-report schema.
 142: - `rustynet ops generate-live-lab-findings`
 143:   Convert live report failures into prioritized Rustynet findings.
 144: - `rustynet ops evaluate-live-coverage-promotion`
 145:   Fail closed on exploit coverage promotion unless required live evidence is strong.
 146: - `rustynet ops generate-attack-matrix`
 147:   Create canonical attack matrices.
 148: - `rustynet ops generate-assessment-from-matrix`
 149:   Produce a markdown scaffold from the matrix.
 150: 
 151: ## Non-Negotiable Constraints
 152: 
 153: - Rustynet only
 154: - lab-only, authorized-only for live validations
 155: - default-deny and fail-closed are the expected secure outcomes
 156: - one hardened execution path per security-sensitive workflow
 157: - no fallback or downgrade suggestions
 158: - do not weaken Rustynet gates to make reports pass

===== /tools/skills/rustynet-security-auditor/references/attack-catalog.md =====

   1: # Attack Catalog
   2: 
   3: Use this catalog to choose the smallest set of attack simulations that best cover the highest-risk trust boundaries.
   4: 
   5: ## How To Use This Catalog
   6: 
   7: For each family:
   8: 1. state the security hypothesis
   9: 2. define the minimum lab setup
  10: 3. define the expected fail-closed behavior
  11: 4. collect runtime evidence
  12: 5. map any failure back to source and tests
  13: 
  14: Do not run every category by default. Pick the categories that meaningfully exercise the target's trust model.
  15: 
  16: ## 1. Control-Plane Authenticity, Replay, And Rollback
  17: 
  18: **Goal**
  19: - Prove that stale, replayed, downgraded, or forged control artifacts cannot mutate runtime state.
  20: 
  21: **Typical lab simulations**
  22: - replay an old signed bundle
  23: - substitute a bundle with a lower generation or older watermark
  24: - remove or corrupt verifier keys
  25: - tamper with a signed artifact after issuance
  26: 
  27: **Expected secure behavior**
  28: - reject the artifact
  29: - preserve current secure state or fail closed
  30: - log an actionable validation error without secrets
  31: 
  32: **Source audit targets**
  33: - signature verification
  34: - nonce, epoch, watermark, max-age checks
  35: - equality-vs-greater-than rollback logic
  36: - artifact loading paths and temp-file custody
  37: 
  38: ## 2. Local Control Surface Spoofing
  39: 
  40: **Goal**
  41: - Prove that local clients cannot be tricked into talking to a spoofed daemon or helper surface.
  42: 
  43: **Typical lab simulations**
  44: - symlink a Unix socket path
  45: - create a world-writable socket or parent directory
  46: - replace a trusted runtime socket with an attacker-owned endpoint
  47: - race a client against a stale or malicious local IPC surface
  48: 
  49: **Expected secure behavior**
  50: - reject the path before connecting
  51: - verify ownership, permissions, and path integrity
  52: - refuse insecure parents and symlinks
  53: 
  54: **Source audit targets**
  55: - socket validation
  56: - helper-client validation
  57: - peer credential checks
  58: - parent-directory trust checks
  59: 
  60: ## 3. Host Trust And Bootstrap Downgrade
  61: 
  62: **Goal**
  63: - Prove that node onboarding and automation do not silently trust a malicious or changed host identity.
  64: 
  65: **Typical lab simulations**
  66: - swap host keys in a lab SSH target
  67: - delete pinned trust data and observe reconnect behavior
  68: - present a new host with the same IP
  69: 
  70: **Expected secure behavior**
  71: - host verification fails closed
  72: - no TOFU downgrade or auto-accept path
  73: - operator sees a precise trust error
  74: 
  75: **Source audit targets**
  76: - SSH wrappers and automation harnesses
  77: - host-key handling
  78: - setup and provisioning flows
  79: 
  80: ## 4. Route, Exit, And Path Hijack
  81: 
  82: **Goal**
  83: - Prove that an attacker cannot widen routing or redirect traffic through an unauthorized path.
  84: 
  85: **Typical lab simulations**
  86: - inject unexpected routes
  87: - replay or forge exit-selection state
  88: - force ambiguous egress-interface conditions
  89: - attempt endpoint substitution for a peer or exit path
  90: 
  91: **Expected secure behavior**
  92: - path is rejected or reconciled back to signed state
  93: - traffic fails closed rather than leaking
  94: - authorization boundaries remain intact
  95: 
  96: **Source audit targets**
  97: - route installation
  98: - exit-selection workflows
  99: - endpoint mutation paths
 100: - interface auto-detection and bypass routing
 101: 
 102: ## 5. DNS Integrity And Namespace Abuse
 103: 
 104: **Goal**
 105: - Prove that managed names cannot be spoofed, silently widened, or resolved through insecure fallback paths.
 106: 
 107: **Typical lab simulations**
 108: - install a stale signed DNS bundle
 109: - point a name at an address not justified by signed assignment state
 110: - query non-managed names against the authoritative resolver
 111: - remove the verifier key or signed zone
 112: 
 113: **Expected secure behavior**
 114: - managed names fail closed when state is missing or invalid
 115: - unauthorized mappings are rejected
 116: - non-managed names are refused, not guessed or forwarded through insecure local overrides
 117: 
 118: **Source audit targets**
 119: - DNS bundle verification
 120: - resolver bind restrictions
 121: - host-integration path
 122: - any `/etc/hosts` or raw resolver fallback
 123: 
 124: ## 6. NAT Traversal And Relay Abuse
 125: 
 126: **Goal**
 127: - Prove that endpoint hints, relay activation, and failback decisions cannot be forged or widened.
 128: 
 129: **Typical lab simulations**
 130: - tamper with traversal bundles
 131: - inject stale endpoint hints
 132: - force relay mode and observe reprobe behavior
 133: - attempt direct-path promotion without fresh handshake evidence
 134: 
 135: **Expected secure behavior**
 136: - traversal artifacts are verified and bounded
 137: - direct promotion requires fresh evidence
 138: - relay fallback is explicit and authorized
 139: - reprobe logic does not trust stale cached state
 140: 
 141: **Source audit targets**
 142: - traversal bundle verification
 143: - handshake evidence freshness
 144: - relay/direct mode transitions
 145: - reprobe cadence and promotion logic
 146: 
 147: ## 7. Secret Custody And Log Leakage
 148: 
 149: **Goal**
 150: - Prove that secrets do not leak through files, temp paths, environment, argv, or logs.
 151: 
 152: **Typical lab simulations**
 153: - inspect temp paths and service credentials during refresh flows
 154: - review logs after failed operations
 155: - scan for world-readable files in runtime custody paths
 156: 
 157: **Expected secure behavior**
 158: - encrypted-at-rest or OS-protected storage only
 159: - strict file modes and ownership
 160: - no plaintext passphrases in logs or long-lived files
 161: 
 162: **Source audit targets**
 163: - credential materialization
 164: - temp-file handling
 165: - secure delete or scrub paths
 166: - debug logging and structured event emission
 167: 
 168: ## 8. Fail-Closed Behavior Under Missing Or Invalid State
 169: 
 170: **Goal**
 171: - Prove that the system becomes restrictive, not permissive, when required trust inputs disappear.
 172: 
 173: **Typical lab simulations**
 174: - remove signed assignment state
 175: - remove trust evidence or verifier keys
 176: - block a refresh path and observe runtime
 177: - stop a DNS or membership update path
 178: 
 179: **Expected secure behavior**
 180: - no silent fallback to legacy or manual paths
 181: - tunnel, DNS, or privileged mutations fail closed
 182: - the error is explicit and diagnosable
 183: 
 184: **Source audit targets**
 185: - `fallback`, `legacy`, `compat`, `auto-detect`, `best-effort`
 186: - shell wrappers around Rust commands
 187: - manual mutation paths that bypass signed control state
 188: 
 189: ## 9. Privileged Helper Input Abuse
 190: 
 191: **Goal**
 192: - Prove that helper boundaries cannot be crossed with argument injection or schema abuse.
 193: 
 194: **Typical lab simulations**
 195: - malformed request frames
 196: - oversized arguments
 197: - invalid token sequences
 198: - command-schema mismatch attempts
 199: 
 200: **Expected secure behavior**
 201: - strict parser rejection
 202: - bounded argument counts and sizes
 203: - no shell interpretation
 204: 
 205: **Source audit targets**
 206: - helper schemas
 207: - input validation
 208: - argv-only exec paths
 209: - fuzz or negative tests
 210: 
 211: ## 10. Supply Chain And Release Evidence Integrity
 212: 
 213: **Goal**
 214: - Prove that release evidence, provenance, and generated security artifacts are bound to the correct source state.
 215: 
 216: **Typical lab simulations**
 217: - verify artifact provenance against the wrong commit
 218: - swap a generated report while preserving filenames
 219: - depend on untracked local evidence paths
 220: 
 221: **Expected secure behavior**
 222: - commit binding is explicit
 223: - evidence paths are canonical and portable
 224: - stale or mismatched evidence fails the gate
 225: 
 226: **Source audit targets**
 227: - gate scripts
 228: - artifact generation
 229: - provenance signing and verification
 230: - report source-path references

===== /tools/skills/rustynet-security-auditor/references/audit-checklist.md =====

   1: # Audit Checklist
   2: 
   3: Use this checklist after choosing attack families. The goal is to find the exact code path that would allow a staged attack to succeed or to prove the control is enforced.
   4: 
   5: ## Review Order
   6: 
   7: 1. security requirements and architecture docs
   8: 2. artifact issuance and verification
   9: 3. privileged boundaries
  10: 4. runtime reconciliation and fail-closed behavior
  11: 5. orchestration and automation harnesses
  12: 6. tests and gates
  13: 
  14: ## Control-Plane Integrity
  15: 
  16: Check:
  17: - every mutation path requires signed, verified, current control state
  18: - replay and rollback protection uses monotonic or digest-bound state
  19: - stale artifact rejection is explicit
  20: - missing verifier keys fail closed
  21: 
  22: Search patterns:
  23: - `watermark`
  24: - `max_age`
  25: - `expires_at`
  26: - `nonce`
  27: - `verify`
  28: - `signature`
  29: - `allow`
  30: - `generation`
  31: - `epoch`
  32: 
  33: ## Fallback And Legacy Path Detection
  34: 
  35: Treat these as immediate review hotspots:
  36: - `fallback`
  37: - `legacy`
  38: - `compat`
  39: - `best-effort`
  40: - `accept-new`
  41: - `TODO`
  42: - `FIXME`
  43: - `|| true`
  44: 
  45: Questions:
  46: - is there more than one path for a security-sensitive workflow?
  47: - does any path bypass signed state?
  48: - does any shell wrapper continue after a failed security step?
  49: 
  50: ## Local Trust Surface Validation
  51: 
  52: Check:
  53: - Unix socket paths are absolute
  54: - sockets and parent directories are not symlinks
  55: - permissions are strict and ownership is trusted
  56: - helper clients verify the target path before connecting
  57: 
  58: Search patterns:
  59: - `UnixStream`
  60: - `metadata`
  61: - `symlink_metadata`
  62: - `PermissionsExt`
  63: - `peer_cred`
  64: - `socket`
  65: 
  66: ## Privileged Helper Boundaries
  67: 
  68: Check:
  69: - argv-only exec, no shell construction
  70: - strict request schema validation
  71: - bounded argument counts and byte sizes
  72: - no untrusted path execution
  73: 
  74: Search patterns:
  75: - `Command::new`
  76: - `sh -c`
  77: - `bash -c`
  78: - `system(`
  79: - `exec`
  80: - `helper`
  81: - `schema`
  82: - `validate`
  83: 
  84: ## DNS Integrity
  85: 
  86: Check:
  87: - only signed DNS bundles are trusted
  88: - records are cross-checked against assignment state
  89: - resolver is loopback-only unless there is a documented secure reason otherwise
  90: - non-managed names are refused by the authoritative path
  91: - there is no `/etc/hosts` fallback
  92: 
  93: Search patterns:
  94: - `dns`
  95: - `resolver`
  96: - `zone`
  97: - `SERVFAIL`
  98: - `REFUSED`
  99: - `hosts`
 100: - `resolvectl`
 101: 
 102: ## Routing And Exit Selection
 103: 
 104: Check:
 105: - exit-node and route changes require current signed state
 106: - default-route or egress-interface detection is validated, not assumed
 107: - split-tunnel or bypass routes are scoped and auditable
 108: - selection restore paths are as hardened as selection paths
 109: 
 110: Search patterns:
 111: - `route`
 112: - `exit`
 113: - `egress`
 114: - `interface`
 115: - `advertise`
 116: - `bypass`
 117: 
 118: ## NAT Traversal And Relay
 119: 
 120: Check:
 121: - direct/relay promotion requires fresh evidence
 122: - stale traversal bundles are rejected
 123: - reprobe and failback decisions use live state, not only cached decisions
 124: - relay activation is explicit and bounded
 125: 
 126: Search patterns:
 127: - `traversal`
 128: - `relay`
 129: - `probe`
 130: - `handshake`
 131: - `latest-handshakes`
 132: - `freshness`
 133: 
 134: ## Secret Custody
 135: 
 136: Check:
 137: - no plaintext secret logging
 138: - temp files are owner-only and scrubbed
 139: - credential injection paths are OS-protected where possible
 140: - secrets do not persist longer than required
 141: 
 142: Search patterns:
 143: - `passphrase`
 144: - `credential`
 145: - `keychain`
 146: - `systemd-creds`
 147: - `temp`
 148: - `NamedTempFile`
 149: - `debug!`
 150: - `trace!`
 151: 
 152: ## Test And Gate Coverage
 153: 
 154: Every security control should have at least one verification path:
 155: - unit or integration test
 156: - negative test
 157: - CI gate
 158: - live lab evidence if runtime-specific
 159: 
 160: Questions:
 161: - if this control broke, what test would fail?
 162: - is there a test for both the good path and the tampered path?
 163: - does the gate validate portable, commit-bound evidence?
 164: 
 165: ## Report Discipline
 166: 
 167: For every finding, capture:
 168: - title
 169: - severity
 170: - attack family
 171: - exact evidence
 172: - exact file and line or subsystem
 173: - secure expected behavior
 174: - actual behavior
 175: - exact remediation
 176: - required regression test or gate

===== /tools/skills/rustynet-security-auditor/references/comparative-vpn-exploit-catalog.md =====

   1: # Comparative VPN Exploit Catalog
   2: 
   3: Use this reference when the user wants to benchmark Rustynet against well-known exploit classes that affected Tailscale, WireGuard-based clients, OpenVPN, NetBird, and similar networking systems.
   4: 
   5: This list is intentionally primary-source-driven and security-focused. It is not a claim that every item is identical in mechanism or impact to Rustynet. The goal is to turn real historical failures into concrete Rustynet audit and lab-check targets.
   6: 
   7: ## Scope Notes
   8: 
   9: - Prefer vendor bulletins, vendor advisories, vendor security announcements, or first-party project docs.
  10: - Where the upstream project does not publish a rich advisory stream, include first-party design limitations and public research that affected the project class.
  11: - Treat every item as an exploit class to test, not just a historical anecdote.
  12: - For Rustynet, map each item to:
  13:   - the closest trust boundary
  14:   - the expected fail-closed behavior
  15:   - the exact local tests or gates to run
  16:   - the live-lab playbook to stage later if a lab is available
  17: 
  18: ## Status Vocabulary
  19: 
  20: - `covered`: Rustynet already has a strong local test or gate that directly exercises the exploit class.
  21: - `partially_covered`: Rustynet has relevant controls, but the exploit class is only indirectly exercised or still needs live-lab evidence.
  22: - `architecturally_not_applicable`: Rustynet does not currently expose the vulnerable surface in the same form, but preserve that invariant.
  23: - `future_surface_gap`: The comparable feature is planned but not yet implemented; the exploit class must stay on the backlog and be blocked into the design before that feature ships.
  24: 
  25: ## Current Rustynet Live-Lab Coverage Upgrades
  26: 
  27: The following previously `partially_covered` exploit classes now have dedicated live-lab validation scripts in the Rustynet repo. They still remain `partially_covered` until those scripts are run against an authorized lab and their evidence is reviewed.
  28: 
  29: | Historical Class | Rustynet Live Validation |
  30: | --- | --- |
  31: | Tailscale `TS-2022-005` peer API DNS rebinding analogue | `scripts/e2e/live_linux_control_surface_exposure_test.sh` |

===== /tools/skills/rustynet-security-auditor/references/lab-playbooks.md =====

   1: # Lab Playbooks
   2: 
   3: Use these playbooks to stage concrete, lab-only attack simulations. Each playbook is intentionally narrow: it should test one trust boundary at a time and produce evidence that maps cleanly back to source and tests.
   4: 
   5: ## Common Rules
   6: 
   7: Before running any playbook:
   8: - confirm the environment is isolated and authorized
   9: - snapshot current state when practical
  10: - record exact node names, roles, and custody paths
  11: - define the expected fail-closed outcome in advance
  12: - stop if the action would broaden beyond the agreed lab scope
  13: 
  14: For each playbook, capture:
  15: - preconditions
  16: - exact commands or file mutations used
  17: - observed runtime result
  18: - logs or reports
  19: - source files and tests that explain the outcome
  20: 
  21: ## 1. Control-Plane Replay And Rollback
  22: 
  23: **When to use**
  24: - signed assignments, trust evidence, traversal bundles, DNS bundles, or membership artifacts exist
  25: 
  26: **Preconditions**
  27: - one valid current artifact
  28: - one older or modified artifact for the same subject
  29: 
  30: **Procedure**
  31: 1. record current runtime status and active generation or watermark
  32: 2. replace the current artifact with the stale, replayed, or tampered version
  33: 3. trigger the normal reload or reconcile path
  34: 4. observe whether state is rejected, preserved, or incorrectly accepted
  35: 
  36: **Expected secure result**
  37: - stale or tampered artifact is rejected
  38: - current secure state remains or the system fails closed
  39: 
  40: **Evidence to collect**
  41: - status output before and after
  42: - validation error messages
  43: - artifact verification logs
  44: - unit or integration tests covering replay rejection
  45: 
  46: ## 2. Local Control Surface Spoofing
  47: 
  48: **When to use**
  49: - local clients connect to a daemon or helper over a Unix socket
  50: 
  51: **Preconditions**
  52: - a non-production test user or temp runtime directory
  53: 
  54: **Procedure**
  55: 1. create an attacker-owned or insecure socket path in a temp area
  56: 2. make the parent directory symlinked or group/world writable
  57: 3. point the client at that path if the interface allows explicit path selection
  58: 4. observe whether the client rejects the path before connecting
  59: 
  60: **Expected secure result**
  61: - client refuses the path based on ownership, symlink, or permission checks
  62: 
  63: **Evidence to collect**
  64: - client error message
  65: - file metadata for the spoofed path
  66: - code references for socket validation
  67: 
  68: ## 3. Host Trust Downgrade
  69: 
  70: **When to use**
  71: - automation reaches remote lab nodes over SSH
  72: 
  73: **Preconditions**
  74: - pinned host keys for the lab nodes
  75: 
  76: **Procedure**
  77: 1. replace the host key for one lab VM or point the IP at a different VM
  78: 2. re-run the provisioning or test harness against the pinned entry
  79: 3. observe whether the connection hard-fails
  80: 
  81: **Expected secure result**
  82: - connection is refused with a host-identity error
  83: - no TOFU or auto-accept path is taken
  84: 
  85: **Evidence to collect**
  86: - harness error output
  87: - pinned known_hosts entry
  88: - code path or wrapper enforcing host-key checks
  89: 
  90: ## 4. Route Or Exit Hijack
  91: 
  92: **When to use**
  93: - the system supports exit selection, route advertisement, or path programming
  94: 
  95: **Preconditions**
  96: - one valid route or exit configuration
  97: 
  98: **Procedure**
  99: 1. attempt to introduce an unexpected route, endpoint, or exit selection artifact
 100: 2. trigger reconcile or reload
 101: 3. inspect the programmed route set and selected path
 102: 
 103: **Expected secure result**
 104: - unauthorized route or exit state is rejected
 105: - data plane does not widen beyond signed or authorized state
 106: 
 107: **Evidence to collect**
 108: - route tables before and after
 109: - selected exit or endpoint status
 110: - policy or assignment verification logs
 111: 
 112: ## 5. DNS Integrity And Namespace Abuse
 113: 
 114: **When to use**
 115: - managed DNS is implemented through signed state
 116: 
 117: **Preconditions**
 118: - one valid DNS bundle and verifier key
 119: 
 120: **Procedure**
 121: 1. install a stale or mismatched DNS bundle
 122: 2. query a managed name and a non-managed name
 123: 3. optionally try a record whose target node does not justify the address
 124: 
 125: **Expected secure result**
 126: - managed name fails closed when the bundle is stale or invalid
 127: - unauthorized mapping is rejected
 128: - non-managed names are refused by the authoritative path
 129: 
 130: **Evidence to collect**
 131: - resolver outputs
 132: - daemon status or inspect output
 133: - bundle verification logs
 134: 
 135: ## 6. Traversal Hint Or Relay Abuse
 136: 
 137: **When to use**
 138: - the system accepts signed traversal bundles or relay/direct path transitions
 139: 
 140: **Preconditions**
 141: - one direct-capable or relay-backed test path
 142: 
 143: **Procedure**
 144: 1. install a tampered or stale traversal bundle, or force relay mode in a controlled way
 145: 2. trigger reconcile and observe direct or relay selection
 146: 3. verify whether direct promotion requires fresh handshake evidence
 147: 
 148: **Expected secure result**
 149: - stale or forged hints are rejected
 150: - relay failback occurs only with fresh evidence
 151: 
 152: **Evidence to collect**
 153: - netcheck or status outputs
 154: - traversal logs
 155: - source locations for probe freshness enforcement
 156: 
 157: ## 7. Secret Custody And Log Leakage
 158: 
 159: **When to use**
 160: - the system handles passphrases, signing keys, temp files, or service credentials
 161: 
 162: **Preconditions**
 163: - access to the isolated lab host filesystem and logs
 164: 
 165: **Procedure**
 166: 1. exercise a refresh or issuance flow that materializes sensitive state
 167: 2. inspect temp directories, service runtime credentials, and logs after completion
 168: 3. confirm whether any plaintext secret remains or was logged
 169: 
 170: **Expected secure result**
 171: - secrets are encrypted or OS-protected at rest
 172: - temp files are tightly permissioned and scrubbed
 173: - logs do not contain plaintext secret material
 174: 
 175: **Evidence to collect**
 176: - file modes and ownership
 177: - log excerpts without secrets
 178: - tests that assert redaction or secure temp handling
 179: 
 180: ## 8. Missing-State Fail-Closed Validation
 181: 
 182: **When to use**
 183: - trust-critical state can be removed or blocked in a lab
 184: 
 185: **Preconditions**
 186: - a working baseline state and a restoration path
 187: 
 188: **Procedure**
 189: 1. remove or invalidate one required trust input
 190: 2. trigger the normal runtime path
 191: 3. observe whether the system becomes restrictive or permissive
 192: 
 193: **Expected secure result**
 194: - relevant operation fails closed
 195: - no legacy, manual, or insecure fallback path is taken
 196: 
 197: **Evidence to collect**
 198: - runtime status
 199: - gate output
 200: - exact error or enforcement path
 201: 
 202: ## 9. Privileged Helper Input Abuse
 203: 
 204: **When to use**
 205: - a privileged helper accepts structured commands from an unprivileged component
 206: 
 207: **Preconditions**
 208: - negative-test harness or fuzz-like request path in a lab
 209: 
 210: **Procedure**
 211: 1. send malformed, oversized, or schema-invalid requests through the supported test path
 212: 2. observe whether the helper rejects before any privileged action occurs
 213: 
 214: **Expected secure result**
 215: - request is rejected deterministically
 216: - no shell interpretation or partial privileged execution occurs
 217: 
 218: **Evidence to collect**
 219: - helper response or log
 220: - negative test outputs
 221: - source validation routines
 222: 
 223: ## 10. Release Evidence Integrity
 224: 
 225: **When to use**
 226: - the project ships provenance, OS matrix reports, or generated security evidence
 227: 
 228: **Preconditions**
 229: - current source state and previously generated evidence
 230: 
 231: **Procedure**
 232: 1. verify evidence against the current commit
 233: 2. inspect report source paths for portability
 234: 3. substitute stale or mismatched evidence where safe in the lab
 235: 
 236: **Expected secure result**
 237: - stale or mismatched evidence is rejected
 238: - canonical source paths are required
 239: 
 240: **Evidence to collect**
 241: - gate output
 242: - report commit binding
 243: - source-path references within the report

  17:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/privileged_helper.rs`
  18:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs`

  20:   - `all_daemon_sockets_secure`

  22:   - `all_helper_sockets_secure`

  24:   - `no_rustynet_tcp_listeners`

  29:     - peer underlay could query managed DNS directly

  32:

  34: - Report mode: `live_linux_server_ip_bypass`

  37: - Primary exploit family:
  38:   - `route-hijack`

  40:   - `scripts/e2e/live_linux_server_ip_bypass_test.sh`
  41: - Likely enforcement points:
  42:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs`
  43:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/dataplane.rs`
  44:   - `crates/rustynet-backend-wireguard/src/lib.rs`
  45: - Key failure meanings:
  46:   - `internet_route_via_rustynet0`
  47:     - protected internet route bypassed the tunnel
  48:   - `probe_endpoint_route_direct_not_tunnelled`
  49:     - peer endpoint bypass route is wrong or overly broad
  50:   - `probe_service_blocked_from_client`
  51:     - endpoint or management bypass widened into real service reachability
  52:   - `no_unexpected_bypass_routes`
  53:     - extra bypass routes created broader leak surface
  54: 
  55: ## Endpoint Hijack And Traversal Fail-Closed
  56: 
  57: - Validation key: `endpoint_hijack`
  58: - Report mode: `live_linux_endpoint_hijack`

  60:   - WireGuard host-integration / endpoint-mobility risk class
  61: - Primary exploit family:
  62:   - `traversal-abuse`

  64:   - `scripts/e2e/live_linux_endpoint_hijack_test.sh`
  65: - Likely enforcement points:
  66:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/daemon.rs`
  67:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/traversal.rs`
  68:   - `crates/rustynetd/src/phase10.rs`
  69: - Key failure meanings:
  70:   - `hijack_drives_fail_closed`
  71:     - tampered endpoint assignment did not force secure denial
  72:   - `restricted_safe_mode_engaged`
  73:     - runtime trust failure was not made explicitly restrictive
  74:   - `netcheck_reports_fail_closed`
  75:     - operator diagnostics do not surface traversal integrity loss
  76:   - `rogue_endpoint_not_adopted`
  77:     - forged endpoint was accepted into runtime state
  78:   - `recovery_restores_secure_runtime`
  79:     - restore path is incomplete or non-deterministic
  80:   - `recovery_keeps_rogue_endpoint_rejected`
  81:     - rogue endpoint survived trusted-state restoration
